-># GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II.<-

...a slave for a slave, a woman for a woman, and so forth. All of these things Christ wished for us to refer to the office of the judges <note>Postel argues that while Islamic law (following ancient Near Eastern traditions) emphasizes literal "eye for an eye" retaliation, Christian doctrine should leave judgment to legal authorities or divine mercy.</note>. But it was necessary for you to "Judaize" <note>To "Judaize" was a common 16th-century polemical term for adopting Jewish-style legalism or rituals instead of Christian spiritualism.</note> with those for whom you were the Messiah, and to trample upon the holy precepts of Christ. Indeed, he even instituted a fast according to the custom of the ancestors—lest he fail to "Judaize"—which he then exchanges for almsgiving, so that he might flatter everyone. He says:

« *In the month of Ramadan, in which the Quran <note>original: *Alcoranum*</note> itself descended for the guidance*
« *of men, and the wisdom of the Criterion <note>original: *Alphurcan*; referring to Al-Furqan, an Arabic title for the Quran meaning "The Criterion" between right and wrong</note>, whoever among you is able during that*
« *month, let him fast; and he who is sick, or on an expedition, shall postpone*
« *the number of days, as God will advise.*

In this place it is clear that before Muhammad there was no Quran or Criterion. From this it appears, as I noted above, that Muhammad told a manifest lie when he said it was given to Moses. Indeed, one must look at the Quranic fast:

« *And it is permitted to you during the fast to be with women. For*
« *God is merciful. Eat and drink until the white line*
« *(that is, the dawn) appears to you against the darkness, then*
« *begin the fast again.*

An extraordinary fast, and one worthy of its author! In it, the night—given for rest and meditation—is turned entirely into gluttony <note>original: *crapula*; implying excessive eating and drinking</note> and a life worthy not of a man, but of beasts. It is as if the fast were given so that you might abstain during the day, but gorge yourself by night, rather than to weaken the desires of the flesh. In truth, in this fast, two types of men had to be satisfied: he wished for them to fast according to the custom of the Hebrews and Christians—this he did at the beginning of his persuasion by prescribing the fast—but so that he might accommodate himself and those Arabs like him, corrupted by luxury and Venus <note>A common Renaissance metaphor for sexual desire or activity.</note> and accompanied by a multitude of wives, he willed that throughout the night the reins of the throat and gluttony be loosened. This was so that their strength might satisfy Venus; for this prophet, who boasted that he had from God the sexual vigor of forty strong men, did not wish to suffer from thinness or to desist from such a "noble" gift. Who does not see that this impious, pagan Epicurean <note>A follower of Epicurus, here used as a slur for someone devoted to physical pleasure.</note>, under the false name of piety, forced himself upon the simplicity of unlearned men?

A little later, he speaks again concerning war, saying that those who die in it will be most happy [blessed], provided they believe in him: all who oppose them must be killed until they submit. What kind of "prophetic" virtue is this? What tyrant, robber, or murderer would not similarly encourage his followers? Such things are far removed from the gift of prophecy. But he was in the *Hijra* <term>the "Migration" or flight of Muhammad from Mecca to Medina in 622 AD</term>, that is, in exile. He had deserved this through his factions, and because of it, he was armed against the citizens of Mecca. For this reason, it is likely that this chapter, although its place of writing is not stated, was nevertheless written in Medina. This is because he is armed by the favor of the citizens of the Jews (of whom there were many in Yathrib <note>original: *Iezrab*; the pre-Islamic name for Medina</note>), whose labor he easily used alongside the peasants, because they were most ready for plunder. He says, therefore, that those adversaries in the temple of Mecca are to be killed in the same way they previously killed his own people in that same temple. That matter is explained more at length there.

Furthermore, so that the cause might appear more just, he tells the soldier there is the *Hajj* <term>the pilgrimage to Mecca</term>, in which they fast for three days, and seven days upon their return, so that religion might cover the vice. But to the point:

« *And they will ask about wine and the recreation of the gaming-board. Say,*
« *in them is a grave sin, and a help to men; but the sin is*
« *greater than the benefit.*

He condemns games and wine: the former, lest his soldiers be preoccupied and he be unable to rule them. Because he himself was disturbed by wine, he prohibited this most excellent gift of nature so that others would not be different from him. And although many gluttons and drunkards ruin themselves with it, nevertheless, for refreshing weary bodies and even afflicted souls, nothing greater was ever born. He acted so that the most excellent part of nature would be lacking among his people, and a most abundant harvest lost, so that he might hide his own illness <note>Postel refers to the historical polemic that Muhammad’s revelations were actually symptoms of epilepsy.</note> and gratify his wife. The things he adds concerning the laws of divorce, the lawful oath, and bringing war upon his own citizens: since all those things are against public peace and opposed to what is fair, good, and honorable—moreover, they fight against divine law—they therefore need no other refutation than...

by themselves. But the follower of Muhammad <note>original: *Muhamedicus*; a 16th-century term for a Muslim</note> will say, "There are many good things in these precepts; who would have wanted to receive such a massive pile of apparent absurdities unless something of the true and the good had been mixed in?" There is indeed something of the good, though it is the very minimum, in the Quran; but in the Gospel—which Muhammad admits is from God—there is nothing that is not most absolute and most worthy of God as its author.

Indeed, he takes the pretext for war from the children of Israel, when they were pursuing the wicked Canaanites. Yet he persecutes the Jews, whose law he approves; he kills the Christians, whose Gospel he says is from God; he sheds the blood of citizens, even though he seems to be doing the same thing as the Israelite cohorts under Saul. He mentions Saul, however, so that his followers might establish a leader for themselves—not Saul, but Abu Bakr and Umar <note>original: *Vbecharum & Ahmerum*; referring to the first two Caliphs, Abu Bakr and Umar ibn al-Khattab</note>, most bold and abandoned men, from whom he might receive secured power. After he has spoken of Talut <note>original: *Talot*; the Quranic name for King Saul</note>, he proceeds to act foolishly regarding Goliath; but I almost passed over the fable attached to the history of Saul, where he says:

> "When Saul had set his ranks in order, he said: 'If God makes you pass
> across a river, he who drinks from it is not of mine, or from me; and he
> who does not eat <note>The Latin text here reflects a specific translation of Quran 2:249, where the "test" of the river is described.</note> is of me, except for him who laps a handful with
> his hand.' And they drank from it, except for a few. For he did not cross
> over, nor did those who believed with him, because the enemies were in

that place and fortune, such that victory could be had over them." Saul had proclaimed with a curse that if anyone touched any food that day, he would be cursed—that is, he would die. Saul’s son, Jonathan, was not present then, but was fiercely attacking and pursuing the enemies. By chance, he touched a little dewy honey with the tip of his staff, which frequently tends to drip from the sky in Syria. Because of this, he was made guilty of the curse, and was sought for death by his father on account of the oath. The multitude obstructed his efforts, saying it was unworthy for him to be dragged to death, since it was by his work and diligence that they had obtained the victory. For Jonathan was not the cause of the calamities, but rather his imprudent father and leader, who had imprudently bound the people by a religious vow in a time of greatest necessity. For if it had been permitted for the people to drink and eat and recover their strength, they would have brought back an absolute victory with the enemies entirely finished; nor would they, through extreme hunger, have eaten meat with the blood, contrary to the divine precept. 

Now, let the things this scoundrel <note>original: *nebulo*; a harsh insult Postel uses for Muhammad</note> has lied about be compared. "If you cross the river, he who drinks from it is not of mine, except as much as the hand can hold; they all drank except a few." First, he turns food into drink; he brings in a river where the matter concerns honey; he says all failed except a few, when not even one person departed or went against the commands, except for Jonathan, who (as I said) had not heard them. There are as many words here as there are lies. 

But we know where this is heading: because he was embarking on a "religious pilgrimage"—that is, the slaughter of all good men—he wanted his own people to be bound by similar laws so they would not desert him, and so that, devoted to death or vengeance, they might rush in before taking food. Meanwhile, he was abusing sacred examples to animate them by terrifying them. He could have written this accurately among so many learned Jews, but he did not want his cunning to be open to anyone. Furthermore, he wanted his "sacred" things—that is, things sprinkled with lies—to be entirely like himself, lest they should seem true and be attributed to their real authors. Regarding *Galot* <note>Jalut, the Quranic name for Goliath</note>, that is, Goliath, he does plainly the same thing when he makes him a leader in that war; whereas he is neither read of as a leader, nor was he in that war, but long afterward, when the strength of the Palestinians <note>original: *Palaestinorum*; Philistines</note> was restored, he challenged the Jews as a common soldier. 

Finally, he subjoins things worthy of himself: that wars ought to exist among men, lest the world be corrupted. No greater plague can be compared to men than war; and yet he says war exists lest the world be corrupted, and that this is a "benefit" of God on earth. If God said those things, I appeal to you, O Nature, who places the happiness of all things in rest and tranquility. Who taught you thus, if not that God—the highest and perfect Rest—whom this "prophet" posits as the author of the "benefit" of war?

## GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II.

...when among all men, unless one is insane, not even a single person can be found who would approve of this in word, though at times he may approve of it in deed. The envy of the devil, the wickedness of men, the stubbornness of matter <note>Postel often uses the term "stubbornness of matter" (*materiae peruicacia*) to describe how the physical world resists divine perfection</note>, and corruption stir up war, while God permits all things so that we might repent; and meanwhile, with Muhammad as the author, God gives us this same war as the highest good, so that the prophet might grow rich and take possession of things. Who does not know that robbers and tyrants, and those who plot against the lives of others, approve of such things, and banish peace from the world as much as they can? And for that reason, he [Muhammad] so frequently says that riches belong to God and that He gives them to whomever He wishes, so that, evidently, he who has pounced upon another's riches gained with great sweat might have an equal right to those very things as the one who is their just possessor. This is the "good prophecy" of Muhammad, and meanwhile, he seriously asserts that this is a sign of his prophecy.

<margin>«</margin> "These miracles of God," he says, "are truly read in your presence, because you are a prophet."
<margin>«</margin> These things are connected to the preceding points, which say that unless men attacked each other with mutual force, the earth would turn to stone <note>A reference to Quran 2:251: "And if it were not for Allah checking [some] people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted." Postel interprets "corrupted" or "ruined" as "petrefacturam" (turning to stone)</note>. But I move on to other matters. "Certain of such prophets," he says,
<margin>«</margin> "we have ordained over others; some of them God spoke to, and he raised some by certain degrees. And we gave
<margin>«</margin> wisdom to Christ, the son of Mary, and we created him from the Holy Spirit, and if God willed, He would not have
<margin>«</margin> killed those who came after them, after wisdom had come to them. And for that reason they argue, and among them
<margin>«</margin> are those who believe, and among them are those who believe wrongly; and if God willed, they would not be
<margin>‘</margin> killed. But God does what He wills." I do not know what to examine first. What he has already granted to Christ, I do not think needs repeating. When he says: "if God willed, He would not have killed those who came after them," he means those after the prophets. The God of the Quran is a murderer, who kills those whom He chooses as prophets; man does no evil, nor does he have **liberum arbitrium** <term>free will: the theological concept that humans have the power to choose between good and evil</term>. Therefore, God kills men through the tyrants of the world—oh, what an abominable sentiment, worthy of a thousand punishments! Some among our own people disagreed: the **Nestorians** <note>original: *Nestorij*; a Christian group accused of heresy for emphasizing the distinction between Christ’s human and divine natures</note> err, as do the **Jacobites** <note>original: *Iacobitae*; a Monophysite or Miaphysite Christian group</note>, and as for the Christians [at large], a judge ignorant of both causes had to be appointed as an arbiter; and because he was helped by the favor and benefits of **Baheira** <note>original: *Baheira*; the monk who, in Islamic tradition and Christian polemics, is said to have mentored or influenced the young Muhammad</note>, therefore the Jacobites and Nestorians "believe best." This is his reasoning for agreement. Little kings and robbers from among the Armenians, coming into the borders of Arabia—because "dog does not eat dog" <note>original: *canis caninam non est*; an idiom suggesting that even the wicked do not turn on their own kind</note>—once a "prophetic peace" was settled, were said to "believe well," being most worthy of that judge, because a tyrant and a robber lacked supporters, nor could he profitably wage war with those like himself (for there is neither ample plunder from a robber, nor an easy victory); once peace was settled with them and the dogmas were strengthened, while one hand rubs the other, the plague creeps over the whole world. But as for what he says in the last place—"if God willed, they would not be killed"—what else would a most monstrous murderer say, even mockingly, while he slaughters everyone without any regard for humanity? If God wills those things, then He is no longer God. For if He is unjust, He is nothing. Therefore He does not will it—oh, ruin of men!—He does not will what He permits to human will. But He wants the actions themselves to be done by us sincerely and holily. Indeed, even if we wish to commit evils, He permits it; He does not "will" it. For even if it seems an evil [that we can sin], it would nevertheless be far worse for all men to lack free will and be like a stone, rather than being unable to commit vices, since there is especially a place for punishment and reward; which very thing you confess in words and assert, but deny in your life. He says a little later that God gave the kingdom to Abraham himself and that he possessed it. For he did not use the word **Vaada** <note>original: *Vaada*; from the Arabic *wa‘ada*, meaning "to promise"</note>, which signifies "to promise," but **attha** <note>original: *attha*; from the Arabic *ātā*, meaning "to give" or "to bestow"</note>, which signifies "to give" and "to assign." And yet, in truth, this is false. For he held this kingdom only in promise and faith; which God handed over to his descendants four hundred years later under the leadership of Moses. He does this so that his followers might hasten to snatch things from everywhere and prepare a kingdom and wealth for him. A little later, when he speaks of the ruined city—although the Sacred Scriptures have nothing about it—yet that...

### ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD, BOOK II

...it tends toward this goal: that Yathrib, which was called by him *Medinat al-nabi* <note>original: "Medinat alnebi" — Arabic for "City of the Prophet," now known simply as Medina</note>, that is, the City of the Prophet, could be restored by his followers, and with the Jewish inhabitants driven out, be ascribed to the prophet. For a little while before, it had been overturned by robbers and those similar to that prophet. 

And so, as if to ensure that no crime seems to lack a precedent, he ascribes wicked examples to the patriarchs—crimes which are all unknown to the miserable Muslims today. This is because his successors and the Caliphs <term>Caliphs: the political and religious successors to Muhammad</term>, loathing and dreading these things, took care to abolish them from human memory, and wished to cover them with other interpretations so that the crimes from which their tracks and acquired power remain would not be open to posterity. Those books submerged near Damascus, amounting to 60,000 or more volumes, intended this very thing for themselves; the unlearned are ignorant of those mysteries. 

But since he sensed that his lie would eventually betray itself, he cautioned at the end of the chapter against doubting or disputing what he says was sent to him. Indeed, he says:
» The prophet believed in that which was sent to him by his Lord, and the faithful also; everyone 
» believed in God and His angel, and His scripture, and His prophecy. Let there be no doubt 
» among us regarding any of his prophecy. And they said: "We have heard and we have obeyed," etc. 
<note>A paraphrase of Quran 2:285, emphasizing absolute obedience and the prohibition of doubt.</note>

He decreed among his followers that no matter should be doubted; from this, it is clear that it is a lie and a falsehood. For just as gold does not fear the fire by which it is purged, so the nature of truth voluntarily seeks out the disputes and altercations of all so that it may show its light. Falsehood flees from being tested at all, such that there is no greater proof of falsity in the entire Quran than in this place. For if he had forbidden public dispute or doubt among adversaries because of "mysteries" not to be revealed to the common people, he might perhaps have seemed to act with merit. Truly, however, to allow no doubt among his own followers, where he could have provided satisfaction, is the most certain sign of a lie, of fear, and of a guilty conscience. 

Christ voluntarily asked the disciples to question Him if they doubted anything (even though in the presence of such great power there was no room for doubt). If anyone today wishes to propose something against Christ or His decrees out of a desire to seek the truth, he is heard and satisfied, even publicly. Muhammad’s "reason" is placed in the sword and power; whence it happens that he used the word for "authority" and "power" interchangeably and equivocally. For *Sultanet* <term>Sultanet: from the Arabic *Sultan*, meaning authority, power, or dominion</term> signifies both, according to that saying of the tyrant: "Right is in arms." These few things are from the *Bacara* <note>Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow), the second chapter of the Quran</note>. If I had wished to pursue everything—since no word or sentence (unless taken from us) lacks a lie, blasphemy, or vice—the work would have grown to an immense size, causing only weariness and nausea.

->THE SURAH OF IMRAN, WRITTEN IN MEDINA. CHAPTER II. 200 Verses.<-
<note>Postel numbers this as Chapter II, but it is Surah 3 in the modern Quran. He identifies the title "Humran" as Imran.</note>

Just as the preceding chapter was collected partly for catching or refuting the Jews, so the second acts partly against us [Christians], and begins from Joachim, whom they call *Humran* <note>Postel identifies the Quranic 'Imran' with Joachim, the traditional father of the Virgin Mary</note>. Therefore, all things in this one must be observed more diligently. It begins thus: 
» God is, there is no God but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, who sent down upon you the 
» true and certain book for that which is in your hands; and He also sent down from heaven 
» the Law and the Gospel, already before for the guidance of men. 
<note>A translation of Quran 3:2–4.</note>

Just as he tried to commend his own teachings in the first chapter by claiming a shared sacred society, so he does now. For there he said, "that which was sent before you"; now he also specifically says that the Law and the Gospel sent from heaven preceded it, so that the QURAN might be believed in the same way. One must seize what is conceded by an adversary: he admits that the Gospel and the Law must be accepted by the followers of Muhammad. For as I have said, either there must be a lie in the Quran, or our own scriptures must be approved. With the same cleverness, he concedes this to us as he did above, so that we might swear by his laws. If the Quran contains a lie, it is not the Law of God. If our scriptures are true and from God, the Quran—contradicting them in innumerable places—is lying. Therefore, etc. A little later, speaking of paradise, he amplifies what was said above.

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD
## BOOK II

...[Muhammad] could not establish or confirm the status of Christ in the persuasion of those people who listened to him. For if Christ were assumed to be merely a dead man—though God drew him into heaven through Himself—it would necessarily follow that he rose again without anyone praying for him, which is an act of God alone. Therefore, from those half-truths which he granted us, he employs the same tactic toward us as he does toward the Jews: so that, charmed by the truths he concedes, we might also acquiesce to his wicked claims. To the Jews he said he followed the law of Abraham; to our people <note>Referring to Christians.</note> he says all laws are good. 

But all things must be weighed carefully. Those conversations of Zechariah and Anna with God, and their vows—although they seem plausible—are nevertheless not to be approved because they are not contained in the sacred scriptures. Those accounts, along with what follows regarding Christ, are taken from little books about the infancy of the Savior <note>Postel refers here to the "Infancy Gospels," such as the Infancy Gospel of Thomas, which were considered apocryphal and not part of the official Bible.</note>, which the Church chose not to use. It did not seem necessary that Christ should have created birds from mud and animated them with a breath, or that celestial fruits were sent when food was available from elsewhere. For it would seem superfluous to use an extraordinary remedy when an ordinary one exists. 

Furthermore, he speaks against scripture when he says the angel gave a three-day silence as a sign to Zechariah; for in truth, he was made mute for nine months, until the circumcision of the boy. That he says the angels argued over who should have care of Mary is not true; for all separate powers <note>original: *potentiæ separatę* — a term for angels as purely spiritual beings.</note> depend on the nod of the Creator, nor can there be any discord among the good ones. 

But when he says Christ did all things by the command of God, that is true; yet nevertheless, in his own name he raised the dead and healed all kinds of diseases of the mind and body. Moreover, when he says Christ said, "Worship my God and your God," we do not deny it. For he was equal to the Father according to his divinity, and less than the Father according to his humanity—according to which he prayed to God the Father, endured evils, struggled against evil, suffered, and so on. For he is not simply God, nor simply man, but one God-man, not otherwise than how a human consists of a soul and a body, which are most diverse natures. That he suffered is shown by the histories of all nations. 

A little later, when he says God created Jesus Christ from mud in the manner of Adam: that indeed we do not deny, but we reject the manner of it. For Adam was created without man or woman; all other humans are born from both; Christ received flesh from a woman alone—flesh subject to all sufferings, sin excepted—nor is he for that reason not God. We showed this sufficiently in the first book. 

But to what end should we listen to these things? He saw that all Christians professed whatever had been promised before the promises—that is, the promise of Abraham and the prescriptions of the Law—and insofar as they are removed from ceremonies and hardness of heart, all those things are embraced in the Gospel. So that he might also be permitted to ascribe his own authority to divine command, he wanted his law ascribed to Abraham as if it were the most ancient. Therefore he says:

<margin>,,</margin> "Ho there, you people relying on scriptures, it is not necessary for us to agree with
<margin>,,</margin> Abraham, since the law was sent from heaven, and the Gospel long after his times,
<margin>,,</margin> and yet you do not pay attention."

See where the craftiness and cunning of the scoundrel <note>original: *nebulonis* — Postel frequently uses such derogatory terms for Muhammad.</note> tends. He wishes to undermine the faith of both scriptures by stripping away their primary authority, so that neither the Jews may say they have the law of Abraham, nor Christians his law and that of Moses. Just as he himself had no promise (which is the true foundation of religion), he would ensure not only that we did not have one, but that he might spread his own foundation beneath himself. Thus, in any way possible, he persuaded the common and unrefined people by sowing errors. It is necessary, therefore, before any religion can be true, that it be predicted from heaven many centuries before its arrival, and that the predicted things be fulfilled according to the holy prophecies: which has happened to no other than the Christian and the ancient Jewish religion. And so, O Muhammad, you attempt in vain to creep in there, since no promise of your law preceded you, and all your fathers were idolaters, to whom the fellowship of the promise was forbidden by divine decree. Which also...

# GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II

...this is clear even from the chronicle of your own life. For Kedar <note>original: "Cahidar"</note>, the son of Ishmael—whom your dreaming historians say possessed the light of prophecy—how could it be that he was impious toward a religious father, and established those rites and that temple <note>The Kaaba in Mecca.</note>, for the purging of which you stirred up so many seditions, were driven into exile, and killed citizens? If that lineage of kings, which they assign to you—a poor man and a worshiper of idols—was devoted to ancestral worship in Mecca, as is the custom of religion, how could it be that it preserved absolutely nothing of that worship? Truly all your ancestors were degenerates, like an illegitimate, proscribed, and idolatrous father. Otherwise, some remains of true worship would have survived. Just as among the children of Israel, although many degenerated and worshiped idols, and even criminal and wonderfully wicked prophet-slaying princes committed crimes, nevertheless religion was never so endangered that it was not always at the summit <note>original: "colophone"</note> of the State. In vain, therefore, do you wish authority to protect you, for you can show not a single trace of it, either in writing or in deed, and we prove that countless things contrary to you oppose you.

> Hark, those things are necessary for you in which you have knowledge, and that for which you have no understanding is not necessary for you. Since God understands, and you do not understand. Abraham was not a Jew, or a Christian, but an absolute Muslim <note>original: "Muſſulman"</note>; and he was not an idolater, because those men are with Abraham who follow him, and his prophet, those who believed; and God is the patron of the believers.

> He does not want men driven to anything other than what they know, or to follow anything other than what they understand.

Wherefore the previous laws given by God were in vain—which no one understood before they came—and there was always enough knowledge, whether of God, or an idol, or a vegetable, or an Egyptian fart <note>Postel refers here to Juvenal’s *Satire XV*, which mocks the perceived Egyptian practice of worshipping various animals and plants.</note>; since those who worshiped them knew nothing else. In vain do you also obtrude your own law; in vain did God send wisdom, the Law, and the Gospel to those who were before you, if nothing was to be believed beyond what men in Arabia understood. See where you fall back, and how you destroy yourself. There is no idolater, nor has there ever been, who—though they do not glorify God as God—does not nevertheless believe Him to be God, and a certain great and powerful divinity, even when they think there is great power in the smallest thing. These are opinions, but the one truth lies hidden. It is as if many people were striving toward a certain city, conceived in their hearing and mind, and said they were striving toward it, but in the first villages or inhabited places on the road they settled down as if they had reached the city; all nevertheless agree on this: that there is some most happy city. But they differ in this: that some stop at the beginning, others in the middle, and others in the spaces between, knowing or approving nothing besides their own. According to Muhammad, it is not necessary for them to know anything else besides what they know in order to be happy. 

But it was necessary to turn away—for this is the aim—unrefined men, who were informed only by the use of natural things (for this is what he seems to mean by *Kitab* <note>original: "Chitab," meaning "The Book" or Scripture.</note>, that is, the book), neglecting the prescription of Moses and Christ. And thus he persuaded them that they should be kept perpetually in natural law and ignorance of the truth, so that he might draw them to himself. He would affirm that men of all religions are blessed, and meanwhile call God foolish and vain for giving laws to the fathers that were not necessary. Are these things not a denial of God? All nations of the whole world, even if they are ignorant of what kind of God they ought to have, nevertheless think they must have one; and so whatever they know is enough for them. Therefore, all are "Muslims" who naturally think there is a God. Most wickedly, therefore, do you bring war upon them, since they believe. O foolish man, fighting with himself in all things! Truly, in this place, just as he had captured the Jews with flatteries and terrified them with threats, and in this chapter strove to capture the Christians: so now he soothes the Gentiles by approving their religion, so that, having given their trust, they might allow themselves to be led. For that reason he adds:

> And a portion of the heathens said: we believe in that which was handed down regarding those who believed in the face of the day (that is, the common people) and went astray...

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

> ...he watches them if perhaps they return. Do not believe anyone except him who follows your faith. Say: guidance is the guidance of God. If one is appointed, just as it was handed down to you, it is a necessity for your use, before your Lord. Say: good things are in the hand of God, and he grants them to whom he wills, for he is a wise listener. These are the words of mysteries. 

To this point all things are to be referred, for they tend toward this: God gives good things to whom he wills. Therefore, the goods of robbers are equal to those of rightful owners. O, what a perverse law! It makes followers of people from all religions, so that they may do whatever they please with impunity; and if they seize anything, he immediately says it is theirs and that God gave it. In this way, power is gathered. Indeed, in instilling this into people’s souls, it seems to me he used the same art as any rising tyrant, armed to acquire an empire. For in order to draw all kinds of men to his opinion, if he finds slaves, he asserts that nothing is more excellent than slavery and says their power is to come; with the same words he soothes the great nobles; he treats the peasants with the same art; he praises defectors, outlaws, and every kind of criminal, provided they obey him, promising that all things will turn out successfully for them. He claims a single power is to be prepared, in which all may live freely according to their own character—yet he fits the feet of all into a single wooden shoe <note>original: "calopodio" — a shoemaker's last or a simple wooden clog, used here as a metaphor for forced conformity</note>, until he reaches his goal and exercises tyranny over everyone. This is exactly what Muhammad <note>original: "Muhamedes"</note> did. For once he joined everyone to himself, he immediately oppressed them. And yet, this blind people does not blush to attribute the law of this most cruel tyrant to God. A little later, he says that all the religions of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, the tribes of Moses, and Christ are good and are included in his own. Thus, he says he hands down now only the law of Abraham, now of others, now of nature, so that you will find nothing more changeable than this Proteus <note>A Greek sea-god capable of changing his shape at will.</note>. In short, this entire chapter does nothing else but strive to gather a multitude from everywhere, out of all nations. When he says that Christ is not God, that is true according to his humanity; otherwise, it is false. But I have already demonstrated this enough. We do not understand God to have a partner because of this. For the one and the same God is powerful, wise, and benevolent: three and one. His wisdom is the Son, not needing a physical place, begotten from eternity; He joined our humanity to Himself and so animated His own that there was almost no one who did not seem to see a god—which would not have happened without the divinity transforming men. There remain innumerable things in this chapter to be refuted, where nothing is sound; but I proceed to the rest.

->Surah An-Nisa, that is "The Women," written in Medina, 175 Verses.<-
<note>original: "Sora elnasæ... 175 Aiet"</note>

In this Surah <note>A chapter of the Quran.</note>, he treats chiefly of the rights of women and the goods of orphans, saying by what law they ought to be preserved and administered: 
> Take as many wives as please you, two, three, or four; and unless you fear that you cannot rule them together peacefully, take as many as your power can subdue. 

This is the opinion of the legislator, which, even if the interpreters moderate it, is nevertheless arbitrary up to the number of four, and is so used among the great nobles. How unjust this is and contrary to public peace, I leave to be judged by either the Greeks or the Romans, who nevertheless, with the greatest natural liberty and without any fear of God, made a trial of all pleasures. What peace can there be where you nourish four or five wives with their children like a flock at home, when you can hardly satisfy the necessity and desire of even one? How much more fortunate was the ancient law of the Arabs? Which gave 12 brothers as husbands to even one sister (it was permitted for those lacking law to neglect kinship)—how much greater was the rest and happiness anywhere in the world, whether at home or abroad? Since they ought to enjoy both the body and the goods of the husband by an equal law, who could maintain such equity for even one hour so that many complaints do not arise? ### GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II

...hardly one man could be sufficient? Nor is the evil only a domestic one; judges everywhere hear nothing but the lawsuits of women, daily divorces, daily weddings, the reclamation of dowries, legal assignments, the injuries inflicted by husbands, and the miseries and oppressions of all the children. To put it in a single word, nothing more turbulent or unhappy can be imagined. Thus the unhappy woman—the partner of man, endowed with a rational soul just like a man, and born for freedom—occupies the place of the vilest slave. She is burned by the lash and led by commands like a beast rather than by reason, according to the whim of her husband. It follows from this that innumerable orphans perish from hunger or are killed by their brothers so that the inheritance may be kept whole; for this reason, they are not even regarded as brothers, but (unless they are kept for the sake of honor) they are slaughtered like cattle. Nothing is more common than for a Mohammedan <note>original: "Muhametanū" — Postel uses this term for Muslims throughout the text</note> prince to remove his brothers from the scene, and for the beginnings of a reign to be taken from a brother's blood. There are even those who kill their own children. I myself know of one Mohammedan king who, when he came to power, killed or arranged the killing of seventeen brothers; he also finished off just as many relatives, not by the law of war, but by poison, snares, and private violence. I also know those who have killed their own children. These are the effects of your law: that man—for whose sake the lower world exists, whose soul no price can compensate, who was born for the sake of cultivating the world through virtue and good deeds, and to whom life was given by the Most High God as a distinguished gift—is held in viler esteem than lice, for which there is a four-month truce in the year according to Muhammad. <note>Postel is likely mocking the "Sacred Months" of the Islamic calendar, during which certain types of killing/hunting are forbidden, sarcastically suggesting the law protects vermin more than human relatives.</note> O miserable men, who has bewitched your eyes? God made male and female and joined them, so that a man should seek no others; He joined them so that no one may separate them, such that Christ gave no place even for divorce (except on account of fornication). Muhammad, the author of a new nature, wants men to be able to enter into various women after the manner of bulls in herds, and for a husband driven by an oath to divorce his wife, and not only to call her back once, but even three or four times. Where there is no longer a place for receiving her back, he ordained that she should be taken again as if new after being "subdued" by another <note>This refers to the "tahlil" marriage, where a triple-divorced woman must marry and divorce another man before returning to her first husband; Postel views this with extreme hostility</note>, so that in that state it is most certain that nothing is certain. Indeed, lest this "excellent" law have too little scope, he wanted the number of wives to be placed at the discretion of money and possessions; and meanwhile, he mixes in with the wives young catamites and <term>cynaedi</term> <note>original: "catamittos cynædos" — terms for passive male partners in same-sex acts, used here as a polemical accusation of decadence</note> who have been converted to his law. Although his interpreters veil these things with explanations, the true understanding concerns perverse lust; and lest this seem strange, much greater things are permitted with brutes. Whence, as I have already noted, there are those among the Mohammedans considered most holy who have intercourse with beasts. If anyone should deny this, I will produce testimony from the *Sorat Sori* <note>original: "Sorat Sori" — Postel’s transliteration of a Sura (Chapter) from the Quran, likely referring to Ash-Shura (The Consultation)</note>. Lest they say I am making anything up in such an absurd matter, I subjoin the Arabic: 

*Phatíru, ssamauatí uelardhí geala lechum, mín anphussicum u azuagian, uemín elanhamí ezuagian, iedreuchum phihí*

which is, word for word: "The Creator of heaven and earth gave you spouses from among yourselves, and from the beasts He permits you spouses therein." <note>Postel is quoting and intentionally misinterpreting Quran 42:11. The Arabic *azwajan* means "pairs" or "mates," referring to God creating livestock in pairs for breeding, but Postel translates it as "spouses" to support his accusation of bestiality.</note> What do "spouses from the brutes" mean? Is this not a work of your "holiness"? Otherwise, how could it be that what heaven and earth shudder at, what even the most ferocious and barbarian nations cannot bear to hear, and what all other laws punish with the most bitter penalties, would be held among the Mohammedans as a sign of holiness—and no common one at that—unless it had authority from your divine lawgiver? Men would not have such authority unless the law offered its assent. That <term>cynaedi</term> are understood in this chapter there is no doubt, for he joined them to the handling of women for that reason, and he wants "Mussulmans" to be made for the sake of sexual intercourse (which is also written elsewhere, lest it be thought doubtful here). You hold all kinds of men among you in a condition of slavery, yet it is not the custom for a "Mussulman" to be the slave of another "Mussulman." Therefore, they would not need to be converted if they were acquired for uses other than as <term>clinopales</term> <note>original: "clinopales" — from the Greek meaning "bed-wrestlers," referring to male concubines</note>. But hear, I ask you, most blind of men, a comparison...

# ON THE CONCORD OF THE WORLD

...the reason of divine law and your own: and instructed by this argument, you must admit that at least part of your law is from the devil. Moses, by divine authority, decreed thus concerning both crimes: *If a man lies with a male as with a woman* (that is, for the sake of sexual intercourse), *both have committed an abomination: they shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them.* <note>Postel is quoting Leviticus 20:13</note> These are the statutes which are from God, and the penalty for such a stain. It follows a little later: *Whoever has sexual relations with an animal or a beast shall surely be put to death, and you shall kill the beast. If a woman approaches any beast to lie with it, she shall be killed along with it; their blood shall be upon them.* <note>Postet is quoting Leviticus 20:15-16</note> These are the statutes which are from God, and they are contrary to the <term>Muslims</term> <note>original: "Mussulmanis" — a term for followers of Islam</note>. For this reason, young male prostitutes publicly practice their trade in all parts of Africa. I saw catamites in Tunis, shouting with loud voices in the marketplace to exhibit themselves; I saw "holy men" held in universal admiration and pointed out with a finger because they had coupled with she-asses or mules. This is their "holiness." If a soldier on an expedition brings a woman, he is punished; if he brings a catamite, it is allowed. These are the decrees of the law of Muhammad; these are its effects.

O the morals! O the times! O wretched depravity, devised for the destruction of nature! And yet—if it pleases the gods—he taught, gave, and professed the natural law and the law of Abraham. As for the fact that he wishes wives to be ruled by lashes like beasts, he does this out of his own "humanity," so that he might be permitted to do the same to his own fifteen wives. For since they were from wealthy families, they could not endure the unfair and filthy habits of the "prophet"; therefore, he dictated laws of the whip to them. Furthermore, toward all other men he burns entirely with war; he encourages plunder, says that all goods belong to those who can seize them, and hammers home such precepts.

I truly wonder how anyone can say there are no contradictions in this <term>Quran</term> <note>original: "Alcorano"</note>, when there is hardly a single sentence that does not contradict another. I have already shown this in many instances, and it is evident in these: Muhammad is called *Mustapha*, that is, the "redeemer of all," <note>original: "uniuersorum redemptor" — While the name Mustafa means "The Chosen One," Postel interprets it here as "Redeemer."</note> and yet he possessed no other language or nation than his own. He says in many places that Christians and Jews will be saved, but then elsewhere says only his own followers will be, and elsewhere that all laws are good. There are places where he says one ought not to urge his law except with modesty, yet in almost the entire Quran he deals with nothing but blood. He says the Quran was sent first to him, but elsewhere to Moses. Likewise, that Abraham was the first <term>Muslim</term> <note>original: "Mussulmanum"</note>, but elsewhere that he himself was commanded to be the first Muslim. He approves of the condemnation of the Sodomites, and yet in three places he commends their crimes; elsewhere he says all sins are forgiven by God, yet elsewhere that criminal acts are by no means forgiven.

Who could collect them all? It is more than enough. He proceeds to other blasphemies and the goal for which he devised this law, saying:
> » "And their impiety (the Jews) and their word is a great blasphemy against Mary.
> » Their word is: We killed Christ Jesus, son of Mary, the prophet of God.
> » But they by no means killed him, nor crucified him: but they thought so, 
> » or it appeared so to them." <note>Postel is paraphrasing Surah An-Nisa 4:156-157</note> Or as I might represent the Arabic in French: *it seemed so to them.* <note>original: "il leur a semble"</note>

Everything tends toward this. How? Hey, O plague of the world, are you not ashamed to rise up against the testimony of the entire world? The Jews admit it, they feel it, they even curse themselves because they have been slaves everywhere on earth since his death. Romans, Greeks, Pagans, Christians, and the judge Pilate himself (who wrote about him to the Emperor Tiberius), saw the countless thousands of men lead him to the cross, heard that he had risen, as it is handed down in the sacred letters, confirmed by the miracles of the cross, and approved by the martyrs. Tell me, come now, how could it be possible that in a judgment before the eyes of everyone, a very well-known man could have been substituted? Have you ever read of such a thing happening? It cannot be done. Therefore, you must admit that you have lied impiously. You wanted to be called the "general redeemer" among the ignorant by this trick, while you deny things that are most proven. The unrefined common people believed that what is venerable and salvific to all was instead something injurious. But that a man could be substituted in a most flourishing city,

Truly, one should not linger against you in a matter so clear. You must allow yourself to say anything, since you dare to contradict facts so well-attested. It follows a little later:

And since all who heard of him wanted to believe in him, he says they have enough time before the day of judgment—as if there were a place for belief and faith after death, and as if he were still to die.

These things are written to enchant the eyes of souls, so that they would not defect from that new prophet <note>Postel’s polemical name for Muhammad</note> and follow Christ, the way of life. By flattering the ignorant, he forced this idea upon them—those who could easily believe that the Jews claimed this death wrongly and that it was shameful to us; and they easily believed that out of fear of death, God summoned to himself a man who was his friend. But one must hear this man's impiety, which he connects to truths:

> Certainly Jesus Christ is nothing but the son of Mary, a prophet of God, and his word <note>Greek: "Logos"</note>, which he destined for Mary, and a spirit from himself. Therefore believe in God and his prophet, and do not say "three." Complete what is good for you, because there is no God but one (to whom be praise), nor does he have a son. <note>Quoting Surah 4:171</note>

We likewise say in many respects: Christ is the son of Mary, a prophet of God, and his word, conceived from the Holy Spirit. But as for your claim that there is no Trinity, nor that God has a son—you lie both impudently and imprudently. You possess no understanding of God, since you judge him in a human manner. But I will take an argument from your own words, so that I may lead you back to the path of truth. You confess that God has a "Word," and that Christ is the Word of God. Now, God does not have a word in our human manner, for he who is without a body does not speak. Therefore, the <term>Moor</term> <note>original: "Maurus" — a term Postel uses to refer to Muslims generally</note> will not deny that the Word of God has been with God from eternity; for no new quality or change can happen to God. Therefore, he had the Word with him from eternity, and the Spirit: therefore it is necessary that he be a triune and one God, based on what you have already conceded. 

But although in the first book I pursued the subject of the Holy Trinity most fully and attempted to explain it, I will not be burdened to repeat the arguments in a few words here. We agree that God exists. Why then did he call that which was to be seen in the man Christ "the Word"? All the names by which we signify something about God are taken from the use of our own senses and intellect; from these, we may form a certain conjecture about the nature of the divinity. First, we call a "word" an indication, a proclamation, and an explanation of the mind and thought; for whatever lies hidden in the mind will never become known unless it is explained by words. That notion which we conceive of things, as it was whole within the mind, is expressed as that same whole in the word. For a word is nothing other than an explained notion. From the conception and the word, an effect proceeds, which is nothing other than what was conceived and said. 

So also in God, we call "the Word" the explanation of his power, through which whatever exists in these lower realms comes into being. Therefore, God is whole in his power, whole in his word and wisdom, and whole in his work, will, and effect. He must either be granted the name of the Holy Trinity, or denied altogether. For he could not exist without the Trinity, nor could anything subsist without it. For before things were created, it was necessary for there to be a pre-powerful God, and necessarily also a wise one; for you will be powerful in vain unless you know how to use that power. Nor was it enough to be powerful and wise; it was necessary for the will and the love of acting to be added, proceeding from the power and wisdom of God. We call the Power of God, God the whole and the Father; the Wisdom...

we also call him entirely God and the Son: love and will, we call entirely God and the **Holy Spirit**. We also call the Father "God Almighty," his Word—the Son—"God Almighty," and the Holy Spirit—his effect everywhere—"God." It is impossible for God to act without these properties, and yet it is clear that he acts in all things. By analogy, we ourselves must be able, must know, and must will before we can act in any way. In all arts, there must be creative potential, a process, love, and delight. For the sake of example, take a potter; he must have the creative potential <note>original: "fœcunditatem"</note> of his art and such power that it cannot be exhausted by use. This power is not merely hidden, but proceeds into an effect, which cannot happen without will and love. When fire heats or breaks things apart, it must have an inexhaustible power of acting, an unceasing process of action, and a certain natural delight, so that it loves to act naturally and cannot *not* love it. Therefore, those three are one power distinguished by certain properties. The creative potential of the fire is the fire in its entirety; the process of action from the fire is the one and same fire; that heat and love of acting is the same fire. The first is not the second, nor the second the third, nor vice versa. In the same way, there are not three gods, but one God. Therefore, God could not help but generate the Son from eternity, by knowing future things as if present through wisdom, and by creating in this manner. Thus we say that God has a Son, Wisdom, and the Word. Whoever desires more on this should return to the first book. Therefore, **Muhammad** spoke wrongly when he said God does not have a Son, nor is he Three and One. He wished to overturn all the established beliefs of our religion so that he might introduce his own new religion with a new God—who is the author of evil, as we have already seen. He adds:

"**Christ** will not deny that he is a servant of God, nor will the angels who are close to God." <note>Postel is quoting Surah 4:172</note>

He never wished to deny, insofar as he is a man, that he is a servant of God, whose form he took <note>A reference to Philippians 2:7, where Christ takes the "form of a servant"</note> so that he might make servants free. Therefore, insofar as he is God, he is entirely equal to the Father, differing only in property and person. Insofar as he was a man, he wished to undergo the most humble and dejected rank of dignity; he who was highest in divinity became the lowest in human condition. Yet, having taken flesh from a Virgin, he did not receive into himself any stain of the sin he was meant to take away. Although, even if he had been born in our usual way, he could have cleansed us just the same by the benefit of his present divinity. For in one composite being (if divine power could indeed be confined to a place), he united the whole divinity with a soul—or spirit—and a body. This union created a ladder to heaven for believers. Truly, enough has been said of this prophecy.

# SURAH AL-MA'IDAH, THAT IS, THE CHAPTER OF THE TABLE,
## written in Medina. <note>original: "SORA ELMEIDEH, ID EST CAP. MENSE"</note>

Here he speaks of choices, washings, and so many other things that this **Quran** <note>original: "Alcoranum"</note> holds the privilege of being impossible to summarize. He said in the previous sections that four things were prohibited; now there are far more. "It is prohibited to you to use carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and the flesh of an animal killed without the invocation of God, or one suffocated, burned, crushed, killed by any fall, or whatever wild beasts have touched." <note>A paraphrase of Surah 5:3</note> I have placed this here to point out the inconsistency and contradictions of the man. Our faith is good because of you, and confirmed by God, just as you wrote a little while ago regarding the **children of Israel**. Therefore, whoever lived under those holy laws by keeping the commandments is approved by God by reason of their goodness and their observance of the law.

Therefore, both Laws <note>The Old and New Testaments</note> are holy and good, containing no fault. If men who live under that Law argue and contend, because the Law is good, it cannot be obscured or diminished on that account. It is as if someone were to say gold is brass <note>original: "aurichalchum"</note>, another calls it copper <note>original: "æs Cyprium"</note>, some call it iron or lead, while a few others call it gold and name it so; it does not follow that it is not always gold. For as is commonly said: "nothing in the substance of things is changed by affirmations or negations." Therefore, because of the arguments of our people, or anyone else, our Law cannot be evil, even if many forget it. For it is written and preserved in so many literary monuments that it can never fall into oblivion unless the whole world is overturned. As for your making God the author of sects, heresies, and evil—are you not entirely impious for making God the author of evil? For if what he once gave is good, it is evil to overturn it.

As for your claim that God is not among our people (for you do not reveal whom you mean by "them"), if you say this of the Nestorians, Jacobites, Arians, and other impious heretics, we also admit it. We say that God is so far from them that they are driven by the devil, the author of perfidy. But if you say this regarding that constant belief in Christ and the Gospel, which the Catholic Church received through the hands of the Apostles and their successors, it is clear that you speak impiously. The seal of God’s power was and always will be in the Church, which the saints have testified to through miracles and most famous divine works, proven by the two most famous empires <note>Likely the Roman and Byzantine/Holy Roman Empires</note> and infinite kingdoms of the whole world. Whereas among the impious heretics (unless perhaps someone was a sorcerer <note>original: "goeticus"</note> or a conjurer), none has ever possessed miracles, purity of life, or any public peace.

Therefore, since the devil could not force any society of perfidy upon the convictions of the faithful, he armed Muhammad against piety and religion, and he was equipped with a sword for the ruin of nature. Hence it is no wonder that among his followers there are at least 70 sects, from which only one will be saved. For Muhammad alone received into himself the poisons of all heretics: he denies the Holy Trinity with **Sabellius**; he says that there is God and the Soul of God, placing a duality in divine matters; where he seems to agree with **Arius**, it is to remove Christ from the midst. He certainly thinks Christ is a creature, like **Arius**, whose intestines were cast out into a latrine because of his blasphemies—certainly a divine vengeance. That Christ was only a holy man is a view he holds in common with **Cerdon** and **Marcion**. With the **Nicolaitans**, he approves of multitudes and flocks of wives; he places paradise in luxury with **Cerinthus**. In short, no plague of any heretic is absent from the Quran <note>original: "Alcorano"</note>, just as no vice was absent from its author.

To return to the matter: our Law or that of the Jews could not become evil through ambiguity, forgetfulness, or neglect; rather, the fault was in those who ought to have instilled it. Just as it is not the fault of a gem or gold that it lies hidden—for it is always gold—but it must be ascribed to the negligence and ignorance of men (assuming that is the case). There was no need, therefore, to invent other laws, but rather to instill those good and neglected ones. But let us proceed.

His disciples did the same in his name, and even greater things, as he had promised. The Prophets performed miracles by invoking the name of God; thus no one, however holy, could perform anything unusual without the invocation of God. Therefore, Jesus Christ was God. He is from eternity, and shall be. But having become man in time, he transformed nature in the true believers, so that they would shudder at vices worse than death, and would voluntarily seek death itself for the sake of protecting the truth, living for other men and not for themselves: things which those led by nature do quite the opposite of. They are not blasphemers, therefore, who call Christ God, but impious and damned are whoever dare to deny it.

# GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II #

God punishes. Philosophers never considered a man unhappy in his body if he seeks, grasps, and practices virtue with all his effort. Therefore, Christians are not unhappy because they are afflicted by physical punishments or the plundering of their fortunes. They are, in truth, far happier because they choose to suffer those things rather than desert God in any way or break the prescriptions of His law. If virtue consisted of possessing wealth and being free from troubles, what would a tyrant or a stone be? Would the tyrant not be the happiest of all, since he has scraped together the wealth of everyone? And would stones be happy because they enjoy a total absence of pain? You betray yourself, O prophet <note>Referring to Muhammad</note>; you approve of the "highest good" of Epicurus <note>Epicurus was an ancient Greek philosopher who defined the highest good as the absence of pain and the pursuit of tranquility, often misinterpreted by critics like Postel as mere sensual pleasure</note> and prefer the life of a pig to a human one when you think those overflowing with all the delights of the body are the friends of God. Virtue has nothing in this life worthy of itself. God and the future, eternal life are its reward. Tyrants snatch and will continue to snatch the property of others from pious, patient men, and in this life, men will be nothing other than men: some good, some evil. God punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills. You call the splendors of fortune, wealth, pleasures, and fame "mercy"; but you call humility, patience, endurance, justice, and similar things "punishments"—yet we would rather have these than wealth. You have had your happiness in this life, you and those like you, and you will lack the future reward.

What shall I add regarding the fable of the two men, whom he wished to send ahead of Moses, when mention is made of the whole army in the sacred scriptures? I do not refute what is foreign to the sacred texts. What about the raven, which went out to seek a companion? Are these not contrary to the sacred stories? One raven went out to a corpse a second time, but there was no other raven outside the ark with which it might meet. Furthermore, Noah—not God—sent it. When Muhammad says that he who does not judge according to the prescriptions of Moses is wicked, does he not speak against himself, since he hands down and follows different things almost everywhere? But concerning Christ, he says:

> And we sent in their footsteps <note>Referring to the earlier prophets</note> Jesus, son of Mary, the most certain confirmer of the law, and we gave him the Gospel, in which there is light and certain direction regarding those things held in the law, and a firm direction for those who fear, so that the people of the Gospel might judge according to what God sent down in it. And those who do not judge according to what God sent in that Gospel are wicked. <note>original: "Et destinauimus in uestigiis eorum... Iesum filium Mariæ..." This is a paraphrase of Surah Al-Ma’idah 5:46-47.</note>

This is the eulogy for the Gospel which we accept as if from an adversary. He gave this to the Jacobites <note>A Middle Eastern Christian sect</note> and the people of Bahira <note>original: "genti Bahyranæ," referring to the monk Bahira, who in polemical traditions was said to have instructed Muhammad</note> who had joined him, so that they might finally grant that he was a prophet sent to the nations who follow the natural law. To what end did God, after the Law of Terror <note>The Law of Moses/Old Testament</note> and the Law of Grace <note>The Gospel/New Testament</note>, preserve that which was prior and make it posterior? Any unrefined and unskilled pagan could clearly profess the same: that a natural light was given to him from heaven, by which he might follow what is desirable and avoid what should be fled. Anyone relying on the sword was as much a prophet as Muhammad.

Although he says both laws are good and there is salvation in all of them according to Muhammad, yet a little later he permits governmental authority to Christians or forbids it to Jews. You hunt for nothing other than power and tyranny, while Christ commands us to obey all magistrates and princes. He then encourages his attackers that they should fear nothing as they seize whatever the non-believers possess, for he asserts that all goods belong to God, and He gives them to whom He wills. Finally, he wishes to attack and draw the Meccan pagans to his opinion by any way possible. And if, he says:

> you would receive the law and the Gospel, and what is destined for you from your Lord, you would have such an abundance of food that it would be above you and under your feet. <note>A paraphrase of Surah 5:66.</note>

So that he might force everyone into one law—an impossible one, indeed—he grants the "happiness of the belly," in which even the beasts themselves surpass us. 

Then he says:

> O pagans, you are nothing until you receive the law and the Gospel, and what was sent to you from your Lord. <note>A paraphrase of Surah 5:68.</note>

I wonder, you followers of Muhammad, since you have so many and such great testimonies of the Law and the Gospel, why do you not believe in the Gospel and in Christ? Why do you persecute Christians, the best kind of men? Either those statements are false, or they are true. If they are false, your law is evil; if they are true, our things must be believed. But when he introduces Christ speaking—

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD #

...speaking to the children of Israel, telling them to serve his God and their God, from which he <note>Muhammad, whom Postel is arguing against</note> infers that Christ is not God: this argument carries no weight against us. For insofar as he is man, he is the servant of God, as I have already stated; but insofar as he is God, he is equal to God the Father. Whatever he said or did as a man, he did while acknowledging the name of God; whatever he did as God, he said or did in the manner of God. When he raised the dead, he simply said, "Rise," and they rose. When he healed lepers, he said, "Be cleansed," and they were cleansed. When he commanded demons, he said, "Be silent and come out of him." In all his miracles, he acted by no authority but his own name—which he never could have done unless he were God.

But someone will object to me: "If he were God, he could not be ignorant of anything." When the Apostles asked about the day of judgment and the restoration of Israel, he said he did not know. He said this in his capacity as a man, because it is not beneficial for us to know the ultimate end, whether of our own life or of the world. For if they knew, the wicked would practice their impiety with total security; even now, though uncertain of the day of their certain death, they still commit every kind of crime. "It is not for you to know," he said, "the times and moments which the Father has put in his own power." <note>A reference to Acts 1:7</note> The fear of God's arrival and of death must always be kept in uncertainty, for the sake of virtue and the good.

As for the other argument he brings forward—that he does not seem to be God because he and his mother ate food—there is no contradiction here. The body joined to God also ate; and he is recorded as having used food after the resurrection to testify to his true humanity. Does our soul require food and eat just because the body requires it? And yet the soul is divine and immortal. Even the spectral appearances of angels to Abraham, and Raphael to Tobit, appeared to have eaten or consumed feasts; we should not think it absurd, then, that God-as-man ate and drank.

When he <note>Muhammad</note> says that we affirm "three trinities," he lies, nor could he ever have known what God or the Trinity is. We say there is only one God, one and three: three in unity and one in trinity—Power, Wisdom, and Love. From whom, through whom, and in whom are all things; without these "persons," nothing could be or have been brought into existence. For as I have often said, and I say it again to you followers of Muhammad: Power by itself, without knowledge or wisdom, acts not; Power and Wisdom act not except from the will and perpetual love of acting. This is present in all of nature, and it could not be so unless it were there from the beginning. I say nothing of the fact that he prohibits the recreation of wine and dice. For I have already shown above

> >> for what reason he did that. Now I append again one eulogy of Christ. He <note>God, in the Quran</note> says: On the day of gathering, God will say to the prophets, "What was your desire?" They said, "We have no knowledge, for You are the Knower and the Hidden." When God said, "O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and your generation: how I formed you by the Holy Spirit; you spoke to men in the cradle and in swaddling clothes; and how I taught you the Book and wisdom, and the Law, and the Gospel; and when you created from clay the figures of birds by My command, and you breathed into them, and they became birds by My command; and you healed the scabs and the leprosy by My command; and when you raised the dead by My authority; and when I restrained the children of Israel from you when you came to them with wisdom." <note>Postel is translating Sura 5:109-110 here</note> But the impious among them said, "This is nothing but manifest enchantment." And when I revealed to the Apostles that they should believe in Me and My prophet, they said, "We believe, and you are witness that we are faithful." And the Apostles said, "O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord obey you and send down to us a table from heaven?" He said, "Fear God, if you are faithful." They said, "It seems to us that if we eat from it (the table), our hearts will be strengthened, and we will know that we have been confirmed and made certain, and we shall be witnesses (that is, martyrs) for it." Jesus, son of Mary, said: "O God our Lord, send down to us a feast or a table from heaven, which shall be a foundation for us and our descendants, and a miracle from You; and enrich us, for You are the best of the providers." God said: "Behold, I send it to you, and whoever among you..."

### WILLIAM POSTEL, BOOK II. ###

“...should be doubly impious after that, I will punish him with such a unique and unheard-of torment for all ages and nations.” And when God said: “O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to men: ‘Receive me and my mother as two gods besides God’?” <note>A reference to Sura Al-Ma'idah 5:115–116. Postel is quoting a Latin translation of the Quran prevalent in his time.</note> He [Jesus] said: “Praise be to You, Lord”—that is, far be it from me that this should happen, that I should say that which is not true of me. “If I said this, You know it; You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Yours, for You are the Knower of the hidden,” etc. All the preceding points were intended to lead to this: to portray him [Jesus] as denying that he is the omniscient God; therefore he ascribes everything to the command of God. Nor do we entirely deny that these things proceeded from God the Father; for although the person of the Son is distinct from the Father—that is (to speak more familiarly), Wisdom is distinct from Mind and Power—nevertheless, whatever the Son has, he has from the Father, since it is one and the same divinity. They differ in this: that our body and soul are joined to Wisdom <note>Postel uses "Wisdom" as a title for the Second Person of the Trinity, the Son.</note>, but not to the Father or to Power. Therefore Christ says: *All things have been handed over to me by my Father.* <note>Matthew 11:27</note> Thus he ascribes to Him everything whatsoever he has, even though he is also God; just as the whole thought is in the whole word, and the whole word in the thought, and the whole word and the whole thought are in the effect, love, or will. O followers of Muhammad, even if Christ were as he is depicted here and were not God, which of the two is more excellent: Christ or Muhammad? One may discern this from their flaws and their deeds.

As for what he says about the sacrament of the altar <note>The Eucharist or Holy Communion.</note> being obtained from God, he truly wishes to take that away from Christ, even though in it is truly the very body of Christ, possessing both divinity and humanity, which he [Muhammad] could not deny was divine. For the frequent miracles of the presence of divinity in that sacrament of Christ’s death have always been seen, with which the ancient doctors of the church abound. Yet he [Muhammad] imposes ignorance upon God when he argues that Jesus said what he had not said. For he wishes to imply this: Christ never said this, and yet God questions him. Therefore, the god of Muhammad is ignorant, unfair, unjust, foolish, an idolater, and a murderer—titles by which no one believes God to exist. But I come to the other matters.

->Surah Al-An'am, that is, 'of the Cattle' <note>original: "Sora elanham, id est bonorum." Postel identifies this as Sura 6 of the Quran.</note>, verse 167, written in Mecca.<-

He puts forth nonsense immediately at the beginning when he speaks of the punishment of Sodom and the remaining five wicked cities. For he says that after the rain, the Lord sent rivers beneath them; he attributes the same thing to the paradises. Indeed, the Jordan loses its healthy waters in the Dead Sea, but only after the impious cities were submerged. Therefore, this also is false. And in their place, or after them, we have restored other cities; for that place shall never be rebuilt. And he says: “Unless we had sent you the book on paper <note>original: "in charta," referring to a physical codex or scroll.</note>, that is, in booklets, and they had touched it with their own hands, those who do not believe would have said: ‘This is plain sorcery.’” If you had the book in booklets, then it did not descend in a single night—or conversely: it must be that you lied in one place or the other. Or is it that, if you showed a booklet, it must therefore be believed to have come from heaven or by divine power? As if everything written on paper were divine. Moreover, so that you may appear to have a common and similar cause with Moses and Christ, you say that you are called a sorcerer, just as they were called by their adversaries. And they say: “An angel does not come to him.” “And if we were to send an angel to him, the matter would be settled”—that is, they would ask for nothing more. Finally, they do not look back. “And if we were to appoint an angel, it would be necessary to appoint a man, and we would clothe him as they clothe themselves.” He attempts to evade with trifles. If God were to send an angel, they would ask for a man, and it would be necessary for that angel to be a man and to be clothed according to their custom. It is as if he wants to say: “They do not believe that an angel comes, and if an angel were to come, they would not believe unless he were a man. Thus in no way will they be satisfied. Therefore, what I say about the angel is enough.” And for that reason, he says, they laughed at those who came before, and that which they predicted was turned against them. These are mere terrors. He says, “Speak...”

» "...it was commanded to me that I should be the first Muslim <note>original: "Muſſulman"</note>, and that I should not be among those who assign a partner [to God]." <note>A paraphrase of Sura 6:14 or 6:163. Postel is attacking the claim that Muhammad was the "first" to submit to God.</note> See how he contradicts himself: for if this is so, then before him no one was faithful—neither Abraham, nor Moses, nor the Christians. If you say you were the first of all men, you lie. If you were the first of your own law, you lie again, for a Jew—and not a Muslim—is circumcised, and yet you remain silent about your own circumcision. In your own persuasion, the first was Zayd <note>original: "Zeidus"; Zayd ibn Harithah, the Prophet's adopted son.</note> from your family, and Abu Bakr <note>original: "Vbecharus"</note> from among the nobles. We [Christians] certainly do not "assign a partner" to God, because Christ is one and the same God, as are the Father and the Holy Spirit, differing only in Person. We do not adore or worship **images** as if they held any divinity in themselves; rather, we preserve them in memory of holy men so that we may be stirred toward a similar way of life, and that we may praise God in His saints, who gave such grace to men who follow Christ. He [Muhammad] says at last: » "And although it may be a heavy burden to you, turn away from them if you can, and seek a tunnel <note>original: "ſpeluncam"; Postel uses this to mean a burrow or hole in the earth.</note> in the earth, or a ladder to heaven, so that you may come to them with miracles; if perhaps God might gather them together, and they might not be among the foolish." <note>Refers to Sura 6:35.</note> No prophet before you spoke in such a way, nor did they seek a ladder to heaven or a tunnel to produce miracles, and yet they were believed. You, however—so that your "tunnel" <note>original: "naphaca", likely from the Arabic *nafaqa* meaning a tunnel or an expenditure.</note> or cave might seem to have divine authority—thrust it forward as if it were an oracle. And yet you yourself said you performed no miracle, except for that of the palm trunk, the excrement <note>original: "cacationis"; a reference to various polemical accounts of hadith involving the Prophet's physical nature or the camel's dung.</note>, the cloud, and similar things; whereby you make yourself ridiculous. Indeed, when they asked to see miracles, he would say: » "God is powerful enough to send a miracle, and therefore many do not understand." An excellent inference: "God is able to perform a miracle, therefore Muhammad is a prophet." It is as if you were to say: "A man is an animal, therefore the crow is white." From this follows that miraculous and portentous affirmation: » "There is no animal on the earth, nor any bird flying with its wings, that is not a nation like unto you; and lest you should not believe, He has written nothing for you that is not from God." <note>Refers to Sura 6:38.</note> These are "prophetic" voices indeed! It is no wonder if the demons became Muslims, since cattle, fish, and birds are rational animals, similar to men. Are you not ashamed, O Muslims? You cover these things with interpretations and say, "they are not men," meaning "they cannot be men." But the prophetic proposition is affirmative, not conditional. A little later, when miracles were demanded, he says: "God does not send prophets except as announcers." Therefore all men are prophets, since they announce things and advise their friends. Whoever says something and persuades others is, in that manner, a prophet just like Muhammad. But the saints demonstrated the power of divinity within themselves through the innocence of their lives and through predictions—not of death and the day of judgment, than which nothing is more certain, but of various events that followed afterward. Moreover, many were famous for miracles. This man, however, prevails by words, by the sword, and by cunning.
