An excellent evasion! The dreams would not return to the dreamer's mind, which he took badly, because a strong suspicion of fiction arose from it. A little later, what does he not lie about regarding Lazarus and Abraham? What does he not invent? The father of Abraham was **Terah** <note>original: "Therah"</note>, not Lazarus. <note>In Sura 6:74, Abraham’s father is named Azar. ### GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II ###

He recalls what he said before: that the Jews are not the sons of Abraham—that is, their law is not the law of Abraham. But I gather from this place that if they are sons and successors, they are therefore heirs; and if they are heirs, they are heirs of the law as well. Therefore, both laws belong to Abraham. Ishmael has been banished and is not to be counted among the children. As for what he <note>Muhammad</note> was saying:

> I do not accept a reward from you:

That is utterly false, and was said only for the sake of turning the common people away from obedience to their princes. For I ask, what does he mean by <term>alzache</term> <note>original: "alzache"; likely a Latinization of *Zakat*, the Islamic practice of almsgiving or religious tax.</note> and <term>elharegh</term> <note>original: "elharegh"; referring to *Kharaj*, a land tax or tribute.</note>—that is, tithes and canons—unless this is a reward? What else is given to the head of a Republic in the whole world but tithes and tributes? And yet, like a robber, you do not ask for it, you seize it; and elsewhere you speak against this very point. Arabia was peaceful and happy before you, but you have placed it in perpetual upheaval. In this part of his persuasion, he used a "rhetorical occupation" <note>A device where a speaker mentions something while professing not to mention it.</note>, by which rhetoricians say exactly what they claim they do not wish to say. While he was receiving from everyone, he said he wanted nothing and asked for nothing, so that they might follow him. But when he was accused of bringing many things contrary to the Divine Law, he immediately devised an answer:

> And they do not truly attribute to God His power when they say: "He sends nothing down from heaven upon men." Say: "He sent the book with which Moses came into the light and for the direction of men, which they arranged through pamphlets, from which you hide many things and conceal many things." <note>A paraphrase of Sura 6:91.</note>

It is not enough to say this; it is necessary to demonstrate it. Since this concerns the actions of men, if it is to be established, it is not enough to have said it; it must be proven, at least by conjectures. Since Muhammad is unable to do this, it follows that he is lying impudently. For not even one "jot or tittle" <note>The smallest marks in Hebrew writing.</note> of the Law has perished; it was preserved so diligently that every single sentence, period, and letter was counted. Muhammad was being refuted by the Holy Scriptures, and since he could not say they were false or corrupted, he devised another excuse: that the entirety of the scripture is not what is currently held. Yet nothing of those letters has perished. To be sure, the interpretation was handed down to the wise, and not all things are permitted to everyone; but the whole was always kept intact. Nor could he produce a single omitted passage. 

As for what he says a little later against Christ—that God Himself has no son, since He had no wife—no one has ever believed that the Son was born from the Father in divine matters in the way we are born here. For God is an incorporeal Mind, generating from Himself Eternal Wisdom, through which all things were brought into being, preserved, and restored; without this Son, nothing at all would subsist. In the Son—that is, in His Wisdom and His Word—He created the world; in that same Son, clothed in our flesh, He reformed the world within man, which is the compendium of all things. Therefore, He does not generate by means of a woman or a partner, as you, most impudent <term>anthropomorphite</term> <note>original Greek: "ἀνθρωπομορφίτα"; one who attributes human physical form or characteristics to God.</note> suppose; but in His own image He produces all things, and by His finger—that is, the Holy Spirit—He gives them life. I am forced to repeat these things frequently because the aim of this scoundrel—who is most cunning in earthly matters but most ignorant in divine ones—tends toward this point especially. 

One must hear the extraordinary judgment of this beast in divine matters, to see what genius he possesses. He says:

> O companies of demons and men, did there not come to you prophets from among yourselves, telling you of miracles and announcing to you your day? They said: "We are witnesses against ourselves." And the present life seduced them, and they confessed among themselves that they were impious. <note>A paraphrase of Sura 6:130.</note>

Thus the most wicked race of demons, turned toward and intent upon the destruction of men, and unconvertible, performed God's embassy! Hence, according to Muhammad, it must be said that there are "good demons," and that they have Republics and embassies, and turn themselves to the good, and enjoy present delights. Thus elsewhere he says they were made into <term>Muslims</term> <note>original: "Mussulmanos".</note>. And meanwhile, he makes them all ignorant of themselves, since they would not know they were impious without an ambassador of their own kind sent to them. This is Muhammadan theology. Take heed, you miserable and blind <term>Muslims</term>!

<meta>This page continues Guillaume Postel's polemic against the Quran. Having just dismissed Muhammad's claims to be the "first Muslim" in the previous section, Postel now turns his attention to the theological errors he perceives in the Quranic accounts of creation, the fall of Satan, and various stories of the prophets, which he characterizes as "old wives' tales."</meta>

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD #

Since **separate substances** <note>A Scholastic term for angels and demons, who were believed to be pure intellects existing without physical bodies.</note> are endowed with a most lively intellect, and one that understands all things except God, how can it be that they are ignorant of their own condition, that they are held by present delights, or that they might arrange an order worthy of a Republic, especially since their fall spreads through all of nature? As for his rejection of Jewish decrees, he does so unjustly, since he brings forth no authority against their holy authority. Furthermore, that he introduced a law on account of various sects brought in by heretics is more certain than certainty itself. For he took the exiled sons of Satan from holy religion into his fellowship, and he considered them the highest because they favored him; for that reason, throughout his entire work, he said they "believed well." Finally, he repeats that he was commanded to be the first **Saracen** <note>original: "Sarracenus"; a medieval term for Muslims.</note> or **Muslim** <note>original: "Mussulmanus"</note>. In whatever way he takes it, it is a lie, as has already been demonstrated.

->Surah Al-A'raf, Meccan, 205 Verses<-

Right from the threshold, he immediately repeats an error already refuted: that God told the **angels** to adore Adam, and Satan said to Him, "I will not adore him." And God said, "What prevented you from adoring Adam, when I commanded you to do so?" He said, "I am better than he, because you created me from fire, but him from clay." God said, "Depart from it (paradise) and do not be proud within it." He said, "I will wait until the day of judgment." There are as many errors in these words as there are sentences. God is made the author of evil and idolatry by commanding angels to adore a man, even though He reserves honor and glory for Himself. He says the demon was damned for not adoring a man, when it was actually because he did not honor God as God. He says he was created from fire, yet no **separate substances** <note>angels/demons</note> consist of fire; for if they did, they would be corruptible in the manner of matter. Finally, he says they will be saved, all of which fights against that nature. He says, lastly, that God corrupted Satan—whereby he makes God the author of evils, and a non-entity. Where Holy Scripture placed "you shall be like gods," he said "like angels," which is different. Finally, regarding what he says, "**Their private parts were revealed**," they could not be revealed if they had not been covered. But Holy Scripture has: *And the eyes of their knowledge were opened, and they saw that they were naked.* Thus, he always wished to add, subtract, or change things in the sacred texts. When he brings up the old wives' tales of Thamud, Had, Hud, the camel, the companions of Madyan <note>Postel lists several figures and groups from the Quran: the people of Thamud, the prophets Hud and Salih (associated with the miraculous She-Camel), and the people of Madyan (Midianites).</note> and similar things, these are the dreams of the old women of Arabia, which were usually sung by babbling nurses long before him. To the objections that he was a fool and out of his mind, he cannot satisfy them enough to prevent people from believing it is true. But meanwhile, I had forgotten to mention from the commentators regarding the **camel** <note>The miraculous She-Camel of the prophet Salih, which Postel claims the commentators described as being two miles long.</note> that its body was two miles in length. It shames me to report how many fables he attaches to the history of Moses and the departure from Egypt—just so he could boast to the Jews and say that he possessed things which they did not have in their own law. He claims Moses threatened the cross against those more conquered by him, even though he had no legal right before Pharaoh. He makes Moses call himself the "first of the believers"—thus neither Abraham nor Muhammad was the first. The Golden Calf lowed; Moses took Aaron by the hair. He says God made the children of Israel go astray, and yet He was calling them back to Himself and to justice. Fish near the sea came voluntarily to the shore on the Sabbath day when they were worshipping; and when they were not worshipping, they did not come. Yet on the Sabbath, it would not have been permitted to gather manna, so how much less to catch and cook fish? He says twelve springs gushed forth where there was only one. In short, almost everything is full of lying fictions, which I leave aside because they can be refuted by the sacred letter.

->Surah 8, Al-Anfal, written in Medina<- <note>Postel marks this as Surah 7 in the text, but the name Al-Anfal refers to the 8th Surah.</note>

This is the beginning of the law, a prescription for plunder and slaughter. So that nothing might be holy before his followers, he encourages them as much as he can. He asserts they are damned if they ever turn their backs, and that all goods belong to God and to whomever He wishes to give them. This chapter, indeed...

<meta>This page continues Postel’s polemical analysis of the Quran. He is currently critiquing specific chapters (Surahs) to argue that Muhammad’s motives were political and "tyrannical" rather than divine, contrasting him unfavorably with Moses and Christ.</meta>

## GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II. ##

It is called **Profit** <note>original: "Quæstus"; referring to Surah Al-Anfal (The Spoils).</note>, since it was written against the citizens of Mecca who had driven him out of the city due to sedition: it claims that all gains are good spoils, provided that a fifth part goes to the prophet. These are his "prophetic" laws. Moses saved his own people; Muhammad destroyed his citizens, despoiled them, killed them, and drove them away. Christ willed that all things be brought together for the use and charity of men as brothers; the Arab prophet willed his own followers to be enriched by the spoils of others. Truly, he inculcates nothing else but tyranny and blood in this chapter: he kills, he takes captives, he converts, such that no tyrant in the whole world could have written laws better suited to absolute power. Therefore, one may rightly call Muhammad a soldier and a robber, but not a prophet. Indeed, he is so far from being a prophet that nothing more alien to God and nature was ever born.

Of the same sort is the following Surah, which is called **Conversion** <note>original: "Conuersionis"; referring to Surah At-Tawbah (Repentance).</note>: and for that reason it was also written in **Medina**, where he lived as an exile. Furthermore, he wishes all to be received provided they give tithes, except for those upon whom he wished to take vengeance; from this he shows what his "prophecy" was and at what target it aimed. Finally, he commands, against nature, that they should kill fathers, brothers, and other parents if they refuse to believe. Then he teaches that one must "spend in the way," which is to say, to waylay the roads, for it is a most "just" source of income. 

He had the **Quraysh** <note>original: "Choraisios"; the ruling tribe of Mecca to which Muhammad belonged.</note>, his own kin, as enemies, and he attempted to intercept them with their merchandise and camels in four or five attacks, but was repulsed. Though he previously said, "follow those who ask no reward from you, and are guided," he now says, "pay and spend whether you want to or not, because you are unjust." Indeed, he pressed them so hard with robberies that he himself said they would flee into caverns if they could, so as not to suffer the things he imposed upon them. After he had tortured them remarkably, he saw nevertheless that almost all those whom he had bound by oath were failing him; therefore, he threatens them with destruction, as in the times of **Noah**, **Hud**, and **Thamud** <note>Biblical and Arabian prophets cited in the Quran as warnings to those who reject messengers.</note>, so that he might retain them by any artifice. If he could not do so by force, he would attempt it through the fear of God. 

Indeed, except for **Zayd**, **Abu Bakr**, **Umar**, and **Amr** <note>Early followers and companions of Muhammad.</note>, almost all were peasants who followed him partly out of fear and partly out of hope for plunder. Moreover, so that he might have an excellent pretext to kill his brothers, he said **Abraham** did not spare his father. Yet Abraham preferred to leave his father's goods and believe in God rather than plot anything against his father. He did indeed leave his parent and kindred in Chaldea, but he never wished to rage against nature under the pretext of religion; he left all that he could rightfully seek in order to obey God. But this "prophet" did not fear to do away with nine brothers—a man born for the destruction of nature. 

Whoever weighs these two chapters more carefully will see that laws more suited to a faction could not be set down by any bloodthirsty tyrant in the whole world. For there is nothing in them without blood, yet he makes God the author of this impiety. In this, he seems very similar to the ancient impostors who faked conversations with the gods because of the ignorance and fear of men, and gave laws suited to their own faction. This might have been tolerable in him if he had given anything by which nature might be helped—as did **Solon**, **Lycurgus**, **Zamolxis**, or **Charondas** <note>Famous lawgivers of Greek and Barbarian antiquity.</note>—but he overturned many good statutes and wrote many more for the destruction of nature and reason. We must move on to other matters.

***

Now that the slaughter has been carried out in Mecca, vengeance taken on his enemies, and the citizens killed, he seems to have written this song; for in it he reveals his purpose more clearly than before, which he would not have done unless matters had been settled. On account of this, once the fellowship was established, he was asked to publish the **Quran** <note>original: "Alcoranum"</note>, which he says he will not do. But from the beginning of the chapter, something must be noted.

### Surah Yunus, that is, Jonah. The Ninth Chapter, Meccan. ###

> Are these miracles of the Wise Book not a cause of wonder to men, that we have revealed to a man from among themselves, and that he should forewarn men...

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD #

> » ...and let him preach to those who have believed, that they **HAVE** the firstfruits of truth with their Lord. The Infidels <note>original: "Chaphiri"; referring to the Arabic *Kafir*</note> said: "This is manifest sorcery," because your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days: then he was elevated above the throne, where he disposes the command. Nor is there any redeemer, except after his command; thus he spoke. <note>This is a paraphrase of the Quran, Surah Yunus (10:2-3).</note>

All these things must be weighed more exactly. See with what judgment he attributes prudence, wisdom, and justice—for he grants the Quran these and similar titles in many places—to a book written in quires and booklets, since these are qualities that cannot exist except in the soul, and flow from there into action. Inanimate things, such as a book, cannot act, neither simply nor by deliberation. By what means could he be an object of admiration to men, since he described nothing beyond the law of nature and the common condition of things known even to the most unlearned, nor did he produce any sign? A prophet was never wonderful simply because he was chosen from among men, but because he excelled other men in divine works. 

Yet men wondered that this man was a prophet from among themselves—that is, one like them, a worshiper of idols in his youth, a man of luxury, frequently seized in his mind <note>Postel likely refers to the seizures or trances associated with Muhammad's revelations, which medieval critics often labeled as epilepsy or madness.</note>, a disturber of all things, bloodthirsty, bringing no miracle worthy of God or proceeding for the use of men. Moreover, because he did not want his words to be weighed by anyone, they were indeed rightly amazed. For God would be most unjust if He sent such prophets for the restoration of nature. If men had already believed, they had no need of a prophet. 

But if he says those who believed were the "firstfruits of truth," how can that be possible when Abraham existed two thousand and more years before him? When Moses and the children of Israel were chosen and proven by God? And when he himself admits that Abraham, Moses, Christ, and the prophets were among the messengers of truth? This, therefore, is an impudent lie and a contradiction. Who ever told you that your message was "manifest sorcery" when you produced no miracle? You merely repeat this objection made by the Jews against Christ so that you might seem to have something in common with Him. 

If indeed you performed any miracle in the presence of certain people, it was "bringing the moon down from heaven." <note>A reference to the *Splitting of the Moon* (Surah Al-Qamar), which Postel mocks as a magic trick.</note> For all other things were never done with any witness, except for the watering of the palm trunk. If you led the moon down from heaven, what mortal perceived it, since the whole world would have been deprived of it as long as it was in your sleeves? <note>original: "manicis tuis"; referring to the legend that the moon entered Muhammad's sleeve.</note> Suppose that Bugellinus <note>A likely reference to a legendary or specific witness in the polemical tradition.</note> saw it; how did the others who were deprived of it not notice, since even tiny eclipses are preserved in the records of the nations? How large were your sleeves, that they could contain a twenty-seventh part of the earth? <note>Postel is comparing the physical size of the moon to the earth to show the absurdity of the "sleeve" legend.</note> 

These are trifles and the ravings of old women, just as in the past sorceresses and hags mocked the minds of men with illusions and promised the same things as you. For this reason, Circe, Medea, and Calypso were infamous as celebrated sorceresses in both Greek and Latin literature. If the Arabs called you great for this reason, they did so rightly, because you were playing with illusions. 

The miracles which God produced in the heavens in the name of His people are commended in the literature of all nations. The Persians committed to writing the standing still of the sun under Joshua, and its backward movement under Hezekiah. The Greeks thought there would be future conflagrations resulting from this and committed it to their writings—fabulously, to be sure, but hinting at this truth. What shall I say of the eclipse of both luminaries at the death of Christ? Phlegon <note>Phlegon of Tralles, a 2nd-century Greek writer whose mention of an eclipse was often cited by Christians as evidence of the darkness at the Crucifixion.</note>, living in Rome, mentions it; the Chaldeans noted it in their annals; the Egyptians saw it. In Heliopolis, Dionysius and Apollophanes disputed about it. Those are real miracles; yours, however, are either trifles or illusions. 

Afterward, in your usual fashion, you make God a being who lacks a location and is finite, when you claim that after matter was arranged He sought heaven and was moved from place to place in the manner of a man, comprehending nothing in your entire work that is truly worthy of God. You do not notice that you deny God when you make Him finite and subject to movement from place to place. But you will object to me, I know, that it is written in the sacred texts: God [descended]...

Postel is arguing that Islamic theology regarding God's "throne" (the 'arsh) and the nature of Muhammad's revelation is logically flawed and inferior to Christian concepts of divine accommodation and the unique role of Christ.</meta>

### GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II ###

"...I will go down and see if they have completed their iniquity in deed" <note>original: "descendam & uidebo"; a reference to Genesis 18:21</note>; and that our Christ descended from heaven, and many other places where the divine words seem to attribute local motion to God. When we speak of God or His power in the sacred scriptures, we accommodate ourselves to the sense and capacity of the reader, so that we seem to place many passions or actions in God. We do this because the effects seen in these lower realms are the sort that humans would produce if they were moved by similar feelings. Therefore, we understand those effects as coming from the effect itself, not from any motion or agitation of the immovable God, yet we never cast God down from His own heaven. For although His force and power are seen everywhere and represent Him through His traces, we nevertheless assert that His majesty exists chiefly in the higher heavens. 

But you, who affirm that the *hers* <note>original: "herſſ"; referring to the Arabic *'arsh*, or Throne of God</note>—that is, the seat or throne—is the proper place of His majesty, you make Him move from place to place when you contend that He is beneath His own throne. Thus we differ greatly: we recognize His power everywhere, but His majesty as being above all matter. You, however, wish for His majesty to be thrust down from heaven into these lower things along with His power, and to have performed manual labor. 

Furthermore, we contend that whenever we read that a "specter" of God was represented, it was the ministry of angels that God willed to be carried out as a bodily office. The claim that God, after returning to his throne, "disposed" the things that were to be done here—that is false. For before the constitution of the world, all things were clear, foreseen, and ordered by the Divinity; He then finally brought them into being when it seemed best to Him, and as it seems best now. Therefore, He disposed nothing "after" the world was created, for that would mean there was a new will in Him, which is repugnant to His nature. 

It follows: "Nor is there any redeemer except after his command." << These things were written for the sake of Christ’s grace and redemption, << since it was both believed and seen that the remission of sins is held through Him. For whoever has been baptized in Christ, and the martyrs, have shown themselves to have obtained remission from Christ in such a way that no deed was so arduous—excepting only creation itself—that they could not do it in the name of Christ and God; and yet all those things are ascribed to God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. 

This plague of a man <note>Referring to Muhammad</note> was not ashamed to want to take away from Christ the Redeemer that which this most impure man attempted to ascribe to himself through a forged revelation. For he says that God—whom he had approached within "a bow-shot" <note>A reference to the *Mi'raj* or Night Journey, where Muhammad is said to have come within two bow-lengths of God's presence</note> in the highest heaven even above Christ—gave to him that he should be "Muhamed Mustapha," that is, the redeemer and sanctifier. For *saphia* means to act holily, whence *sophi* means "holy," and *estephaia* means "to sanctify." From this comes the participle or active verbal noun, *Mustaphai*, that is, "sanctifier." <note>Postel is attempting a linguistic analysis of the Arabic title *Mustafa* (the Chosen One), though his etymological connections to "Sufi" or "sanctifier" are idiosyncratic to his era's scholarship.</note> 

O impious and lost man! You wished to snatch for yourself the title of God and to take away from God what you did not grant to Christ, who is both man and God. Let the fair reader see how many errors and blasphemies are in these three or four verses of this law, and let him judge the credibility of the whole work by them. For if it were permitted to examine it thus, there would appear as many errors as there are words where he wished to defect from us—which he did by design. 

Now I shall pick out certain things here and there. "And when our miracles are read << to them, those who do not hope for our meeting said: 'Bring a Quran << without this, or change it.' Say: 'It is not permitted for me to change it << by the judgment of my own soul, since I follow nothing except what has been revealed << to me, because I fear the Lord if I should offend Him.'" <note>A paraphrase of Surah Yunus (10:15).</note> 

He calls the miracles of God and nature "his own" throughout the entire work; this is impious and a claim to participate with God. Furthermore, he announces all the acts of God indefinitely without changing the person or the manner of speaking after he has spoken of himself. But it is a common thing, found in every single verse of the Quran, that—silently indeed—he confesses there are many lies, things contrary to sacred scripture, and impious things which he cannot deny. Yet, so that he might not seem to be changing his dreams, he says it is forbidden for him to change anything in it. If nothing in the Quran is to be changed, how can it be that God is foolish and unskilled...

Having previously argued against the Islamic conception of God’s "throne," Postel now focuses on the internal contradictions he perceives in the Quran and the character of Muhammad, whom he views as a strategic impostor rather than a true prophet. ->### ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD ###<-

Let Muhammad be considered "wise"! For if his law was revealed with God as its author, yet it conflicts with the divine law in six hundred places, how can it be that God is not false, wicked, or a liar? Or rather, is Muhammad not treacherous, impious, and an impostor? Thus, he recognizes what is false, but out of fear of losing his power, he refuses to change it; that is the true reason for his "revelation" and the aim of his law. If he had published it clearly, he could have been refuted by even the least of men, since he contradicts himself in every single verse <note>original: "Aiet," likely a Latinization of the Arabic *aya* or verse</note>. Tell me:

> Can any of your associates or idols direct you toward the truth? Say: it is God who directs toward the truth. Is he who directs toward the truth not more worthy to be a leader than he who cannot direct unless he himself is directed? What is the matter with you, that you judge in such a way? Most of them follow nothing but opinion. But opinion can take nothing away from the truth, for God is wise in what they do. And let it not be said that this Quran <note>original: "Alcoranum"</note> was fashioned without God. Rather, it confirms what came before it, and explains the Book in which there is no blemish, from the Lord of the ages. Do they say: "He has forged it"? Say: "Bring a chapter <note>original: "capite," referring to a Surah</note> like it, and call upon whomever you can besides God, if you are truthful." Indeed, they have called false that which they did not comprehend with knowledge, before its interpretation had even come to them.

In this passage, while he pretends to speak against the Meccans <note>original: "Mechenſes"</note>, he also rises up against those whom he has approved in countless other places. For he wishes to turn away the foolish common folk so that, having abandoned the prescriptions of the holy laws, they might follow him. It had already been proven by many miracles that what preceded him was from God; therefore, he says that "direction" belongs to God, so that those who came before him might seem to have lacked it. He certainly could have followed them if he had wished, but he preferred to deny God and follow his own lusts. God is surely the one who directs toward the truth, but He uses humans as His instruments and grants greater gifts to one than to another. 

Therefore, those whom He sent previously were not false; because you contradict them all, it must be that you are the liar. Who are those who follow nothing but opinion? Certainly not the followers of either Law <note>Postel refers here to the Old and New Testaments</note>, because both establish God, though one explains Him more fully. Before the Messiah <note>original: "Meſſias"</note> came in the flesh, the mystery of the Trinity <note>original: "trinitatis"</note> was not commonly known, except only to the wise. But after Christ arrived, those mysteries were made clear, without which the world can neither be built nor restored—much less saved. 

Therefore, those things are not matters of "opinion," but yours are, and they are most false. For what is more subject to opinion, or more foreign to the truth, than that a man should be a prophet who brought about the destruction of nature, who performed no signs, who contradicted all good men, and who has nothing in common with anything except heresies and condemned opinions (outside of our own)? He is a man who thirsts for the blood of all, who seizes fortunes, and who kills his own citizens and brothers. 

Furthermore, since God gave all the prophets before him—through whom a depraved nature could be directed and illuminated—how can it be that He gave this "prophet" to the world after Jesus Christ <note>original: "Ieſum Christum"</note>, the greatest of all? This man would lead people back from the written law and the law of grace to a natural and corrupt state. Would providence not be utterly insane to have undertaken such great labors to form man, sending the greatest of prophets—than whom no greater can be given—only to finally recall everything back to the state from which He had led it? 

See how absurd these things are, and how full of mere "opinion." Muhammad had heard that "opinions are pushed aside by other opinions" in false religions; therefore, he said that the truth was similar to opinions, so that those wretched men, blind in divine matters, might prefer his "opinion." For such people, at the devil’s persuasion, falsehood is generally more acceptable than the truth. Furthermore, when many people objected to him that the Quran was a fiction—as it seemed to be, and indeed was—he says that nothing like it could be fashioned without God. I might subscribe to that sentiment, were I not afraid of pinning such impiety upon God. For if all extremes of things were attributed to God, He would undoubtedly seem to be the author of the Quran. However, just as when we speak of the Supreme Truth...

# GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II.

We attribute truth to God: so here we must attribute the highest lies and foolishness, which agree with no kind of learning, to their supreme author—who, since he cannot be God, must be the worst of all demons. And because they used to say this fiction was not the law of Abraham, nor of Moses, nor of Christ, since it contradicted all of them, he [Muhammad] devised this excuse (which I mentioned before): that it was a "distinction and confirmation" between those things already in hand—that is, the New and Old Testaments—so that he might always find some way to evade the truth. But how can there be a middle ground between two extremes that actually steps outside the boundaries of both? It is impossible. He would have spoken more accurately if he called it a "contradiction" against both Testaments, since in six hundred places he misses the mark of both. But I proceed to other matters; I have already satisfied the argument against those who deny the divinity of Christ and that God has a son, which he repeats three hundred times here and elsewhere in the Quran <note>original: "Alcorano"</note>. Indeed, when he was urged to admit that the other laws were good and proceeded from God, he would then say:

> I have my labor for myself, and you have your labor for yourselves. I am innocent of what you do, and you are innocent of what I do. <note>A paraphrase of Quran 10:41</note>

He does this for the sake of retaining everyone under his power. He makes Moses out to be impious when he says that Moses prayed to God against Pharaoh—whom he was trying to convert, or at least convince to release the people he had come to lead. For although God had "hardened the heart of Pharaoh"—that is, left him in his "purely natural state" <note>original: "in puris naturalibus," a theological term for human nature without divine grace</note> and in his opinions corrupted by desires—nevertheless, God’s Apostle [Moses] should never have committed the act of calling upon God to destroy a man, for that would be against His majesty. As for what he calls the "people of Jonah," that people of Nineveh (to whom Jonah was sent from the region where he was born) differs greatly: Jonah was a Syrian from Phoenicia, while Nineveh is in Assyria. But to have been ignorant of that is a small thing. When Muhammad says,

> Will you not force men until they believe? And it is not placed in the power of man to believe except by the command of God: <note>A paraphrase of Quran 10:99–100</note>

He is impious and wicked, for he compelled people through force, slaughter, plundering, captivity, and blood, even though God had not yet granted them the grace to believe—even if his law had been good. Therefore, religion was not to be introduced by the sword when God did not yet wish them to believe; for He is the one who can make all peoples come together. But at this point, Muhammad was sated with the blood of citizens, and having given place to vengeance in the two preceding chapters, his fury, saturated with blood, became less savage.

->Surah Hud [Chapter 11]. Meccan.<-

Repeating the story of the creation as having been done in six days, he immediately admitted an error just to differ from Moses. For where Moses has, "And the Spirit of the Lord moved over the waters," he [Muhammad] put, "And his *hers*"—that is, his throne—"was upon the waters." <note>Postel uses the term "hers," a Latinization of the Arabic *'Arsh* (throne), referring to Quran 11:7</note>. Although the greatest divine power is seen in the nature of water—so great that all things seem to be born from it—nevertheless, the true seat of divinity was never attached to a corruptible element. The supreme power of God, creating all things through wisdom, effects everything through His Spirit as if by the "finger of God," showing the greatest strengths of His power in the waters. Nor was it enough for him to have admitted an error in this change, but he also added another: that God placed his throne upon the waters "to prove which of us was of better conduct." He makes God needy of a place and a proximity in order to know our crimes and deeds; yet God fills heaven and earth, replenishing all things, and is "unplaceable" <note>original: "illocabilis," meaning God cannot be confined to a specific location</note>, to be known only through what He is not. Shortly after, Muhammad acknowledges how he gathered power from peasants and commoners who had joined him for the sake of plunder; and yet those men, however unlearned, laughed at his nonsense, which is why he threatens them with the punishment of fire. He adds a little later, in his usual fashion, to the history of Noah <note>original: "Noachi"</note>: that one of his sons refused to follow his father and sought a mountain, and perished; this must be called false because it is not in the Sacred Scriptures. All—

# DE ORBIS CONCORDIA

Then he fills his head with those mythical prophets—Hud, Thamud, and Ad—whom he mixes with the true ones: Abraham, Noah, and Moses. He does this to draw people to himself with rustic terrors <note>Postel refers to the Quranic stories of destroyed civilizations as "terriculamentis rusticis," intended to scare common folk into submission.</note> and force them to swear by his words. He uses this trick throughout the entire Quran <note>original: "Alcorano"</note>: after listing many sent by God, he expects people to believe he is also a prophet. It is as if someone argued: "this sword is sharp, and that one, and another, therefore this axe must be too." The rest are his usual repetitions.

->Surah Joseph, 11. Meccan.<-

He treats this history of Joseph more truthfully than any other from the whole of Holy Scripture. Nevertheless, he fills it with many fabricated fables: how the mistress tore away a piece of his garment as he fled and showed it to her husband; how the neighboring women gave a judgment that if it were the front part, he would seem the aggressor, but if it were the back part—suggesting she had tried to violate Joseph’s modesty—then the tear would be in the back. The back part was seen to be torn, and yet Joseph was in prison for thirty years, as he says, even though judgment had been rendered in his favor. He also describes how women were dying for him because of his beauty and cut their own hands. Regarding those thirty years in prison: he calculates this from the age Joseph was when he was led to Pharaoh, for he was actually in prison for only thirteen years. Then, recounting the travels of his brothers, he says Joseph gave them a staff to place over their father’s face so that he might see. To put it briefly, in almost every sentence he adds something of his own invention so that it might be called "sound" <note>original Greek: "ὑγιὲς" (hygiès). Postel uses this term ironically to suggest Muhammad is trying to make his narrative appear "wholesome" or more complete than the Biblical one.</note>. These things will be refuted by the Holy Scriptures.

->12, Chapter Ra'd [The Thunder], Meccan.<-

He brings nothing else here but a repetition of things said a hundred times before, setting forth the miracles of nature in an attempt to strip Christ the Lord of the glory of His divinity. Therefore, he very frequently asks: "What have those whom you have made partners created?" If he concedes to me that God’s power could have created the world without wisdom and will, then I will no longer argue with one who attributes ignorance to God—which would be ridiculous even in a man. However, if he concedes to me that God alone performs His miracles in His own name, without invoking any greater power, he must necessarily confess that Christ is God, who performed all His miracles in His own name. When he asks "What did He create?", is it not clearly equal to or greater than creation to make a new creature out of a corrupted one in His own name? Christ raised the dead (with the Father and Holy Spirit always accompanying Him), and all in His own name—an act which, in the entire Quran, you rightly equate with creation. But I am becoming too frequent in these points, though the man's impiety forces me to do so. For himself—as he does in the whole work and in every word—he sets down a law especially for his own benefit: he says he is allowed to have more wives because the prophets had them, as if they had a herd like Muhammad, or as if Christ had any.

->15. Abraham, Meccan.<-

Here he satisfies the Jews who object to him. They said: "If he were their Messiah and a prophet directed to them with the law of Abraham, why does he not write in the holy language <note>Hebrew</note>?" He says he was not sent except in the language of his own people. But they replied that he was nothing but a flawed man, lacking miracles. If he would at least bring a sign or a reason! He brushed everything aside using God as an excuse, saying that God gives His grace to whom He wills. When he had already perverted those who listened, and called them so desperate and blinded, they said: "It doesn't matter then, for if God were to guide us, we would believe." He then adds a dialogue of Satan to call them back:

» And Satan said, after the command of the Lord was fulfilled: "Indeed, God promised you a true promise, and I promised you so that I might lead you astray. I have no power over you, except that I called you and you answered me. Therefore, do not accuse me, but accuse yourselves. I am not your helper, nor are you my encouragers. I have become a blasphemer in that you previously made me an equal [to God], for the wicked suffer a great punishment." <note>Postel provides a Latin translation of Quran 14:22</note>

# GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II.

He contradicts himself, since elsewhere he says that men are in the power of the demon, yet now he says the demon has no power over them; this is completely false. For as many men as are outside the knowledge of the one God and His wisdom, they are in the power of Satan. But he rightly brings in the author <note>original: "authorem"—referring to Satan</note> here, under whose jurisdiction he was. Men ought to blame themselves, yet not without the fault of the demon. He depicts the demon as repentant and better than men, as one who acknowledges himself as blasphemous and impious, while men deny and ignore it. But it is worth the effort to hear what fables he attaches to the history of Abraham. And when Abraham said:

> Lord, make this region faithful, and protect me and my sons so that we do not adore idols, Lord, since they have destroyed many men. And whoever follows me, he shall be of me: and whoever resists me, You are merciful and propitious. Our Lord, I have dwelt, and I have made my generation to dwell near a river without seed <note>The Quranic "sterile valley" (Surah Ibrahim 14:37).</note>, by the cursed house: Our Lord, so that they may offer prayers. Therefore, make a propitiation for men according to their desire, and enrich them with fruits, so that perhaps they may praise You, etc.

None of these things are found at all in the Holy Scriptures; in fact, many things are contrary to them. First, Abraham was chosen and set apart by God through a calling; he did not believe in God by his own spontaneous choice, as is said here. What he adds—"Whoever follows me is of mine"—he fabricates and adds to the Sacred Scriptures so that those unskilled in holy writ might think, by a similar reasoning, that cohorts followed Abraham, and therefore they might follow Muhammad with an equal mind. 

As for what he says—that when Abraham came to the faith, he lived by a sterile river near the forbidden temple in Mecca—that is utterly false. Mecca is in *Arabia Felix* <term>Arabia Felix: "Happy Arabia," the classical name for the fertile southern/coastal parts of the Arabian Peninsula</term>, whereas Orchoa <note>Orchoa likely refers to Ur of the Chaldees.</note> (from where he proceeded into Mesopotamia, and from there into Syria and Egypt) is distant from that place by more than five hundred thousand paces. Nor, after his departure from that region, was he ever moved from Syria, where he always lived among the Canaanites, except when compelled by famine, which forced the man to seek Egypt. 

Therefore, Muhammad, the basis of your law is false, which you wish to attribute to Abraham for this reason: that he worshipped in an accursed basilica <note>original: "execrata basilica"—Postel's derogatory term for the Kaaba in Mecca.</note>. For how could it be, if he had handed down a holy religion there, that you would have had to labor so greatly in overturning a false religion? If your ancestors had been faithful, as you say and as your "evangelists" of the *Siyar* <note>original: "Hassiar"—referring to the *Sira*, the traditional biographies of Muhammad.</note> write, how is it that your father was a "faithful" one, yet the father of a prophet was so unhappy that out of twelve children he had only one imbued with the true religion? And that the others were so hostile to piety that all but one or two were slaughtered by the prophet? To such an extent were they alienated from him by the dreams and madness of an impostor that they were the authors of his exile, and they considered it most pleasing for him to be as far as possible from home—he who brought disgrace and reproach to his kin, a stain upon religion, and the subversion of his fatherland. 

If there had been even one or two survivors from that "faithful" lineage imbued with true persuasion, there would have been no need to give freedom to the slave Zeid <note>Zayd ibn Harithah, an early convert and adopted son of Muhammad.</note> so that he might become the first Muslim <note>original: "Mussulman"</note>. Nor would that injustice have had to be inflicted upon masters, whereby a number of believers was prepared for you through the defection and flight of their slaves from their masters. 

But you will allege to me that soldiers of little integrity were collected by David for the sake of his kingdom. But David did not subvert the commonwealth; he was preserving his person and was anxious for his life. He was a king chosen and anointed by a divine oracle through a prophet and priest, the prince of the commonwealth, while a tyrant was lying in wait for his life. What similarity is there? Muhammad was therefore nothing other than an impostor, abusing the rudeness of men to lead them into credulity, since none of his ancestors were anything but idolaters. As I have already noted, the chroniclers of *Cahidaru* <note>Likely a reference to the historian Al-Kindi or similar polemical sources used by Postel.</note> confess this, writing that he himself was the builder of the cursed temple—in which Abraham could not have prayed, since the sacred house had not yet been built. Behold how the lie betrays itself, and is always consistent with its own nature. O wretched men, buried in deceit and darkness! Will you not at last, having regained your sight, turn your attention to...

# CONCERNING THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

...was imposed? <margin>The Hijr. 14. Of Mecca. <note>original: "Elhageiat. 14. Mechense." Postel refers to Surah 15 (Al-Hijr), which he or his source numbers as 14.</note></margin>

> We never destroyed any city without it having a known book: nor shall a people anticipate their end, nor shall they postpone it. They said: "Hey you, upon whom the remembrance has come, you are possessed by a demon; why do you not show us an angel, if you speak the truth?"

He says that there is no city that does not have its own law and remembrance: therefore, he was fruitlessly thrusting his own remembrance upon those who already had one. For he calls the Quran *dilzicri* <note>original: "dilzicri," a transliteration of the Arabic "dhikr," meaning "remembrance" or "mention."</note>, that is, endowed with memory, which is to say, full of the recollection of created things. Truly, it is most false to say that all people have a just knowledge of the law of nature. For some are so depraved that they rise up against its prescriptions even against their own conscience, such as the **Anthropophagi** <note>literally "man-eaters" or cannibals</note>, **Cannibals**, and however many peoples plot the ruin of nature—as does Muhammad, who approves of promiscuous intercourse and initiations with brutes, and persuaded his followers toward perverted lust. Therefore, not all cities or peoples have a "book" in the sense he usually takes it. For all have it only as far as *knowledge* is concerned, but few have it for *emendation* <note>the process of moral improvement or correction</note>, and those few are only the best Christians. I say "the best," because not everyone who has given their name to Christ is immediately a Christian. Thus, only those gifted with the divine spirit through Christ have the law by which they recognize sins and flee from them; other mortals merely know of it. 

As for what you say—that no peoples or cities can accelerate or delay their misfortunes and appointed periods—you completely take away **free will** from men. In such a case, the Republic of men is nothing more than a herd of oxen or sheep. Laws, corrections, and counsels are in vain if human efforts profit nothing in this life. It has resulted from this that those among the followers of this law who claim a special holiness—and who are in the second place only after the beasts—do not move from their spot when rain, hail, or the harms of the air arrive. Instead, they say it is **fate**, and it must be endured because God sent it. If we have no choice, let us go and rush into pleasures and crimes like beasts, for we cannot do otherwise. See where this opinion leads. 

A congregation of many men is far more excellent than one or two individuals; therefore, it can resist evils and prolong its own existence by any remedy. But not everyone knows where these things tend. After the circumstances in **Mecca** changed, Muhammad wanted to soothe the minds of the survivors with these words: claiming that the outcome was not his fault, nor had his will sinned, but that God had sent the end of things in such a way that no one could escape. This is true insofar as you consider the ultimate reality, but it is false regarding the timing. God indeed predestines all things by inclination, not by necessity; by necessity, not by time. And if He did this in all circumstances, "who are you, O man, to answer back to God?" <note>A reference to Romans 9:20.</note> Certainly, God never sends the necessity of evil, otherwise He would be evil; but sometimes He sends what *appears* to be evil to someone, specifically when a certain great good follows from that event. 

You, therefore, Muhammad, undeservedly take away the place of human prudence for the sake of covering up your crime. When they said you were seized by a demon, they were not lying. For the sake of covering up your **falling sickness** <term>morbus fontici: an archaic term for epilepsy, which medieval Christian writers often attributed to Muhammad as a sign of demonic possession or as the source of his "visions."</term> in the presence of your wife **Khadija**, you feigned that you were a prophet, and Satan began to twist you against your will, as you perceived everything speaking to you and calling you. This is evident in many other places, but especially in the last **Sura** of the Quran, in which you defend yourself with God from *uisnass* <note>original: "uisnass," likely a transliteration of "waswas," meaning the "whispers" or intrusive thoughts attributed to Satan in Surah 114.</note>, that is, from the mental disturbance sent by a demon. Therefore, it is no wonder that these lies are so poorly connected, since two ruined authors devised them: a man with a disturbed mind, and the demon inhabiting him. Truly,

> how do you dare, you ruined scoundrel, to say that the laws of the ancients have vanished? "Now," he says, "the law of the ancients, or of the first ones, has vanished."

How can it be that the law has vanished, when its worshippers were the most numerous in the whole world? The world was occupied by Jews and Christians, except for a few idolaters, when this plague flowed from you into it, and of those...

Thus, you spoke falsely when you said they had perished. ### Surah An-Nahl, 15 <note>Surah 16, "The Bee." Postel numbers it 15.</note>

Hear the usual blasphemies. He has already confessed in innumerable places that laws were given by God before him, and yet he now says the devil is their patron. How can it be that Satan, the adversary of God, is the patron of those under God's law? Certainly, the Jews have a demon for a patron from the time they rejected and killed Christ, who was promised to them in countless places. Because of His death, sixty-hundred thousand men <note>6,000,000—an exaggerated medieval/early modern estimate of casualties during the Jewish-Roman Wars.</note> were destroyed in two Roman assaults shortly after the death of Christ. 

Indeed, when they wished to restore the temple **Elmihrab** <note>original: "Elmihrab," from the Arabic "Al-Mihrab" (the prayer niche), here used by Postel to refer to the Sanctuary or the Temple in Jerusalem.</note>—that is, the Holy Place or the Jerusalem Temple—under the authority of the Emperor **Julian the Apostate**, a divinely sent earthquake arose from the site of the foundations, and balls of fiery flames consumed the builders, once and then a second time, until they stopped. These things were written by pagan authors and those foreign to us; we did not invent them. From this, it is certain that the one religion of Jesus Christ is true. Over it, Satan has no patronage, but rather over the impious liar Muhammad.

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

Authors of commentaries mention that whatever he <note>Referring to Muhammad.</note> received from the sacred scriptures in the common tongue, he explained in Arabic. What the word *agemij* <note>original: "agemij"; from the Arabic *'Ajam*, a term used to refer to non-Arabs, particularly Persians. Postel is discussing the sources of Muhammad's information.</note> means in this place, I do not quite grasp. Some think the Latin language is meant, while others think it is the Persian. Whatever it was, it was distinct from Arabic. For this Arabic which Muhammad used is clearly vulgar, and devoid of any grammatical art such as is observed by learned writers who handle the humanistic disciplines. For Muhammad wished to be bound by no rules, neither of reason nor of eloquence; though his followers claim he is the most eloquent of all because he wrote almost entirely in rhythmic prose, yet even this was done without any laws of composition. For he will make a sentence of two hundred syllables square up through *homoioptoton* <note>original: ὁμοιοπτώτως; a rhetorical device where clauses end with words in the same grammatical case or with similar sounds.</note> with the very shortest ones. To summarize in a few words: he wished to be considered lawless in all things, just as he struggled with inconsistency in all things. In this chapter, he prohibits four things: carrion, the flesh of swine, blood, and that which is sacrificed to idols—even though he had already forbidden them ten or twelve chapters earlier. When, a little later, he calls this law the "Law of Abraham," it is clear how falsely he asserts this.

<margin>Surah of the Children of Israel, 16. Meccan. <note>This refers to Surah 17, *Al-Isra* (The Night Journey), also known as *Bani Isra'il*. Postel's numbering differs from the modern standard.</note></margin>
From the very beginning, he sets forth that foolish vision and the riding of the Buraq <note>original: "Borachi"; the winged steed that carried Muhammad during the Night Journey.</note>, and says that God spent the night with His servant. Indeed, the interpreters pour out so many absurdities, blasphemies against God, and ignorance of facts, that no patient person could endure hearing them. They claim that holy men are separated by different heavens; that animals of every kind, larger than the whole world, reside in the heavens; that there are gates in the heavens made of tangible matter; that God is finite; that the name of Muhammad is written in all places alongside the name of God; and that all angels and prophets adore Muhammad. They even say that the holy and the blessed pray to a "Lerna of crimes" <note>original: "scelerū lernam"; Lerna was the swamp home of the Hydra; Postel uses it here as a metaphor for a bottomless pit or source of evil.</note> so that he might pray for them before God, as if the blessed in heaven could still be in need of anything. From this he relates great privileges, all of which I have noted before. Yet he did not dare, even though he had supposedly climbed to the highest heaven, to not confess that Christ was greater than himself; he even prayed to Christ to ask God on his behalf. These are the absurdities. Now, if one were to add the various levels between the heavens described by the interpreters, who would not burst into laughter upon hearing them? Everything is worthy of the authors and those who believe them.

But perhaps the followers of Muhammad might wish to argue with me because I said that Muhammad gathered strength and assumed ferocity from the factions of the Jews—specifically when he was believed to be the Messiah, or the one who would lead them back to Jerusalem. Let them hear the meaning of this passage, which the ignorant read and admire, but the learned understand, disregard, and laugh at. He says:

> We gave the book to Moses, and placed it as a direction for the children of Israel, so that you should not take any patron besides Me. The generations of those whom we carried with the glorious servant Noah; and we told the children of Israel in the book, that they would be corrupted upon the earth, and twice they would be exalted with great exaltation. And when these promises arrived, we sent against them our most cruel servants, and they shall search out the recesses of the dwellings, and the promise made shall be fulfilled. At last, we shall give you a turn over them. We shall endow you with wealth and sons, and make you a great multitude. If you do good, you do good for yourselves, and you shall enter the temple just as they entered it the first time, and you shall destroy those who exalt themselves with destruction. Perhaps your Lord will have mercy on you, and perhaps your promise is our promise: and we shall place Gehenna <note>Hell.</note> as a barrier for the impious. Because this Quran directs the leaders of the people.

And even if that sentence sufficiently reveals its author, nevertheless, because of that prophetic phrasing which is not accessible to everyone, I judge it should be explained a little more broadly. He says it was written in the Law of Moses that the Jews would be dispersed twice (for he understands that by *tupsidune* <note>original: "tupsídune"; a transliteration of the Arabic *tufsidunna*, meaning "you will cause corruption."</note>, that is, "they would be corrupted") and twice gathered together. I have never read this in the Law, nor do I remember seeing it. But the Jews were easily going to grant this to a new Messiah, provided he had shown himself a man in restoring them rather than in despoiling them.

## THE WRITINGS OF GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II.

They <note>The Jewish people.</note> had indeed many captivities: many under the judges, one under Saul, and another under the empire of the Greeks. However, two are more famous: the captivity of Nebuchadnezzar and that of Titus. He <note>Muhammad</note> therefore wished to make promises to those eager for revolution, and to those whose temperaments he knew were prone to factions. He suggested that if they were willing to follow him and rage with every kind of cruelty against whoever they encountered, a leader would not be lacking for them. For once the inner rooms of others' houses were broken open, everything would be their prey. If they were willing to follow a leader in this matter and "do well"—that is, to fight and plunder manfully—they would achieve this for themselves: that they would be endowed with great wealth and an abundance of children. Truly a distinguished title did that man assume for himself—a self-styled prophet, endowed with a vehement cruelty—so that he might capture those he addressed with his eloquence. For they shall never have any leader except the Antichrist, who, in the manner of Muhammad, will join wealth and crimes of every kind under the authority and pretext of divinity. Such was each "Son of a Lie" <note>original: "Barcoziba"; a derogatory play on the name of Simon bar Kokhba, leader of the Jewish revolt against Rome (132–136 AD). "Bar Kokhba" means Son of a Star, while "Bar Koziba" means Son of a Lie.</note>, and that future leader in the sea, called the "second Moses" in Crete <note>A reference to a 5th-century messiah-claimant who convinced many Jews in Crete to jump into the sea, promising it would part for them.</note>. Such was Muhammad. There was also a man shortly before these years who incited Christians toward Judaism and wished to be called the "Thaborite King" <note>This refers to David Reubeni, a 16th-century Jewish traveler who claimed to represent the "lost tribes" of Israel. "Thaborite" refers to Mount Tabor.</note>. When he was asked what he thought of the Messiah, he answered ambiguously: תוֹחֶלֶת <gloss>Expectation</gloss> "perhaps you will see," asserting this of himself in the Hebrew fashion. I understood that this wicked man was sentenced to the flames by Charles of Austria, the fifth Emperor of this name <note>Holy Roman Emperor Charles V. Postel likely refers here to Solomon Molcho, Reubeni's associate, who was burned at the stake in 1532.</note>, because in Spain he wanted to draw many who were not averse to various persuasions toward Judaism. Muhammad likewise in this place sought to capture followers with a doubtful word: "Perhaps," he said, "your promise is our promise; perhaps God will have mercy on you and lead you back to your sacred rites, as in the past." With these ambiguous responses he toyed with the wretched nation for ten years, until his follies were exposed to the rest by Bensalone <note>Possibly a reference to Abdullah ibn Salam, a Jewish convert to Islam, though Postel portrays him as exposing Muhammad's errors.</note>, and they gradually began to fall away, so much so that he deals with nothing so frequently as the "perfidy" of the defecting Jews.

The title of this prophet must not be neglected by us, since he approved of that name for himself and placed it in a position of honor—a name with which we usually gift impious, wicked, and nefarious tyrants. And yet (if it pleases the gods <note>A Latin idiom for "if you can believe it."</note>) he is a prophet who turns this divine virtue not against the enemies of his state, nor toward the preservation of sacred things, nor toward the care of parents, but toward the slaughter of kinsmen, the overturning of sacred rites, and the disturbance of all things. Under his leadership, the citizens could have achieved wide dominion over affairs and he could have performed great duties, if he had been of sound health. But since he suffered from diseases of both mind and body, was marked by the suspicion of sorcery <term>prestigiarum</term> <note>original: "prestigiarum"; refers to illusions or magical deceptions meant to trick the senses.</note>, and meditated the ruin of his own citizens, no one would have wanted to obey him without a religious fiction. From these fates, he became known. Moreover, he was not satisfied with having favored the Jews, unless he also attacked Christians to please them and blasphemed against Christ. He says God does not have female angels; that is certain. That there are not two gods: we also firmly affirm and believe this. "Therefore Christ is not God": this does not follow. God does not beget in our human manner; therefore He does not beget at all: it is impossible for Him not to beget a Son from eternity, that is, the Word and Wisdom. Nor are there two gods because of this, because the whole divinity is in the Father, the whole in the Son, and the whole in the Holy Spirit. For, to repeat an example often used for those unskilled in divine matters: the conception of any thing (for example, the building of a house) exists entirely in the mind, and the same is entirely in the word and explanation, and the same is entirely in the building itself; and yet there are not three buildings, but one building. So God, the most powerful, must know what is to be done and must will it before He creates anything by His immense power; and unless He perpetually begot the Son—just as any thing has its own duration or birth—nothing at all would exist in the world. No form could be joined to matter unless power bound the forms of matter, wisdom fitted them to their proper shape, and will preserved them in existence for a very long time. But that bloodthirsty scoundrel did not grasp these things, he who recognized nothing of God except through the word, the belly,

...and he justified himself through shameful acts and glory. To the Jews seeking miracles, he says that God did not grant him miracles for this reason: because when God sent them in the past, they rejected them under the pretext of falsehood. An excellent evasion, and his usual trick. Was it the case that if some did not believe Moses at first sight, before it was known whether he came from God, no one believed him? Six hundred thousand men with their families eventually believed, for whom he composed and handed down a most peaceful republic. If the Jews did not obey Christ, the God-man, was there therefore no Christian nation? Within a hundred years of his death, without any force or blood—except that of the martyrs—Christ was accepted. If, therefore, you were bringing miracles, it would not have been necessary to kill, plunder, and drive away your citizens and brothers. If not immediately, you would have eventually conquered like the others. I accept, however, what he grants: when he confesses that he had no miracles. Therefore the "trees of defecation," <note>Postel is mockingly referring to Islamic descriptions of the Zaqqum tree or other fruits of paradise/hell, using vulgarity to dismiss them as absurd.</note> the split moon, and such things are fables and dreams. After he brought forth many trifles, as he does in the whole work, he says: "If all demons and men wished to compose a similar Al-Quran, they could not." <note>A reference to the "Inimitability of the Quran" (I'jaz al-Qur'an), a central doctrine in Islam.</note> Which I believe and grant to the man, because—being outside of reason, method, and any form other than repetitive babbling <term>battologia: the constant repetition of words or phrases, often seen as senseless</term>—it seems impossible for rational animals to compose anything similar. For if it were according to God and the order of nature and the method of the sciences, there would be some art of imitation, as we see in all other sciences. Here, truly, there is neither order, nor light, nor any greater trace of reason than if an old woman were to repeatedly heap up mentions of heaven and earth, man, ship, ox, milk, fruit, food, and cattle, and everywhere attach the name of God the Creator (whose name not even idol-worshippers are ignorant of). In considering this matter, there is no peasant who is not superior to this legislator. And so, he asserts that nothing similar can be composed by anyone who might deservedly bear the name of a man.

But hear the man’s distinguished doctrine. "They will ask you," he says, "about the spirit. Say: the spirit is from the command of the creator Lord, and you have but little knowledge." <note>A translation of Surah Al-Isra 17:85.</note> A definition worthy of such a teacher! It is as if someone were to ask, "What is a sword?" and the teacher replied, "It is that which he who is in need commanded to be made." By Muhammad’s definition, a dog is a spirit, or a stone is a spirit, since all things are from the command of the Creator. How much better he would have distinguished it! Firstly, the Spirit of God is His efficacy in lower things, in which all things are preserved and consist; while the spirit of nature is that by which all things are vegetated by the command of the Creator. For if it were worth the effort to say anything regarding this definition of the prophet, I would say he binds God to matter, and creates himself daily. This is not the only such instance; all his sayings are similar, wherefore I truly think Muhammad is refuted by no one better than himself.

He even makes angels corporeal, and subject to wounds and death, when he says: "They said, 'God has sent a human apostle.' Say: 'If angels remained safe on earth, we would also have sent angel apostles from heaven.'" <note>A paraphrase of Surah Al-Isra 17:94-95.</note> O, what distinguished judgment of the man! He thinks substances devoid of a body (except insofar as they take on a deceptive airy body) are subject to the injuries of men. O, what a "good" legislator, and one well-skilled in nature (with which he was supposedly familiar)—a total rustic, who believes spirits are violable; or if he does not believe it, he writes falsely. When the tributes given to him did not seem large enough, and the Jews excused themselves on account of poverty, he said: "If you possessed the treasures of my Lord’s mercy, even then you would withhold them for fear of expenses, because man is greedy." <note>Reference to Surah Al-Isra 17:100.</note> Furthermore, regarding what he says about God giving Moses nine miracles: He actually exhibited ten before Pharaoh, and innumerable others.

->## GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II.<-

...the divinity of Jesus is evident, so that he may prove the resurrection of the dead. I expound this story to them:

When the Emperor Decius <note>Decius (reigned 249–251 AD) was a Roman Emperor known for initiating one of the first empire-wide persecutions of Christians.</note> was instigating a persecution against the Christians, there were in Ephesus seven young men, the sons of the wealthiest and most prominent citizens, who, along with many others, had devoted themselves to the name of Christ. And so, when Decius wished to be present at the punishments—acting like a torturer thirsting for the human and innocent blood of his subjects—he consumed many by martyrdom. However, for these young men, on account of the nobility of their parents (as he said) and their youth, he allowed several months for them to shrink back from Christ and perform sacrifices to the idols. He warned the parents not to doubt that if they persisted, they would perish by unheard-of tortures as soon as he returned.

When the impious Emperor departed, the young men began to deliberate together on how they might deliver themselves from the tyrant’s power. Therefore, having taken some money from their parents, while they deliberated and consulted about either flight or voluntary exile, they agreed to hide in a certain cave very near to Ephesus, on a spur of Mount Mycale, <note>Mount Mycale is a mountain on the west coast of central Anatolia in modern-day Turkey.</note> for as long as it took for the fury of that wicked prince to cease. Thus, for many months, they sang praises to God. One of them, however, at appointed hours and by turns, sought from the city the necessities with which they might sustain their lives.

When the Emperor returned, he sought the young men for punishment of mind or body; he ordered their parents to be seized in their name and threatened them with immediate tortures unless they produced their children—for his mind was greedy for blood. The place of their entrance was betrayed, but they did not come out. See what insanity and the agitation of a demon can do in a man: he ordered them to be enclosed alive within the cave, and his commands were immediately obeyed.

However, a certain Theodore, a pious man who had concealed his true belief, inscribed the acts and deeds and the names of their parents, along with the date and the name of the persecutor, upon lead plates. He placed these within the structure by which the cave was being closed in such a way that no one would notice; yet, if it were ever torn down, it would be revealed. Thus, for a total of 181 years, they remained enclosed in the cave until the time of Theodosius. <note>Postel refers to Theodosius II, who reigned from 402 to 450 AD. The story of the Seven Sleepers is traditionally set during his reign.</note>

By chance, it happened that a certain citizen wished to construct a building in a nearby location. While he was debating how to transport the material more conveniently, the workmen said that not far away there was a certain mass like a wall, and that stone could be taken from there. He heard them, tore it down, and hauled the stone away. He saw the cave but sought nothing else. Once the air was let in, the seven young men—as if awakened from sleep and hungry—sent their companion for his usual duties. He went out, suspecting nothing of the situation, and approached Ephesus. Immediately, the new face of all things terrified the youth; he hesitated, wondering whether he was dreaming or awake. Ignoring everything else, one thing especially stunned him: he saw the sign of the cross, which the impious Emperor had persecuted only yesterday (as he thought), placed above the city gates. Approaching each gate, he found the same thing. He asked with great fear whether this city was Ephesus; they said it was.

Meanwhile, as if he were beside himself, he went to the market to purchase bread and other provisions for the others and himself. No one recognized the coinage he offered; indeed, they said they would turn him in unless he gave them a share of the treasure he had found. He denied having found anything and, leaving the money, wished to flee lest he be betrayed. He was captured and brought before the magistrate. He was asked whose son he was; he replied that he was a citizen, the son of such-and-such a citizen. He brought no less wonder to everyone than he felt himself; seeing all the citizens, he recognized none. He referred everything back to "yesterday"—even the Emperor, who it was established had died 180 years before.

He said he had six companions in the cave and had come to buy food for them. Once the sacred magistrate was involved, the miracle was recognized. The Bishop, approaching the place with almost the entire city, found everything consistent with what the young man said, except for the timing. Entering the threshold of the cave and using a light, he saw the lead tablet left by Theodore, which provided proof of the blockage and the time passed. A whole circle of citizens was gathered; whoever wished spoke to the young men, and there was a great and palpable proof of the resurrection. Immediately, the Bishop and the magistrate wrote to Theodosius, who was staying in Constantinople, and summoned him to the sight of this miracle. He came and saw with...

These are the main points of the story, which Muhammad does not treat with the purity of the sacred scriptures, for he everywhere adds something of his own: as here, he introduces a dog with them <note>The dog is known as Qitmir in Islamic tradition.</note>, so that we might believe in the resurrection of dogs along with him. For he places the bodies of certain animals in heaven along with his *Alborach* <term>Al-Buraq, the winged steed that carried Muhammad during the Night Journey</term>, and those miserable people believe that God will gather the spirits of all animals together with the spirits of men at the resurrection. No more impious blasphemy than this can be given. Furthermore, those youths suffered these things for the sake of Jesus Christ the crucified, and they did not set up any partner with God, since he himself is that one same God, both Father and Spirit, as I have often taught. I do not wish to say anything of the paradise of Eden, except that in addition to the things mentioned above, there will be golden bracelets, and green garments of silk and fine linen, and they will recline upon cushions in a good mansion, and so forth; so that in Muhammad’s view, the life of the soul and the body is the same. Moreover, since he proposes a parable of the rich and the poor man and says that the poor man without wealth enters paradise more easily than the rich man, how is it that he himself wished to plunder everyone and amass such great power? He did that, in my judgment, out of charity: so that once he had stripped them all bare, they might seek paradise more unencumbered, while he himself took on the burden of everyone’s obstacles. I will not speak of God, Adam, and the devil. For I have already shown many times that he makes God the author of idolatry. Who could recount how many fables he attaches to Moses, concerning the boy and the fish? <note>This refers to the story of Moses and Khidr in Surah 18.</note> These are entirely foreign to the sacred scriptures, but they will be refuted by their own nature. Those fables and parables which he weaves into the history of Moses are allegorical, and are not sufficiently known to me. But they seem to deal with an orphan whom he despoiled of his paternal estate and home in *Iezraba* <note>Likely referring to Yathrib (Medina).</note>; no deed is more foul than this.

### Miriam, that is Mary, [Chapter] 18. <note>Postel refers to the section of the Quran covering Mary, primarily found in Surah 19, though he labels it 18.</note>

In the first place, he set down a lie concerning Zechariah, claiming he was mute for only three days as a sign, when in fact he did not speak for nine whole months; and when the boy was born, he even wrote his name while he was still not speaking. His claim that John [the Baptist] had a book (that is, the Law) is false, for he was the herald of Christ. Concerning Mary, he trifles in this way:

# WILLIAM POSTEL, BOOK II.
