### ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

Therefore, Muhammad, who wavers concerning this, is no prophet. But he was hard-pressed by the deserting multitude and did not know where to turn. Some objected: "The law of Moses is better"; others: "Yours is a fiction"; others: "These are the writings of the ancients"; others: "He is delirious and insane." Surely these things would never have been thrown in his face so frequently if there had been no cause for it. For it cannot be that what everyone frequently objects to is not true, or at least plausible. Such things were never objected to any of the [true] prophets, because there was not even a suspicion of such things in them. To Jesus Christ—the God-man—the leaders of the Jews objected three or four times while he was casting out demons that he was an enchanter; but that proceeded from a matter being misinterpreted. Therefore, Muhammad frequently used this injury as a pretext for himself, as if he shared a common cause with Christ. For he would have wished to be considered and to be an enchanter <note>Postel suggests Muhammad tried to equate the accusations of madness against him with the accusations of sorcery against Jesus to gain legitimacy.</note>. But those things have already been noted by me above. It remains to speak of the demon listeners. Since Muhammad could hardly gain faith for his trifles among men, he borrows it from demons, so that he might force it upon men from there. And he says:

> And when we directed toward you a multitude of demons <note>The Quranic text (Surah 46:29) refers to 'Jinn', but Postel uses the Latin *dæmones* to imply evil spirits.</note>, so that they might hear the Quran, and when they attended it, they said: "Be silent"; and when it was completed, they returned to their people as heralds <note>Original: *evangelizantes*—literally "evangelizing" or "bearing good news." Postel likely uses this word to mock the idea of demons acting as missionaries.</note>, and they said: "O our people, we have heard a book sent down after Moses, confirming what came before it, guiding to the truth and to the right path. O our people, respond to the caller of the Lord and believe in him; he will forgive you your sins and save you from a grievous punishment."

This is the true confirmation of this law, which no man could prove, but the devil could confirm. A vote <note>Original: *suffragium*.</note> worthy of the work and the author. The demon, that nefarious plague of mankind, adds his vote <note>Original: *calculum addit*—literally "adds his pebble," referring to the ancient practice of using white or black stones to vote in a trial or assembly.</note> to the law for the destruction of nature and the contempt and disgrace of the written God. No one—not even a philosopher—will deny that all works of a demon are evil and sinful. But since the demons heard the Quran, preached it to their people, and believed in it, becoming Muslims <note>Original: *Mussulmani*.</note>, whoever does the same must be a companion of demons. Truly, the spirit compelled Muhammad to babble these things prophetically in this place to suggest that whoever should join this persuasion should also be joined to the company of demons in eternal punishment. O Muslims, at least from this place recognize the author of your law, and unless you perish willingly, return to your senses. I will not speak of how wicked it is to believe there is a "people" of demons, and that they perform preaching for each other and repent—since those substances <note>In 16th-century theology, "substances" refers to the essential nature of spiritual beings like angels or demons.</note> are so confirmed in evil that by no art are they able to repent. But I understand. God wished to be just and the punisher of crimes, and to use the works of evil demons for the punishment of the impious; but Muhammad brought salvation to the demons and freed them from the underworld and gloomy places, and took away the place of divine justice. For this follows: if indeed they can be saved from the same kind, then all can; if all, the wicked will not suffer punishment; if the wicked do not suffer punishment, there is no God. For he who acts unjustly acts as nothing <note>Postel argues that a God without justice is no God at all.</note>. This is the inference from the opinion of Muhammad, the redeemer of demons. Truly, while you were babbling these things, a demon presided over you, so that while you persuade the unlearned that he [the demon] can be good, they do not guard against his tricks and fraud, which he truly cannot [be good]. For with the sign and the author of the cross removed, the devil takes possession of all things, as is clear enough from the previous book where we dealt with separate substances and their kinds. It has already become very clear that the man raged violently in two places—although in the whole book nothing else is urged but the shedding of blood—especially after the Jews had defected from him, and after the women returning to their parents' homes had revealed his fables and impostures. ### WILLIAM POSTEL, BOOK II

bearing the name of <term>slaughter</term> <note>original: "elcatal"; referring to *Al-Qital* (The Fighting), an alternative name for Surah 47 of the Quran</note>, he commands the sword to be drawn against the faces of all, and that they be forced to the faith by death or captivity. The Africans and Arabs call this chapter *elcatal*, that is, "the slaughter"; others call it "Muhammad," so that those terms—slaughter, plague, destruction, and Muhammad—are clearly synonymous. Hear the edict:

> And when you encounter those who resist your law, strike off their necks until you have overcome them, then bind them tightly with chains, so that they may afterwards ransom themselves from us, until the war or its campaign is finished. And if God willed, He would take vengeance upon them Himself, but He wishes to test you by one another. And those who are killed in the way of God, their works are not in vain, for they shall be guided and shall prosper with God, and shall enter the paradise destined for them. O you who believe, if you defend God, He will defend you and confirm your steps, etc.

God is the author of slaughter, who took up the protection of nature. Indeed, He permits and sometimes commands the sword to be drawn against the wicked; but against those who live peacefully, who possess the laws of God, who observe them, and who have done no harm, violence ought by no means to rage. Now, however, we have seen frequently in this book that the law of the pagans is good, if one does good, and likewise the law of Moses and of Christ; therefore, none of them ought justly to be killed. But it is no wonder that the God of Muhammad, the author of evil, even for the ruin of nature, has sent a fire into the midst of the world and commanded that war be brought upon innocent peoples for the reason that they refuse to believe that which even delirious old women could hardly give assent to. Truly, that this same God promises paradises and prosperity to unspeakable murderers—what wonder is it? Since his paradise is most similar to that God: certainly entirely foreign to the God of nature.

> In the paradises, he says, they shall dwell, beneath which flow rivers of clearest water, rivers of milk whose taste shall never change, and rivers of most sweet wine for those who drink, and rivers of purified honey, and they have in them every kind of fruit, and mercy from the Lord.

Now, if there be added to these the cushions upon which they may recline, and the grey-eyed women, and the young boys serving with golden cups, and silken garments, necklaces, and whatever else is written in other places, who could wish for a greater happiness for <term>Sardanapalus</term> <note>An ancient Assyrian king legendary for his extreme decadence and self-indulgence.</note> or <term>Heliogabalus</term> <note>A Roman emperor infamous for his luxury and eccentric religious practices.</note>? All these things are most similar to one another: the God, the creature, the prophet, the soldier, the paradise, hell, and finally the law itself is everywhere most similar to itself. But since there are two powers in nature—one commanding, powerful in producing and preserving all good things, yet winking at evils as long as there is no place for repentance; the other, which tends toward and aspires to the ruin and hatred of nature—it is easy to judge from which one this law proceeded. We can conjecture from this passage that even those who had believed him from the beginning had fallen away, based on these words:

> And those who believe say, "Why has a prophecy never been sent to him?" And when a decisive prophecy is sent, in which there is mention of slaughter, you see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the look of one fearing death; and it would be better for them to acquiesce and say, "It is well." And when the precept is urgent, if they believed God, it would be better for them, and so forth.

As he held God to be favorable, whom he might appoint as the servant and approver of his desires according to his whim, because even in good and necessary things, God, the pitier of human nature, is not accustomed to act at first glance unless greatly moved by prayers. Thus, that God, the prince of darkness and author of human destruction, reveals himself by many conjectures, covering pestiferous and ruined things with the color and gloss of good things; lest, while he employs his machinations openly without disguise, he should immediately betray himself and perish like a mouse by his own evidence. He could not persuade against nature that it is just to kill brothers, to finish off parents, to remove friends, to fly into the fortunes of all, to oppress the poor, to exalt tyrants, to make a way for wickedness with the sword: but under the guise of religion...

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

And under the pretext of the divine name, the most foul deeds have become the most holy. The devil was unable to resist the power of Christ, but under the pretext of preserving divine honor, while he pretends to give many great things to Him, he takes everything away. For there was, is, and will be one and the same honor of God and of Christ, which nevertheless cannot now truly be known or referred to God except through Christ, the Son of God. Thus he denies not only Christ himself, but also the Father: which I have shown before with many arguments. This is the cunning of Satan. Under the pretext of religion, Muhammad and his followers are now permitted to arm themselves for the destruction of nature; and while he promises the correction of all religions, he utterly subverts them all, so far as he is able. For he who confuses the false with the true, and calls the whole mixture true, sins more gravely than he who asserts, holds, and approves what is false as true. For the latter does not deceive and harms only himself, unless perhaps he also sins by example; but he who persuades through the pretext of truth draws both himself and others headlong into ruin. Whence, although this law seems to confess one God, it is nevertheless worse than the laws of all idolaters, because they undermine nothing but themselves. This law makes God the author and approver of all crimes that can fall within human sense and action. But these "good and murderous" prophecies armed the soldiers against Muhammad’s fellow citizens, and he wished to put to the test those who were willing to fall into danger in the name of the law. Therefore, the following chapter, or prophecy, is called **phatha**, that is, the **gate** <note>original: "phatha"; referring to *Al-Fath* (The Victory), Surah 48 of the Quran. Postel translates it as "gate" or "opening"</note>, because one may enter into persuasion through war. Indeed, in it he mentions the deeds committed by him in the valley of Mecca, where he put the citizens to flight:

> And He it is who withheld your hands from them and their hands from you in the valley of Mecca, after He gave you victory over them, and God sees what you do. They are those who are <term>Chaphiri</term> <note>original: "Chaphiri"; from the Arabic *Kuffar*, meaning disbelievers or infidels</note> and have opposed you in the forbidden temple. The victim is bound, so that its slaughter may be completed, and were it not for the faithful men, etc.

Because of the victory already won before, he encourages his followers to kill their fellow citizens, parents, kinsmen, and friends in the manner of a bound sacrificial victim. And a little later: *The testimony of Muhammad is enough, and those who are with him are stronger than their adversaries.* While other laws may be good, yet it is enough to be a testimony that Muhammad is stronger. What else can a robber say? It is enough for any destroyer of the world if he and his followers are stronger. For this is his "right." No one is unaware that almost all empires are either occupied or increased by tyranny; but no one before him dared to use the authority of Providence as a pretext for crime. Those who crept into the name of divinity achieved it by grace of some miracle cleverly devised by their parents or acquired by their works; legislators prefixed the name of divinity to their laws without any blood; the glory of their parents elevated others; Muhammad alone dared to ascribe the ruin of the world to God as its author.

### 51. Eltur.
<note>Referring to Surah 52, *At-Tur* (The Mount)</note>

He ascribes the authority of his law to Mount Sinai and to shaved parchment—that is, he says it is the law of Moses and Abraham. The interpreters say that the Quran was actually written on the skin of the ram which Abraham sacrificed, and therefore it is the law of Abraham. I say nothing of the paradises described in this prophecy, since they are similar everywhere. Here there are meats of all kinds, wines that do not intoxicate, boys dressed in <term>multicolored garments</term> <note>original: "polymitis"; referring to ornate, woven, or damasked fabrics</note> serving them, and many things indeed contributing to satiety. This troubles me: where such an abundance of food is to be excreted, I do not read. For that part seems quite necessary in that paradise. Many other things also seem to be lacking there.

### 52.
He swears by the "head of the stars" <note>Referring to Surah 53, *An-Najm* (The Star)</note> concerning the miracle of **Alborach** <note>original: "Alborach"; Al-Buraq, the winged creature that carried Muhammad during the Night Journey</note>, that he ascended to heaven and contemplated God, distanced from Him by two bow-shots, and saw things to be revealed, etc. All miracles are of this kind, such that they have no witness besides himself.

I have already shown how fittingly he perceived the divinity during that ascent into heaven <note>This refers to the *Mi'raj*, Muhammad’s miraculous night journey to the heavens</note>. God is considered finite according to Muhammad—which is to say, He is nothing—since one reaches Him at a certain fixed distance. For whatever has a beginning also has an end. I pass over the stars which he swears are here, fixed with golden chains so that they might drive away the demons approaching paradise. I will not speak of the brute animals inhabiting heaven; there is nothing surprising in this, since they are to be resurrected. I say nothing of the angel whose head is a hundred thousand times larger than the world, by which he surpasses his "finite" God. Meanwhile, he seems to mock the divinity with three goddesses. These are Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat <note>original: "alleta, alhozaí, elmenauta"</note>, whom interpreters call Diana, Venus, and Minerva. Al-Lat and Al-Uzza were worshiped by the people of Mecca and by Muhammad himself before he became a "Messiah" through the Jewish faction. When they turn a man away from such worship, they draw him into destruction and into the ruin of himself and others.

In Chapter 53 <note>Postel refers to Surah 53, *An-Najm* (The Star), though the moon-splitting story is usually associated with Surah 54</note>, the moon was split while Bugellinus was present and requesting it, as I have taught before. Since no one else asserts this, I do not believe it either. For the moon, serving the entire world, does not enter the sleeves of prophets. The following chapter imitates the 135th Psalm of David <note>In the Vulgate numbering; this is Psalm 136 in modern Bibles, famous for the repeated refrain "For His mercy endures forever"</note>, because it interposes a certain repetition among various sentences in the manner of a true prophet, so that it might seem related to him. In it are the women of paradise <note>The *Huris*</note>, whom they enjoy without defiling them, and men and demons created from a flame of fire. There are also pomegranates and fruits in that paradise, and many other things. The same paradise, with a similar hell, is depicted in the following Chapter 55.

At the end of *Al-Hadid* <term>Surah 57, "The Iron"</term>, Chapter 56, he even gives testimony to Christ, saying that His followers are pious, merciful, and religious. Therefore, I wonder why he wished to introduce a law different from the Gospel, or why the Muslims <note>original: "Mussulmani"</note> do not now rise up against him, since their own prophet confesses the Gospel is good.

One thing remains for us to note out of many lies, when in Surah 60 <note>This likely refers to Surah 61, *As-Saff*, verse 6</note> he ascribes these words to Christ:

> And when Jesus the son of Mary said: "O children of Israel, I am sent to you by God to confirm what you have in your hands of the Law, and I announce to you a prophet after me whose name is Ahmad." And when he came to them with miracles, they said, "This is manifest sorcery." And who is more unjust than he who forges a lie against God?

I would like to ask the Muslims to show where in the Gospel it is written that Ahmad (Muhammad) was to come after Christ. There exist copies of the Gospel in the Indian language, in Armenian, in the Jacobite tongue, in two Chaldean dialects, and they have even been translated into Hebrew by the hostile Jews. The Greeks, Georgians, Serbians, Dalmatians, and Latins all have the Gospels in their own characters and languages. I pass over the innumerable vulgar tongues in which the same books are available. These nations are widely separated from one another. Let them also consult the Nestorians, Armenians, and Jacobites: if they find it, we shall admit defeat <note>original: "porrigimus herbam," a Latin idiom meaning to yield or concede victory</note>. How could it be that this was in the Gospel, and yet no one anywhere possessed it? It is an impudent lie, Muhammad, used so that you might retain your soldiers and make them obedient to you. Christ did not give his vote to a lie. When he spoke of you, he designated you as the Antichrist, not a prophet—unless you mean a "prophet" in the sense of a false prophet. He promised that after him he would send the <term>Paraclete</term> <note>From the Greek *parakletos*, meaning Advocate or Comforter; in Christian theology, this is the Holy Spirit</note> to the disciples, which he manifested ten days later. After the greatest of prophets, after the Son of God—conceived of a virgin by the Holy Spirit, speaking in his cradle and swaddling clothes, exhibiting every kind of miracle, taken up to God in body and soul into heaven, and destined to be the judge of the living and the dead—no one greater could be promised or could come, except a fake and an impostor. For you would strive in vain to restrain with a stake or fences that animal which the fortress’s guard-post does not hold back. If something is not confined by the greatest forces, you labor in vain to restrain it with a weaker power. They could not [bring] better [things]...

...that better things could be given than those which were given by Christ, so supreme a prophet. If they will not observe the most excellent laws, how can it be possible to keep them in their duty with lesser ones? Ahmad <note>Ahmad is another name for Muhammad used in the Quran (Surah 61:6)</note> was set to "correct" the Gospel by permitting promiscuity instead of a lawful marriage bed, countless wives instead of one, and even allowing sodomy and bestiality <note>Postel is using extreme polemical language here to characterize Islamic law as libertine compared to Christian asceticism</note> instead of natural use. He preferred vengeance over patience, war over peace, and theft, robbery, and slaughter over justice. He preferred the deaths of citizens, brothers, parents, relatives, and friends over the preservation of life; he placed theft and plunder above the charity that gives all. This is how he "corrected" the Gospel. I know that he was satisfying certain Jews who had already been drawn to him by force; when they sought testimony about him from the ancients, he could not produce it from the Old Testament, and far less from the New. But because he knew the Jews were ignorant of the Gospel, he told them that it was written in the New Testament about him. This is the reason for his statement, which is clear from both the beginning and the end of the chapter <note>Postel is likely referencing Surah 61, "As-Saff" (The Ranks)</note>. At the beginning he says: 

<margin>>> </margin> "God loves those who kill in the way of God and oppose the enemy like a wall," and toward the end: "O you who have believed, does it not please you that I should free you from a great punishment? Believe in God and His prophet." 

He wants (as I noted before) for faith to be placed in him just as in God. 

<margin>>> </margin> "And strive in the way of God with your wealth and your bodies. This is beneficial for you, if you understand. He will have mercy on your sins and introduce you into paradises beneath which rivers flow, and into good dwellings in the paradises of Eden. This is the great refuge." 

And a little later: 

<margin>>> </margin> "O you who have believed, be the Christians of God <note>Postel translates the Arabic term "Ansar" (helpers) as "Christiani" to suggest Muhammad was co-opting the identity of Christ's followers</note>, as Christ the son of Mary said to his disciples: 'Who wants to become a Christian in God?' The pure apostles said: 'We are the Christians of God.' And some of the children of Israel believed, and some blasphemed." 

With these words, he tries to ensnare both our people and the Jews, since he was dealing with the people of Mecca, who were more powerful.

61. He acts against those who preferred to remain Jews rather than imitate the prophet.

64. Regarding divorce, he contradicts himself. For previously, four witnesses were needed to prove a woman unworthy of marriage so that she might be repudiated; here he employs only two, so consistent is he with himself. After three months, whoever wishes may marry them again or repudiate them entirely. Thus, nothing is more unhappy than to live under a law in which there is nothing certain or constant.

However, we must see how he grants himself a release from a bound oath. In the next chapter, he writes as follows:

<margin>>> </margin> "O Prophet, do not make a religious matter of the perjury that God has forgiven you; you seek favor from your wives, and God is merciful and pious. God has already absolved you from the violation of faith, and God is your prudent and wise patron. And when the prophet communicated a certain secret of his to one of his wives and she revealed it, God manifested it to him; and it was acknowledged by some, but denied by others. And when he revealed it to her (the woman), she said: 'Who revealed this to you?' He said: 'The wise Knower revealed it to me.' If you both turn to God, He will cleanse both of your hearts. And if you conspire against him, God is his patron, and Gabriel and the good believers, and the angels hereafter will be his avengers. Perhaps his God, if he repudiates you, will give him in your place wives better than you: faithful Muslim women, diligent, industrious, religious, etc." 

These things tend toward the satisfaction of Hassa and Hafeza <note>Refers to Muhammad’s wives, Hafsa and likely Aisha</note>, who had returned to him led by the persuasion of their parents; thus they were throwing those perjuries and adulteries in his face. They said that if he attempted anything further against them, they would destroy the man by conspiracy. He terrifies them with a divine decree and takes care to satisfy them. Clearly, from this chapter, the imposture and the fable become manifest. For what he had revealed to his wives, they in turn revealed to the following crowd: namely, that it was a fiction and "scriptures of the ancients," and that nothing had been revealed to him. Yet he says he immediately learned from God what his wife had betrayed.

But the example was of no use to her, for as long as she lived, she was a public harlot: upon whom, as I have said, the faith and interpretation of the Quran and the Sunnah <note><term>Sunnah</term>: The body of traditional social and legal custom and practice of the Islamic community.</note> depend.

In chapter 66 <note>Surah At-Tahrim</note>, he seems to speak of Abdullah ibn Salam <note>Original: "Abdalla ben salone". A Jewish rabbi who converted to Islam.</note>, a very wealthy Jew, who was his secretary for seven years. For I know that the prophet never had a secret that he did not fear would be found out. He who fears is necessarily conscious of guilt. If Muhammad had not been an impostor, what need was there to complain about a revealed secret, and to say to the women, "It does not concern you to speak of that matter"? A divine prophet never said or did anything that he feared everyone would know. Fear is the argument of a man with a guilty conscience.

In the 70th chapter <note>Postel likely means Surah 72, "Al-Jinn".</note>, the Muslims become a great crowd of demons, so that they might praise the Quran and utter blasphemies against God and Christ. It is well known that evil men silently make a pact with a demon; otherwise, I do not remember ever reading or understanding it. Where he thinks that neither demons nor men speak or fashion a lie about God, I wonder what came into his mind to judge so, since the devil, the father of lies, fashions nothing else but a lie against God while he persuades men toward false opinions of Him. But I understand: because of his constant familiarity with Muhammad, the demon had made a pact so that this prophet would preach that the demon was good, and retract those things which he said about him before. And having entered into that pact, he even wished to commend it to posterity so it would not be unknown, for he says:
> Indeed, certain men from among the humans entered into a covenant with
> certain men from among the demons, and they increased their fear.

There are men and women among the demons; otherwise, this lawgiver would have said "men from among the demons" in vain. For whenever he speaks thus, he understands a part of the species and an individual of the same kind. But those covenants were entered into when he ascended to heaven with Elborac <note><term>Elborac</term>: Al-Buraq, the celestial steed that carried Muhammad during the Night Journey (Isra and Mi'raj).</note>. Then he saw that there were I-know-not-how-many guards in heaven, and 18 in hell. He waited at the doors of heaven and listened to the secrets of heaven with those who listen, and the other miracles which he mentions in this chapter. He wishes to repeat those things in that chapter. There are six hundred similar things: but those things will be examined in the Arabic version rather than in this one. For I have enough, from certain principal places, to have revealed this plague to our people, so that our sleepy monks may at least be moved by these follies to pity the wretched nation, and if they do not busy themselves to heal its blindness for the love of Jesus Christ, they may at least feel compassion. I add only a few places. For although the Lord Jesus Christ will reveal himself to the whole world at his formidable second coming, it is certain that he will first appear in a specific place in the hemisphere, since he is corporeal <note>Meaning he possesses a physical body.</note>. For even though he will then sit in the air, he will nevertheless move with a successive motion. Nor will the entire world be forced into that narrow place near Jerusalem, but rather wherever the Redeemer and Judge wishes; for wherever he judges, there will be the **Judgment of the Lord** <note>original Hebrew: משפט יהוה (Mishpat Yehovah)</note>, that is, "The Judgment of God" or "God judges." Indeed, even the book of the **Sunnah** <note>Original: "Suneh." The Sunnah refers to the body of traditional social and legal custom and practice of the Islamic community, often viewed as second only to the Quran.</note>—which in many matters carries greater authority than the **Quran**—concedes that Jesus Christ is the one who will raise the dead and judge the world. In that place where it explains the passage of the Quran where God snatched Christ to himself so that he would not be crucified, the Sunnah says: *And Jesus, the son of Mary, will descend from heaven to the earth, and he will judge upon it with a just judgment.* <note>Original Arabic transliteration: "Veionzilu... Iisa bin meriame ila elardhi ueiahcumu phihæ hachiman hadilan."</note> Since they confess this, and since judging the earth is a property belonging only to God, it is a wonder that they are so mentally captive that they do not also confess him to be God, whom they acknowledge as the future judge. Thus has Satan played with their minds. I proceed to the end.

91. Concerning himself, he confesses—contrary to the craftiness and deceits of the **Caliphs** <note>Original: "Chalephorum." The successors of Muhammad.</note> who invented fables about his lineage to keep the foolish multitude in check—for he says regarding his original condition:
> Did God not find you an orphan and cherish you? Did he not find you wandering and guide you? Did he not find you poor and enrich you? Therefore, do not oppress the orphan, etc. <note>A translation of Surah 93:6-8 from the Quran.</note>
These things fight against the light of prophecy, against a faithful lineage, against the miracles of his infancy, against the birds, winds, and angels, against his circumcision in the womb, and against the idea of him being the most perfect of creatures. For being poor is at odds with having royal blood. Poverty does not suit a kingdom, nor does piety suit error. He was "guided" only when he was made crafty, when he learned how to deceive, and when he was instructed by the Jews so that he might acquire a tyranny for them. It does not seem that he had much regard for his own "orphan" status, seeing as he made countless others orphans, plundered them, and killed them. For what else he did during his whole life—at least from the time his fable was published—I do not see. I leave it to others to judge.

The following chapter reveals the miracle of the disemboweled prophet <note>A reference to the "Purification of the Prophet's Heart," a story where angels were said to have opened Muhammad's chest to wash his heart.</note>.
> Did I not split open and disembowel your chest, and take away from you your sin, which was breaking your back? etc. <note>A translation of Surah 94:1-3.</note>
This is attributed to his nurse, **Halima**. I have already related these things above. He mentions aromatic winds, clouds, and seventy-six angels, which all came from the same workshop. Elsewhere he swears by "scatological trees" <note>Postel uses the term "cacatorias," likely a derogatory or misunderstood reference to trees in the Quranic afterlife.</note>; in the following chapter, he swears by the cloud walking with a man. 95. The "Powerful Night" <note>A reference to Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Power (Surah 97).</note>: all of which denote those miracles I have frequently mentioned. These "linear" prophecies were added many centuries later, recovered from the recitation of Halima, or on the faith of a harlot, or by men who wrote them down, or as they were found in holes in walls. Nevertheless, they are all very similar to one another.

But the final part clearly betrays the author and the handle of this entire business. For he says:
> Say: I defend myself with the Lord of men, the King of men, from the evil of the *vesuas*—that is, the hidden disturber of the mind—who disturbs the hearts of men, from demons and from men. <note>A translation of Surah 114, the final chapter of the Quran. Postel transliterates "waswas" (whisperer) as "vesuas."</note>
In this chapter, he hints at what he could not deny to his wife **Khadija** <note>Original: "Hadegæ."</note>. For when he had attributed his "falling sickness" <note>Postel, like many Renaissance polemicists, characterized Muhammad’s revelations as epileptic seizures or "falling sickness."</note> to an uncertain cause—to wine, to an angel, to God, or to fasting—and that untimely disturbance nevertheless remained, he was forced to confess that there was in his soul a *vesuas elhannas* <note>Original Arabic: "al-waswas al-khannas."</note>, a "hidden disturber," that is, the devil, from whom he defends himself with God. In the previous chapter, he calls him a sorcerer and a wrapper, which tends toward the same meaning. There, indeed, he even makes God the author of evil, since he wishes to be delivered from the evil that God created; which [is inconsistent] with piety...

# GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK II.

...and fights against the reasoning of philosophy.
   Here you have, out of countless similar examples, some chapters of the law of the God of Muhammad: see, weigh, and judge. If these please you, more will come forward. Although these things are clear enough and depict the man in some way, yet when each is gathered into classes and confined as if by barriers and boundaries, they will seem to receive greater light. First, therefore, we will note a few from the many ways in which he sinned against God, the angels, demons, heaven, nature, right reason, and public peace.

### ->ON GOD AND THE FINAL END<-
#### ->*Errors.* CHAPTER XIV.<-

Now, if I wished to touch upon the nonsense of the **Sunnah** <note>Original: *Suneh*. The body of traditional social and legal custom and practice in Islam.</note> and the **Hafsiar** <note>Original: *Hafsiar*. Likely referring to the *Tafsir*, or Quranic commentaries.</note>, the work would grow tenfold. It will be enough, therefore, to reveal in a few words what both the prophet himself and the authors explaining his dogmas feel about the first and ultimate cause—which is God and Paradise. We cannot better inquire into the quality of Muhammad’s God than from the moment he visibly showed himself to him in the highest heaven. We have already seen the memory of the night, and the "two bow-shots" <note>A reference to the *Mi'raj* (Night Journey), where Muhammad is said to have come within two bow-lengths of the Divine Presence.</note> by which he was distant from God. The interpreters say that when he was in the seventh heaven, after he had commended himself to Christ, Gabriel did not dare to proceed further, leaving him to complete the journey. Then, through swirling places, waters, and countless snows, he traveled so far that he was entirely exhausted by the way, and he stopped until he heard a certain voice saying to him: "Muhammad, approach and greet your Creator." But as he approached the voice, he saw such a great light that it broke the edge of his vision; nevertheless, he came near to God at a distance of two bow-shots. God himself, having seventy thousand veils of light before his face, did not offer a view of his face to Muhammad, but touching his shadow with his hand, he affected him with such cold that he could scarcely stand; and he told him many secrets, which are truly so numerous in their writers that two hundred pack-mules could not carry a single copy of each book. 

But meanwhile, before we depart from that truly cold God, it is necessary to know the distance from the earth to heaven, so that we may strive toward it. Listen, reader, to the oracles and the prophetic manner of citation. **Abdullah Muhammad al-Qurtubi** <note>Original: *Hebdullahius Muhamedes Cartibius*. A famous 13th-century Andalusian jurist and scholar.</note> in the **Tadhkirat al-A’imma** <note>Original: *Tezchere elimam*, meaning "Memorial of the Imams," described by Postel as a compendium of faith.</note>, writes thus:
   Aben Waheb reports, and Akhberbi Rachman son of Ziad, son of Anham, says that he heard Hatebetum son of Abdulzabi (on whom may God have mercy), who reported concerning this fact of the levels, that **Zagel** <note>Likely a reference to a celestial messenger or a specific interpretation of Gabriel in the Hadith literature.</note> came to the prophet (may the prayer of God and peace be upon him) and said: "O prophet of God, how many levels are there from here to paradise?" He said: "One hundred levels, between any two of which the distance is as great as from the earth to the heaven. The first of those levels—its space, its construction, its gate or entrance, its base, and its height—is made of silver. The space, building, entrance, base, and height of the second is of gold. The parts of the third are of hyacinth, carbuncle, and pearls, and after that, up to ninety-seven levels, no one knows what it is except God alone." But **at-Tirmidhi** <note>Original: *Thermindus*. A famous 9th-century collector of Hadith.</note>, etc. This is "sensible" theology <note>Meaning a theology based on physical senses and material objects rather than abstract spiritual truths.</note>, which needs no refutation because it does not deserve belief. Among the **Muslims** <note>Original: *Mussulmanos*.</note>, God is devoid of quality, yet infinite, incomprehensible, localized, finite, and susceptible to accidents <note>In Aristotelian philosophy, "accidents" are non-essential properties, such as being in a specific location or feeling cold, which Postel argues are incompatible with a truly infinite God.</note>. I say nothing of the heavens being wrapped one inside the other made of gold and silver—dense bodies; that there are snows and cold above the heaven where there is no matter; that there is the most solid matter there, which by excellence (if you except diamond) could be given the name of "matter." For in all nature, nothing is denser than gold among those things that have become known. But the God of Muhammad delights in the same things as...

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD.

...him and his prophet. Regarding God as the final cause—and the happiness and goal of all things, whether mediated or immediate—we have already seen much. For the Paradise of Muhammad has frequently presented itself to us. Indeed, he does not grasp God in his essence and in contemplation as the source of happiness. He wants to drink, to eat, and everything that follows from those things: otherwise, he thinks it is in vain for there to be a paradise unless it has an abundance of milk, wine, honey, meat, bread, fruit, banquets, luxury, women, **catamites** <note>Original: *catamitos*. Referring to young male servants or companions, a common polemical target for Christian critics of Islamic Paradise descriptions.</note>, garments of gold, silver, and silk, necklaces, cushions, meadows, greenery, and so on—whatever are the instruments of luxury. 

Indeed, he does not only want God to have his due in those paradises, but he says that in the sixth paradise (for there are various kinds according to him) which his followers will possess after death—near the seventh where **Christ** is—there is a fountain called **Al-Kawthar** <note>Original: *Alcausaram*. In Islamic tradition, a river or fountain of abundance in Paradise.</note>. Its diameter is a journey of seventy thousand days; its water is whiter than snow and sweeter than honey, and all who inhabit that paradise shall drink from it. After the Day of Judgment, Muhammad will go to Hell and take the "bad Muslims" who were damned with black and filthy faces, and he will carry them to that fountain and wash them there. They will then become perfectly white and like the others. Thus, God will have no right over the "bad Muslims," nor will Hell serve any purpose. In this way, Muhammad will be far greater than God: because those whom God has damned, he shall absolve. 

But meanwhile, those who are in Paradise will drink the washing of his filth—of his backside, his private parts, and his feet—because that same water will receive the filth and the blessed will drink it. O nonsense! O delusions! O blasphemies! Even in a hundred years, I could not finish transcribing the paradises of Muhammad. Truly, as long as they are in Paradise with God, one must not overlook the tree that is there, equal in size to Paradise itself, with gold and silver leaves upon which are written the name of the prophet and the name of God in these words: **"There is no god but God, and Muhammad is his prophet"** <note>Original: *La alla illa alla Muhamed rassul alla*. This is the *Shahada*, the Islamic profession of faith.</note>. 

From this great tree, the Muhammadan persuasion takes its beginning; for they utter those words with an erect index finger when they give their names to Muhammad. But it is a wonder if this tree is equal to Paradise—where then do the men live? Where is that great fountain? Where are the rivers, the cooks, the ovens, the weavers, the goldsmiths, the cushion-makers, and the other citizens and craftsmen who prepare everything for those who arrive? Perish these wretched fables! We must see if he speaks better of the angels than of God. For in this place, I do not wish to bring up too often in this examination a "God" who is described as impious, unjust, an impostor, and an approver and commander of perjury, adultery, pederasty, brutality, slaughter, homicide, theft, and the like, since these things have become more than well known.

### ON THE NATURE OF ANGELS. CHAPTER XV.

This nature, just like the divine nature, is according to Muhammad corporeal, visible, and tactile—similar to us except for their size and wings. We have seen that the angels are subject to wounds; otherwise, they would come as prophets and messengers in place of men, but they fear being killed. In the third heaven, there was one with **Abraham** of such proportion that the space between his eyes was seventy thousand days' journey in width. Indeed, the more the heavens increase in number, the larger the angels become: so that in the seventh, where **Christ** is, there appear those who have seventy thousand heads, and in each head as many tongues, and from each tongue as many voices speaking praise to God. 

Some look forward perpetually, never sleeping; others are always prostrate, never rising from the earth; others are bowed, others standing, others with a bended knee. Some cry out with such a strained voice that they put their fingers in their ears lest they go deaf. From this are taken the **ceremonies of prayer** <note>Original: *ceremonia herandi*. Postel is linking the physical descriptions of angels to the liturgical postures of Islamic prayer.</note>. For the individual **prayers** <note>Original: *tzalauat*, referring to *Salat*.</note> are performed partly by standing, partly by kneeling, or by prostrating and kissing the ground.

Those ceremonies are called **erchet** <note>Original: *erchet*. Likely a corruption of the Arabic *rak’ah*, the cycle of standing, bowing, and prostrating during Islamic prayer.</note>, that is, a double bowing and prostration. To these two prostrations and the bowings to the right and left correspond individual prayers, such as those we saw at the beginning. Indeed, those angels whose cult is observed here also possess a certain powerlessness, even though the head of one might be seventy thousand times larger than the world. For when the Judgment is complete and it is time to come to the banquet, God will send **Gabriel** to bring the keys of holy Paradise. He will go to another angel who will pull seventy thousand keys out of his mouth, each of which is as long as a journey of seventy thousand days. Since Gabriel will be unable to lift them, he will go to God and say: "I cannot bring the key of Paradise." To him God will say: "Turn yourself around and invoke my name and the name of **Muhammad**, then you will carry it easily." He turns, he invokes, he brings it, it is opened, they enter, and they sit at a table of adamant <note>A legendary stone of indestructible hardness, often associated with diamonds.</note> seventy thousand days in length.

Yet, although the angels are so great and ought to be equal in wisdom, they are the ones who advised God to create a "homicide" <note>Referring to the angelic objection in the Quran (2:30) regarding the creation of man, who would "spread corruption and shed blood."</note>; they are mortal; and some are even damned or afflicted with punishments in this life, such as **Harut and Marut** <note>Original: *Arot & Marot*. Two angels mentioned in Quran 2:102 who were tested at Babylon.</note>. Thus did the lawgiver Muhammad, the "companion of God," explain the blessed spirits and sacrosanct intelligences—he whom the angels cannot act without invoking alongside God. And lest anyone think this is a fiction, these are articles of faith among the Muslims, contained in the books of **Hashiya**, the **Sunnah**, and the **Imams** <note>Original: *Haſſiar, & Suneh, & Imamin*. Postel is citing the vast body of Islamic tradition and commentary beyond the Quran.</note>. It is a marvel that, while in the entire Quran he so often forbids men to make anyone a "partner" with God, his interpreters want him to be acknowledged and invoked as a partner by the angels themselves, even though men, compelled by the necessities of matter, ought to make no partner with God. Liars ought to have good memories and say things consistent with themselves. Otherwise, the deceit would not betray itself.

## ON DEMONS. CHAPTER XVI.

He is not unlike himself when it comes to depicting their foul nature. For he says they were created from fire and flame, and he repeats this ten times; but while he says they were disobedient to God, he makes them out to be wiser than God. Since nothing but the eternal ought to be worshiped by man or angel, God could not help but be the impious author of idolatry by commanding the Devil—created from the highest element—to lower himself so far as to adore man, who was made from a foul and muddy nature. Therefore, the Devil did better by not obeying than God did by commanding; and yet he is damned for that reason. 

But Muhammad does not want to admit that the Devil was damned because he sought the honors of divine power and thought to cast God down from his heaven; for that would make him irreconcilable, and he would not become a listener of the Quran, its preacher, and finally a **Muslim**. For just as he wanted all idolaters, or anyone at all, to be saved through the law of the Quran, so too he wanted to save the demons who had sinned less. But it is a marvel how these things agree with one another: the demons become Muslims and preach to their own people; and yet, when Muhammad was born, the book of history says that the **Great Demon** (namely **Lucifer**) was cast into the sea by the angels, from which he barely emerged after forty days. Ascending **Mount Qubays** <note>Original: *Coba*. A mountain near Mecca.</note> and calling the demons together with a horrendous shout, he said to those asking the cause: "I rouse you with such a horrendous sound because **Muhammad son of Abdullah** is born, whom God has sent with a radiant sword that penetrates all things, unto our ruin." And a little later: "Because of this prophet, God has damned me and made me the accursed Satan." To which his henchmen respond: "Why are you moved, Satan? Do you not know that **Adam** was created with seven virtues, of which only one remains? Do you fear that we, who prevailed against **Christ**, will be unable to resist this prophet?" These things are in the *Hashiya*. When the Devi...

ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

If the devil had been condemned by Muhammad, and even a small infant could put him to flight, how did it happen that Muhammad did not fear him when he was armed and protected by a guard, but instead Muhammad went over to his belief and was saved? How is it that he could make someone forget the prophecies they believed? You see that God is not the author of the devil's condemnation, but Muhammad is; nor was there a devil before Muhammad. Certainly, Satan resisted the Gospel of Christ through Muhammad, and before he became a Muslim, he could not resist the Gospel. The companions could do what one man could not. Satan was not converted to the law of Muhammad; rather, Muhammad followed the law of the demon of darkness, of ignorance, and of the subversion of nature. He spoke prophetically only in the sense that he said the demons had followers of his religion. I say nothing of the lower regions and the tree of **Zaqqum** <note>Original: *Zacomi*. In Islamic eschatology, a cursed tree in Hell whose fruit resembles the heads of devils (Quran 37:62-65).</note>, whose branches are the heads of demons; for there would be innumerable things to add. It is enough for us to know that the demon is supposedly corporeal, fears the sword, is converted to the faith of the **Quran** <note>Original: *Alcorani*.</note>, will eventually die, and will finally be brought back to life with the beasts. 

As for the silver and gold heaven, and the stars clinging to it with golden chains, which drive away the demons so they do not seek Paradise—what need is there to speak of it? Yet it truly troubles me: why do the stars fear that demons might enter Paradise, since the gates are always bolted, and were not even open for the prophet himself when he arrived with **Gabriel**? He must be worse than the demons; otherwise, the doors would have opened for him of their own accord, as they do for the demons, who can only be driven away by stars hanging from chains. When I was speaking of the levels of heaven, I spoke of the matter of the sky. Now you have understood that there are mountains, precipices, cold, and even snow in the highest heaven.

### WHAT HE ADMITTED AGAINST NATURE.
### CHAPTER XVII.

Throughout the entire law, it has been plain enough that he overturned the order of things and the natural disposition of all people, since he wished to persuade men that whatever crimes he allowed were from God and were lawful. He wanted the "grace" (as he called it) given to him by God for perjury, adultery, fornication, effeminacy, and the killing of parents, citizens, and friends, to be lawful for everyone, so that he could not be condemned for that which he granted to everyone by law. What can be thought of that is more foul than brutal intercourse or **pederasty** <note>Original: *pæderastia*. Here, Postel uses the term in a polemical sense to attack the moral character of the Prophet and his followers.</note>? Or what could be given that more thoroughly turns into a blight upon nature? Who could have generated a greater plague among men than to set them against one another under the pretext of piety, so that the most faithful man is simply the strongest and the victor? What republic will ever be blessed if a citizen, in the name of persuasion, could justly be armed against his fellow citizens and parents? Those forces ought to have been turned against enemies. 

There were many very famous cities in Arabia devoted to idolatry; he ought to have compelled or despoiled and overturned those, not his own city. He would have converted his own people sufficiently if he had administered justice to his other neighbors. But it was not religion, but factionalism that persuaded him. **Abu Bakr**, **Umar**, **Ali**, **Zayd**, **Ammar** <note>Original: *Vbecharus*, *Homarus*, *Halys*, *Zeidus*, *Achmarus*. These are Latinized names for the Prophet’s prominent companions and the first Caliphs.</note>, and the other influential and factious citizens of **Mecca** <note>Original: *Mechenses*.</note>, could not have supplied the prophet with strength and factional leaders elsewhere; the prophet did not seek vengeance elsewhere. Those who knew him for what he was and had offended him by describing him had to be finished off: that was his "true religion." Thus, today, in the whole world, nothing is more inhumane than a Muslim who fashions himself after the example of the prophet. For since men can scarcely be kept to their duty by the strictest laws, what do we think will happen when they are armed with laws that go against nature? Whatever pleases them is allowed. Whatever the prophet did was considered holy; therefore, similar things are allowed. All these things take up arms against nature, they go against reason and public peace, and in truth, they are so wicked that they seem to be wickedness itself.

WILLIAM POSTEL, BOOK II.

### HOW THEY OPPOSE REASON. CHAPTER XVIII.

If it is permitted to judge the nature of things by similar things and their effects, who could ever persuade himself that a man whom everyone knows and sees to be lacking in no part of vice is different from others and divine? What prophet was ever burdened by such a foul collection of vices, and carried such supreme impurity in both soul and body? Who among them did not confirm their words by at least a single miracle, or a true prediction, or a life of singular innocence? Since, therefore, none of the ancients appear similar to this man—while he is in all things equal to the most wicked scoundrels—who would think he should be held among the prophets? Even if such a man spoke the most divine words or performed miracles, I would never believe him. For humanity, charity, innocence, friendship, chastity, sobriety, integrity, and the other better endowments of both soul and body are held in virtue in vain unless they have a place in the best of men. 

Hence we do not hesitate to assert that he was an evil man, who not only lacked these virtues but was also most uncontrollably urged and burdened by their opposites. Indeed, in Muhammad there was not merely a total absence of those virtues, but in their place reigned cruelty instead of humanity—with which he raged against his own blood; instead of charity, the casting out of his own people to make room for mistresses arriving from every side; instead of innocence, the injustice with which he crushed everyone; instead of friendship, the deceit by which he slaughtered his dearest friends while they slept; instead of chastity, that lewdness by which he mixed with fifteen wives <note>Original: *15 uxoribus*.</note>, maidservants, beasts (for what he approved in others, he seems to have done himself), and catamites; instead of sobriety, the greatest luxury, which he permitted even during his forty-day fast <note>Original: *quadragesima*. Referring here to the fast of Ramadan, which Postel compares to the Christian Lent.</note>; instead of integrity, the imposture with which he deceived everyone. 

And this man, if it please the gods, was an intimate of God! If such a wicked life is good, then God gave the natural knowledge and desire for virtue to man in vain. Either our opinions on the good and virtue are empty, or no one more wretched than Muhammad was ever born. For reason forbids that a man who is a source of guilt, agitated by a demon, a liar, an impostor, a deceiver, impious, and ignorant of divine matters, should be a friend to divinity.

### HOW MUCH UNHAPPINESS REPUBLICS SUFFER UNDER THIS LAW. CHAPTER XIX.

It is inevitable that any Republic that receives this doctrine will be oppressed by perpetual disturbances and losses. For it sins while it obeys this law through the lack, the abundance, or the fear of certain things. For what purpose did God, in His supreme goodness, wish the use of wine to exist in nature? Was it not so that we might use it moderately to the praise of His name? Now, through both private and public lack of wine, a most excellent part of nature perishes. Therefore, those skilled in the law laugh at this precept if wine presents itself; courtiers, soldiers, and merchants laugh, and they gorge themselves on it all the more passionately because it is so rarely permitted. For "we strive for the forbidden, and we desire what is denied" <note>A quote from the Roman poet Ovid (*Amores* 3.4.17).</note>. The prohibition of wine is a useless prescription and most damaging to the Republic, whether you look at private matters or the public treasury. 

What shall I say of the prohibitions in which the **Quran** <note>Original: *Alphurcan*. From *Al-Furqan*, another name for the Quran meaning "The Criterion."</note> agrees with the Jews? What is the religious offense in an animal torn by a dog, a wolf, or a bear? Do not many animals perish which would be useful to the poor? I am silent about the rest. What evil does a pig have in itself? I know Moses had prohibited this, having granted it from an ancient rite to the children of Israel because in Egypt there were many subject to leprosy, with which this animal is frequently believed to suffer. They suffer among us too, but let them be inspected before the slaughterhouse; their meat will not harm the body it nourishes, and their lard is most fit for many uses. Nor are they more harmful in hot regions, as some say; for in all of India, under the equator, in the **Moluccas** <note>The Spice Islands in modern-day Indonesia.</note>, among the **Chinese** <note>Original: *Quinas*.</note>, and in **Paria** <note>A region in modern-day Venezuela, often used by Postel to refer to the New World.</note>...

### ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

...nothing is more healthy or more common than that animal <note>referring to the pig, discussed on the previous page</note>; therefore, it is forbidden in vain. What shall I say of the **hunting ban** for four months <note>Postel refers to the "Sacred Months" in the Islamic calendar during which certain types of hunting were restricted</note>, by which not only is utility lost, but poor farmers are also hard-pressed by boars, roe deer, stags, wolves, and lions, to whom all things must be permitted at that time? I have seen such a great abundance of boars in many places in **Anatolia** <note>original: "Natoliæ"; the Asian part of modern-day Turkey</note> that for many miles they leave no crops undamaged. If a Christian catches one, he is beaten and crushed by a **Muslim** <term>Mussulmano; an early Latinization of "Muslim"</term>. He would rather it rot and perish without use than be put to the uses for which God had given it. I say nothing of the superstitious slaughter, such that some, in the **Jewish fashion**, never taste anything that was not slaughtered before their eyes, as if the soul remained in the little morsels. These things are drawn from ethnic <note>heathen or pagan</note> rites.

Passing over these lighter matters, if we proceed to estimate how many inconveniences the **Muslims** suffer from the abundance of ceremonies, wives, children—or rather slaves—and wandering bandits, and what calamities they feel and experience, truly the fellowship and approval of this wicked law will seem not only useless, but adverse to peace, equity, and humanity. 

And to begin with **ablutions** <term>ritual washings; in Islam, this is "Wudu"</term>, if anyone remains in the ceremonies of the law, what else, I ask, can he be occupied with all day but washing? At cock-crow, at noon, in the evening, late at night, and at the first watch, everyone must be washed before he begins to pray <term>salauat; from the Arabic "Salat," the five daily prayers</term>. And if water is lacking, he must be smeared with dust <note>original: "puluere infici"; referring to "Tayammum," the ritual purification using dry sand or dust when water is unavailable</note>, than which I do not see what could be more superstitious or more inconvenient. If water takes away sin, then there is no need for God; if God takes it away, there is no need for water. But if both water and God do so, then the dust is useless. For it is a contradiction to wash the face, hands, arms, feet, shins, legs, and private parts, and then be smeared with dust. If it were established for the sake of bodily cleanliness, then you apply the dust badly, for it defiles. 

But the **Muslims** will object to the **baptism** of Christians. It is nothing like it. Once, into the death of Jesus Christ, we are not merely washed or rinsed, but dipped in waters purified by the blessing of the Word of God; we do not believe that the power to wash away sins is in the water, but by the power of the divine word and faith, when such things are done, we hope for and obtain the remission of sins from God. What you do has nothing in common with us. These things come from the **Jews** and the **Anabaptists** <term>Catabaptistis; literally "re-baptizers," a radical Reformation group Postel views as similar to Muslims in their legalism</term>. 

Let us estimate the necessities of nature: the passing of wind, excretion, urine, sexual intercourse, and nocturnal emission—add to these the sins committed between ablutions and prayers—who (if he wished to be considered a just observer of the law) would spend his time doing anything other than living his whole day and life in the water like a **heron, a duck, or a goose**, if he wished to be washed afterward as the law commands? I leave the difficulty of winter to be considered; these are follies and delusions, which are so judged by the prudent as they utterly despise them. 

I remain silent on the fact that everyone is held by the same laws, nor is any distinction made in that law, although those performing sacred rites have far more and more frequent duties to perform than the others. **Muhammad** understood no distinction of orders <note>social classes or clerical ranks</note> whatsoever, just as he neither instituted nor cared for any, though he had overturned the state of things. What shall I say of that **pilgrimage of four months**? No hunting is permitted then, so much so that many spare lice, bedbugs, and fleas. 

I do not touch upon the troubles of **circumcision**, when a boy in the vigor of youth, in the fourteenth year of his life, with the sharpest sensation, suffers his foreskin to be drawn off. The **Jews** are much wiser; though they are condemned for not believing in Christ if they have heard of Him, they nevertheless circumcise on the eighth day as prescribed by divine law. For that fresh flesh is healed more easily than that of an adult. Moreover, the small child gives his name to the profession through the silent faith of the parents. But there was no need for them to become like those who, after they had instituted a prophet, fell away from him. 

Now, if I should add by what terrors the unskilled in these matters are agitated when they come to death, when they think of the **two angels beating the bodies in the tomb** <note>In Islamic tradition, the angels Munkar and Nakir question and, if necessary, punish the deceased in the grave</note>, and of the soul which, in the manner of a shirt garment...

...the body, and raises it up; of which belief this provides proof: that the tombs are made very wide, in which the corpses may be able to be moved about and stand while sitting <note>Postel is mocking the Islamic belief in the "Trial of the Grave," where the deceased are said to be questioned by the angels Munkar and Nakir</note>. To whom would these things not cause laughter? What "old wives' follies" were ever greater? 

But the greatest unhappiness is especially evident in the perpetual discord of those joined in marriage. Or do you think human weaknesses are willing to be endured with a calm mind by each other, when there is room among the contracting parties for six hundred slanders, prepared testimonies, and false oaths? You hear nothing else before the judges than **divorce** <term>original: "talca"; from the Arabic *talaq*</term>, **wrongdoing** <term>original: "dulum"; from the Arabic *zulm*, meaning injustice or oppression</term>, **dowry disputes** <term>original: "tzebin"; likely referring to the *thaman* (price/value) or specific marriage contract terms</term>, and the rest: namely, repudiations, injuries, and dowries. There can be no true faith where there is hope that it will not be lasting. Friendships ought to be eternal and, as far as possible, most similar to God, who is their origin. 

Suppose that frequent divorce is useful because of frequent inconveniences; what mortal could ever manage to make a flock of women, participating in the same rights, live together in harmony? Even if you beat some of them to death, you could not dictate terms to them, especially if it concerns the rights of marriage. What do we think will happen when they not only have companions [co-wives], but see maidservants and slaves sought from everywhere preferred over them? What peace, love, or concord can exist in those houses? Therefore, this law is in more frequent use among tyrants and the powerful, who settle women in various places. The poor, condemning the law by silent consent and their actions, are usually content with one wife. Prudent, sober, and continent men are even more so. No one who has not seen it can believe how tyrannically and imperiously women—who are half of nature—are treated.

Let us now consider what happens from the effect and power of the law. Let us assume a marriage is fertile on both sides; both can procreate from the age of 14 to 50 (assume the power of the man and woman is equal). A woman can give birth every single year. I have known many who have borne 30 or 35 children. But taking away half the time—since from 15 to 50 is 35 years—let there be 18 years, and as many children from one wife; multiply 18 by four <note>Referring to the four legal wives allowed in Islam</note>, and in 18 years there will be 72 children. If an arbitrary number from maidservants is added to these, a private man will be able to procreate not just 72, but 100 or more children—or slaves—for the State. See from where he can nourish such a flock; so it is no wonder there is no nation in the whole world more greedy than the **Muslim** <term>original: "Mussulmana"</term> one. 

If, however, mothers are lacking for such a great multitude (for anyone can have sought that number from various women), and other women are added, what do we think will happen when one stepmother can scarcely bear to see even a single stepson? Will she not strive to remove all those who are not her own? If she does not attack them, she will certainly never care for them. A maidservant, unless the master is present, cares even less; for she may be manumitted for free with a small gift or sold at his whim. Now the burden of such a great family must fall back upon the wretched head of the household. 

But nature has taught how fit men are for ruling a domestic family; she made them with a stronger body and a more sagacious mind so that they might bring home the fruits of external labors and cares, which a diligent mother of the family would then look after for the common household and the children. I do not say how gravely this law sins against nature, since it even removes paternal love from one's own children. For although it is certain that all men are held by the desire for offspring, yet if very many children are born, affection cannot be seen as equal toward all, even if they were born from a single, irreplaceable, and most beloved mother. But if they are born from maidservants and women who are little loved, the father does not even care to see them. Maidservants are cast out to beggary, the newborns are abandoned <note>original: "exponuntur"; a reference to the ancient practice of child exposure</note>, and they are raised as beggars. And if anyone, out of greater humanity, sees to it that the offspring of a maidservant is raised at home (unless he is otherwise entirely lacking in legitimate children or is very powerful), it is done so perfunctorily that death and life are esteemed just the same. Thus the bastards of poor and unjust men are accustomed to...

# ON THE CONCORD OF THE WORLD

...they are either consumed by hardship or spend their childhood and youth in a state of languor, and they very rarely reach maturity. If they do happen to succeed, it is not due to their education, but through the benefit of their own persistence. For while they are barely born—still babbling and learning to walk—all domestic duties are cast upon them as if they were slaves <note>Postel argues that because of the instability of polygamous households, children are neglected and forced into labor early.</note>; yet through endurance they overcome and sometimes emerge successful. Indeed, who could doubt that almost all Muslims are held in such low estimation when all women are valued as nothing more than man-servants and handmaids? If they are valued more highly, it is for the sake of the dowry and family connections, not for the sake of the person or for love. 

These are the "illustrious" effects of the Quran. Yet that "prudent legislator" <note>A sarcastic reference to Muhammad.</note> provided for this great and nearly destitute multitude. For he established an order of those who, having abandoned their own property, "fight in the way of God," and he urged more than once that alms should be distributed to them. Truly, there is such a common dross of these sects wherever the name of Muhammad is heard, that it is never safe to travel even two miles—especially if the journey is made through Africa, Egypt, Arabia, Syria, and Asia Minor (which they call Anatolia). Therefore, it is hardly ever safe for one man, or ten, or twenty, or even a hundred to travel there unless they are just like those desperate men themselves. A **caravan** <term>original: "Carouana"; a company of travelers, merchants, or pilgrims</term> is necessary—that is, a cohort of several hundred or thousand men—which even then can barely protect itself from those poor wretches. Indeed, these people are so destitute that many living in Mecca drag out a miserable life on scraps and the rinds of cucumbers and other fruits.

Some, especially in the deserts of Arabia and Syria, have reached such power that, having elected a leader for themselves, they are formidable even to the Prince of the Turks <note>The Ottoman Sultan</note> himself, who is forced to buy off their harassment with payments. 

Consider how true the philosophical axiom is: *Once an absurdity is admitted, countless similar ones follow.* <note>original: "Re abſurda ſemel admiſſa, innumera ſimilia ſequuntur."</note> Once a nefarious scoundrel was accepted as a prophet, a most wicked law was approved. Once his decrees were received, marriages that are illicit and contrary to nature and friendship were introduced. From these was born a mass of needy orphans driven to desperation by their poverty; while they pretend to be preserving their law, they bring ruin and disgrace upon the entire commonwealth. 

Indeed, this plague, creeping through the fields, begs for alms in such a way that if you do not give, they seize it; if you are met alone, they rob you and punish you with terrible beatings. This "plague" has various sects: some go naked, others semi-naked; some with heads bare, others covered. They wear various colors, some in garments made of patchwork of every color <note>A reference to the *khirqa*, the patched cloak of a Sufi dervish.</note>; some with mangled bodies and wide wounds which they say were received in the name of the prophet, provided you pay out some coins to them. 

Truly, the "holiest" of all are those who, from the whirling of the body in a circle, lose their minds and collapse <note>A description of the "Whirling Dervishes" or Mevlevi order.</note>. Holier still are those who refuse to move from their spot despite the insults of the weather. The "greatest" are those who, pretending to have no reason, mate with she-asses or any animal, and if none is available, they openly expose themselves. Some are devoted to specific clothes, some to rituals, others to certain foods, regions, or places. No place is free from this pestilence, which has at times proceeded to such audacity that they have even attempted to secretly attack and kill princes. 

The miserable common people have grown callous to the injuries and harrassments of these men; in many places, they have abandoned agriculture and either fled or joined them, preferring to live miserably by plunder than to be defrauded daily of their labors. Because of this pestilence, Asia Minor, Syria, Mesopotamia, Arabia, and Egypt—once the wealthiest and most cultivated provinces—are now almost sterile. Where there were once ten wealthy cities with their villages and villas, now there is scarcely a single fort or small hamlet. Since their affairs were shattered by Muslim warfare, the wretched inhabitants have never been allowed to rebuild cities, cultivate fields in peace, or pay just wages to the treasury; for everyone plunders, and no one preserves. For although judges are appointed in every province by the diligence of the princes, nevertheless, the acts committed by those scoundrels wandering under the pretext of religion are not considered crimes if...

...if they remain hidden, no suspicion of wrongdoing falls upon these religious figures. But if one of them is caught, the others terrorize people with terrible curses; they stir up and frighten the common folk so that those caught are not punished and their order is not shamed. Some among them are powerful in illusions and sorcery—much like the **witches** <note>original: "sortilegae foeminae"</note> among us—and they bring blight to the crops and the livestock. Others deceive and hold the common people captive with ambiguous answers, appearing to have predicted something certain out of a mass of nonsense and dreams. This is a trait peculiar to the whole race of impostors, for while everyone recognizes a chance prediction, no one can pin down a lie or an ambiguity. For while the one who consults them is being deluded, he does not reveal the trick—partly so as not to admit he was fooled, and partly because he hopes for the future; and anyone who thinks he has gained a benefit from it never stops praising them. The people have become stunned, hardened, and calloused by these injuries to both soul and body. The experienced magistrate tolerates and ignores it, appearing to approve of what should be condemned out of a desire to maintain his command. To anyone rightly judging the condition of human affairs, there has never been a more miserable state of land in the whole world than where this wretched persuasion has taken hold, and where a region allows and nourishes this "army" of spontaneous wanderers in the "Way of God" without selection or a leader. For it is enough for that crowd to profess the name of religion (which anyone may do) to go about plundering everything. Commerce is ruined by these "plagues," who inflict injuries and unbearable losses upon all provinces. For how many people can wait while a cohort gathers itself, prepares, arms, and assembles its baggage? A whole year passes you by in deliberation. O most powerful ruler of the Eastern Empire <note>A direct address to the Ottoman Sultan.</note>, has this crowd fascinated your eyes—you, a prince experienced in affairs and ruler of the most noble part of the world—or do you knowingly and willingly approve of the losses to your subjects and yourself? The farmer is worn down by poverty, expense, looting, and raids; the traveler by dangers; the merchant by costs; and the treasury by loss. If, after the manner of Christians, every man were content with his own wife, and that whole "plague" were proscribed at once so that no one would dare—under pain of death—to be in those fellowships or to be enrolled in them, and if the privileges and immunities granted by princes were abolished, that seedbed would undoubtedly vanish immediately.

Indeed, one should not be moved by the "miracle" which they say happened under **Murad II** <note>original: "Hamurate secundo"; Sultan Murad II, reigned 1421–1444 and 1446–1451.</note>, a prince who loved truth and justice. For it is certain that it was done by the agency of the devil. The story, as it is told, goes like this. When the prince was contemplating the destruction of this unspeakable dross of men on account of their crimes—and even if some among them seemed good, he still wished to favor the **Imams** <term>original: "Imamos"; Islamic prayer leaders</term> and the **Teachers** <term>original: "Taalimanos"; likely from the Arabic 'talim', referring to scholars or instructors</term> and others who perform the duty of teaching, as the Republic <note>Postel uses the Latin "Respublica" to refer to the Ottoman state.</note> neither can nor should be without them—he wished for a decree of the supreme court to be promulgated. On the night before the day the edict was to be issued, Prince Murad was rousd from his bed and driven to a certain narrow place near his own house to obey a "vehemently urging call of nature" <note>A euphemistic reference to the Sultan needing to use the latrine.</note>. While he wished to sit there, the floorboards suddenly broke, and he was left hanging high up over a beam. When he called upon God, a certain man appeared in the habit and clothing of the primary sect of these scoundrels, freed the man, and placed him back in his bed. Moved by this, the prince ordered at dawn that as many **Dervishes** <gloss>original: "Dermischler"; the Turkish 'Dervişler'</gloss> (as they call them) as were present in Constantinople should come to the court at a set hour, and he would give them all a bounty. They came, and he distributed it, meanwhile looking to see if he could recognize the one who had rescued him from danger; they all passed by, but he was not there. An elder rose from the whole flock and said that the one who had been present and helped him was not one man, but the "common procurator" <note>A spiritual representative or collective manifestation.</note> of them all. He said the Sultan should judge from this who were more useful: those who preach, or those who travel and pray. Thus they were not expelled, but were even preferred over those useful men whom the State cannot do without, even in the falsest of religions. Who [could believe] this...
