to bring forth <note>original: "adferre"; continuing the sentence from the previous page</note>, though I strive for brevity, how many were the conflicts between Simon Peter and **Simon the Samaritan** <note>Simon Magus, a practitioner of magic mentioned in the Book of Acts</note>. It shall be enough to know that in a single meeting, Peter took away three thousand men from Simon (who was the leader of the **Sadducees** after **Dositheus**) and drew them from magical illusions to the true faith. Indeed, he refuted Simon so thoroughly that there was no place left for him in all of Syria, for the people whom he had previously deceived were now hunting him down. This plague, departing from Syria, sought out Rome, intending to find supporters there. Once Peter had established his seat in **Antioch**, he followed Simon to ensure his poison would not infect the Romans, and he entered Rome both for the sake of preaching the truth and for tearing down what was false. 

For his sustenance, Peter used only bread with olives, and occasionally vegetables, with water as his drink; his clothing consisted of a small cloak and a tunic. These were the only "baggage" of the prince of the apostles: these were his pomp, his triumphs, and his chariots. Yet under that meager appearance lay a power that could command nature itself. Meanwhile, Simon the Samaritan so deluded the men in Rome with his illusions that they erected a statue to him, inscribed **"To Simon the Holy God"** <note>original: "Symoni Deo sancto"</note>, which remained by the **Tiber** river for a long time. 

Among the conflicts held in Rome with Simon (for they were many and various), I will bring forward only the two most famous. Since the apostles eluded all his tricks and showed that his arts—with which he held great influence over that most curious monster and seeker of novelties, **Nero**—were vain, dangerous to men, and useless, a pact was made between Peter and Simon in the presence of a great crowd: that whoever could not raise a dead man should be put to death. Conveniently, a certain young man had died just shortly before. First, Simon approached and whispered his incantations; the lifeless corpse seemed to move its head, at which the frenzied mob, incited by the magician, began to rush at the holy apostles. Only with great effort was silence obtained, and Peter said: "If the dead man lives, let him rise, walk, and speak; if he cannot do this, you should know these are the illusions of evil demons. Let Simon step away from the bed, and you will see that nothing moves at all." 

Therefore, when Simon stepped back and the dead man lay still, Peter approached and said: **"Young man, in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene who was crucified, rise and walk"** <note>original: "Iuuenis in nomine Iesu Christi Nazareni crucifixi surge, & ambula"</note>. And immediately rising, he walked and spoke, and lived for a very long time afterward, providing testimony for the apostles. 

The other conflict was Simon's last, and the catastrophe of his life. Claiming he was offended by the "Galileans" (as he called our people out of envy), he affirmed to Nero that he wished to leave the city which he had taken under his protection. He named a day for the multitude to gather at the **Capitol**, for he claimed he would fly from there into heaven. On the appointed day, the people were present, the Emperor was present, and the apostles were present. Simon, crowning his temples with a laurel wreath like a victor, ascended the Capitol and began to be carried high into the air by the work of demons. But when Peter and Paul prayed, he was abandoned by the demons and fell to the earth half-dead. From there, he was carried by his followers to **Aricia** in disgrace, where on the following day he surrendered his unhappy soul to the demon. 

This was the end of Simon’s life, which became the cause of the apostles’ death. For Nero, seizing this opportunity against them, did not rest until they were destined for punishment. Thus, **Paul** ended his life with his neck severed by a sword; **Peter** closed his days on a cross after the manner of his Teacher, but with his head turned toward the ground <note>Peter was famously crucified upside down at his own request, feeling unworthy to die in the same manner as Christ</note>. This is the end of those who taught the truth and lived most innocently. This is the sign of the presence of **Jesus Christ**, His divinity, death, and resurrection, when such remarkable miracles are performed in His name. These accounts and what follows are drawn from **Luke**, **Clement**, **Linus**, **Cletus**, **Hegesippus**, **Tertullian**, **Leo I**, **Jacobus de Voragine** <note>original: "Ianuensi"; referring to the author of the *Golden Legend*</note>, **Gennadius**, etc.

When a certain young man had joined himself to Andrew, the boy’s mother, driven by a demonic madness, lusted for her own son’s bed. When the son would not comply, she accused him of attempting to violate his mother’s modesty. The youth was summoned and stood before the judge, calling upon Andrew as his advocate. For the unhappy woman added this weight to the case: that the son had attempted this act from the moment he joined himself to Andrew. After the judge’s unjust sentence and the rebuke of the woman, Andrew was thrust into prison. As he prayed for the youth’s liberation, a bolt of lightning from heaven and an earthquake from the ground arose at the same moment, consuming the wretched woman. It struck down those who were present and filled everyone with such terror that they begged the Apostle not to let them perish. 

In **Nicaea** in Asia, he raised a youth who had been killed by dogs and restored him to health. Having been raised, the boy came to Christ, as had the judge of the woman and his family previously. Forty men were also coming to him by ship for the sake of faith and baptism. A demon sank them by wrecking the ship, and none survived. Hearing of the miserable fate of the corpses cast upon the shore, Andrew called upon the name of Christ and restored them all to life, instructing them in the sacred teachings. Finally, famous for many other miracles, for the innocence of his life, and for his doctrine, he was fastened to a <term>decussate cross</term> <note>original: "cruci in decussem"; a cross shaped like an X, now commonly called a St. Andrew's Cross</note> by Aegeas, the proconsul of Achaia. He was seen to embrace the cross with a most burning vow so that he might follow Christ.

### PAUL

Truly, it can scarcely be judged whether we owe more to Paul for the integrity of his life, his indefatigable labors, and his miracles, or for his most holy writings. Certainly, a greater fruit comes daily to the Church from his writings, which breathe that divine heart, than from his miracles—to which our "modern Christians" <note>likely a jab at contemporary skeptics or reformers</note> deny credit. 

It is clear from the **Acts of the Apostles** that by his imprecation, the sorcerer and false prophet **Bar-Jesus** <note>original: "Bariehum"; also known as Elymas</note> was struck with blindness; this occurred in **Paphos**, a city of Cyprus. At **Lystra** in Asia Minor, a lame man was healed. At **Philippi**, he expelled a demon from a girl whose masters were making a great profit by her fortune-telling. In **Troas**, he restored to life a youth who had been killed by a fall from the roof windows while Paul himself was preaching. At **Ephesus**, he obtained the grace for the Holy Spirit to glide down into twelve men in a visible form. 

But what is more miraculous than his own calling and transformation? In **Sicily** <note>The biblical account places this in Malta, but Postel identifies it as Sicily</note>, having been cast up by shipwreck, and the men who were in his company having been saved by God's grace, he was not harmed at all by a biting viper. Through prayer, he freed a man sick with dysentery; as many as were sick from the entire island and were present were healed. Now, if anyone considers how many countless wonders he performed in **Corinth** and **Athens**, where he spent so much time, no one would believe it; he cured all kinds of diseases and raised the dead to life there, as witnessed by his disciple **Dionysius**—whom the Greeks call "the Great" for his remarkable erudition and "the **Areopagite**" <note>A member of the Athenian judicial council</note> because of his office, though we use only the second title. 

While active in Rome and frequently conferring with Peter, he was an aid in uncovering the deceptions of **Simon Magus**. From the imperial household, he restored to life a youth very close to **Nero** named **Proclus**, and brought him to Christ. Finally, he was punished by beheading at the order of Nero, and with him and Peter, a countless crowd of martyrs.

Both because of his intimacy with Christ and because of his remarkable knowledge of divine things, John claims a place for himself among the first. For nothing was purer than his flesh, nothing more divine than his soul (excepting God), and nothing more sublime than his writings. Before **Domitian**, regarding religion...

Truly, no one could fully explain how great the restraint and innocence of life were among all the followers of Christ. They considered immense weights of offered gold to be as worthless as dung. Chastity, humility, charity, patience, fasting, nakedness, and the rest of the virtues were peculiar to all of them; whatever the world considers of the highest value, they did not even deign to look upon. This is the most holy and certain transformation <term>metamorphosis; original Greek: μεταμόρφωσις</term> of Jesus Christ. These men had surpassed human capacity. 

It was possible for unlearned, poor, and weak men to overturn the power of law across the entire world. For he who disturbs religion must also necessarily disturb the civil state. For a Commonwealth <note>original: "Respub."</note> never allows the sacred rites of the gods to be overturned without the civil power being forced, by the greatest force—whether divine or human—to defend the accepted religion. And yet, although the followers of Christ were unarmed and attempted to tear down the wealthiest persuasions of the world, and by the word of the cross or its sign alone they overturned all the temples, altars, and statues of false gods, what riots were not stirred up by the innumerable multitude of priests and pontiffs, who boasted that they held the reins of empires? Princes, however excellent, were compelled to obey those pestilential impostors <note>Postel refers here to pagan priests and advisors</note> lest they incite the people to rebellion. Therefore, it is no wonder that there were countless thousands of witnesses to the truth of Jesus Christ. But what you might wonder at more is that the more they were afflicted, the greater the multitude that approached imminent death; this is a thing that fights against the nature of other men. Therefore God was, is, and shall be the one in whose name those things were done. 

Now, by contrast, those most famous for their crimes must be approached: those **Caliphs** <note>The religious and civil leaders of the early Islamic empires</note> who, for the sake of greed, pride, ambition, and lust, oppressed so many thousands of men and destroyed one another, such that nothing more clearly hostile to nature was ever born. One must also refute and attribute to the devil those miracles which occur among the **Muslims** <note>original: "Mussulmanos"</note>. For even among the idolaters, many things used to happen by the author of the devil, even though none of them knew or worshiped the true God. The devil inflicted diseases so that he might seem to cure them while the idol was being worshiped. This very thing witches, jugglers, and sorcerers still do today, by the same author. Truly, divinations which are found in sacred matters (unless you seek to have them revealed to you by God through a holy man) are prohibited, yet it must be pointed out that they were frequent among false beliefs. For that reason, not only were there prophets for those impostor-gods **Apollo** and **Mercury**, but also for every single god and goddess, who daily reported either ambiguous dreams or true ones by the impulse of the devil. Yet those laws were not good because of this, but rather were the most false of all. 

False miracles and divinations must be refuted by certain examples. I will bring forward one or two, for example’s sake, which are commonly recited in the dominion of the **Turks**. When a nation of those abandoned men (whom they call religious and holy) had once conspired to murder a prince, and the leader of that faction wished to wash away the discovered crime before the same prince, yet could not clear himself of the charges, he said that he was prepared to undergo a test of his integrity in the middle of a fire unless the prince believed him. A pyre was lit; he stayed in it for a long time unharmed (as they say), and certain parents of his showed his sandals untouched by the fire to create belief in the matter. These are trifles: few parents knew that which had been done in the middle of the city by the judgment of the prince, and such a famous crime was not handed down in public records. [most] fiercely rise up against him; these are the tricks of the Devil, devised to deceive the minds of foolish peoples. What shall I say about the illusions of **Gothuel Mirsini** <note>Likely a reference to a contemporary or legendary Eastern magician or "saint" whom Postel views as a charlatan</note>, who is most famous and considered most holy among those who have lost something? The eyes of men are so mocked there that people passing through a single place a hundred times do not see what immediately offers itself to everyone’s eyes once a "vow of eating" <note>original: "comedendi uoto"; likely a reference to a specific ritual or communal meal associated with Eastern travelers</note> is pronounced with those pilgrims I mentioned above. If the saints indicate something holy, they do not torment people for so long, nor do they sell their services for the sake of eating. They do not bewitch the eyes. Furthermore, the saints are little concerned with fleeting and perishable things; unless it concerns a person’s life or health, they are hardly ever present even when called. The **Nephesougli** <note>Turkish: *Nefes-oğlu*, literally "son of the breath"; Postel interprets this as "sons of the incubus"</note>—that is, the sons of the incubus (if such exist, for I have heard of them only by rumor)—are to be hissed at and regarded as the offspring of demons. Thus, by the collision of the true and the false, the truth will reveal and prove itself without any ill-will.

Therefore, from the benefits bestowed by God upon man, from the corrupt nature of humanity itself, and from the demonstrated excellence of both Christ and his followers, we must proceed to the proof of his divinity, frequently repeating the points made above. 

**First**, he could not be merely a man who performed miracles in his own name, without invoking God. 

**Second**, the greatest of prophets could not have spoken a lie; yet Christ in many places called himself God, and in that word it was impossible for him to lie. 

**Third**, he who rose of his own accord while no one prayed for him must necessarily have carried Divinity joined to his humanity. 

**Fourth**, the judgment of the world belongs to God alone. And yet, even they <note>Referring to the Muslims/Muhammadans</note> confess that Christ will be the judge of all with the most just judgment; hence they must believe he is God and all-knowing. 

**Fifth**, he who is conceived of the Holy Spirit cannot lose his source from the woman; but since the Holy Spirit is God, it is necessary to confess that Christ is God. For although he is not from the Holy Spirit as if by descent <term>traduce; a term from "traducianism," the idea of inheriting the soul/essence through birth</term>, but rather as if by guidance, yet it cannot be that he did not always have divinity with him. 

**Sixth**, from the integrity of the apostles and saints. For if his disciples preferred to die rather than bow to an idol or be given great honors, it is far more to be believed that they abhorred a lie. But in all places, they called Christ "God." Therefore, he is God. 

**Seventh**, he in whose name all miracles have been performed cannot but be God. But by invoking the name of Christ, all kinds of miracles were performed by the apostles and saints, and are still performed. 

**Eighth**, the transformation of his followers and their dissimilarity to worldly people proves that their author was God. 

Now, if they admit the Gospel at all, how many arguments for his divinity will offer themselves—things that could not be done by a mere prophet? He has testimony from the Evangelists that he exists from eternity. A voice from heaven taught this when he was baptized, sent by the Father: "This is my beloved son." This was confirmed by the Transfiguration, the prediction of his death and resurrection, the Ascension, and the sending of the Holy Spirit—all of which can belong to no mere creature.

As a **conclusion** <term>colophon; originally the "finishing stroke" or end-note of a manuscript</term>, there should be added to the fact that they confess from the **Sunnah** <note>original: "Suneh"; the body of traditional Islamic law and custom</note> that Christ will be the judge of all, also an article of their faith which I have taken from the **Tezchere elimam** <note>Likely *Tadhkirat al-Imam*, a "Memorial" or religious manual</note>, where they have it thus: *That in the judgment, Christ will extract Gog and Magog from their places, and they shall die; then Christ and the true believers shall survive. Nor shall anything be worshipped on earth except God, and he shall travel as a pilgrim, and the sharers of his happiness shall travel with him: and these are his disciples.* This tradition especially (even though it is false) will confirm our own, since "one fold and one shepherd" can be made only by God and Christ. He <note>The author of the Islamic text</note> places the happiness of paradise on earth, along with the **Nicolaitans** <note>A sect mentioned in the Book of Revelation, often accused of sexual immorality and heresy</note> and other heretics. However, it is permissible to take testimony from a falsehood as long as it is believed, just as one might wrest a sword from an enemy in order to finish him off.

# GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK IV: THE ARGUMENT FROM THE ORDER of things, and the duty of man.

After the knowledge of God and man, the subjects to be taught will be the order of things and the duty of man: how the universe consists of a super-celestial, a celestial, and an elementary mass <note>Postel is describing the Renaissance worldview: the "super-celestial" (the realm of God and angels), the "celestial" (the stars and planets), and the "elementary" (the earthly world of the four elements)</note>, and what things and creatures are within them. Four types of things in the lower realms are evident to our senses. For some things merely **exist**; others **live**; others **feel**; and others **understand**, such as man. Beasts are destitute of intellect; plants lack sensation; and stones, metals, and elements lack life. Therefore, just as intellect is added to the first three—namely, essence, life, and sense—to reach the highest perfection, giving completion to all, so too it was necessary for divinity to be added to the highest perfection of man (which already consisted of a triad: body, soul, and intellect). Thus, the first creature <note>referring to the human nature of Christ</note> was joined to the highest, primary Intelligence <note>God</note>. For just as man is the fourth level up from the lowest things, so too God is the fourth level up from the angels. The possibility of this thing lies in God; the will of God, who wills all things to be best, is behind it; and it is necessary for the salvation of man. Therefore, Christ was, is, and shall be God for eternity. See the arguments in the first book.

In this life, man was born for the sake of three things. First, for the sake of **God**, so that he may worship, acknowledge, and love Him; that he may seek Him through the obedience of good works, with pure benevolence mixed with humility and faith. Second, he is for the sake of **himself**, so that he may strive to prove himself most worthy of his Father through the greatest purity and innocence. Third—which proceeds from both the former—is that he should show, through kindness and whatever skill he can toward his brother (another human being), that he was not born into this life in vain. 

Although this goal is set before everyone, nevertheless, because of a depraved nature, no one hits the mark. Therefore, there was a need for a physician and a corrector of this life who might heal men affected in this way and restore them to their original life. God does not do this by simple inspiration, and an angel could not restore it—much less a man. Therefore, there was a need for a God-man joined together <note>The doctrine of the Incarnation</note> to mend nature, the likes of whom the entire world has seen in the true followers of Christ. For they referred all things to the goal of divine honor, their own innocence, and charity—something that has happened to no one estranged from Christ. These and similar things have sufficiently revealed the divinity in Christ. From there, however, one must gradually come to the disapproval of the wicked law <note>original: "nefariæ legis"; Postel is referring to Islamic law, which he viewed as a corruption</note>.

->HOW THE FALSE<-
->*persuasion is to be refuted.*<-

Since the highest truth, wisdom, and the other gifts and virtues of the mind are from God, and since He is never the author of evil, falsehood, ignorance, or any vice cannot be in Him or from Him. But in the Quran <note>original: "Alcorano"</note> there are nine thousand lies and falsehoods; whence it is clear that it is from the devil. That law which commands one to take up arms against nature (which God desires to be preserved) is not from God. Such is the Quran. To this must be referred those things which, in the entire second book, were seen to fight against divine goodness, nature, art, and public peace. 

And meanwhile, while the old bond is being dissolved, it must always be kept in word that princes are to be obeyed. For when the old law is abolished and a new one introduced, care must be taken lest any sedition arise. Christians are armed with patience until, once matters are entirely settled and a Christian magistracy introduced, it is permitted to pursue one's rights through the law. For in this we are most tested: if we suffer patiently. Restoration ought to be similar to the origin. The examples of Christ and his followers must be brought forward; there must be frequent talk about the uncertainty of accidental things; that princes and commoners are of equal use, origin, and final catastrophe <note>meaning "conclusion" or "death"</note>; that they can differ in this one thing: that they consume [different things] at lunch or dinner...

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

princes, who have enough to satisfy countless ordinary people, should nourish the infinite poor.
Let the great be covered in silk, purple, and fine linen: while hardly a rag remains for the poor. In God's eyes, he is the most blessed who has the fewest things, because he owes the least.
Many passages from the <term>Quran</term> <note>original: "Alcorano"</note> are already persuasive on this point. But because these things are good, they should be translated into the Gospel: so that it may clearly appear that if any good is seen in that law <note>Referring to Islamic law</note>, it is delivered much better and in a better order in the Old and New Testaments. Thus, while they leave behind the seeds of a false persuasion, they will feel they have made no loss.

But once our own people are persuaded and the foreigners are dissuaded, the greatest difficulty arises from the variety of ceremonial rites. The <term>Muhammadan</term> <note>original: "Muhamedica"</note> people burn with no greater hatred toward us than because of our use of images. Therefore, for a time, the images of the saints should be removed, or they should be permitted their own temples. It would certainly seem far better to abolish them than to have the new converts and <term>catechumens</term> <note>students undergoing instruction before baptism</note> take offense at the various forms of worship. The liturgies preserved in the Calendar could be equally observed and celebrated daily without the presence of an image, which can do nothing. 

However, if they do not wish to set aside their own worship immediately, they should be tolerated rather than abolished, until through constant preaching of the Gospel they reach the sincerity of doctrine and worship. Those who have married multiple wives should be allowed to keep them, but as those wives die or are divorced, they should be permitted to have only one. Regarding the sheep that are slaughtered at <term>Easter</term> <note>Postel likely refers to the Islamic festival of *Eid al-Adha*, which he synchronizes with the Christian Pascha</note>: if someone does not want to give up that rite immediately, let the meat be eaten with the poor after invoking the name of Christ. 

If they do not wish to be bound immediately by all the rites of the sacraments and prayers, they should not be pressured at first. Likewise, they should not be driven from their own customs against their will, except for those things which are manifest sins against Christ. The more serious crimes with which that nation is burdened, and for which that wicked law made a way and gave its assent, must be driven out with dire imprecations and forbidden by law. 

In this way, through constant preaching and social interaction, any prince may draw the people to true piety without any riot. To make this easier, he ought to abolish all privileges favoring the false law and proclaim by edict that anyone may freely debate it in private or public, and that it is permitted to prefer philosophical opinions over it. In the meantime, so that whoever wishes may read the Gospel, let all the <term>Alfakih</term> <note>original: "Alphachi"; Islamic legal scholars and jurists</note> and <term>Imams</term> <note>original: "Imami"; Islamic prayer leaders</note> have it. Thus, a good portion will spontaneously shrink back from foolish blasphemies. This is the method of dealing with <term>Muslims</term> <note>original: "Mussulmanis"</note>.

## THE MANNER OF DRAWING
### the Pagans to the Truth.

<term>Idolaters</term> <note>original: "idololatrae"</note> and those imbued with any false opinions about God are to be approached using the common precepts (as they were delivered in the third book). Nothing is more excellent than God, and everything is owed to Him. One must grant something to human weakness. Their opinions should not be fought against immediately; rather, one must use a degree of "turning a blind eye" <note>original: "conniuentia"</note> to certain things until the people are attentive, and then persuade them with these logical inductions:

That a human being is more excellent the more he is subject to and familiar with the Greater. And even if lower things seem to have some power, all things are nevertheless subject to the Supreme God and Father of all. If the Sun is believed to be God, it must be demonstrated that it is a servant and obeys God of necessity. This is because it has no will of its own, nor can it rest; since it is compelled, it has no choice. Because it lacks liberty, it serves; because it serves, it cannot be a god. For gods must be, by far, the most free, the most blessed, and intelligent. 

From this it will follow that statues, cloth, forests, and all other such things are not to be held as gods. It must be shown that they are made of the same common material in which there is no holiness. Furthermore, so that the matter can be settled with the arbiters of religion, they should be warned that if they do not wish to abolish their ancient [ways] at first sight...

The just judgment of God must be placed before their eyes. [One should explain] that no inferior power created the universe, but rather God, the highest; before whom man must give an account of the actions of his entire life. While they <note>the missionaries</note> consult the weakness of the people—if it cannot be done otherwise from the beginning—the power of the deity they believe in should be restricted to certain conditions: all other things should be attributed to the Supreme God, who is even capable of those things they believe a lesser power can do. Once the Supreme God is introduced in this way, any image of an idol will immediately be cast out. 

To make this easier, they should be questioned about their own rites and gods, and a refutation should be introduced based on their own words. For it is impossible that those things believed and said about any inferior power are not unworthy of God. Since whatever is believed to be the Supreme and God must necessarily be most powerful, most wise, most beneficial, blessed in Himself, and subject to no corruption or injury, it is impossible that anything [unworthy] should suit Him. Therefore, the inferior things will betray themselves when they are compared with that power. From an enumeration of God's benefits, and in a certain order, when the evangelist begins to speak, the common people will easily find rest. 

Truly, by means of reason, the prince and the primary power must be persuaded; by this art, the hearts of their people may be retained while true persuasion and faith are admitted. The people should be reminded of the benefits received from the treasury <note>original: "fisco"; referring to the state or public funds</note>, namely the institution and preservation of justice, the defense of the province, the restoration of roads, the founding, growth, and preservation of cities, and the legal, sacred, and military orders, so that they may always be willing to rest content with their princes. It should be promised that after they have worshiped the true God and chosen to live according to His prescriptions, they will be most happy. 

Histories of Christian affairs should be brought forward so that they may be enticed from these false opinions to the true ones. For it will happen that while those who are not drawn by the truth itself are led by a false opinion, they may at last, by complying, become most like the good. For the counsel of Paul in the beginnings of persuasion must be imitated. For he says:

> Provided that whether by pretext or by truth, Christ is announced:
> and in this I rejoice, and will continue to rejoice. <note>Philippians 1:18</note>

For although the true goal of a Christian is to value nothing of earthly things, splendors, fame, or glory, it must nevertheless be said that these things are greatest among them, and in such abundance that no one lacks enough, but rather abounds in them; this truly does not conflict with one's vow. The hope of temporary happiness (by which sense all men are most strongly held) will be able to draw many to the persuasion of the truth, who afterwards, through holy fellowship, will begin to despise the false and empty vow along with the good. 

Once faith in the Supreme God is received and confirmed, faith in the Trinity will also necessarily follow. For no one can understand the Creator without understanding Him as most powerful, most wise, and most benevolent. Therefore, power, wisdom, and will must be admitted in God. Finally, the demonstration must be completed with other arguments, so that the evangelist may immediately come to the dual generation of Jesus Christ, both eternal and temporal. In all these things, the most holy precepts of the Gospel—and how much peace they bring to those who observe them—must be taught, so that it might seem as if paradise is present among true Christians. Once these things are persuaded, external testimonies of the Gospel histories should be brought forward, by which it is established that Christ was God.

### ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

...both the treacherous and the good and faithful; although they seem hopeless, they must not be neglected. For this reason, when the testimonies of external authors and those different from us are added to the Gospel truth—than which nothing is greater—certain people are prone to come to their senses. The faith they do not receive from the Gospel, they seek from the authors of human literature. Not infrequently, descending into themselves from that point, they acknowledge their error and grasp the truth from the original sources. Therefore, signs known to outsiders must be brought forward to lead them to faith in sacred things.

Nothing presents itself as more famous or earlier than that visitation of the **Magi**, who—from the parts of the East, if you look from Judea (for every position in the world is named relative to something else), but from the western part of Persia—hastened to Jerusalem. They did this to inquire in the primary city of the whole region about the boy they had come to worship. There were three of them, as we learn from the Gospels themselves.

They were men of primary authority and wise, which is what the word *Magus* <note>original: "Magus"; a term for a Persian priest, scholar, or astrologer</note> means. Having seen a star in their region—not fixed in the sky like the others, but wandering in the region of the air toward the earth—they turned their eyes toward it more attentively. As they were a people most attentive to observing celestial things, they discerned what it meant. In that star, as they themselves reported and as has been faithfully handed down, there appeared the form of a boy with a body entirely of fire. He said to them that a boy was born in Judea who would rule over the Jews and the world, and that they ought to go there and worship him.

They put faith in these words and ordered camels and dromedaries <note>swift, single-humped camels used for travel</note> to be saddled quickly. Passing through the borders of Desert Arabia and the Midianites, they entered Jerusalem on the 13th day and inquired of the wise men about the newborn boy. Our interpreters are mistaken when they say the journey of thirteen days from the East to Judea was miraculous; they are hallucinating regarding the word "East," thinking it has one simple meaning, whereas it is manifold. For "East" is said relative to something else. Nor is there any position of the east that is not also south and west by different comparisons. For at every point in the sky where the sun acts, it always creates an east, a noon, and a west. Therefore, they poorly understand "from the East" to mean a distance of 90 degrees or a quarter of the sky.

For although dromedary camels can travel 60 miles <note>Roman miles</note> in a natural day, they would have come from the "East" of Judea to Jerusalem in no fewer than ninety days. They came, therefore, from the region of the Magi, which is contiguous to Persia, Chaldea, and the Persian Sea, and is distant from central Syria of the Phoenicians by 13 degrees of longitude, at clearly the same latitude. In that latitude of 31 degrees, or thereabouts, a degree of longitude has 55 miles; this journey clearly tallies with a moderate course for dromedaries. For the fastest daily course is 60 miles, as I said; the slowest 45; and the average 54. If these were degrees of the equator, they would have had to cover 60 miles every day. For the total journey would have comprised 690 miles. But in thirteen days, allowing some care for the body, they arrived by a moderate course covering 515 miles.

They had to pass through the region of the Midianites so that the prophecies might be fulfilled. For Isaiah says in chapter 60: *A multitude of camels shall cover you, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all those from Sheba shall come, bringing gold and incense, and announcing the praise of the Lord.* These things hit the mark precisely. For Midian is the eastern part of Desert Arabia, Ephah marks the same part in **Arabia Felix** <note>literally "Happy Arabia," the fertile southern part of the Arabian Peninsula</note>, and the region of Sheba denotes all the Arabias, especially the fertile part. Therefore, their dominion pertained to the Persian Gulf.

Furthermore, David calls them kings, saying of God: *Kings shall offer gifts to You* (Psalm 68). And likewise in Psalm 72: *The kings of the sea and the islands shall offer gifts, the kings of the Arabians and of Sheba shall bring presents.* They were indeed kings of the islands and the Persian Sea, and truly the only ones worthy of such a holy name; for that reason, Christ approved their empire as if it were the only legitimate one...

# WILLIAM POSTEL, BOOK IV.

...revolved. For they were such men as the most fortunate republics have experienced, and such as Plato desired for his own republic, which he wrote would then truly be blessed: either when a prince philosophizes, or a king is a philosopher. <note>This refers to Plato's famous "Philosopher King" ideal from the *Republic*.</note> For under others, the world is usually no less shaken than it is ruled. Indeed, the literature of all nations testifies that the **Magi** of the Persians were men of distinguished wisdom. It has been handed down in writing that they were kings and were in charge of the highest affairs of state. That region which was ruled by the Magi selected twelve men, foremost in wisdom, to be in charge of the highest matters. From that number, by their votes, they selected three each year to hold the reins of the kingdom, who would both keep watch over the heavens and, if anything urgent arose, could attend to it immediately. These three elected that year were the highest philosophers and true kings, most worthy of the name.

Coming from such a distant region, when they had asked the leaders of the Jews for the location of the born boy, they greeted him in the city of David <note>Bethlehem</note> and offered gifts worthy of emperors to the infant, who was surrounded by the greatest poverty of all things. Having completed these tasks, they departed to fulfill the rest of their administrative duties in their own magistracy. They died as happy men and Christians in that same region. Later, three hundred years afterward, **Helena** (the mother of the Emperor Constantine), while she was searching for the Holy Cross, arranged for their bodies to be brought to her, and they were carried to Constantinople. From there, through the Saint **Eustorgius**, the Bishop of Milan, they were transferred to his diocese; and from there, they were brought to **Cologne** by the Emperor Henry, where their power is famous for miracles. <note>The "Shrine of the Three Kings" in Cologne Cathedral remains one of the most famous pilgrimage sites in Europe.</note>

Now to the deeper history. When King **Herod**, a foreigner <note>Herod the Great was Idumean, not Judean, by descent.</note> who had killed all men of royal blood, was desperate to retain his power (for he had been a servant of the **Maccabean** princes), he heard from the Magi about a "King of the Jews." At that time, with feigned benevolence, he asked them to report back to him about the boy. When he heard that they had not done so, but had departed, he ordered that—lest the boy escape—all children from two years old and under within the borders of the city of David (which is called Bethlehem) be removed from the midst and killed. 

This crime was not only known within the narrow borders of Judea, but was immediately reported to **Augustus Caesar** in Rome. **Macrobius**, a man entirely foreign to our faith, will be a rich witness to us of this matter. For he writes thus among the jokes of Augustus: "When Augustus had heard that among the boys whom Herod, the King of the Jews, ordered to be killed in Syria within the age of two, his own son had also been killed, he said: *It is better to be Herod's pig than his son.*" <note>original: "Melius est Herodis porcum esse quam filium." This is a famous pun on the Greek words *hus* (pig) and *huios* (son); since Herod followed Jewish dietary laws, his pigs were safe, while his sons were not.</note> These are the words of Macrobius, a man otherwise unpious. Listen, you unpious ones, who have greater faith in the authors of humanity than in the Gospel: Macrobius subscribes to the Evangelist. It is established that it was done. 

What great madness could have seized a man otherwise most desirous of splendor and glory, that he would take upon himself the stain of such a monstrous crime and receive such a mark upon himself? How could that most innocent age have sinned against him so much that he would destroy even his own son along with the others? Certainly, he had received word from the Magi that a King of the Jews, an emperor of the world, had been born; otherwise, he would never have committed such a crime. The lust for reigning and seizing a tyranny alone can arm a father against his sons; the splendor of empire dissolves and tramples all laws, both divine and human. It was necessary, for the sake of that occasion, that the man's madness reached such a point that he turned the sword against his own flesh. **Josephus** subscribes to this when he says: "Whomever he knew to be of royal blood, or from whom anyone could reach any hope of kingship, he ordered them all to be killed." He removed and killed the entire Senate, saving only one who had predicted his rule. So great was the man's cruelty in that part, that the number of those killed seemed innumerable. The histories of the Romans support the Gospel. It was a firm conviction among the Jews, as **Suetonius** says, that an emperor of the world would then be born among them. This was so widely spread among foreign nations that the power of the Jews was formidable to the Romans at that time. Therefore, they broke that province with so many wars, and with their own...

# ON THE CONCORD OF THE WORLD

...to men, they handed them over to be ruled by a Roman governor on account of seditions. That rumor was not false. For then He was born, who "came unto his own, and his own received him not." <note>A reference to the Gospel of John 1:11.</note> Many literary records give credit to the miracles that happened in that year. Three suns were seen for a long time, and finally they merged into one—a thing which is not recorded to have happened at any other time. For **sun-dogs** <note>original: παρήλιοι (*parhelioi*), an atmospheric phenomenon where mock suns appear</note>, though they occur frequently and represent two or three suns as it were, never merge, but vanish as the reflection from the cloud disappears. They were certainly a proof of the Divinity visiting men more closely, and signifying the One and Triune God. 

The Romans did not realize that their most majestic, recently built temple—constructed because of the long-lasting peace they enjoyed under **Augustus**—was struck from heaven for the reason that a virgin had given birth. For in that year, which was the 42nd of Augustus’s reign, the **Temple of Peace**, which was believed to be eternal in public opinion and was called so by its inscription, was struck by lightning. Indeed, when that temple was first built, the Romans, no less needy than they were desirous of lasting peace, consulted the oracle of **Apollo** as to how long such a noble temple dedicated to Peace would last. The response given by the demon <note>Early Christian writers often characterized pagan oracles as being voiced by demons.</note> was that it would last until a virgin should give birth. They, thinking it would be an eternal work, inscribed the title before the doors: *The Eternal Temple of Peace*. Finally, in the 12th year from that time when Christ was born, the immense mass collapsed to its foundations. After Christians living in Rome heard of this many years later, they established a temple there to the Divine Virgin, which they now call **Santa Maria Nova**. <note>Today known as the Church of Santa Francesca Romana, built near the ruins of the Temple of Peace.</note> How could it happen that a work so recent, so intact, and so great should collapse like that, with no earthquake troubling the city? Certainly a peace other than a human one had come into the world: God, the author of peace, had descended among men, so that He might confer upon all inhabitants of the world who believe in Him that peace which we are unable to achieve in this life by any human skill without Him. For peace is not merely a rest from war. There is a need for settled minds (as the best philosophers have urged) before there can be any rest in a human being. It is not within human skill for someone to achieve this without the knowledge of the wisdom of God. 

What shall I say of the **Augustan basilica**, which later turned its name from a "praetorium" <note>A general's tent or administrative building</note> to sacred use? Certainly, without witnessing a miracle, a prince estranged from the true religion would not have made a sacred place and a basilica in the middle of his own house. Yet the place is dedicated to the Virgin in the **Golden Sky**, where a constructed temple stands today. <note>This refers to the Basilica of Santa Maria in Aracoeli on the Capitoline Hill.</note> **Orosius**, a diligent historian, says that in a clear sky at the third hour, Augustus saw a golden color surrounding the sun. Struck with wonder at this sight, he consulted the **Sibyl** <note>A legendary prophetess of the ancient world.</note> as to what this sign meant. She said that very soon one would be born who was to be worshipped by him and the whole world. She said he ought to take the greatest care not to receive the divine honors offered to him by the Roman people, but should instead worship Him who was about to be born. For this reason, Augustus wished the place where he had seen that vision to be sacred to the "Unknown Deity," until a temple was dedicated to the child-bearing Virgin by our people who know the true God, and it was called "in the Golden Sky." Following this example, basilicas were constructed under the same title in many places in Italy. 

What shall I say of the fountain from which a spring of oil bubbled up in Rome for a whole day when Christ was born? <note>The *Fons Olei*, associated with the church of Santa Maria in Trastevere.</note> I could bring forward innumerable miracles from our own authors, but they would not give credit to our "apostates." <note>Postel likely refers to Christians who were viewed as having "abandoned" the traditional Roman state religion.</note> For pagans, pagan doctrine is needed. They would rather believe **Lucian** than an Evangelist. If we come to those signs which occurred at the death of Christ's humanity, what a great abundance of external witnesses will support our Evangelists! There was that marvelous eclipse, which lasted for three hours, and which was kept in the Roman archives for a very long time, noted in the diaries of the Persians, written about by **Phlegon**, and observed by **Dionysius the Areopagite** and **Apollophanes**. Since it was against nature...

...and by the span of time and the opposition of the stars, it could not fail to signify that its author was also suffering a decline in his body. Moreover, that this was **contrary to nature** is shown by the opposition of the heavenly bodies. For it was the 14th day of the moon <note>The day of the Jewish Passover and the full moon.</note>, during which the moon itself can be deprived of the sun's light when the earth is positioned diametrically between them <note>a lunar eclipse</note>, but the sun cannot be eclipsed at all; for a solar eclipse can only happen during a conjunction <note>a new moon</note>. Furthermore, the duration was also against nature, lasting **three hours**, whereas the natural limit for the total duration of an eclipse never usually exceeds fifty minutes <note>original: *dextantes*—ten-twelfths of an hour</note>. It was fitting that the Author of all things should suffer according to his humanity, while the most noble parts of the heavens failed at his death. Who does not know that there was a **universal earthquake** beyond the memory of all literature? For its violence was noted both in Asia and in Rome; whereas otherwise, other earthquakes are never universal—indeed, they barely extend to the visible horizon on earth, or about two hundred miles. If they do exceed that, they only distress specific regions or provinces. For it is necessary, when it occurs naturally, that the other parts of the earth remain steady and fixed to resist, while one part is shaken. For without resistance and a fixed point, motion cannot occur, even in animals—how much less in such a vast mass of earth? **Pliny** noted that this occurred during the times of **Tiberius**. At the time of that same prince, what did those shrieks of demons mean, so swift a messenger of that same event? What was that same agitation of demons even at the ends of the world? Certainly, upon the death of even the greatest man or prophet, nothing similar ever happened. Let the passing of the holiest men be weighed; let the ends of the most famous men be considered. Let **Osiris**, **Cambyses**, **Xerxes**, **Alexander**, and **Augustus** be brought forward: what greater men has the world seen? Who had greater supporters and flatterers, such that they would even make an elephant out of a mouse? Yet at their departure from life, clearly no similar prodigy occurred. Had this not happened at the death of Christ, how could the **Apostles** and **Evangelists**—the lowliest class of men, destitute of human protection—have dared to propose such things to a most sharp-sighted world and to the most diligent observers of all famous events? If even the slightest suspicion of a lie had fallen upon them, the Gospel would never have found a place. Our accounts were attacked by **Porphyry**, **Celsus**, and **Julian**. All of these men admitted these feats of a straying and struggling nature <note>The pagan critics admitted the eclipse and earthquake happened, but tried to explain them as natural anomalies.</note>. Unless these events had been proved by the monuments of all nations, they would not have passed them over, since they picked at even the tiniest details <note>original: *apiculos*</note> (and if there is anything smaller) in our writings with the intent of contradicting us. I do not even bring forward the opinion of **Josephus** concerning Jesus Christ and his wonderful works. I pass over the **Letter of Abgar**. I do not repeat the writings of **Pilate** to Tiberius concerning him. I omit the judgment of **Philo** regarding our **Therapeutae** <note>An ascetic Jewish sect in Egypt whom early Christians like Postel identified as the first monks.</note>. All know from the letters of **Pliny the Younger** of our innocence and with what worship they performed sacred rites to Christ. The **Letter of Marcus Aurelius** survives regarding the water obtained by divine means by a Christian soldier <note>A reference to the "Thundering Legion" miracle where rain saved the Roman army.</note>. For this reason **Suetonius** called our people "maleficent," because the priests of the idols interpreted the miracles performed in the name of Christ in a sinister way. **Tacitus** is in the same error. In the same vice are the **Jews**, who in their **Talmudic** traditions never cease to attack Christ. Some call him a sorcerer and a worker of evil; others say he performed miracles using the **Divine Name** <note>original: יהוה (the Tetragrammaton)</note> taken from the sacred stone of the Temple and hidden for a thousand years by lion-shaped gatekeepers. All agree on this: that he surpassed human capacity. Indeed, his divinity is confirmed by the prediction of the overturning of Jewish affairs. For, as we have seen from the Jewish records, because of the killing of Christ, six million men were slain in two Roman expeditions; from the death of Jesus Christ, the Jews serve everywhere on earth, oppressed by slavery and entirely destitute of liberty. But the greatest confirmation of the divinity of Christ was provided by the Emperor **Julian the Apostate** from the truth at Jerusalem, when indeed in his hatred of the "Galileans" (as he [called us]...

## ON THE CONCORD OF THE WORLD

...Julian was accustomed to prick and mock with sarcasm) wishing to bring back the Jewish people—who were suppliant and interrupting the impious man with gifts—to Jerusalem to provoke hatred and disgrace <note>Julian intended to prove Jesus’ prophecy about the Temple wrong by rebuilding it.</note>, he gathered a huge number of them. Before others could arrive from elsewhere, they were to restore the Temple in the place where it had been three times built and overturned. It is a wondrous thing to tell, and an admirable deed: it happened that as the foundations were dug deeper, and while the nobles together with their craftsmen were about to lay the foundations of the work, balls of flames erupted from the bowels of the earth. These consumed many people once and then a second time, until they ceased from the undertaken work, having even been touched by celestial fire. Moreover, so that they might know these things were by the will of Christ, the sign of the cross appeared on the clothing of all the Jews. They recognized then that the word of truth was true. For Christ had said:
> Behold, your house shall be left to you desolate.
And likewise:
> Amen I say to you, there shall not be left in the temple one stone upon another that shall not be overturned.
Furthermore, that 
nefarious emperor paid the price for his treachery. For while he held camp near Ctesiphon, a city located on the borders of Assyria and Media, a spear launched by divine power pierced the man’s chest. He ended his life, crying out these words against Christ:
> "You have conquered, O Galilean!" <note>original: *Vicisti Galilee*—traditionally the final words of Julian the Apostate.</note>
Thus he surrendered his soul, which had been possessed by a demon. The fact is well-established; even profane authors record it. Indeed, to his Quaestor Libanius <note>A famous pagan rhetorician and friend of Julian.</note>, who was at that time a stranger to religion and who had educated Julian in letters, there appeared on the night closest to his death Mercury the Martyr, a Christian soldier, seen to hurl a spear at Julian and finish off the Emperor. When Libanius realized the next day that this was true, placing faith in the dream, he left his questorship and hurried to Saint Basil <note>Basil of Caesarea, a leading Church Father.</note>, and professed Christ through baptism—all the more ardently because, while the apostate was being finished off, the same thing had occurred to Basil and Libanius in a dream. Nor was it only Julian who paid the price for violating Christ and for his neglected and belittled religion: Arius <note>The theologian whose teachings led to the Arian heresy.</note> paid the penalty for his impiety, his intestines spilling out into the latrines. One Herod, on account of his harassment of Christ's infancy and the most cruel slaughter of the innocents, and another <note>Herod Agrippa I.</note>, on account of lusting after honors due to Christ, were consumed by a disease of lice. The same plague consumed Lucius Hieronymianum in Cappadocia, a most savage harasser and persecutor of Christians. With a similar end, Galerius and Maximian, who had finished off the martyrs of Christ with every kind of cruelty, closed their unhappy lives.
<margin>To Huneric</margin>
The same thing happened to Huneric, the 
Vandal king, when he rose up against the established religion. Emperor Arnulph paid an equal penalty for plundering Christ's temples and afflicting the sacred orders. Constantine, surnamed <term>the Dung-Named</term> <note>original Greek: *κοπρώνυμος* (Copronymus)</note> and <term>the Image-breaker</term> <note>original Greek: *εἰκονομάχος* (Iconoclast)</note>, on account of his treachery, gave up the remains of a worm-infested body to leprosy. Aegeas, the proconsul of the Peloponnese, after subjecting the apostle Andrew to punishments, suddenly driven into a frenzy by a demon, breathed his last. To the Eastern Emperor Valens, on account of his afflicting the sacred orders and forcing men devoted to the sacred rites into military service, a miserable end was foretold by Paphnutius; he ended his life having been cooked rather than burned by the fire of straw by his enemies, the Goths and Vandals. Nero partly laid hands on himself, and was partly stabbed by his own people. A domestic servant strangled Domitian. Commodus, who was a nuisance to everyone and savage toward our people, was strangled. Macrinus had the exit he deserved. Heliogabalus closed his days with a worthy end, because it had not been enough for him to have labored most impotently in all vices and to have dragged others into crime, unless he had also robbed Pope Callixtus of his life along with many martyrs. Maximian, stabbed by his soldiers, perished by divine vengeance for the innumerable deaths and slaughters of Christians; otherwise, he was most burdensome to the soldier by whom the low-born man had been called emperor. Decius died not much more happily. Valerian was killed in Milan. A servant took the life of Aurelian. To run through them all, no emperor of the Romans, or of others...

...of all those princes who persecuted the Christians, none perished without a violent death, except for Diocletian. He, lest the same fate should befall him as had happened to almost everyone before him, laid down the insignia of his empire and grew old and died as a private citizen. However, although the condition of a life should not be judged entirely by the death of the body—since God reserves eternal punishments for the wicked—nevertheless, since God gave the use of life not so that it should be ended violently, but that death should be undergone with a prepared mind and quiet senses, it is a kind of evidence of future perdition when God allows a man to perish in such a way that, infected by a whole "marsh of crimes" <note>original: "scelerum lerna," a reference to the Lernaean Hydra, implying a bottomless pool of wickedness.</note>, he cannot even think of the First Cause <note>The "First Cause" refers to God as the ultimate origin of all things.</note> except to his own condemnation. God also wishes to terrify the wicked with these examples so that, even if they judge that souls are nothing after the funeral, they may still be frightened by the example of a most foul and unhappy death; for such men direct all their efforts toward leaving behind the longest and most honorable memory of themselves possible.

Let the histories of all nations be revolved most diligently, and let the deeds since the birth of Christ be weighed: where Christ was not received, scarcely one prince in ten approached the "son-in-law of Ceres" <note>original: "generum Cereris." In Roman mythology, Ceres's son-in-law is Pluto, god of the Underworld; thus, this is a poetic way of saying they died a "dry" or natural death.</note> by a natural death. Among Christians, scarcely one in ten has perished by an ill-fated death. I except certain petty kings and princes of a "Roman heart," as they say, who always have Christ in their mouths while blaspheming, but think "God" is merely a word. For although they act under Christ’s empire, they think nothing more noble than to kill a man. If "retaliation" <note>original: "talio," referring to the *lex talionis* or the law of "an eye for an eye."</note> is frequently returned to them, it is no wonder.

But Machiavelli <note>original: "Machianellus." Postel is critiquing Niccolò Machiavelli’s views on Christian political weakness.</note>, that peer of the wicked, will say that Christian men, born for servitude and knowing nothing of liberty, are therefore unable to remove their princes; he claims they accept any commands, however unjust, with an even mind, and therefore it is no wonder that no princes are killed among them. If he had weighed the strengths of nature, and what has been done by Christians now and for a thousand years, he would undoubtedly never have asserted that a mind conscious of its own goodness diminishes the strength of the body; on the contrary, a guilty conscience has everything filled with trembling. 

Nor is there any reason for him to oppose us with the example of the Romans. For if the Romans were to come back to life today, victory over all peoples would not be as easy for them as it once was over worn-out or unarmed regions. It is not a lost or oppressed liberty because of Christ that causes unjust princes to be endured, but rather prudence and the public peace. For it is better, when things are well-ordered under a tyrant, to bear his commands (however unjust) at some cost, than to experience as many tyrants as there are neighbors and magnates while he is being removed through sedition. An unjust prince invades fortunes but spares bodies. In a revolution, however, it is necessary for everyone to be despoiled by disputes and factions, and for many to be killed if they oppose it. All things must be permitted to the soldier who chooses the prince and removes him when he wishes; for he who commands the commander never pays the penalty. 

How great was the unhappiness of the Roman people from Julius Caesar to the emperor Constantine for almost four hundred years? Certainly, he who was the most outstanding in happiness among those emperors is not to be compared with even mediocre Christians. Therefore, there is no more excellent condition of affairs (although among Christians there is no lack of "sneerers and pests" <note>original: "sannæ & pestes."</note> and the highest craftiness) than where Christ is heard. 

Wicked men are found anywhere in the world; but they are more noticed among Christians both because he who is evil under the best law is more wicked, and because among many good people, wickedness betrays itself more clearly, as opposites reveal one another. By these persuasions, the heathens are to be gradually drawn to the knowledge of the truth: so that while they repent out of terror of the punishments inflicted on the wicked (lest the same happen to them), they may also be invited to good things by the hope of a better fortune and condition of the state. For they will eventually become true followers by the example of the good, even for the sake of the Highest Good itself. By this

Moses employed the skill of attracting people to a happier fate when dealing with a stubborn people, even though the ultimate goal of his religion was eternal life, just as it is in the Christian faith. However, while he promises a land flowing with milk and honey, while he promises longevity and "earthly goods," as he calls them, he keeps the people under the Law until the truth of happiness itself should arrive. David calls these the "goods of the Lord," not earthly ones, but found in the "land of the living," when he says: *I believe that I shall see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living.* <note>Psalm 27:13</note>. And elsewhere: *I shall be satisfied,* he says, *when your glory shall appear.* <note>Psalm 17:15</note>. To these must be added the prophecies of the Sibyls <note>The Sibyls were legendary prophetesses in the ancient world whom early Christian writers claimed had predicted the coming of Christ.</note>, the responses of the oracles, and whatever else bears witness to Christ. The Sibyls, a class of women divinely inspired, left behind writings many years before Christ concerning Christ himself, his divinity, and his wonderful works—writings which we both prove and affirm through Gospel truth. What could be more divine than those poems which the Erythraean Sibyl <note>One of the most famous Sibyls, associated with the Greek town of Erythrae.</note> produced one thousand three hundred years before Christ was born? In the headers of these poems (lest it be believed they could refer to anyone else), the name of Jesus Christ was noted by the letters in these words: **Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior** <note>original: "ἰησοῦς χριστὸς θεοῦ υἱὸς σωτὴρ"</note>. There are as many verses as there are letters. Furthermore, lest these things be thought of as Christian fabrications, they were brought forth to the Romans themselves from their own archives and Sibylline books, and were circulated in everyone's hands. Indeed, how would a class of men destitute of authority—as Christians were for 300 years—have dared to be so impudent as to propose such things to the Senate and the emperors, and claim they were from the Sibylline books, unless the books had immediately revealed these things upon being produced? These Greek verses are extant in the *Royal Oration* <note>original: "ἐν τῷ λόγῳ βαςιλικῷ"</note> in Eusebius, and are cited by Joannes Ludovicus Vives <note>A prominent Spanish Renaissance humanist (1493–1540).</note> in his commentaries on Augustine's *City of God*, Book 18, Chapter 23, where Augustine translates those verses into Latin. They deal with the future judgment, the second coming of Christ, and the transformation of all things. Even the demon in the temple of Apollo was forced to confess Christ when it was consulted as to what sort of man he had been. The oracle said: "He was mortal according to the flesh, but wise and famous for his wonderful works; but having been seized by Chaldean <note>Postel or the oracle likely uses "Chaldean" here as a general term for Eastern or Judean judges.</note> judges and beaten with whips, he died a cruel death." Let Lactantius, Justin Martyr, Augustine’s *City of God*, and Orosius’s *History* be read diligently. Innumerable testimonies concerning Christ are held within them, drawn from the pagans <term>ethnici</term> <note>Postel uses "ethnici" (ethnics) to refer to non-Christian, non-Jewish pagans.</note> against the pagans, which both overturn the worship of idols and confirm the true religion. But we must now look at the practice of how modern forms of worship are to be approached.

### ON THE VARIOUS RELIGIONS OF
### today, and how they may be refuted.

Beyond the Muhammadan <note>Islam</note> and Mosaic <note>Judaism</note> worship, there is the wide-ranging religion of the demon. For wherever people worship spirits <term>lemures</term> <note>Malevolent spirits or ghosts of the dead in Roman mythology.</note>, there the foul image of the demon frequently represents itself and deludes the minds of men. It is worshipped openly and professedly in almost all of India, and in the New World, along with its islands. The Sun is worshipped by many of the Tartars <note>A general term used in the Renaissance for the various nomadic peoples of Central and Northern Asia.</note>. The regions subject to both poles are not yet known to us; therefore, we cannot say what worship they follow. Olaus the Goth <note>Olaus Magnus (1490–1557), a Swedish historian and geographer.</note> has recorded that certain people closest to the Lapps worship a square fragment of red cloth. We will certainly be able to conquer the falsehood of them all, as I noted above, by refuting them out of their own sayings. For in all things, but especially in divine matters removed from the senses, it is easier and more common to argue against what is false than it is to reach the truth. Suppose, then, that the foulest demon, the author of false worship, is offered to you (for under him all types of idolatry are fostered) and that he is held to be a god, as among the Cisgangetic Indians <note>Indians living on the "near" side (the west) of the Ganges River.</note>; if they confess one supreme God (which almost all of them do), since it is far more excellent...

To give one’s name to the prince in an army rather than to the master of the soldiers, and to him rather than to a <term>chiliarch</term> <note>original: "chiliarchae"; a commander of a thousand men</note>, and to the chiliarch rather than to a centurion, and so on with the rest—how is it then that men are so terrified in spirit that, even when they recognize God as the creator of heaven and earth, under whom even Satan trembles, they choose, in the manner of a slave, to neglect the person of the prince and act only as the followers of an inferior and lost wretch? What soldier is so insane (even assuming Satan were good) that he would not strive to prove himself to the prince rather than to a leader of the lower ranks? Does not everything tend toward this: that we receive the grace of a good deed from the highest leader, and acknowledge him who is supreme? *If an injury has been done to us, from where do we wish for a power to avenge us, if it does not proceed from the highest power? From whom do we either fear punishment for a misdeed or hope for the reward of a benefit? All things certainly tend toward the highest, proceed from there, and return there.* Many examples must be put forward from the arts, high offices, and other such things that are familiar and known to those peoples among whom one is acting, so that through familiar reasoning they may be made more attentive. In the second place, one must insist on the matter of honor and violated majesty <note>Lèse-majesté, or treason against a sovereign.</note> by dealing with these and similar examples. If someone were to serve under any leader who depends on the highest power, and knew that primary power and encountered it, but thought that he should only worship and observe the one in whose troop he is enrolled, while neglecting the sovereign, would not that highest authority (whether it belongs to one, to a few, or to all, but united in one head) be rightly angered? Would it not not only discharge that soldier, but also condemn him as guilty of treason and as an author of sedition? For what order could ever be held and preserved in a Republic unless all bowed their necks to the primary power? To not acknowledge a leader as a leader is the same as if you wished to be held as the leader yourself. Therefore, anyone who does not defer everything to the primary power is immediately held as a traitor. You therefore, O <term>Indians</term> <note>Postel uses "Indi" to refer broadly to non-Christian peoples encountered in the Americas or the East.</note>, and all <term>devil-worshippers</term> <note>original: "διαβολόσεβοι" (diaboloseboi)</note>, are acting as those guilty of treason against God, buried in error and perdition. As for your assertion that you worship this foul power so that it may not harm you, and that you wish to provide "rest" for the highest God so that He is not intent upon or occupied with the labor of condemning and directing you—what is this but to deny that He is the God you claim Him to be, by contradicting yourselves? If He is God, as He truly is and as you affirm, He must be omnipotent. If He is omnipotent, He is always omnipotent, and He is not burdened by any labors in administering the world as you think, but He surveys and penetrates all things. Therefore, your demon—whom you worship as the executor of God's justice so that he will not be cruel when you must pay the penalty for iniquity—if he were able to do anything against God’s command and permission, would he not first look out for himself? Would he not cancel the sentence of the highest judge and receive less punishment upon himself than has been inflicted on him by God? How could it happen that he would punish you more lightly than God wills, when he was damned immediately at the creation of the world and is an exile from heaven and that blessed company? You believe these things falsely, O Indians. He who fails himself through his own powerlessness cannot help others. Furthermore, since every law and religion ought to, and usually does, lead men toward a better hope and toward happiness, how is it that through a multitude of sacrifices, the blood of men, the countless injuries of unviolated serpents, and the greatest expense of life, you wish to undergo hell and the punishments of the devil, when there is no need for religion to go to hell? The more wicked someone is, the closer he is to your "happiness" and end? And yet you want these things prepared for you through so many labors and dangers. You deny God, O Indians, you deny God when you think the judgment of moderating His sentence is permitted to the devil. The devil has no right in inflicting or moderating punishments. The state of your affairs is just as if—

->### ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD ###<-

...if the citizens of a single Republic, because they might at some point deserve punishment by committing a crime (as anyone might) and undergo a capital sentence, were to worship, serve, and court with favors no one else in the entire Republic but the **executioner**, while meanwhile neglecting the judges and the arbiters of law and condemnation. What prince would tolerate such foolish citizens in his empire? Indeed, what private citizen would tolerate a son, a house-born servant, or a slave, if he chose to acknowledge authority from anywhere other than his father or master? What house can remain intact for long unless all things are referred to the judgment, praise, and glory of the one supreme head? You must acknowledge the **Supreme Commander** of the whole world, who commands even the unhappy demon; otherwise, you will burn in eternal punishment, and there will be no moderation of the divine sentence for you. All of you have perished up to this day. Repent, you wretches, and if the calamities of eternal life do not warn you, let the condition of your present life incite you.

Consider how much misery this unspeakable persuasion has brought upon you and convinced you of until now. What animal has nature produced that is more terrifying, harmful, and hostile to human nature than **serpents**? Yet they are so sacred to you that you do not dare to harm them or even pray against them. What dearer thing has God given to man in external matters than his own children? Yet their death is considered most happy if they are devoured or killed by serpents. What greater care has been given to man by nature than the preservation of his own life? Yet the devil has persuaded you to end it voluntarily by the most cruel death of the flames. What greater plague can strike terror into even a strong man in control of his mind than the foul image of a demon? Yet when your people are drawing their last breath, if the form of the foul specter is missing, the devil has taught the physicians, priests, and <term>hierophants</term> <note>original: "hierophantas"; priests who interpret sacred mysteries</note> to visit the sick who are dying with masks fashioned in that figure, as foully as they can be made. Certainly in **America**, to anyone either dying or suffering from a very grave illness without the aid of a deputy, the foul image of the demon is present, even escorted by a large retinue of the same kind. These are the fruits of your religion, Indians. A serpent is more holy to you than a human, dearer than your children; an infernal life is more precious than your own; the devil, the destruction of human life, is prior to the Supreme God, the author of all things.

By these and similar arguments drawn from false religions, false religion must be discouraged and the true one offered. For there is almost no one who—even if they do not immediately confess one Supreme God (as the <term>Cisgangetani and Transgangetani</term> <note>original: "Cisgangetani & Transgangetani"; peoples living on "this side" and the "other side" of the Ganges River, i.e., Indians</note> do)—will not nevertheless acknowledge that there are various kinds of demons. However, among various and diverse things, all will concede that there must necessarily be one **Supreme Being**, than whom nothing greater can be given. For even the inhabitants of the Western islands of **Cuba**, **Paria**, and the entire continent, all confess that certain demons are more excellent than others.

It is truly the work of the Evangelist to be armed against these plagues with the greatest faith and, as Jesus Christ says, with **prayer and fasting**. There will be certain victory in the cross. We ought to hope for this as something more certain than certainty itself. For the supreme power of Jesus Christ has not vanished, as our impious people think. Christ, or the holy Virgin, and his saints, hear their followers no less today than in the past—provided that work is done especially among those who have never heard of Him. This is evident even from these arguments: **Jerome of Prague**, after leading a solitary life for twenty years during the time of the Hussite faction, was sent from Poland into **Lithuania**, a region devoted to various and false cults. <note>Postel refers to Silvester Jerome of Prague, a Camaldolese monk who went to Lithuania in the early 1400s, not the famous reformer Jerome of Prague who was burned at Constance.</note> King **Wladyslaus** of Poland had sent him with letters of recommendation to Prince **Vytautas** of Lithuania, so that, having expelled false superstition, he might substitute the true religion. Some worshiped domestic serpents, others a sacred and perpetual fire, others a hammer with the sun, and by far the largest part worshiped the forests. He immediately did away with the first three superstitions. In...
