...is the stump <note>original: "ti truncus est" – completing "sancti truncus est" (is the holy stump) from the previous page, a reference to Isaiah 6:13.</note> [of the tree]. He [the prophet] says that this hardening and contradiction will last until the overthrow under Titus and Hadrian occurs; for nothing of a universal overthrow was done until they entered Judea. For in the Babylonian captivity, many remained in the holy land. But if you understand this as being about the Babylonian captivity, to what law was that tenth part converted? Certainly, the Law of Moses lasted from the construction of the second house <note>The Second Temple in Jerusalem.</note> for nearly 500 years, and that tenth part could not have been converted to any other law since there was only one law. It remains, then, that once the Law of Christ was given, that overthrow of affairs was to happen; whence, when they heard and saw Christ, and thought about him, they did not wish to yield to him, but killed him, as the prophets predicted would happen. And with the vengeance that followed, a tenth part remained, which—because it was converted to Christ—was punished in both property and body in the manner of martyrs.

But how great a slaughter of your people was made shortly after Christ and around the time of his death is read in no literary monuments anywhere. For if you, who kept everyone in your records <note>original: "diario"</note> because of your sacred rites, are to be believed, there were lost—in the region of Cyrenaica as well as Egypt, Syria, Cyprus, and Mesopotamia—six million, eight hundred and sixty thousand men <note>original: "sexies decies centena octingenta & sexaginta hominum milia." Postel’s math here calculates the total population based on a "tenth part" remaining.</note>. When the emperors themselves saw this slaughter, according to the accounts of both pagan and Jewish histories, they said that they were not the cause of such a massacre, but that God demanded it. Indeed, it was so great that for seven years and more, from the streams of blood flowing very far and the rotting [remains], the fields and neighboring vines were fertilized. A tenth part of that multitude was 686,000 men—slightly more than those who had gone out of Egypt.

Nor did your wretched nation find it enough to have killed Christ and to have paid such bitter penalties, or to have chosen two Bar Kokhbas <note>Simon bar Kokhba led the Jewish revolt against Rome (132–136 AD). Postel refers to "two," likely following a medieval tradition or conflating different figures.</note>; but under Theodosius, the Jewish people were expelled from Alexandria in great numbers because they incited a faction. They followed Muhammad, that false prophet—a mad, criminal, and wicked man—and provided him with strength; eventually, as a reward, hundreds of thousands of Jews were slaughtered by him and his followers. They gave their faith to a false Moses in Crete <note>A reference to a 5th-century messianic claimant who promised to lead the Jews through the sea, resulting in many drownings.</note>, who, when he promised them a passage through the sea, drowned countless numbers. Because of a violated image of Jesus Christ, they were slaughtered in Constantinople. Because of the shameful insults directed at the sacred host of Jesus Christ, they were expelled from Paris. Because of wicked crimes and unspeakable cruelties in dishonor of Christ, they are exiled from Britain, Spain, and the Gauls [France]. They were recently expelled by the Archbishop of Cologne because every day at dawn they call down curses <note>original: "imprecentur"</note> upon Christ the Redeemer, his mother, and Titus. 

From this, the saying of the prophet is most evident: that their hardening <note>original: "obduratio"</note> is as if eternal. They feel and recognize such great power in Christ that, from the moment they sinned against him, they have never been able to be anything other than servants; and yet they do not cease to curse him daily. Who is so mad and captured in mind that—if his liberty depended on the will of some prince or tyrant—he would not study to win him over with gifts and every kind of service, rather than provoke him? They think Jesus is an avenger and so powerful that he cannot be overcome, and yet they continue to irritate him. What is this if not to fall away into a reprobate sense <note>original: "reprobum abire sensum" – a theological term for a mind that can no longer distinguish right from wrong.</note>? To fight so against the judgment of the soul? 

You owe this to your Rabbis, and to their pride and greed. Because the Lord had freely rebuked them, they conceived such hatred against him that, when they saw he was already held as God among almost all nations because of his holiness and that of his followers, they dared to invert the interpretations of the scriptures for you, to desert the ancient doctors, and—as if that were not enough—to rave everywhere with hatred against him. This has fascinated your eyes, and continues to fascinate them: that you subscribe to their opinions and interpretations rather than to any...

...to any reason and the clearest text. Thus, possessing the "key of knowledge," <note>A reference to Luke 11:52, where Jesus accuses the experts in the law of taking away the key to knowledge.</note> as the saying goes, they neither enter themselves nor permit others to enter. But I return to your rejection. "The sin of Judah," says the prophet of Anathoth <note>original: "Anathotites propheta" — referring to Jeremiah, who was from the town of Anathoth.</note>, "is written with an iron pen and with a diamond point; it is engraved upon the tablet of their heart, and upon the horns of their altars." And a little later: "And you shall be left alone, separated from your heritage that I gave you, and I will make you serve your enemies in a land which you do not know, for you have kindled a fire in my anger, which shall burn forever." This threat cannot be referred to the Babylonian captivity, toward which you distort everything. For that punishment was not eternal, like that which is carved in diamond. Furthermore, that scattering into "lands which you do not know" did not happen then, but rather into Persia, Babylonia, Assyria, and Egypt, since you were already familiar with those regions. It follows, therefore, that this must be understood as the captivity in which you now find yourselves, which will last not only in this life, but also in the future in hell. You ignited this fire by killing Christ Jesus, and it will burn against you forever. You are so far alienated from God—since you preferred to trust in a human rabbi rather than in God—that you experience nothing except eternal captivity and alienation from your own law.

No one can deny that circumcision comes from you; but the ruined Jews, scattered to the furthest lands, keeping only that rite while worshipping various kinds of idols, sacrifice their own sons to demons and offer human blood in abundance, just as you yourselves did in Tophet <note>A location in Jerusalem associated with child sacrifice to the god Moloch; Postel is accusing contemporary Jewish groups of continuing ancient pagan practices.</note>. From where else would that wicked rite have reached those most innocent peoples? And from where would they have obtained circumcision? They owe both rituals to you. O Israelites, would that you were wise and understood, and provided for your end! Certainly God would have mercy on you—though not on all of you. For it will never happen before the Day of Judgment that the stubbornness of your rabbis yields to the truth. They must be compelled by the fury of the Lord and the second coming of Christ, who will gather them for punishment; but the true Israel will be gathered to the Lord. 

For the Jews alone are rejected from the inheritance that was prepared for them. Entire provinces of the Gentiles have come to the Lord Jesus Christ, while the unfaithful Jews refused to receive him, except for a very few half-forced remnants. The prophet Hosea <note>original: "Osea"</note> foretold this. You are not ignorant of the parable at the beginning of his book concerning God and His people. For it is well-proven in many places that the people of Israel are called a "harlot" or a "fornicating woman" who committed adultery in her inventions with "stone and wood" <note>An Old Testament metaphor for idolatry.</note>. Therefore, the prophet speaks of three children: a son, a daughter, and another son born of harlotry. The first condition, in the name of the first son, concerns the crimes that were the cause of the overthrow and the Babylonian captivity, along with the captivity itself, for which God had mercy. The second condition, placed in the name of the daughter, signifies those consumed by the destruction under Titus and Hadrian <note>Roman Emperors who presided over the destruction of Jerusalem (70 AD) and the suppression of the Bar Kokhba revolt (135 AD).</note>; and for this reason, she is called "Without Mercy" <note>The Hebrew name Lo-Ruhamah.</note>. The third son is called "Not My People" <note>The Hebrew name Lo-Ammi.</note>, by which the present condition of the Jews is signified. Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim, was a certain famous and infamous prostitute of that time, in my judgment, whom he took as a type for this wicked people; just as if someone, because of her crimes, had called the Romans "Flora," or the Athenians "Lais" or "Phryne" <note>Famous courtesans (hetairae) of Greek and Roman history.</note>. Truly he says:

> Go, take for yourself a wife of harlotry, and make for yourself children of harlotry, because the land commits harlotry continually, being alienated from the Lord. And he went and took Gomer, daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son, and the Lord said to him (the prophet): Call his name "Seed of God" <note>original: "semen Dei, seu Iezrahel"</note>, or Jezreel, for yet a little while and I will visit the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and I will cause the kingdom of the house of Israel to cease. And on that day I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel. And she conceived again, and bore a daughter, and He said to him: Call her name "Without Mercy," because I will no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, but I will utterly forget them. And...

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD
### PAGE 368

...I will have mercy on the house of Judah, and I will save them in the Lord their God. And I will not save them by bow, or by sword, or by war, or by horses, or by horsemen. <note>original: "Domui Iuda miserebor..." — A quotation from Hosea 1:7.</note> And she weaned her who was called "Without Mercy" <note>original: "absque misericordia" — referring to the daughter of Hosea, Lo-Ruhamah.</note>. And she conceived and bore a son, and He said: "Call his name 'Not My People' <note>original: "Non populus meus" — referring to Lo-Ammi (Hosea 1:9).</note>, because you are not my people, and I will not be yours; and the number of the children of Israel shall be like the sand of the sea which is without measure and innumerable. And it shall be in the place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people,' it shall be said to them, 'Children of the living God.'" And the children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together, and they shall appoint for themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the earth, for great is the day of the seed of God <note>original: "seminis Dei" — Postel translates the Hebrew name 'Jezreel' as 'Seed of God'.</note>. 

Pay attention to every detail, O Jews; pay attention, I beseech you, by the mercy of God, for your salvation is at stake. Each point must be examined diligently, and it will become clear that the prophet wove this as a history of future events. The fornicating <term>synagogue</term> <note>Postel uses the term 'synagogue' here to represent the Jewish religious community collectively, portraying it as an unfaithful spouse to God.</note> named Gomer is clear enough. For although God did every good thing for her, and expected her to produce grapes, she produced wild grapes for Him. He cultivated her like a vineyard, but she produced fruit like a wild field. He held her in the place of a wife, yet she scarcely held God her Father in the place of an adulterer or a rival. Indeed, His Son—whom the ox and the ass recognized in the manger—His own people did not recognize, but killed most cruelly as an enemy. 

The fact that the first child is called the "seed of God" <note>Jezreel</note> is for this reason: that there were still many good people before the captivity and before Christ, and because the "seed" of Jesus Christ was preserved among them, as Isaiah says: "Unless the Lord of hosts had left us a seed" <note>Isaiah 1:9</note>—that is, the future <term>Messiah</term>—"we would have been like Sodom and Gomorrah." And for that reason, the Lord did not exterminate them, but made the kingdom of Judah rest for 70 years under the power of the Assyrians, which happened shortly thereafter, and the strength of Israel was broken in the valley of Jezreel. For because of the display of the treasures of the house of the Lord, punishment came via a foreign king, and it was accelerated, beginning with the Lord's first servants. 

The daughter is called "Devoid of Mercy" <note>Lo-Ruhamah</note> because, after Jesus Christ was killed, everyone was slaughtered to the point of extinction—regardless of age, sex, or rank—so that God was moved by no mercy at all toward that wicked nation. Otherwise, He is usually accustomed to mitigating the fury of even barbarians, lest they rage against the innocent. Thus the Lord wished to sharpen the anger of Titus, Trajan, and Hadrian <note>The Roman emperors responsible for the suppression of the Jewish revolts in 70 AD and 132-135 AD.</note>, so that the Jews might pay the penalty for their murdered Son, and for the sold Just One and brother. 

Indeed, when the Lord allows wars to be launched against nations foreign to God, He employs some mercy, seeing to it that they are preserved in servitude or that the tender age is spared. But nothing similar happened in the destruction of Jerusalem and Betar <note>original: "Bitterensi" — referring to the fortress of Betar, the final battle of the Bar Kokhba revolt.</note>; they perished to a man at the Passover, with sixty times one hundred thousand people <note>Postel estimates 6,000,000 deaths, an exceptionally high figure even by the standards of ancient historiography, intended to emphasize the scale of divine wrath.</note> counted and recorded—a number which God has scarcely permitted to be killed among wicked and idol-devoted nations over many centuries. Certainly Jerusalem "sinned a sin" so great that the whole world could not have committed a greater one; therefore she was turned backward. And so, He will no longer continue to have mercy on you, but will bury you in eternal oblivion.

There follows: "But I will have mercy on the house of Judah, and I will save them in the Lord their God. And I will not save them by bow and sword," etc. The Lord is speaking here—the Lord, I say, the Father and God of heaven and earth. And yet He will save the *true* Judah in the Lord their God—that is, in Christ Jesus the Messiah, who is both man and God. Thus it appears that "Judah" here refers to the Christians, who truly confess God. They have come into great power and are saved without war, without bow, without sword, without horses and horsemen; rather, through the highest patience, innocence, piety, charity, and humility, they have come through deaths and torments to the highest glory and the majesty of all things. 

Israel saw God, but only saw Him; Judah saw and confessed. Not only in this place is "Israel" used for the rejection of the Jews, but the same sentiment is found in Isaiah 49. It says: "And now, says the Lord, who formed me from the womb to be His servant, that I might lead back..."

-># WILLIAM POSTEL, BOOK IV<-
<meta>catchword: middle</meta>

...I will bring back Jacob to him, and Israel shall not be gathered, and I have been glorified in the eyes of the Lord, and my God has become my strength. <note>original: "reducam Iacob ad eum, & Israёl non congregabitur..." — a citation of Isaiah 49:5.</note> In this passage, the Messiah speaks according to his humanity concerning the Father, who glorified him and was his strength, and placed him for the salvation of Judah and all nations. And yet, "Israel shall not be gathered" is a change from the preceding sentence. For God had said: "You are my servant, Israel, for in you I will be glorified." And I, says the Messiah, "have labored in vain; I have spent my strength without cause and for nothing; therefore my judgment is with the Lord, and my work with my God." For Christ came unto his own, and his own received him not; and he did not only labor in vain among them—for Israel was so far from believing in him that they even killed him with a most cruel death—wherefore he says his "judgment" and his "work" regarding Israel is "with God," that is, before the judgment of God the Father (by which He shall judge all), because he would not have judgment and work within Israel.

Therefore, as if the prophet were retracting his statement that he was a servant who was not to be, he said that "Israel shall not be gathered." As for what is written in the <term>Tikkun Soferim</term> <note>Hebrew: "Scribal emendations"—a list of passages in the Hebrew Bible where the scribes traditionally admitted to changing the text.</note>—that is, the corrections of the scribes, or rather their corruptions and depravations—concerning the <term>Qere/Ketiv</term> <note>Literally "read/written"—the Jewish tradition of noting when a word is read differently than it is spelled in the text.</note>, claiming that "not" <note>Hebrew: "lo" (לֹא), spelled with the letter Aleph.</note> should be read as "to him" <note>Hebrew: "lo" (לוֹ), spelled with the letter Vav.</note>, this contradicts the sense of the prophet. For earlier he had called him a servant, and in the second place he wished to change the sentiment; for this reason he says, "and now," just as if he were saying: "Indeed, when I first called you, you were my servant; but now, after the Messiah has labored between you and your people, I certainly say in vain that Israel shall not be gathered." Nevertheless, Christ called certain remnants and "dregs of the poor" from among them and made them most blessed, and in this they were like God, because they lacked nothing and were of benefit to all.

But let us see if we read "to him" <note>original: "lo" with a Vav.</note> instead of "not" <note>original: "lo" with an Aleph.</note>, what sense will result: it would surely be read, "and Israel shall be gathered to itself." See what an opinion overflows from this depraved writing! If it is "gathered to itself," then it will not be "gathered to the Messiah." For he who does anything for himself—that is, for his own interest—does it not for a leader or a prince. Thus, the corrupters of the scriptures fall into Scylla while desiring to avoid Charybdis <note>A classical metaphor for trying to avoid one danger only to fall into a worse one.</note>. For it makes no plain difference whether you say, "when such a prince comes, that people will not be gathered by him," or if you say "they will be gathered to themselves, not to him," for the subjection of that people will always be foreign to him.

Indeed, the word *lo* <note>to him</note> is a pronoun of the third person. But in this place, Christ speaks for himself: so it should have been said *li*, that is, "to me," so that the sense would fit: "but Israel shall be gathered to me." Certainly, if it had ever been written *lo* with a *Vav*, as they claim, they would have made another <term>Qere/Ketiv</term> and changed *lo* into *li*, since the affinity between the letters <term>Yod</term> and <term>Vav</term> is far greater than between <term>Aleph</term> and <term>Vav</term>, which have nothing in common in their shape. How rightly Jeremiah said of the lost scribes: "How do you say, 'We are wise, and the law of the Lord is with us?' Truly the lying pen of the scribes has worked a lie." <note>Jeremiah 8:8.</note> For those <term>Soferim</term> <note>Scribes.</note> who existed after Jesus Christ, whenever they saw things that could manifestly convict them and could be corrupted during transcription, they attempted to invert them all; and this is but one instance out of many.

There is also another, most clearly betraying the craftiness and wickedness of the scribes in Psalm 22, where it is written concerning Christ, things so fitting to the piercing of his feet and hands that if the prophet had seen it present before him, he could not have described it more clearly. For the passage genuinely has it thus: *ka’aru yaday ve-raglay* <note>Hebrew: כארו ידי ורגלי</note>, that is, "They pierced my hands and my feet." The scribes changed "they pierced" <note>ka’aru</note> into "like a lion" <note>ka’ari</note>. But it helps to look into the place more deeply, and to weigh what precedes or follows. Thus the prophet speaks of Christ, when he was driven to the cross by an impious nation: "I am poured out like water, and all my bones are scattered; my heart has become like melting wax in the middle..."

# ON THE CONCORD OF THE WORLD, BOOK IV
<page-num>370</page-num>

...in the midst of me. My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue has cleaved to my jaws, and you have brought me down into the dust of death. For dogs have surrounded me; the council of the wicked has besieged me. They pierced my hands and my feet; I could count all my bones. Indeed, they looked and stared upon me; they divided my garments among themselves, and upon my vesture they cast lots. <note>original: "Aruit tanq̃ testa uirtus mea..." — Postel is quoting Psalm 22 (Vulgate 21):15-19, a passage Christians traditionally view as a precise prophecy of the Crucifixion.</note> How perfectly this prophecy matches, word for word, the death and torments of the blessed Jesus Christ, I will not say now; it will be made clear in its own place. It is agreed between both sides—however much they may twist and deprave the text—that the Psalm is spoken in the person of one placed in great affliction, who complains in one continuous strain about his sufferings. 

Therefore, let even the most stiff-necked of the Jews judge how fittingly it would be said of a man overwhelmed by all these afflictions: "as a lion, my hands and my feet." <note>Postel is attacking the Jewish reading of Psalm 22:16, which uses "Ka-ari" (like a lion) instead of the Christian reading "Ka-aru" (they pierced).</note> What affinity does a most ferocious lion have with the hands and feet of a man who is so crushed by wounds and torments that his bones, separated from their joints, can be numbered? What fierce courage, or whatever else is lion-like, can fit with such hands? Judge, you blind ones; judge whether these things can stand. And finally, loathing the wickedness of your rabbis, come to your senses.

But for the sake of confirming the wickedness of the scribes, one or two more passages must be added. When they were most wicked in offering sacred things, yet so they might not seem to provoke God, they corrupted the passage where they were rebuked by the prophet. For where it was written in the first chapter of Malachi: "And you have polluted it, in that you say: The table of the Lord is contaminated, and what is placed upon it is contemptible to eat. And you said: What a burden this is! And you have grieved me" <note>original: "diuexastis" or "exuflauistis" — meaning to blow or puff at something in contempt.</note>—or "thought me light," or "puffed at me"—that is how it was once written. Because they were rebuked in this place for treating God poorly and mocking Him even while the business of sacrifice was flourishing, the scribes placed <term>otho</term> <note>Hebrew: "it"</note> instead of <term>othi</term> <note>Hebrew: "me"</note>. That is, they wrote "it" instead of "me," as if by swapping a <term>waw</term> <note>the Hebrew letter 'u/o'</note> for a <term>yod</term> <note>the Hebrew letter 'i'</note> in the scriptures, there would be no further injury against God. This is noted by Rabbi Solomon <note>Referring to Rashi (Rabbi Shlomo Itzhaki, 1040–1105), the preeminent medieval Jewish commentator.</note>, and he says it is one of the fifteen words corrected and changed by the scribes. But now there are not fifteen, but five hundred! If they had dared to note these in the text itself as they do in the margin, nothing in the Bibles would have remained intact long ago.

And likewise in the fourth chapter of Hosea, which serves for your reproof: "My people are cut down because they lacked knowledge: because you have rejected knowledge, I will reject you, that you shall not perform the priesthood for me; and you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children. According to their multitude, so they sinned against me; I will change my glory into ignominy." <note>Hosea 4:6-7.</note> Beyond the fact that I must note this corrupted passage, it should not be omitted that they were more wicked as they were more numerous. For it says: "According to their multitude they sinned against me." 

This was truly evident under Bar Kokhba <note>Postel uses "Barcoziba," the derogatory name for Simon bar Kokhba, leader of the Jewish revolt against Rome (132–136 AD).</note>. For in the whole world, in such a narrow place as Judea—which was cut off forty years before—never were four million people seen, much less killed. A little before that wickedness, in the times of Trajan, the Jews had exercised such cruelty against the people of Cyrene that they were not satisfied with slaying 220,000, but they girded themselves with the intestines of the slain, covered their heads with their skins, and even ate their hearts and flesh according to their lust, until they themselves were slain to the number of 260,000. <note>Postel cites a gruesome account of the Kitos War (115–117 AD) likely drawn from the Roman historian Cassius Dio.</note> God had already rejected the priesthood. 

But the corrupted passage goes like this: where it once was <term>kebodi</term> <note>Hebrew: "my glory"</note>, they replaced it with <term>kebodam</term> <note>Hebrew: "their glory"</note>, so they might change the sentence written by God which they feel in fact. For there <term>Kavod</term> <note>Glory</note> is used for the people of Israel, as in many places. Thus the prophet was declaring that it would happen that God would change His "glory"—that is, He would choose another people for His glory, having abandoned that one. Lest God should do this, they thought they could cancel His decree themselves. O men destitute of sense, who even think they can deceive God! In the same sentiment...

### GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK IV
<page-num>371</page-num>

...they changed in the second chapter of Jeremiah, the same word in the same action. Similarly, in Ezekiel 8 <note>original: "Iechezchelís 8" — The Hebrew name for the prophet Ezekiel.</note> they corrupted it thus: "Surely you have seen, son of man. Is it a light thing to the house of Judah that they commit these abominations which they commit here? For they have filled the land with iniquity and have returned to provoke me to anger: and behold, they apply the stench to their nostrils." (It was once written, as *Genesis Rabbah* <note>original: "Beressit raba" — A collection of ancient rabbinic interpretations of the book of Genesis; Postel cites it to show that even Jewish tradition acknowledges these textual variants.</note> notes, "to my nostrils.") "Therefore, I also will act in fury; my eye shall not spare, nor will I have pity; and though they cry to my ears with a loud voice, I will not hear them." The corrupted passage is obvious. For in truth, they were applying the stench of all their vices to the nostrils of the Lord; but they thought they could remove this by the word alone, and so they "applied the stench to their own nostrils." If that stench refers to sins, as it truly does, it cannot be otherwise than that it rises to the nostrils of the Lord (if He had limbs) <note>Postel adds this qualifier to avoid the very anthropomorphism the scribes were supposedly trying to hide: that God does not literally have a physical body.</note>—that is, it rises before and against His majesty. Whence the sense remains plainly the same, whether you scribes like it or not. For whoever sins in whatever way, at the very least, commits a grave offense against himself and God. If he harms a brother, he does an insult to God, wickedness to himself, and injury to the man. 

If it was said of a stench that could be pleasing to man but displeasing to God, or both, why was such a great punishment inflicted upon you for it? Since the times of Simon the Just <note>A famous High Priest in the Second Temple period, often regarded as one of the last of the "Great Assembly."</note> and the holy man, you have had no priest; from the time of the Maccabees, no king; from the time of Christ, no prophecy; and yet you have never ceased to cry out to the Lord, always praying, fasting, and being afflicted, now for fifteen hundred years. Surely God is truthful. He promised you that He would not hear your prayers; the prophets foretold the present condition of your affairs. Meanwhile, the Rabbis miserably lead you on by referring all kinds of captivities to Babylon, not noticing that God heard you from that place and brought you back. 

But yet, the word of God must be entirely fulfilled, which He foretold in almost innumerable places: that at some point He would not hear you, would not gather you, would even reject you, and would not hear your prayers. His word remains forever; it is true. If you believe His words, you must believe them to be true. The Israelites were to be cast out until the final judgment, for then they will be gathered together with every nation to be judged. For your Messiah was not going to permit you to suffer those calamities forever in this life. It is necessary, therefore, that while He reigns among other nations, you suffer those evils which the truthful God willed to be predicted concerning you. For there were two times promised to you: the time of the Law, and the time of the glorious Messiah. Under the Law, it was impossible for you to be so rejected by God that He would never hear you. For otherwise your Law would be evil, and from an evil author, if it were the cause of evils to you; much less should you have suffered under the Law of the Messiah, had you believed in Him, because the Law of Christ was to be of far greater perfection than the Mosaic Law. Otherwise, it would have been superfluous. 

But you keep the Law, as you say, and yet the Law of the Messiah is not yet known to you, and still you are to be forsaken by God. Whence it remains that you suffer those evils because of the slaying of Jesus Christ and the neglect of His Law, against which your *Nizzahon* <note>original: "Nizahon" — Refers to *Sefer Nizzahon*, a medieval Jewish polemical text written to refute Christian interpretations of the Bible.</note> and certain others have dared to exercise a venomous tongue; you subscribe to them out of obstinacy rather than truth, because they applaud your vices. You shall have no other Messiah, O Jews, than the Antichrist, who will fight diametrically—just as you seek—against the Law of Jesus Christ. This captivity of yours has already lasted since Christ was slain, as I said; from there your calamity took its origin, not to be ended before the Day of Judgment, except for a few years before that day in which you may join yourselves to the Son of Perdition. Had God not been most incensed against you, there would not have been added to all those miseries which have fallen upon you from every side such a famous proof of His wrath under Julian the Apostate. <note>Roman Emperor (r. 361–363) who attempted to rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem to undermine Christian prophecy; the project failed, reportedly due to fire and earthquakes.</note> For when your ancestors—to whom we were an object of

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD
<page-num>372</page-num>

...wishing to please out of hatred for us <note>Postel refers here to the Roman Emperor Julian "the Apostate" (r. 361–363 AD), who attempted to restore paganism and supported the rebuilding of the Jewish Temple to undermine Christian claims of its permanent destruction.</note>, they approached him. He granted them the opportunity to restore the Temple of Jerusalem, so that they might rebuild it with your people. With mortar tempered, stones gathered, materials entirely prepared, and even the trenches excavated for laying the foundations, suddenly—on the day before the first stone was to be laid—such a great earthquake arose that it overturned not only the site of the Temple, but a very large part of Aelia <note>original: "Heliæ" — Aelia Capitolina, the name given to Jerusalem by Emperor Hadrian.</note>. Above all, it destroyed the porticoes, in which an innumerable multitude of Jews, having traveled from everywhere, perished. On the following day, a ball of fire came out of the workmen’s hut during the daylight, which, wandering many times through the whole city and repeatedly returning to the same spot, consumed as many Jews as it encountered. Many sought safety in flight, acting as messengers of such a great disaster. So that it would be clear that these things happened by the will of Christ and not by chance, all their clothes were imprinted with the sign of the cross in such a way that no skill could wash them away. When they saw all these things, almost all the Jews in the whole of Syria became Christians. This is written not only in our histories, but in those of the heathens. Your rabbis would not wish to reveal these things to you, lest you come to your senses.

I return now for a little while to certain scribal emendations <note>original: "*ticun*" — referring to the Tikkun Soferim, or "Emendations of the Scribes."</note>. What would the scribes not have dared to invert? Rabbi Akiba <note>original: "Rabi Atriba" — Postel likely misread or misspelled the name of the famous 2nd-century sage Rabbi Akiba ben Joseph.</note>, the "Light of Israel" as you believe, the greatest of your ten ancestors who were afflicted with various punishments by Hadrian, and in whose memory you celebrate the Fast of Atonement <note>original: "ieiunium propitiationis" — referring to the 10th of Tishrei (Yom Kippur), though the "Ten Martyrs" are specifically commemorated in the liturgy of that day.</note> every year on the tenth day of Tishrei—he, inverting the scriptures, read in favor of the followers of Bar Kokhba <note>original: "*Barcozibarum*" — referring to the leader of the Jewish revolt against Rome (132–136 AD). His name, Bar Kokhba, means "Son of a Star," but his critics called him Bar Koziba, "Son of a Lie."</note> that which is written in Numbers 24: *A star shall rise out of Jacob* <note>original: "Orietur stella ex Iacob"</note>. This is a passage concerning the coming of the Messiah. He asserted it was written incorrectly; where the word was "star" <note>original: "cochab"</note>, he said there should be placed "lie" <note>original: "cozab"</note>—that is, in place of a star, a lie. You have this written in the book *Ta'anit* <note>original: "Taamith"</note>, in the chapter beginning "Three Chapters," and in *Lamentations Rabbah* <note>original: "Echara-bati"</note>. That Messiah was worthy of your unhappiness, both in fact and in name, because you have always preferred the false to the true.

But I wonder less that the scribes and doctors permitted themselves this in the Law of God, since they wanted even servants to have that right. It is written in the Talmud in the book *Yebamot* <note>original: "Iebamoth"</note>, in the chapter on heretics <note>original: "cap. haeret."</note>, that Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Simeon: "It is good that you should remove one letter from the Law so that the name of Heaven might be sanctified in public"—that is, it is good to overturn the Law of God and its meaning to please men. Thus in Hosea 9 <note>original: "Hosa 9."</note>, where it was written: *And my flesh from them*, they wrote: *and when I shall depart from them*, and so on. Innumerable things have been corrupted and changed so that posterity might not recognize the truth. 

But I return to the exposition of the first chapter of Hosea, from which I had digressed to the scribal emendations. We have already noted two places where Israel shall not be gathered. There followed: *And she weaned her who is without mercy.* What is this "weaning"? A slaughter. For by the benefit of nature and the most excellent gift of God, which is life, they were despoiled (as I said) within the 140th year from the birth of Christ, to the number of one million, eight hundred and sixty thousand <note>original: "sexies decies centena 860000"</note> Jewish people; and scarcely a tenth part was saved, which embraced the holy life under the law of Christ—concerning whose holiness one may read in the works of your countryman Philo. The son born in the third place from the fornicating Jewish race was called *Not my people* <note>original: "nõ populus meus" — referring to the name "Lo-Ammi" in Hosea 1:9.</note>, because neither the Jews born since the time of the destructions are the people of God, nor is God their God, although they always occupy themselves with fasts and ceremonies. God is no longer their God any more than He is the God of the heathens and idolaters, because for as long as the law of Jesus Christ has endured—namely, fifteen hundred years—they have been alienated from God, and they have no Republic, miracle, or prophet. With those people proscribed, the prophet now places the true Israel in the place of the false substitute; these are the Christians, innumerable throughout the whole world. Where previously they were not the people of God—that is, outside the Holy Land—there they are called the people of God. They are truly the seed of Abraham, surpassing the sand of the sea. With them, on the day of judgment, all the elect from the Jews and all nations shall be joined, and they shall ascend into heaven with Christ as their leader, and there shall be *one fold and one shepherd.*

-># WILLIAM POSTEL, BOOK IV.<-
<page-num>373</page-num>

...that great day of the seed of God. You have seen the tragedy of your unhappiness depicted with perfect precision <note>original: *ad unguem* — literally "to the fingernail," a Latin idiom used by craftsmen to describe work so smooth that a thumbnail could not feel a joint or flaw.</note>, and the series of events leading even to the end of the world. The **False Israel** will be estranged from God until the very end of the world; the **True Israel**, following Christ and keeping his precepts, shall live for eternity, without any care for human affairs, except insofar as they serve the glory of God, their own innocence, and charity toward their brother. *Some rely on chariots, and others on horses: but we shall be magnified in the name of the Lord.* <note>Postel is quoting Psalm 20:7 (or 19:8 in the Vulgate numbering).</note>

If the <term>Messiah</term> <note>Postel uses the Latin *Messias*, referring to the "Anointed One" expected by the Jews.</note> you expected was greater than Moses—as he certainly was (otherwise it would have been pointless for God to have promised him for so long unless he were better)—then he was going to give you a far more perfect state than you ever had before. Yet, in the bounty of heaven and soil, in the abundance of wealth and every kind of bodily happiness, no nation was ever more fortunate than you were under the judges, David, and Solomon. For in the books of Kings it is said there was such an abundance of gold, silver, and gems as there was of dust or stones.

If this material wealth is the <term>highest good</term> <note>original: *summum bonum* — the supreme goal of human life in philosophical ethics.</note> for you, then certainly **Solomon** was your Messiah, because under that king and his kingdom, nothing was ever more flourishing or abundant. Yet that same man, so wealthy, who had seen to it that riches from the whole world were carried into the Syrian world <note>original: *orbem Syrum* — Postel uses this term to refer to the Levant/Land of Israel.</note>, wished to testify to you in a dedicated work <note>Postel refers here to the Book of Ecclesiastes, traditionally attributed to Solomon.</note> that in the abundance of wealth, gold, silver, provinces, and dominion, there is nothing—beyond what is necessary for use—but **vanity and affliction of spirit.** He meant that momentary mortals are tortured in vain when they neglect heavenly things for these.

Since these things are vain and cannot satisfy a man or make him blessed in every part, it remains that the blessedness promised by God cannot consist in them. For since God is the highest wisdom, He would not place the highest good in something so utterly vain. Therefore it follows that the happiness promised to come under the Messiah was not subject to this luck or the vanity of corruptible things. The Supreme Giver must give something solid.

Therefore, the highest happiness in the whole world is this: the contempt for all material things out of love for God; to marvel at none of those things the world considers supreme; to live as if having all things while possessing nothing; to be born for others, not for oneself; to command one’s pleasures, to overthrow vices, and to avoid whatever fights against a man’s true goal while following those things that lead toward it. 

But all these things **Christ our God** taught us. From this it is clear that He and His precepts are the highest good in this life, and the way to the life to come. Accept, therefore, O Israel, Him whom you have already rejected enough; accept Christ. He is not angry with individuals: He wishes for the old nation and the earthly republic to be lost, but not the man. You live by His spirit, even though you have lived without His religion. You shall be victors—not as bloodthirsty men or destroyers of nature (which is most unlike God), but similar to Him in all things, as much as a man can attain by God's grace.

The law is different now than when you first entered the Holy Land. Then, the way for religion had to be opened by the sword; now, there is a need for the contempt of all things (except for God and one's brother). For a man is far more perfect who restrains his appetite than one who is carried away by every desire—which are often empty and leave nothing to a man but torment and misery. A peasant is happier obtaining only the bread required by the laws of necessity than a prince, or any glutton or gormandizer, who keeps himself and innumerable servants busy for the sake of his throat alone. In the conditions of birth, usage, and death they are equal, except for the fact that he who has more squanders far more than he who has little. He has everything who has God as his Father, who desires nothing for himself, and who treats every man as a brother. Such a man could never be in want, for he consumes little and places every man in the position of a brother.

But I wish to dwell further on your rejection, so that you may completely lay aside the false hope of a coming Messiah, in which your **Rabbis** falsely hold you, and turn to Jesus Christ before the day [of the Lord] comes...

-># ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD<-
<page-num>374</page-num>

...of the Lord, great and terrible, you should return, and lay aside the vain concern for greater wealth and kingdoms, nor should you ever think that Judea is to be possessed by you again. For God grants greater kingdoms than these. Moses knew it would happen that many of yours, when Christ came, would contradict him, and would be consumed by divine vengeance rather than human force.

<margin>Deuteronomy 18</margin>
“And it shall be,” he says, “that whoever does not hear the words of that prophet” (the one whom God, as the author of the law, was to send like unto Moses), “I will be the avenger,” says the Lord. <note>Postel is citing the prophecy in Deuteronomy 18:18-19, which Christians traditionally interpreted as referring to Jesus.</note>

<margin>Isaiah 9</margin>
A very small part believed; the majority refused. In Isaiah 9, after he spoke of the dominion of Jesus Christ and the stubbornness of the Jews in Samaria, he says: “And the Lord will destroy from Israel head and tail, branch and reed in a single day. The venerable elder himself is the head, and the lying prophet is the tail.” These are the times of **Bar-Kokhba** <note>original: *Barcozbæ*. Simon bar Kokhba led a major Jewish revolt against Rome (132–136 CE) and was hailed by some as the Messiah, a claim Postel views as the "lying prophet."</note>. A little later: “The Lord will not rejoice over its young men, and will not have mercy on the widows, because impiety is kindled like a fire.”

<margin>Deuteronomy 28</margin>
This threat dates from the time of the Messiah’s coming. Moses had predicted these very same future events in Deuteronomy 28.

<margin>Isaiah 27</margin>
Isaiah 27: “Therefore he who made him [Israel] will not have mercy on him, and he who formed him will not spare him.” He is not speaking of the Babylonian captivity here, because after the 70th year He did spare them; therefore, this must be understood as referring to this current captivity. And likewise, the same prophet says in chapter 63: “Why have you hardened us so that we would not fear you? And we have become as if you had never ruled over us.” This also refers to this long-lasting rejection, which is certainly longer than the entire duration of the Law itself. And meanwhile, the <term>Rabbis</term> <note>Jewish religious teachers and scholars.</note> deceive you with various expected dates for the end of your exile. But the Jew will object: “If God hardens us, what can we do? We cannot resist.” He never takes away **free will**, or human protections, but He denies grace so that man may see for himself that he can do nothing on his own. Daily you hear the truth, yet you remain obstinate, just as you hardly believed God even when the miracles were present under Moses.

<margin>Jeremiah 15</margin>
Thus God wishes to show Himself angry with you in Jeremiah chapter 15, so much so that He says He will not hear even the intercession of Moses or Samuel on your behalf: “Because the soul of the Lord is no longer toward this people, He wants them to be cast out and to depart.” If therefore He wants them cast out and to depart, and is not willing to hear even the intercessions of the holiest men for them—whereas they *did* return from Babylon after seventy years—it follows that He is speaking of this final rejection. There is nothing in the prophets that is not full of your dispersion. Are you not the most abundant witnesses to the calamity of Jerusalem, which was related by Jeremiah

<margin>Jeremiah ch. 14 & 17</margin>
in chapters 14 and 17, as if he had been present there? And meanwhile, God does not want prayer to be offered for that people for their own good. Scripture mentions your stubbornness and hardening in many places, but especially that same Jeremiah

<margin>Jeremiah ch. 7</margin>
in chapter 7, where he also predicts the eternal desolation of Jerusalem to come, because they refused to hear the truth.

<margin>Hosea ch. 9</margin>
Hosea chapter 9, speaking in the person of God: “Because of their wickedness I will drive them out of my house, and I will no longer continue to love them.” You were therefore destined to be, during the time of either law, without the love of God—not under the Old Law, as I said (which you keep so precisely <note>original: *ad unguem* — literally "to the fingernail," meaning perfectly or exactly.</note>), but under the Law of the Messiah, which you rejected. A little later in the same place: “They shall bear no fruit; even if they give birth, I will kill the beloved of their womb. My God will cast them away” (God says this concerning Christ) “because they did not hear him, and they shall be wanderers among the nations.” Do you hear, O Jews, that you are, and have been for **1542 years** now <note>This helps date the text to approximately 1542–1544 CE.</note>, wanderers because you did not hear your God, the Messiah. That is the sole cause of your long-lasting wandering. Nowhere from that time have you been able to have the right of acquiring land. Nor has it been permitted for you to hold a magistracy or a republic in the places where you live, ever since the death of Christ. You serve among all nations, and you shall continue to serve unless you repent.

<margin>Amos ch. 5</margin>
Again, Amos chapter 5: “Hear this word, for I raise a lamentation over you, O house of Israel. The virgin of Israel has fallen, and she shall not rise again; she is cast down upon her land, and there is no one to raise her up.” This takes away the hope of a worldly empire and a bloodthirsty Messiah.

-># THE FOURTH BOOK OF GUILLAUME POSTEL<-
<page-num>375</page-num>

In your own traditions within the *Seder Olam* <note>original: *Seden holam*; a 2nd-century CE Hebrew subterranean chronology</note>, it is established (from the book *Yebamot* <note>original: *Iebamot*; a tractate of the Talmud dealing with levirate marriage</note>, in the chapter concerning brothers) that the children of Israel entered and possessed the Holy Land twice, but that it is not permitted to return there a third time. Truly, if one wished to select all the passages regarding your rejection, it would be necessary to examine the whole of Holy Scripture, especially the prophetic books; we must come to the causes of such a great evil, which have been declared so often. Isaiah, Chapter 65:

> Because I called and you did not answer, I spoke and you did not hear, and you did evil in my eyes, and you chose the things that I did not want: therefore, thus says the Lord God: behold, my servants shall eat and you shall be hungry; my servants shall drink and you shall be thirsty; my servants shall rejoice, and you shall be confounded. Behold, my servants shall praise with exultation of heart, and you shall cry out for sorrow of heart, and you shall wail for the affliction of spirit; and you shall leave your name as a curse to my chosen ones, and the Lord God shall slay you, and he shall call his servants by another name, and whoever blesses himself in that land shall bless himself in the true God, etc.

All these things were spoken concerning the second calling, which was made by Jesus Christ. For if they were spoken of the calling made by Moses or the prophets, there was no other people of God under that Law except Israel. For although God afflicted His people with various disasters and captivities, He never took up another nation in their place until the scribe and the leader "departed from the thigh" <note>A reference to the prophecy in Genesis 49:10, suggesting the Jewish right to rule ended with the coming of Christ</note>. Thus, it remains that this must necessarily be understood as being because they did not listen to Christ. For those who consented to his death have paid the most bitter penalties; those who did not listen have been dispersed.

And then the name of "Christians" was made great and glorious because of their remarkable innocence, charity, and piety. Truly, the name "Jew" or "Israelite" has become so reproachful that even the pagans, and those foreign to our religion, can today hardly bear to hear the word "Jew" without resentment. Christians, however, abound in a great plenty of things—not because of wealth, but because of sobriety and charity (I do not wish to have the lives of many people thrown back at me, since the Law itself is not at fault); if they abound, they abound for God; if they lack, they lack for God. For the whole aim of Christ is that God should be everything to us, that man should be content with necessities, thinking he possesses nothing, but reaching toward the Highest Good, God Himself, aiming his sight as if at a fixed target. 

The Jews, with their Messiah, seek empires, the slaughter of many men, famous victories, the most ample wealth, the highest honors, and other vain things in which Satan plays with the present world. For them, their Messiah—even if he were a god—would not be enough. But in this place, you ought to note carefully that we are called the "True Israel," our name having been changed to Christians, while your name has been cast out. I know your condition among the Muhammedans <note>Muslims</note>; certainly, a dog is held in almost higher esteem than a Jew; indeed, the Jew is exposed as prey for everyone. Thus your name is execrable and hateful. In this way, for fifteen hundred years now, God has been teaching you that His word is most true, and that you have changed the truth into a lie. You have not only failed to listen to Christ, the true God and man, but you killed him, and you chose the two sons of lies, the **Bar-Kokhbas** <note>original: *Barcozibas*; referring to Simon bar Kokhba, who led a failed revolt against Rome in 132 CE and was initially hailed as the Messiah</note>, and made them your Messiahs. 

There is another cause: because they thought the Messiah would belong only to the Jews, and they suspect salvation comes from them alone. Therefore they object: "If the Messiah had come, Israel would have been gathered." They see the whole world believing except for themselves, and yet they refuse to yield. He came first among them, but there, exposed before the impious, the Truth paid the penalty where he ought to have been received. 

The Holy Spirit is the author, through Daniel (whom he places among the prophets in the chapter *Megillah Nikret* <note>meaning "the Scroll is read"</note>, in the book of *Megillah* <note>a Talmudic tractate</note>, chapter 9), that the death of Christ was the cause of the desolation and that it preceded it. "Know therefore," he says, "and consider diligently: from the edict that Jerusalem be built until Christ the leader, there shall be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks, and again it shall be built..."

-># ON THE CONCORD OF THE WORLD<-

...the street and the walls shall be built even in a time of distress; and after sixty-two weeks <note>Postel is referencing the "Seventy Weeks" prophecy in Daniel 9, where "weeks" represent seven-year periods (hebdomads)</note> the **Messiah** shall be killed, and not for himself—that is, not by his own fault, but by ours; not for his own sake, but for us. And the people of a leader who is to come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary, and its end shall be devastation, and after the end of the war, a decreed or perpetual desolation. But he shall confirm a covenant with many for one week, and in the middle of that week, the victim and the sacrifice shall fail; and because of the summit of abominations, every man shall be astonished, and the desolation shall endure even until the consummation and the end. Nothing clearer than these words can be brought forward to show that the Messiah was to be killed before the desolation. From the command and edict for the rebuilding of the temple, which was published in the 20th year of the reign of **Artaxerxes Longimanus** <note>Artaxerxes I, a Persian King who reigned c. 465–424 BCE; his decree is often used as the starting point for Messianic calculations</note>, until the death of Christ, there are 62 and a half weeks. And from the death of Christ to the overturning of the second temple, there are 7 and a half weeks. Or, as others calculate it: from the 20th year of Longimanus to Alexander there are 132 years; from then until Christ, 322 years. If you add to these the 30 years of Christ’s life, 484 years arise, which is 69 weeks. In the middle of the seventieth week, Christ died, and then, as the true Sacrifice arrived, the old one perished. However one considers the matter, the 70 weeks of years are the 490 years of the duration of the second house <note>the Second Temple</note> and from the times of the captivity. Therefore, when Christ came, many hoped, about 50 years earlier, that they might be able to see him. Yet he was unknown to all, because he sought nothing earthly, wished to possess nothing, and embraced no other sovereignty than that over blessed souls. For this reason, he was despised by all, because he did not savor earthly things. But the impious and treacherous rabbis prefer to call certain others "Messiahs" here in Daniel, rather than acknowledge the true one. Yet the heart of the matter concerns this one who was killed, and the result is the eternal desolation of Jewish affairs—which ought not to have happened unless the greatest offense against God, than which none is greater, had been committed. If the tradition of the house of **Elijah** <note>original: *Hele*; a Talmudic tradition dividing world history into 6,000 years</note> is true—concerning the six thousand years, of which two thousand are without the law, two thousand under the law, and two thousand under the Messiah—how is it that fifteen hundred years of the Messiah’s own time have already passed away? By this reasoning, barely five hundred years would remain for him; what could be more absurd? Indeed, when the Syrian state perished, the Law of Moses perished. Let them interpret it how they will; certainly, the Messiah had to be killed by them before the dispersion, as will be clear in the Gospel prophecy. At one and the same time, a foreign king <note>King Herod the Great, who was of Edomite/Idumean descent</note>, having killed all men of royal blood and removed all priests (except the few who felt he was destined to rule), showed that what **Jacob** had said in his blessings concerning the future Messiah was fulfilled: namely, that he had come who was to be sent. Or as **Kimhi** <note>David Kimhi (1160–1235), a famous Jewish commentator and grammarian</note> explains: his son—that is, the son of the virgin—when the scepter and the lawgiver had failed. For although the kingdom was taken away during the Babylonian captivity, nevertheless the *Mehochechim* <note>original: *Mehhochechim*; Hebrew for 'lawgivers' or 'scribes'</note>—that is, the legislators and wise interpreters of the law—were never lacking, nor were the prophets. For **Jeremiah** and **Daniel**, along with many others, were led there. Furthermore, although the power of the scepter was removed for 70 years, the royal lineage was not cut off to the point of extermination as it was under Herod. At that time, the blessing upon the people in the name of **Yahweh** <note>original: יהוה (The Tetragrammaton)</note> ceased. While **Simeon**, who had received Jesus himself as the Messiah at the purification, was administering the priesthood, the lot was still drawn to the right side <note>A reference to a Temple ritual where a "right-hand" lot was considered a sign of divine favor</note>. Upon his death, the eternal flame failed, and 49 years before the destruction of the temple, it grew weak. Simeon also predicted his own death, because every day a man clothed in white garments entered the temple with him, visible only to him; but in the year he died, his companion entered with him clothed in a black garment. These things are in the Talmud, in the book *Yoma*, in the chapter <insert>The Mixing in the Urn</insert> <note>original Hebrew OCR: טרת נקלש; likely a corruption of *Tarof Ba-Kalpi*, the third chapter of Tractate Yoma</note>. There follows also this, word for word: "Our masters have handed down that for forty years before the destruction of the second house, the lot of the Lord did not ascend into the right hand, nor was the tongue of brightness <note>the scarlet thread used in the Yom Kippur ritual which miraculously turned white if God forgave Israel's sins</note> turned to whiteness, nor the light...

<header>WILLIAM POSTEL, BOOK 4</header>

...the evening light <note>The text likely completes the word "lumen" (light) from the previous page</note> was burning, and the gates of the temple opened by themselves, until **Rabbi Yohanan ben Zakkai** <note>A primary Jewish sage of the late Second Temple era</note> rebuked them, saying: "Temple, temple, why do you destroy yourself? For I know of you that your end shall be destruction. For concerning you **Zechariah** prophesied in the 11th chapter, saying: *Open your doors, O Lebanon, and let fire devour your cedars.*" <note>original: "Aperi Libane portas tuas, & deuoret ignis cedros tuos."</note> These things are from the **Jerusalem Talmud**. The prophecy of Zechariah is most clear; for the gates of the temple were constructed from the cedars of Lebanon, and the fire set by the soldiers of **Vespasian** and **Titus** forty years after the death of Jesus Christ devoured those cedars and the other temple materials composed of that same wood. In countless places, as is noted in **Bereshit Rabbah** <note>A midrashic commentary on Genesis</note>, the council of the 71 judges <note>The Sanhedrin, the highest judicial council in ancient Israel</note> sat outside the **Gazit** <note>The Chamber of Hewn Stone in the Temple</note> for forty years before the temple was destroyed. From there, the judges, having been driven out, were accustomed to wear sackcloth upon their flesh, and they pulled out their beards and hair, saying: "Woe to us, for the scepter has departed from Judah from us, and the Messiah, son of David, has not yet come."

And so those judges, expelled from the **Gazit** where they dealt with capital cases, sat for forty years in **Hamith** <note>Likely referring to the "Shops" (Hanuth) on the Temple Mount</note>, another place where they never again judged criminal matters. Let the book **Baba Batra**, chapter *The Partners* <note>original: "Hassutaphin"</note>, be read. There, worthy of reading, things will be found concerning the removal of both powers, the judicial and the royal: how, after all the heads of royal blood were killed, **Herod** preserved only **Mariamne** as his wife, so that he might be called the heir of the royal house of the **Hasmoneans**—that is, the **Maccabees**—who were also called the *Heads of the Exile* <note>original: "Rasse galliot," referring to the Resh Galuta or Exilarchs</note>. But when Mariamne, scorning the condition of a slave, threw herself down <note>committed suicide</note> by the command of her husband, he took care that she be preserved at home for seven years, seasoned with spices and anointed, for the sake of retaining the royal inheritance. Indeed, with all the judges—whom they call by the title of honor **Rabbanim**—having been removed from the midst, he saved only one, whom the Talmud calls **Bava ben Buta**. **Josephus**, who agrees in reporting these things, calls him simply **Baba**. Although this man had previously predicted the kingdom for Herod, Herod nevertheless gouged out his eyes, while keeping his children in prison. One man, Bava, could not choose fellow judges to survive from such a great senate, since they were not legitimately elected except by five men from the fellowship. Furthermore, Herod chose others for the senate, and he wished them to depend upon him, even having removed the sacred books. He appointed a foreigner, **Ananelus**, as High Priest, and changed things both sacred and profane, so that no traces of the ancient condition of things might remain. In the **Babylonian Talmud**, in the chapter *Seven Days* <note>original: "Sibeat lamim," likely referring to tractate Shabbat or Yoma</note>, it is read that forty years before the overturning of the second temple, the ten miracles that were accustomed to occur in the temple ceased; they can be read there. To this is added that saying of **David**: *We have not seen our signs, nor is there any prophet further.* <note>Psalm 74:9</note>

**Rabbi Moses Hadarshan** <note>An 11th-century preacher and commentator from Narbonne</note> explains that passage in the last part of **Isaiah**: *Before she travailed, she brought forth; and before her pain came, she was delivered of a male child. Who has heard such a thing? Who has seen such things?* <note>Isaiah 66:7-8</note> He explains it in this way: Before the one who would subjugate Israel into the final servitude was generated, the Redeemer was born. Do you see how all things agree? Before Titus was born, the Messiah was born. Read concerning the Arab who, calling the Messiah prophetically **Menahem son of Hezekiah** <note>original: "Menahem filium Chiztriæ," meaning the Comforter, son of the Strength of God</note>, said he was born in **Bethlehem of Judea**. This tradition is in **Bereshit Rabbah**, and even if spoken by a stranger, it is nonetheless consistent with the truth. Mention of him is made in **Eikhah Rabbah** <note>A midrashic commentary on Lamentations</note>. If indeed Christ has not come, he is never going to come, since he was to be born in Bethlehem, which has been completely destroyed. Let at least **Suetonius**, a pagan author and as much a stranger to you as to us, provide you with faith, writing thus: "There had spread," he says, "throughout the entire Orient an old and established opinion, that it was in the fates that at that time, those proceeding from Judea should gain the mastery of things." <note>A famous quote from Suetonius' "Life of Vespasian" regarding Messianic expectations</note> The opinion was certain and established at that time. Concerning the time, he agrees with us, and with your own people. But he uses the insane interpretation of the Jews, which in these matters is corrupt, looking for a prosperity and supreme happiness after the manner of cattle...

<header>ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD</header>

...who place their **highest good** in such things. Judging from their own inclinations, they believed that the Son of God would be born to bring about the ruin of the whole world so that one nation alone might enjoy luxury and empire. Because of this, they were never able, or perhaps never willing, to recognize His supreme humility and His benevolence toward all people, nor could they accept one so humble once they had recognized Him. And yet, as I have taught from the beginning, even if Jesus Christ had been only a man, He would have appeared most like God by His works. Possessing absolutely nothing, He bestowed all things that were within Him. For as I noted in the first book regarding the merchants driven from the temple, if He had come to amass wealth, He could have acquired as much power as He could travel through; indeed, without any change, He could have been the arbiter of the entire world in a moment—just as He will be terrible at His second coming to all those who despised Him. For since they believed Him to be the most excellent of mortals (even if they refuse to believe He is God), they should have judged His power not as similar to that of one or another tyrant or destroyer of the world, but as superior to all. What, then, does this "dross of the world" <note>original: "fex orbis"; referring to worldly power or perhaps the lower classes who followed him, likely used here to contrast worldly filth with divine dignity</note> contribute to His dignity, that a man no less than God should be occupied with it? Avarice has destroyed you, O Jews; stubbornness has destroyed you; the hatred of truth has destroyed you; the cunning of the rabbis has destroyed you. One thing I dare to say: if God willed it, He could indeed bring the whole world under one empire in a single blink of an eye. However, He could not retain it for even an hour so long as <term>Free Will</term> <note>original: "libertas arbitrij"</note> remains. For since the heart of man is "prone to evil from his youth," <note>A reference to Genesis 8:21</note> no laws of justice can so restrain him—even with a prince present and punishment looming—that he obeys every command in all things. 

Of this fact, no clearer evidence can be given than that found among you. For when you saw the presence of God in the lightning, the flashes, the darkness, and the miracles, and heard the voices—when you could not even bear to look upon the radiant face of your leader <note>Referring to Moses after he descended from Sinai</note>—you nevertheless dared to prefer a Golden Calf, obtained at the great expense of your own gold, over God. Why should I mention the sedition of **Korah, Dathan, and Abiram**? <note>Biblical figures who rebelled against Moses' leadership and were swallowed by the earth</note> The gaping of the earth is still an argument for that punished crime. Nor was this vice found only among the wicked. **Miriam** sinned and was struck with leprosy; the Levites sinned. Unless God had taken away your choice as if you were stones, He could not have bound you to a stricter empire than when He was present with Moses. What do you think would have happened if you had been a hundred thousand miles away from that place, and that divine food of manna had been lacking? What crimes would you not have committed? 

Examples of human recklessness are frequent. **Hannibal** lost as many things while living as he had sought to gain. Yet he had joined Africa to Spain, Italy, and a part of the Gauls. **Alexander the Macedonian** was warned by a most wise Indian <note>Likely a reference to the Gymnosophists or "naked philosophers" encountered by Alexander</note> of the signs of human recklessness and persistence. A dry cowhide was brought before him; when Alexander pressed down on one edge, the other parts rose up; when he pressed the middle, all the outer edges lifted. By these signs, they taught him that only those things which are closest to power, and which correspond to it in proportion, are truly subject; everything else is in constant motion. And although the great nobles do not immediately defect from a prince, they nevertheless crush the subjects with such plundering that a rebellion, which does not start at the "head," is stirred up by the "plundered members" <note>A metaphor for the common people suffering under corrupt officials</note>.

What shall I say of that **Iron Scythian** <note>Referring to Tamerlane (Timur), the Central Asian conqueror</note> who, a few centuries before our time, subdued the most famous and ferocious parts of Asia: Scythia, Iberia, Armenia, Persia, Media, the Syrias, and Asia Minor in just a few years? Yet he met the same end for his empire and his life. Let us look at the most celebrated power of the whole world, the **Romans**. As soon as they attained the greatest and most distant provinces, they began to struggle under their own weight, nourishing both foreign and domestic fires, and those things they had gained with such great difficulty...

...to preserve it, and every day to lose it. But the Messiah’s empire is eternal, and of his kingdom there shall be no end. Otherwise, he would have been the most unhappy of men—he who, immersed in the vain cares of this life, would have held his "highest happiness" in that which even many of the most ambitious princes have judged to be misery. 

From being a most wealthy king, Attalus <note>Attalus III, the last king of Pergamon, famously bequeathed his entire kingdom to the Roman Republic in 133 BCE, preferring a life of study over the burdens of rule.</note> became a simple man of the countryside. Diocletian, otherwise a most wicked man, preferred a private life to the empire <note>The Roman Emperor Diocletian famously abdicated the throne to retire to his palace at Spalatum to grow cabbages.</note>. If I remember correctly, Tiberius used to say of the crown, whenever he received the ornaments of empire: "O tiara, more unhappy than happy, you who alone carry so many cares!" Since the Messiah ought to be blessed in every respect, and rule the entire world forever until he delivers the kingdom to God the Father, he ought not to have been "happy" with that kind of happiness which contains within itself the greatest unhappiness. 

But you will object to me the insults against Jesus committed by you: for which I will satisfy you, after I have brought forth the true cause of your present rejection <note>original: "reprobationis"; a theological term for being cast off by God</note> and joined it to the preceding arguments.

Amos, in the second chapter, has it thus: 

> Thus says the Lord: For three crimes of Israel I will turn them back, and for the fourth I will not turn them back, because they sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of shoes. <note>Amos 2:6</note>

The cause of this is the selling of Christ Jesus. Your more recent commentators, as they pervert everything, explain this as being about "respect of persons" <note>legal partiality or favoritism</note> and the bribery of judges in trials, as if that were the world’s greatest crime. Others explain it as the selling of Joseph by his brothers; but these sins, even joined together, would not be worthy of eternal proscription and rejection, since the crime of selling Joseph was expiated by the afflictions suffered in Egypt, as your more sensible interpreters agree. 

As for corruption in judgments, although it is a very great crime, many more serious things can be committed. For this reason, murders are punished far more severely anywhere among nations than thefts; and thefts, when they seem to have a pretext—as among the powerful—although they are greater, are not therefore thought the greatest crime, because the sin is against property. Certainly in the whole world, even among the wise, that disease of greed blinds judges; yet God does not adjudge perpetual punishments where these things happen—and they will happen continually as long as the world lasts. God knows how to lure the powerful with the splendor of fleeting things, so they might adorn themselves and their kin with titles; He knows that a loss (though he who takes it away is most unjust) is sometimes made useful, so that those whom the love of possessing had occupied might return to Him. He knows how to give the greatest gains from those things we are accustomed to call "losses," since man’s goal is not in external things; both the prince and the peasant, or the needy, can satisfy their necessary needs. 

The sin of Israel was far more serious, such that it merited eternal exile. But our interpreter will be the Emperor Hadrian, who explained this in a dialogue held with ten "great men" (as you call them) <note>This refers to the "Ten Martyrs," a famous Jewish tradition about ten rabbis executed by the Romans, often set during the reign of Hadrian.</note>. If someone is found who has stolen a soul from his brother who is of the children of Israel, and has betrayed him and sold him, what shall be the penalty?" # ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

...you. But if they themselves were living, I would bring their judgment before you. Therefore, you shall bear the iniquity of your fathers. And so, he <note>The Roman Emperor Hadrian</note> flayed some alive, others he tore with iron combs, and he ordered the rest to be consumed by fire or other various punishments. This history is very well known to you. For you are so "pious" <note>Postel is speaking sarcastically here</note> that you celebrate an annual fast in memory of those most wretched men who favored the impious Bar Kokhba <note>original: "Barcozibæ." Simon bar Kokhba led the Jewish revolt against Rome (132–136 CE). His critics called him "Bar Coziba," meaning "Son of a Lie," after the revolt failed.</note>. And although they had consented to the unjust and impious crimes of that tyrant and false prophet, who did not want God to lead him, yet you dare to count them among the saints. O blind nation! How could an emperor, who was a stranger to your religion, have inflicted such unheard-of torments upon you on account of Joseph, who had been led into Egypt nearly 1,800 years before—whose sale, orchestrated by divine power, actually resulted in the greatest salvation for his brothers? It is not likely that he would have wished to avenge so cruelly, as if it were a new crime, something your wise men say was barely a sin and had been expiated many centuries before. Who could convince themselves that a wise and prudent man would want to take revenge for a crime already buried in almost eternal memory, upon men who were innocent of that crime and held great authority? The crime he was avenging was recent, which the fathers of these men had truly committed. For these were old men, and 90 years earlier <note>Postel’s chronology places the death of Jesus roughly 90 years before the Hadrianic persecutions</note> the life of Christ had been sold and treacherously handed over by their fathers. The living body of Joseph was sold so that he might live in Egypt; but Christ Jesus was sold so that he might die on the cross. This history has this in common: that it happened that both were handed over by their brothers. These ten men <note>Referencing the "Ten Martyrs," a group of ten rabbis executed by the Romans following the Bar Kokhba revolt</note> consented to the death and sale of Jesus Christ, for by following the most cruel persecutions against Christians, they brought help and provided counsel to that false prophet born for the ruin of the nation. Although Aelius Hadrian was not a Christian, he was nevertheless not a stranger to Christ, whose image he venerated in his private shrine <term>lararium: a shrine to the household gods (Lares) in a Roman home</term> along with Abraham and many others. Certainly, if the faction of the priests of idols had not been so great, he would have openly professed the Christian faith through baptism. He, therefore, was the genuine interpreter of the passage written in Amos <note>original: "Hamos." He refers to Amos 2:6, "they sold the righteous for silver."</note>. For although the sons of Israel sinned by selling their brother Joseph, they could not yet be held by the Law, which was barely given two hundred years later. Moreover, no law punishes crimes committed before it was promulgated, unless it is by the one who issued it. Do you not judge from these and the aforementioned things that you have departed into a reprobate sense? Thus, you prefer to stand by the opinions of four or five wicked modern scoundrels <note>A dismissive reference to medieval or contemporary Rabbinic commentators</note> and neglect your ancient interpreters, rather than embrace the truth. Read, you wretched ones, read the prophets, weighing what you committed against Christ; consider chapter 7 of Ezekiel. You suffer these things because of your perverse judgment against Christ, as the prophet says there: "neither will he spare you." But I have pursued this argument of reprobation enough. For I will persist in it everywhere, since it is never not mentioned.

However, so that all things may be clear, the matters under discussion must be gathered into certain main headings, so that it may be seen where the hallucination occurred in Israel.
