# GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK 4, PAGE 381

...to be considered: **natural law**, **restorative law**, and the **law of grace**. <note>original: "lex naturalis, lex instauratoria, lex gratiæ"</note> The **natural law** was given to all people, but it was so corrupted in Adam and his posterity that, while everyone may judge themselves to be acting poorly, they cannot amend themselves for the sake of salvation without God’s special privilege. The second, the **restorative law**, was given to Moses so that he might explain it to the Israelites. The third was to be given with Christ, God as its author, in such a way that within it, remedies for a depraved nature would be offered to all people. These time periods are joined together like the past, the present, and the future. Since the first and the last laws belong to everyone, they were not restricted to any specific locations. The Jewish law, however, only held a place for a certain time; after it lost its place entirely, it also ceased to have its power. For as long as God wished to cherish that law, He constantly sent it prophets, gave it teachers, and ruled it through judges, kings, and leaders; nor did He send it any calamity without foretelling its arrival and its end, as was evident in the Babylonian captivity. It follows, therefore, that since the prince, priest, prophet, kingdom, location, miracles, and temple have been lost to that nation without any hope of liberation or any prophecy of return, that law has also reached the end of its virtue. For it is impossible for it to retain its power when all its supports have utterly collapsed, and the world has now been without that law for fifteen hundred years.

Since there is no gap between those laws, it follows that the law of the Messiah was instituted in the place of the Mosaic law when the latter perished. There has been a continuous law of God and of the "True Israel" in Judea alongside the Mosaic law, which Jeremiah implies when he says in chapter thirty-three:

> There shall not be cut off from David a man sitting upon the throne of the house of Israel; and from the Levitical priests there shall not be cut off a man before me offering burnt offerings, and kindling sacrifices, and steaming incense for all days. <note>Jeremiah 33:17–18</note>

It is established from this passage either that the prophet lied (which is a sin to even think) or that we <note>the Christians</note> are the **True Israel**. For sacrifices have been made by us now for fifteen hundred years. And there, Christ succeeded in power to Simeon <note>Postel likely refers to Simeon the Just, traditionally seen as the last of the "Great Assembly" in Jewish tradition</note>, who was the last of the good men, though Christ came without the old ceremonies. For He had come to take those away. James the Just succeeded Him, and others in order; although our affairs there are currently afflicted, they nevertheless hold power. For in this our Israel differs from yours: we are not bound to specific places or earthly things. The rewards of your law, however, were an abundance of all corruptible things, depending upon the land of Israel.

From this consideration, it is clear that Christians have preserved that power which you have lost. The "Throne of David" is the Church of God and the fellowship of the faithful; this is what the prophet Nathan revealed to David after he had rested from his enemies, in the second book of Kings, chapter seven:

> And your house shall be stable, and your kingdom shall be for eternity before your face, and your throne shall be firm continually. <note>2 Samuel 7:16. In the Vulgate Bible used by Postel, 2 Samuel is often titled 2 Kings.</note>

For this cannot be understood literally as a kingdom supported by corruptible things. Therefore, it must be understood as being said regarding the power of the faithful who follow the faith of David. Hence, David says in the Psalms:

> Your throne, O God, is for the age of ages, etc. <note>Psalm 45:6</note>

There is also another condition for the people living under the law. For they were to be weighed down by three kinds of captivities: the small ones, such as under the Judges; the seventy-year one in Babylon; and the third, the eternal one—namely, when the grace of the law was to be exchanged for the grace of the Gospel. Therefore, all those things for which God said through the prophets that He would not grant forgiveness must be referred to this final captivity, from which they will not be liberated unless they become Christians. There are also three ways of understanding "Israel": under the law of Moses, under the Gospel (which we have seen from Isaiah), and under the reprobation and wrath of God. There are also three...

# ON THE CONCORD OF THE WORLD

### ON THE THREE GATHERINGS

...three gatherings: one from the Babylonian captivity, another of the few under Christ, and the third of both Israel and all people on the Day of Judgment. The prophets speak of these interchangeably. But wicked interpreters <note>Postel is likely referring to contemporary Jewish scholars who disagreed with his messianic interpretations</note> drag all these prophecies toward the present captivity, as if some tyrant sent by God is destined to come to free them and restore the physical rewards of the divine law to them once again. 

However, that only a very few were to be gathered in the second gathering is clear from the book of the **Sanhedrin** <note>A major tractate of the Talmud dealing with law and messianic expectations</note> in the chapter *Helek*. There it is stated: Rabbi Shammai says, it is said in Jeremiah chapter 3: *And I will take you, one from a city and two from a family, and I will bring you to Zion.* He compares their exit from Egypt to their entry into the land; just as their entry into the holy land consisted of only two men out of six hundred thousand. Rabbi Solomon <note>Refers to Rashi (Rabbi Shlomo itzhaki), the medieval commentator</note> explains this passage in this way: "The rest," he says, "died." 

And likewise, Rabba the interpreter says: *And so it will be in the days of the Messiah, just as it was said in Hosea chapter 1: And she shall respond there as in the days of her youth, when she went up from the land of Egypt.* This shows the same point as above. It is necessary, however, to understand this as the first gathering to the Messiah. For the gathering from Babylon included everyone—or at least very few were excluded. But in the final gathering, all human beings will be collected for the judgment of God. 

These things are confirmed by the **Gemara** <note>The component of the Talmud comprising rabbinical analysis</note> in the book of the **Sanhedrin**, in the chapter *Dine Mamonoth*. It says there is a tradition of the sons of Rabbi Hiyya that, when they were once sitting at a banquet before the Rabbis, they did not wish to discuss sacred matters or explain what they had learned from their father. Therefore, the Rabbi said to the cupbearer: "Give them more wine, and they will speak." When he had done so, one of them said: "The son of David <note>A common title for the Messiah</note> will not come until the two 'houses of the fathers' in Israel have failed—which are the head of the captivity in Babylon and the prince who is in the land of Israel—as Isaiah says in chapter 8: *And he shall be for a sanctuary, but for a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense to both houses, and for a snare and a trap to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. And many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken. Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples, and I will wait for the Lord, who hides his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him.*"

This is the tradition. However, so that the passage of Isaiah may be seen more broadly, it must be repeated from an earlier point: *Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; let him be your fear, and let him be your dread. And he shall be to you for a sanctuary, for a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.* This note is primarily intended to be about the coming of the Messiah, in which by far the greatest part of the people perished, and only the very few disciples and apostles of Jesus Christ were saved. From this passage, it becomes clear both that the Messiah came when your national affairs were overturned, and that we [Christians] have succeeded into your place. 

Regarding the Messiah, we must note two advents. The first, which followed immediately upon the destruction of your commonwealth and gathered your small "remnant." The second, which will gather all of you along with the rest of humanity for judgment, after many of you have followed the **Anti-Messiah** <note>The Antichrist</note>. I think this needs no further proof. 

But meanwhile, it must be carefully observed that when the scripture speaks of gatherings universally, it refers either to the final advent or to the calling of Christians from the whole world, so that God may gather those people from this dross to eternal happiness. The interpretation of the blinded Rabbis, which feeds you with false time periods and mistakes the last advent for the first, is not to be accepted. 

The longest "deadline" of all was that of the trifler and corrupter of scriptures, Rabbi Solomon <note>Rashi</note>, who said the **New Law** would begin from the time the Temple was devastated, but was not to be made public for 1,335 years, and that "blessed will be he who waits until 1,390." This trifler says this so that he may pervert the writings of Daniel, who had said that Christ was to be killed and the Law abolished before the Temple was destroyed. But look here, you most inept trifler—this time, to whom...

# WILLIAM POSTEL, BOOK 4

To which law will it be ascribed: that of Moses or the Messiah? Has it ever seemed possible that a thing was made by God or by art so that it would be useless for 1335 years? <note>A reference to the prophecy in Daniel 12:12 regarding the "thousand three hundred and thirty-five days," which many interpreters read as years.</note> This idea refutes itself. And yet, that period already expired two hundred and six years ago, and that Messiah, who has been sleepy for so long, has still not come. A certain Saadia <note>Saadia Gaon (882–942), a prominent Jewish philosopher and exegete.</note> had said he would come 1200 years from the time of the Temple's destruction. Rabbi Moses the Egyptian <note>Maimonides, also known as Rambam (1138–1204).</note>, a man of the greatest integrity (as far as a condemned Jew can be), stated with certainty that the Messiah would come in the year of the world 4474. But that deadline passed more than a thousand years ago. Moses of Girona <note>Nahmanides, also known as Ramban (1194–1270).</note> and Levi ben Gerson <note>Gersonides, also known as Ralbag (1288–1344).</note> fixed the date at the year of the world 5118. And yet, that deadline passed four hundred years ago.

See, you wretched Jews, what unhappiness you possess from having abandoned the fountain of living water and digging for yourselves broken cisterns that cannot hold water. <note>An allusion to Jeremiah 2:13.</note> Although the "Tradition of Elijah" <note>Referring to a passage in the Talmud (Sanhedrin 97a) stating the world would last 6,000 years: 2,000 of chaos, 2,000 of Torah, and 2,000 of the Messianic age.</note> is considered apocryphal, it still ought to be preferred over the trifles of these scoundrels who overturn the truth. For that tradition had already said the Messiah would come in the year of the world 4000. He actually came in 3963, which is very close to that number. When Isaiah wrote <term>למרבה</term> <note>original: "l'marbeh", meaning "for the increase" from Isaiah 9:7.</note>—that is, "for the increase" of the Messiah's empire—he wrote it with a *Mem Setuma* <note>The Hebrew letter Mem usually looks like an open square (מ) in the middle of a word, but in Isaiah 9:7, it is written as a "closed" Mem (ם), which usually only appears at the end of words. Postel views this scribal anomaly as a hidden code.</note> among other reasons, to show to the skilled that the Messiah would come six hundred years later, and so it happened.

Daniel had said that after 70 weeks <note>The "Seventy Weeks" prophecy in Daniel 9:24-27, often interpreted as 490 years.</note> Christ would come and the Temple would fall in a fire. That very thing happened without any error 490 years later. Isaiah said the Messiah would come before Titus <note>The Roman General, later Emperor, who destroyed Jerusalem in 70 AD.</note> was born; so note the interpreters. You saw that Christ came when the scepter and the lawgiver departed from Israel. For forty years before, the miracles of the Temple ceased; forty years before, the tongue of fire ceased to be carried to the right side; for forty years the senate was outside of *Hagazith* <note>Lishkat ha-Gazit, the "Chamber of Hewn Stone" where the Sanhedrin met in the Temple. According to the Talmud, they left this chamber 40 years before the destruction.</note>. And just as Moses in the desert waited forty years for the people to repent, if they would only know the ways of the Lord, so from the killing of Jesus Christ, God willed to wait forty-two years for repentance. Are not all these things more worthy of belief than those wretched rabbis who lead you to ruin?

But there remains one more condition of things to be noted before the objections. The multitude of the people was divided into three parts at the coming of the Messiah. For there was the "Least Israel" saved through the Messiah, the "Middling Israel" to be destroyed through vengeance, and the "Third/Greatest Israel" to be rejected into the reproach of the nations. We have seen regarding those three. Many prophecies are to be referred to this, which your unskillful moderns <note>Postel uses "neoterici" to refer to contemporary Jewish scholars of his era.</note> strive to overturn with their interpretations. Those men are deceivers and rulers of the people who have made a "covenant with death," about whom Isaiah prophesied in chapter 28; it is because of their impiety and craftiness that you suffer all these extremes. For they laugh at you, and you seriously believe them, even though you are in such a long captivity and have lost your prophets, priests, judges, kings, and miracles. The power of the Law has perished for you. Nor can the Jews be anything other than impious and treacherous for these fifteen hundred years.

But regarding the various partitioning of the people after the Messiah was killed, we must hear Ezekiel in chapter 5. Truly, the soul of the reprobate son of Israel shudders; my soul shudders to recount what he wrote about you. Yet I will say it: *And you, son of man, take a sharp sword, take a barber’s razor, and pass it over your head and your beard; then take scales for weighing and divide the hair. You shall burn one-third in the midst of the city when the days of the siege are finished; then you shall take one-third and strike around it with the sword, and one-third you shall scatter to the wind: and I will unsheath a sword after them. You shall also take a small number of them and bind them in the skirts of your robe. Then take some of them again and throw them into the midst of the fire and burn them in the fire; from there a fire will go out into all the house of Israel. Thus says the Lord God: This is Jerusalem; I have set her in the midst of the nations and the countries all around her. But she has rebelled against my judgments... being more wicked than the nations.*

Before I deal with the *Nizzahon* <note>The *Sefer Nizzahon* (Book of Victory), a famous 12th-13th century Jewish polemical text written to refute Christian interpretations of the Bible.</note>, I wish to note certain things regarding this passage of the prophet, so that you may pay closer attention. I set aside the fact that at the beginning he compares you to hairs—that is, the most useless waste of the body, which alone nourishes no living creature except the bat, and when shaved off, it immediately perishes. Thus, among men, because you depend on God, you were the greatest "dwellers in darkness," carrying around nothing other than darkness under the pretext of God's Law. A part was burned under Titus <note>Roman Emperor who, as a general, destroyed Jerusalem in 70 AD.</note>, for Jerusalem was consumed by fire, in which eleven hundred thousand men perished by war, famine, plague, and fire; nearly one hundred thousand were reserved for slavery and spectacles. Moreover, in the whole war, twenty hundred thousand [two million] men were lost. If you look back at that multitude which was led out of Egypt, three times as many and more were slain. And yet that is only one-third part. For forty hundred thousand [four million] (the other two-thirds, evidently) were destroyed in Bitter <note>Betar, the final stronghold of the Bar Kokhba revolt (132–135 AD), where the Jewish forces suffered a devastating defeat by the Romans.</note>, at the very least. I do not wish to bring up here what Josephus <note>Flavius Josephus (c. 37–100 AD), the Jewish historian who chronicled the Roman-Jewish War.</note>, a Jewish man of great authority among your people, has reported. That author stands as evidence. You will believe him when he does not speak of Christ. A third part was destroyed by the sword; another third is a fugitive and a mockery to the whole world to this present day. From that entire multitude, a few were saved and bound in the hem <note>original: "patio". Referencing Ezekiel 5:3, where a few hairs are bound in the skirt/hem of a garment, which Postel interprets as the small number of Jews who converted to Christianity.</note>, that is, made Christians, and yet not all were good. For Simon the Samaritan [Simon Magus] was baptized, and he wanted to abuse the Holy Spirit for magic; finally, having become impious and treacherous, he led many into error. At last in Rome, while he falsely believed through demons that he could fly into the sky, he fell through the prayers of Peter and Paul and was carried down to hell in the eleventh year of Nero; and upon his death, destruction was immediately decreed, and the war was committed to Titus. From this came fire upon the whole house of Israel. 

What truly is the cause? Because Jerusalem was more impious than the nations. For the nations, as soon as they heard of Christ and his doctrine, were converted—in Samaria, in Damascus, in Antioch, in the neighboring cities we were already called Christians, while Jerusalem was still afflicting our people with every punishment. Before the Messiah came, you had nothing in common with the nations. Nor was there anything in which you ought to have taken an example from them under Moses; indeed, it would have been damnable. For they were idolaters, and likewise evil in morals like you. Therefore, the example of the nations was to be avoided by you in all things. For you were led into captivity because of the imitation of the nations. But now, God says He wishes to establish all extreme examples against you because you do *not* follow the nations. It was necessary, therefore, that the nations should have had something from God in common with you and the other nations, and which the nations would have received before you. But there is no such thing except the Gospel of Jesus Christ, the seed of Abraham, in which all nations were to be saved. For it was a small thing, as Isaiah says, that the Messiah should be a God-man for the salvation of Israel...

Therefore God had placed him for the salvation of the nations. But the scriptures had to be fulfilled: so that God might call a people that was "not a people," and "not beloved" as "beloved." <note>Postel is referencing Hosea 2:23 and Romans 9:25, interpreting the conversion of the Gentiles as a fulfillment of biblical prophecy.</note> Therefore the fishers of men <note>The Apostles.</note> said: *It was necessary that the word of God should first be spoken to you, but because you have made yourselves unworthy, behold, we turn to the Gentiles.* <note>original: "Oportebat primum uobis loqui uerbum Dei... ecce conuertimur ad gentes." Acts 13:46.</note> If you had acted according to the judgments of the nations, at that time without a doubt Israel would have been saved. Thus He favored the pagan leader [Titus] raging against you, so that in the midst of your army, Titus, while besieging the city, could never be harmed by anyone. Where there was not a great supply of materials, in three days he surrounded your city with a very wide, high, and long wall of thirty-nine stadia <note>A stadium is roughly 185 meters; 39 stadia is approximately 4.5 miles.</note>; where eleven hundred thousand men were enclosed, and none dared to come forth into legitimate combat; where mothers cooked and ate their own children <note>A famous and horrific account found in Josephus's *The Jewish War*, intended to show the extremity of the famine during the siege.</note>; where dung and filth were the most welcome food and high in price; where houses were filled with corpses and those dying of hunger; where the crowd of the dying was so great that the earth of the city failed for burial; where bodies were thrown over the walls because of the stench and filled the trenches in such a multitude that as Titus turned his eyes to heaven while beholding them, he said: *I call God to witness that I am not the cause of this misery.* Where finally neither father could embrace son, nor love, nor weep for the dead. Where also (though Titus otherwise had a most obedient soldiery), he could not prevent them from destroying the temple with fire, and turning Jerusalem into a heap of stones. And yet the survivors did not recognize Christ, but again gathered against the holy and just one from all the world in Betar <note>Postel writes "Bitter," referring to the fortress of Betar, the final stronghold of the Bar Kokhba revolt (132–135 AD).</note>; in which, how great the misery was can be guessed from this: it was a city surrounded by a wall of by far the greatest circumference, with nearly four times the number of people as in Jerusalem, and they endured a three-month siege. What the Jews suffered there, I leave to be reflected upon from the history of Jerusalem, for no historian has fully described the calamities of this destruction. Let the histories of all nations since the creation of the world be read; no slaughter similar to this will ever be found. Whence it must be confessed that the Jews committed a sin so immense that none since the creation of the world has been or ever will be greater. From this deed alone, one may certainly judge the divinity of Jesus Christ. For God would never have taken such bitter and unheard-of punishments for the killing of even the holiest prophet in the world—since a man holier than Isaiah or Zechariah son of Jehoiada cannot be given—and yet God forgave both those [sins] and idolatry after seventy years [of Babylonian exile], and still cherished His people for nearly five hundred years; but now, alienated from Him, they have been in exile for fifteen hundred years. Therefore He does not spare you, nor will He ever spare you, unless you believe in His son, Jesus the Messiah, who was violated and killed by your ancestors. For He is pious and waits for you with mercy; though you macerate yourselves with fasts, pour out prayers, cherish one another, and perform ceremonies, you must not hope that He will ever hear you, who has not heard you crying out for fifteen hundred years, dispersed as you are, hated by the whole world, and born to be a reproach and a mockery to the nations. Now let the armored *Nizzahon* <note>The *Sefer Nizzahon* (Book of Victory), a famous Jewish polemical work against Christianity.</note> step forth; let us engage. Although I am equipped with light armor—scarcely a spear and a small shield—nevertheless, with the faith of Jesus Christ as my guide, I hope it will easily come to pass that the more naked I am and less prepared with sacred equipment, the greater the strength He will supply me, so that by movement, leaping, and spirit, I may be able to finish off this Goliath supported by such a crowd of opinions. ...why should we not observe the law, even though Christ himself observed it? I have already shown that we are the people of God because, immediately upon the cutting off of the Law of Moses and its privileges—its ceremonies, signs, magistracy, priesthood, prophecy, and empire having ceased—we succeeded it. That we are not circumcised demonstrates perfection. For Moses in *Deuteronomy* and the prophets, as I have already shown, preferred the circumcision of the heart to the circumcision of the flesh; I have already cited the passages. Therefore, Christ was circumcised so that he might make both one, to join the Jews to the Gentiles, and so that as a mediator he might receive the two extremes into himself—baptism and circumcision. He did this to approve the Law as having been good since it was given by him, and to accommodate himself to your weakness, so that as God and man he might show us, through his total humility, that the established laws which do not fight against God must be obeyed. But now that he has departed, if we were to be circumcised, Christ would be of no benefit to us. The primary reason for approving the Law until his day was to connect the extremes, so that just as he consisted of two natures, divine and human, he might likewise join the law of physical reward and the spiritual law, making both into one.

The Jews object to "idolatry," claiming that we worship images of the saints and of Christ. We do not adore them, nor do we believe there is any divinity within them; rather, we keep them in memory of Jesus Christ and the saints because, through our negligence, few people know the Sacred Scriptures. The ancient law was not exempt from this practice either. For they thought divinity dwelt in the <term>brazen serpent</term> <note>The Nehushtan (Numbers 21), a copper snake on a pole used for healing; later destroyed by King Hezekiah because people began to worship it.</note>. Moses had established it, but *Hezekiah* removed it because of popular abuse. There were two <term>Cherubim</term> <note>Angelic figures</note> in the temple, which can and should be fashioned far less as a physical figure than a holy man can be. Yet the people who saw those signs in the temple did not worship them. In the same way, our people do not adore the images of holy men, but they look upon them in memory of those they represent. The prayers they pour out before them—so that they might compel God with prayers on our behalf—they begin from God and end through Christ our God. 

Indeed, it is reasonable that the saints who, while they were in a mortal body, were heard by the Lord on behalf of the people, should now easily obtain those remedies they demand out of compassion for our miseries, now that they are joined to Him. This is evident in many other places and specifically from that passage of the prophet where He says: *If Moses and Samuel stood before me to pray for this people, I would not hear them.* <note>original: "Si steterint ante me Moses & Samuel..." Jeremiah 15:1. Postel argues that if God says he *won't* listen even to them, it implies that normally saints *can* and *do* intercede.</note> From this place it is clear both that the saints are able to pray, and that even the holiest can obtain nothing from God in your name until you believe in Jesus, whom you crucified. 

I wish that, rather than being a cause of offense or error to anyone, the Church would remove those images for a time, until the <term>Muhametani</term> <note>Muslims</note> and the Jews might embrace Jesus Christ from the heart. If it depended on that alone, you could become Christians if the Church accommodated you in this; or perhaps separate temples could be provided where you might worship Jesus Christ according to your own judgment. 

You say that we neglect the choice of foods and transgress the Law. If those observations had been necessary for salvation, the Holy Spirit would never have wished to lighten them so freely through the mouths of *David*, *Isaiah*, and the other prophets. Therefore, that one Law permitted or prohibited all those things due to the "hardness of your hearts" and for a time (until Christ, the Sun of Justice, should shine upon you), so that you might hold God in memory more frequently by seeing what was permitted or forbidden. Truly, there can be nothing evil in those things, since what God created is good; it cannot generate evil and sin in a man who is a worshiper of God and possesses total purity of heart. For sin does not occur except by the will. Whatever sin existed in those things while the Law of Moses lasted was not because the thing itself was evil, but because it would have been evil to break the Law. 

Those ceremonies with which you were imbued in Egypt He permitted in order to accommodate Himself to you, and because He places nothing arbitrary in the Law, He commanded them. Therefore, we do not sin by using those things which are not evil in themselves, and which were debated by the prophets. For it would have been a far more serious matter to omit the daily sacrifice of the temple—namely, the two rams—than to have eaten pork. And yet the prophets, looking toward the time of the Messiah, said: *Who has required these things from your hands?* <note>Isaiah 1:12</note> Therefore, the true law was to perform mercy and judgment, to help the oppressed and the widow, and to be most like God in doing good to all.

God willed for this to be covered in silence and obscurity. For to know the cycles of history <note>original: "periodos rerum"</note> belongs to God alone, who cannot err; but for a human, over whom death always hangs and the judgment of God always looms, and who yet does not abstain from evil, it is not fitting to know his own end. For if a human commits so many crimes even while placed in the fear of death and God’s judgment, what would he not do if he knew that a certain reprieve <note>original: "inducias," a legal or military truce</note> had been granted to him? Therefore, God willed to accommodate himself to his disciples and to an audience that was not yet firmly established. Among the disciples, there were many very close friends; there were also his mother’s relatives, to whom—had he confessed to knowing something so difficult—they would have importunely insisted that he reveal it. Had he refused to do so, they would have taken it poorly and judged that he did not have enough trust in their integrity. For it was necessary for him to accommodate himself to their tender age in the faith, since even after seeing so many miracles, once he was dead, few believed in his resurrection, despite it having been frequently predicted by him.

But a Jew will say to me: "If he knew, and yet denied it against the sense of his own mind, he lied, which is unbecoming of a prophet." <note>Postel is addressing the common theological objection that if Jesus was God, he could not truly be "ignorant" of the Day of Judgment as claimed in Mark 13:32.</note> However, he both knew, and by saying he did not know, he did not lie. For as a human, no mortal knew; but as God, he truly knew all things. Since he was both God and man, possessing two extreme natures within himself—the highest of the supreme and the highest of the inferior—he also possessed two types of knowledge and two wills. I believe, O wiser Jews, that you will not deny this to me, since you believe that the Messiah will be a man more excellent than any who could ever exist in the world. But if he were only a man, another greater than him could be made by God who was both God and man at once. Therefore, it was necessary for him to be God, endowed with two natures, and likewise with two wills, two types of knowledge, and qualities of the soul which appear different in God than in the human mind.

But you will say it is obvious that he was ignorant of even common things. For when he came to the sterile fig tree, he commanded the disciples to look and see if there were figs on it. Hey there, my good Jew, do you not see that God also acts as if he is ignorant of you, when he confessed to these same kinds of "ignorances"? Why did God say to Adam, "Where are you?" <note>Genesis 3:9</note> Was he ignorant? Was he unable to find him? If he was able to find him, why did he ask where he was? And likewise: "I will go down," says God, "and I will see if they have completed the work." <note>Genesis 11:5, regarding the Tower of Babel</note> Was he ignorant of whether they were building a tower? Does he have need of physical movement? Is he ignorant of anything? The same must be judged regarding the visitation of the Sodomites. These are familiar phrases of speaking in the Holy Scriptures; God accommodates himself to us, and he acts only effectively <note>meaning he produces an effect in us rather than experiencing human emotions himself</note>, not by the stirrings of a mind after our fashion. Repentance <note>original: "Poenitentia"</note> seems to be attributed to him because he made man; had he therefore been ignorant from eternity that man would sin? These things are accommodated to our senses, because otherwise we could not grasp them. Christ willed nothing else except that, while he held everyone's attention on the fig tree, he might both terrify them by the power of a divine miracle and incite them to good works.

That he possessed knowledge of the future is sufficiently shown by the fact that he predicted his own resurrection at a certain and fixed time; he predicted the sending of the Holy Spirit, the deaths and miracles of his followers, he predicted the calamity of Jerusalem, he predicted the resurrection of all and the future judgment, and the melting down of matter through fire. But why did he not add the precise times, so that they might have taken precautions? Here I shall interrupt, and unless you solve a similar question for me by returning like for like, I shall not be satisfied. Could all the prophets, using divine revelation and inspired by the Holy Spirit, announce the future and predict the truth at a precise time, or not? You will not deny they could, because the seventy years of captivity were precisely announced, and the ruin of the temple after seventy weeks was also announced. Why then did they not hand down all future calamities precisely, so that the people in whose times they were to occur could protect themselves? You will say it would have been inconvenient. For then there would have been no merit in hope and faith; the impious would have acted wickedly freely right up to the end, and fear would have been removed until that very hour. There would have been no place for the choice of believing, which is the merit, source, and basis of religion. Furthermore, your Messiah, and the Messiah of the whole world, would have been oppressed while still an infant. For if you had known the settled and fixed day on which he was to be born, you would have flocked there from the whole world, and you would have undoubtedly stirred up a power formidable to neighboring princes and republics, and factions for his exaltation, and you would have oppressed both yourselves and him before there was a place for the Gospel. This is most obvious: because even though he was born in the greatest obscurity...

<header>ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD</header>

Though he wished it otherwise, Herod could not prevent himself from destroying all the male children from two years old and under—the entire generation of youth—in the regions of Bethlehem and Rama, because of what he had heard from the Magi. Regarding this event, if you do not accept our own records, listen to Macrobius <note>Ambrosius Theodosius Macrobius, a 5th-century Roman writer. Postel cites him because he was a pagan, making him an "impartial" witness to the massacre of the innocents.</note> whom I mentioned earlier, writing about the jests of Augustus Caesar. He says: "When Augustus heard that among those boys under two years old whom Herod had ordered to be slain in the borders of Bethlehem, Herod’s own son had also been killed, Caesar said, 'I would rather be Herod’s pig than his son.'" <note>original: "Mallem esse Herodis porcus quam filius." This is a famous ancient pun on the Greek words for pig (*hys*) and son (*hyios*); since Herod followed Jewish law and did not eat pork, a pig was safer in his house than his own children.</note> This author is a stranger to both you and us, and clearly a pagan <note>original: "impius"</note>; it is quite impossible for you to claim he was coached by us. The crime is established. Herod was not satisfied with taking from you the kingdom, the priesthood, the judiciary, and the royal line, unless he also pursued Jesus among the innocents. What would have happened if Jesus had come with a military display? For that reason, the prophets did not wish to touch upon the specific day or month, lest he who was the *Prince of Peace* <note>original: "ssar ssalõ," from the Hebrew "Sar Shalom"</note> should bring war immediately from his cradle. What turmoil and world confusion would have followed the true Messiah, when—even after two million men were killed in Judea and the chief cities overturned—nevertheless forty million (or as others prefer, four million) flocked to the false Bar Kochba <note>original: "Barcoziba," the leader of the Jewish revolt (132–136 AD). Postel uses the name "Son of a Lie," a common pun used by his detractors.</note>? Religion does not usually announce precise times, so that the freedom to yield or not yield to the truth is left to us. In this matter, Jesus Christ wished to be like the prophets, so that he might encourage his followers to faith and lift them up in the hope of future things. He did indeed predict the sending of the Holy Spirit, but not precisely: "But not many days from now," he said. Indeed, on the fiftieth day from the resurrection, and the tenth from the ascension, he sent the Paraclete <note>The Holy Spirit as "Advocate" or "Helper."</note>, whose title the impostor Muhammad—with your favor and assistance—wished to seize six hundred years later. Therefore, you can assert nothing regarding Christ's "ignorance"; otherwise, both God the Father and the prophets (under the guidance of the Holy Spirit) would have been ignorant—which is as impious to believe about them as it is about Christ. That we are called the "True Israel," the other having been cast out, has been made sufficiently clear above, and we have seen Christ in the flesh. But as for the objection raised against us by the *Nizzahon* <note>original: "Nizahõ," referring to the *Sefer Nizzahon*, a famous medieval Jewish polemical text written to refute Christian arguments.</note>—that we should not be called "Israel" according to the interpretation of the name as "seeing God"—by that same logic, the Hebrews who never saw God were called so falsely. We know that the Divinity cannot be perceived with the eyes; and we assert that we now see God as if through a mirror in a riddle <note>original: "per speculum in enigmate," referencing 1 Corinthians 13:12.</note>, until, released from the bonds of the body, we may see him with a free soul face to face.

But now a point arises where the *Nizzahon* exults and seriously triumphs as if a victor: "If the Messiah or Jesus is God, why did he enter into a woman, since a woman is an unclean vessel from which God willed the Israelites to abstain for three days before they received the Law?" A difficult question indeed! Suppose (O pestilent man) that the Divine Virgin was a woman whom you think you can defile with a blasphemous mouth and even fouler words. Can God conceive a stain within himself because he daily sees and tolerates the foulest sins of men, than which nothing is more loathsome? Do you think that into his world—in which he moves even down to the depths of hell, more infamous than any infamy—any stain can penetrate (as David says)? Or that he conceives a stain because he nourishes, sees, and endures such infamous harlots? If he could be defiled by wickedness, he would long ago have ceased to be God. Could he not then enter without a stain into a female body (even assuming God were a physical body)? See how powerless you make him, even inferior to the sun! For the sun's rays join themselves to sewers, stagnant lakes, serpents, and whatever there is of rotten and stinking venom, yet they remain always in their own integrity. But if incorruptible and supreme things could conceive a stain from lower things by touching them, there would long ago have been no sun; its rays would be foul and would bring destruction rather than health. See to what impotence you reduce God, or where you fall, when you compare his power (which is incapable of vice) to a human, whose "every righteousness is as a menstrual rag" <note>original: "pannus menstruate," a quote from Isaiah 64:6 used to describe the imperfection of human works before God.</note> if compared to God. You make him inferior to his own creature, or to a candle or a domestic fire. For place a candle in a latrine (if I may speak politely) for as long as you wish, or place it in any darkness; when you take it out, the light itself brings back no trace of filth. And do you, most lost of men, not hesitate to assert that the majesty of God is lower and more powerless than that? His holy majesty could enter even the vilest prostitute without stain, and purge her, and make her worthy of God—which he does daily through grace when he converts female sinners. For he has no more of the body...

God possesses grace as much as He displays power. Truly, the most holy mother of our Lord **Jesus Christ** was not a harlot—as you dare to assert, a claim I shudder even to repeat—nor was she a "woman" in the sense of one who has known a man, but an eternal virgin. It was a work most worthy of **Jesus Christ** that, just as He held two natures within Himself, He should also receive two modes of creation within His sweet flesh. For as God formed the first man from the mud without seed or a vessel <note>The "vessel" here refers to the womb.</note> fit for generating, yet willed that all others should be born from that man through the instruments of nature; so the Son of God, the Wisdom of the Father **Jesus Christ**, willed to encompass both modes in His own birth. For just as the most powerful God created all things through Wisdom—His Word or Son—in the Holy Spirit proceeding from both, so He willed the human nature produced by God the Creator to be united in a single subject of divinity and humanity participating in both, and to obtain such a generation among humans that He might have within Himself the two preceding modes and proceed from them. There are two things to consider in generation: the seed, and the vessel fit for receiving and nurturing that seed. The first man lacked both; all other men have both; but the third man <note>Postel refers to Christ here as the "third man," completing the sequence of creation types: 1. Adam (no seed/no womb), 2. Humanity (seed/womb), 3. Christ (no seed/womb).</note> had only the latter. For by the guidance of the Holy Spirit, without any seed, He began His growth within the virginal vessel. 

O miserable and faithless **Jews**, have pity at least on yourselves! Let it be enough that through the faithlessness of your **Rabbis**, innumerable people among you have been damned for 1,500 years. See the magnitude of the glorious **Messiah**, how all things in Him harmonize, how no greater man could be given or imagined than He who is at once man and God. How could He have been born more worthily than from a most holy virgin? How better than to first enter the world humbly and obscurely? How could He be more like God than by doing good for all and accepting and asserting innumerable reproaches upon Himself for the sake of the Truth? He who valued humanity so highly that, since man was powerless to pay his own debt, He satisfied the Father in man’s name. If you believe all the highest things about Him, then certainly everything we believe about Him must be approved by you. Furthermore, the prophets did not pass over such a great mystery in silence. *Isaiah* says:

> *Hear then, O house of David: Is it too little for you to be wearying to men, unless you also be wearying to my God? Therefore, the Lord Himself shall give you a sign. Behold, a virgin being pregnant shall bear a son, and shall call His name Emmanuel: butter and honey shall He eat, that He may know how to refuse the evil and choose the good.* <note>original: Isaiah 7:13-15. Postel uses the Latin Vulgate phrasing common in his era.</note>

These words are most clear; they would require no interpretation were it not that the **Rabbis** dared to corrupt them in order to pour a mist before your eyes. Because that lost man *Ahaz*—a king worthy of a faithless people—remained estranged from God and distrustful, refusing to consult the Lord in the danger of war, the prophet spoke these things from the oracle of the Holy Spirit. It was as if he said: "O house of *David* and *Ahaz* king of *Israel*, you who do not wish to test whether God saves His people, nor wish to ask a sign from Him—as if He had abandoned us—is it not enough for you to despise holy men and prophets, unless you also provoke God? Yet though you may hold Him in contempt, you shall not prevent God from bringing forth a sign by far the greatest among His people. For a virgin, being pregnant, shall bear a son, and shall call His name not 'man,' but 'the God who is with us' <note>The Hebrew name "Emmanuel" literally translates to "God with us."</note>." Moreover, when the boy is raised in the ancestral manner on honey and cream, He shall know how to reject the evil and disobedient peoples and choose the good and faithful. The things that follow in the text are clear concerning the rejection of *Israel* and the abandonment of the land. 

Indeed, you all confess that *Simeon* the Just was the last of the blessed priests, and that the "tongue of fire" ceased to be carried in the right hand upon his death, and that those who followed did not bless the people with the name <term>arba othioth</term> <note>original: "arba othioth" (Hebrew: Arba Otiyot), meaning "the four letters," referring to the Tetragrammaton (YHWH), the sacred four-letter name of God which, according to Jewish tradition, the High Priests eventually stopped pronouncing.</note>, and that the other miracles gradually vanished. From this, your rejection was made manifest even before the boy **Jesus Emmanuel** was weaned. For in the very year that he held **Christ** in his arms at the purification of **Mary**, *Simeon* the Just died. All things are in harmony. Truly, who would not marvel at and shudder at the impiety and the zeal of your rabbis for corrupting the scriptures? **Immanuel** is a name that fits only the **Messiah**, for then God was to be with men, whose generation no one could describe. They <note>The Rabbis.</note> want that passage to be spoken of the prophet’s daughter or some other woman as they dream, claiming a man was the father of **Immanuel**. ### ON THE CONCORD OF THE WORLD
AA

...woman <note>original: "mina," the conclusion of "fœmina" from the previous page</note> were to conceive by a man, what miracle does it contain? Did not the daughter of Ahaz, or the prophets, bear children, and yet you lost your land and ruin came? O reprobate men: are you not ashamed, O wretched ones, to follow such delusions? To this, who could speak of a "virgin being pregnant" without involving a lie, if it were understood according to the common manner of conceiving? If she conceived from a man, she is not a virgin. Therefore, since the scripture speaks of a "virgin being pregnant," it describes a great sign and a miracle. 

So that there would be no ambiguity, the prophet used the name *harah* <note>original: *harah*, Hebrew for "pregnant"</note>, that is, pregnant: which (as I said) involves a contradiction if understood as a deflowered virgin. It refers, therefore, to the Virgin Mary alone, who conceived without a man and remained a virgin; for from her, Jesus Christ came forth having taken on flesh: just as he went along passing through the midst of those who wished to seize him, or when he vanished on the mountain from which they wished to cast him down. Mary, the mother of Christ, was a virgin during childbirth and after childbirth. Therefore, God was not defiled by descending into the holy virgin. 

The Temple of Peace at Rome collapsed when the Virgin gave birth. The Romans thought that new structure was eternal, but when the mass fell, struck by heaven, it gave place to the true Prince of Peace. An altar in the temple of Isis in Egypt had been placed previously for "the virgin who was to give birth"; likewise in Gaul in the time of the Druids of the Carnutes <note>The Carnutes were a Celtic people whose territory centered on Chartres, where tradition holds an altar was dedicated to the "Virgin who will bring forth" (*Virgini pariturae*).</note>, which was later said to belong to the one who had given birth. A spring of oil flowed at Rome for a whole day following the birth of the Lord. A golden iris was seen that day, a star led the Magi, and three suns merged into one. All these things are noted in the annals of various nations and are in harmony with the prophetic writings. 

Jeremiah mentions the same miracle in other words in chapter 31: "How long will you turn here and there, O rebellious daughter? Surely the Lord has created a new thing on earth. A woman shall encompass a man." This is the "new thing" the Lord does: a woman encompasses a man without any male work. For what would otherwise be "new," if she conceived in the manner of others? Therefore, a little later he speaks of the old law being abolished, and of the new law of that man—whom the woman shall encompass—to be received; he who was called a "man" even in his mother's womb because of his divinity, which was his perpetual companion both inside the womb and out. For this reason Isaiah says, where he deals with his death in chapter 53: "Who shall declare his generation?" as if to say, no one, unless God reveals it. 

For from eternity, Wisdom, and the Word, and the Son of God remains begotten, and is always with the Father—a Son without a mother, through whom the world was created in love and the Holy Spirit. Thus, in his second generation, he had a mother without a father, from whom he took on flesh and came to redeem us, and to lead us back into the way of truth, since he had created man. 

But I return to Nizuah <note>Nizuah likely refers to a specific Jewish polemical text or a personified opponent Postel is addressing in his debate.</note>. He says: "In your Gospel of John, it is written that Christ said he had from the Father and God whatever he possessed; therefore he was not God." This argument is the same as if you said, "I did this by the impulse of my mind, therefore I am inferior to my mind." Jesus is less than the Father according to his humanity, but equal according to his divinity. For as I stated above, there is an equal explanation of all things in the Word, just as in the mind and in the work. Thus the whole wisdom of the Father is in the Father, and whole in the Son; for as a man, Christ takes the form of a servant. Otherwise, he is equal in divinity, since there is one and equal deity in the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, though the persons are distinct. 

Another objection: "God did not choose the Christians as a people, since it is written: *He has not done so for every nation, and he has not manifested his judgments to them*." That is understood as referring to the Law. For elsewhere it says: "All nations, clap your hands; shout to God with the voice of exultation, for Zion is founded in the exultation of the whole earth," etc. For all nations were to come and adore you, Lord. Since, truly, the eternal Israel is in Jerusalem, it follows (as we hold) that Jerusalem was, and is, the Church of God, which you alone held under Moses. But for 1500 years it has been open to the whole world, and the true Israel has been revealed to be the people of that Church. 

But a far greater and harder question presents itself. "If Jesus was God," says Nizuah, "why was he hanged <margin>why</margin>, and why did he endure all kinds of afflictions in himself? Why did he cry out that he was forsaken by God, etc.?" I will satisfy this first by reason, and then by authority. Let us start again from the beginning. It has already been said many times that a man is more perfect the more...

# WILLIAM POSTEL, BOOK 4.

...so that he might be more similar to God, and conversely. God gives to all and receives nothing; He bestows His goods upon enemies and blasphemers just as upon friends; He does all things for the sake of man; He exercises the greatest charity <note>original: "charitatem," meaning selfless, divine love</note> toward all; He makes truth perpetual in things through the continuation of species in matter; whence He rejects the disordered, the evil, and the false. Since the Messiah was to be the most perfect man, such that no greater could be given, he ought to have become like God in all his operations. Therefore, he was most poor, possessing nothing, bestowing whatever was placed in him, but receiving from no one. He loved all men equally, since he prayed for those crucifying him; he also did all things for the salvation of man. For man without God could not return to the innocence lost by Adam: which was proved most extensively in the first book. 

If having the greatest charity toward all is to be most like God, no one can have greater than when he lays down his life for the sake of the salvation of many and dies willingly: which Christ willed through his divinity, though in his body he certainly dreaded it, even to the point of sweating blood. Whoever wishes to show the greatest charity to a brother must necessarily have the primary care for the salvation of his soul. He who undertakes the care of souls takes up the assertion of truth; he who takes up the assertion of truth must necessarily displease the "great ones" <note>The "magnates" or powerful political and social leaders of the time.</note>. For they foster vices in public affairs for their own utility and opinions; whatever they stir up, they seem to rebuke the vicious person. Whence the proverb: "truth breeds hatred." Hatred immediately prepares evil for the asserter of truth. 

But if he is a man most like God, he ought not to be bent; he ought rather to die than to suffer the loss of truth. For what God does in the perpetuity of the species, likewise the attendant of truth ought to do regarding the true assertion, and see as diligently that the vice of falsehood does not creep into the soul, as God ensures that no blemish or disease creeps from nature into the body. Whoever is such a person must undergo death. Indeed, the prophets reveal these things more broadly, as will be clear in the prophetic Gospel. I will be content with one place for now, as if pointing it out with a finger: Isaiah 53. *The Lord placed on him the iniquities of us all, and by his bruising we are healed. He was wounded for our iniquities, and bruised for our crimes.* <note>Postel is quoting the "Suffering Servant" passage of Isaiah 53, a cornerstone of Christian interpretation of the Old Testament.</note> It is necessary that those things be understood concerning the Messiah, however much the Rabbis <note>Postel frequently engages in polemics with Jewish scholars (Rabbis) over the interpretation of Hebrew scripture.</note> may pervert them. 

Therefore, if your Messiah was to be most excellent, he ought to have excelled by far in goodness of soul, and always to profess the truth, nor to have "courtly"—that is, outward—justice, which whoever strives for the splendor of things must have. The soul is far more excellent than the body, and therefore its virtues are superior to the virtues of the body. Therefore, the Messiah was to be of a better excellence. For he who flourishes in abundance of things and in power cannot be good and most like God. Since there will always be poor and needy people in the whole world, if they are despised by him who possesses something, he is not perfect, because he keeps things for splendor and vain opinion while they do not have what is necessary; brothers die of hunger while one man devours everything. If he gives to all equally, he will immediately be like them and poor. If he gives and always abounds, he despoils others to clothe some, and becomes an unjust predator who bestows the blood of others. 

But the Messiah was not to have sin in himself: whence it was necessary that he was poor, humble, cast down, hated by the evil, and approved by a few good men: such as was Jesus Christ. But I proceed to the sum of the life of Jesus Christ, so that the Jews may see that it is not just one or another distorted passage that fits him, but that the entire history is found in the prophets, no differently than in the Gospels. Unless all these things had been said of him, it would be impossible for them to agree so perfectly in every detail. Thus it will happen that they may recognize what kind of person he was to be. At the end, I will run through the other objections and resolve them in a few words, which the Jews object against his coming. For they are so stupid and addicted to their Rabbis that because there are two advents of Christ, they expect two Messiahs. <note>Postel refers to the Jewish tradition of "Messiah son of Joseph" (who suffers) and "Messiah son of David" (who conquers), arguing these are actually two arrivals of the same person.</note>

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

...[the Messiah] had been revealed by Moses and the prophets through the Holy Spirit, who had previously opened these things to Abraham and Jacob. In his second birth, he was born in Bethlehem of Judea of a virgin, so that he whom the Father had formed as man through the Word <note>original: "p eū," referring back to the Word/Son</note> might, when man was utterly corrupted, be led back to the way of justice. Furthermore, immediately when he willed to be born into the world, he embraced poverty in his very deeds, and thus altered the affairs of Israel and transferred them unto himself. Born on the 13th day, he was adored by the Magi kings, and at last fled into Egypt. John the Baptist preceded him like a new Elijah, and in the desert invited people to repentance in his name. Then, when he had grown up and become a perfect man, he called the apostles—for the most part fishermen—so that he might make them "fishers of men." To them, he began to explain the law which would be useful and salutary for the whole world, so that they might preserve piety entirely within their souls. 

He willed that the things he taught be confirmed by the highest and unheard-of miracles. Because of these miracles, an incredible envy toward him was conceived by the leaders of the Jews, who sought an opportunity to destroy him. Then he entered Jerusalem, with the people crying out "Hosanna," <note>A Hebrew exclamation of praise or plea for salvation</note> even though he rode as a most poor man upon a donkey. He acted as a King, however, when he dared to drive the "sacred trade" <note>referring to the merchants in the Temple</note> from the holy place, overturning the tables of the money-changers <note>original: "trapezitarū," from the Greek for table-merchants</note>. Shortly thereafter, by the deceit of one of his own, he was sold for thirty pieces of silver; the hour and place were named where he would be handed over. Having found an opportunity at night, [the traitor] led cohorts to the Mount of Olives, where [Jesus] was captured and his followers dispersed. 

Once he was led away, the leaders and Pharisees convened concerning his death. Herod and Pilate became friends because of him. Judas, led by repentance, returned the price, which the leaders refused to put into the temple treasury <note>original: "corbanā," from the Hebrew 'korban' or offering</note>, but instead used for the purchase of a potter’s field destined for the burial of foreigners. He was afflicted with every reproach, insult, and stripe by those who ought to have cherished him. At last, with false witnesses asserting false things about him, he was judged to death between two thieves. His hands and feet were pierced, and he was fixed to the cross with nails; the entire frame of his body was undone by torments and mangling. His face, due to spit and the blood flowing down from his head, was so deformed that he seemed like a despised leper, the most abject of men. And so that he might feel every kind of cruelty, they offered vinegar from a sponge to him while he thirsted on the cross. 

Meanwhile, when the soldiers wished to divide his clothes among themselves, they finally settled by lot whose they should be. Finally, having opened his side, they did not break his bones. Moreover, an eclipse of the sun and moon occurred at that time on the fourteenth moon—which is naturally impossible—and it lasted for three hours. He was buried, he rose again, he walked with his followers, and he ascended into heaven. He sent the Holy Spirit to the Apostles and disciples, by whom—speaking in the languages of all nations—the holy law of the New Testament was published. It is preserved by us until he returns in his second coming, terrifying to all who despise his law. Then, when he shall judge the living and the dead, he will deliver the kingdom to God the Father, with all corruption abolished. These are certain chapters in which the sum of the matter consists. If the prophets support all these things, it is not possible that they refer to anyone other than Jesus.

### THE NEW-OLD GOSPEL, OR THE PROPHETIC GOSPEL
<note>The title "Caenopalaeum" is a Greek-Latin hybrid coined by Postel, combining 'kainos' (new) and 'palaios' (old) to show the harmony between the two Testaments.</note>

Although I have resolved primarily to bring forth those things which we hold by faith through the authorities of the Old Testament, I have nevertheless decided not to neglect reason whenever it can support authority. All philosophers and Jews alike in whom there is reason will grant me that God is the one creator of heaven and earth, of things visible and invisible. They cannot deny that it is impossible for anything to be created by God unless it is made by supreme power, through supreme wisdom, in the will for the sake of some end. For power would be in vain if it did not know by what art or in what manner things were to be done; and both would be present in vain unless the will and love of a certain end induced the action. 

Therefore, the entire creation of things is in God the Almighty [the Father]; it is also entirely in the most wise and almighty Son or Word; and it is entirely in the almighty Will, Love, or Holy Spirit proceeding from both. And yet there are not three almighties, but one almighty. We see that we can do nothing in the image of God—that is, the soul placed within us—unless we have the whole thing to be done in our mind, the whole in the explanation, and the whole in the work and thought. There can never be a will unless power and knowledge precede it. Moses, the standard-bearer of the prophets, indicated these three things in the first two

<meta>This page continues Postel’s theological argument, transitioning from the historical life of Jesus to a deep philosophical and scriptural defense of the Trinity. He connects the first verses of Genesis with the nature of the Messiah as both God and Man, specifically addressing Jewish interpretations of scripture and tradition.</meta>

->WILLIAM POSTEL, BOOK 4.<-

...placed in the cycles of Genesis. "In the beginning," he says, "God created the heaven and the earth; but the earth was formless and void, and the spirit of the Lord moved over the waters." There you see God, the Beginning, and the Spirit. "In the beginning"—that is, in the Son—God created all things, which received their material existence through the effect of the Holy Spirit as if by the "finger of God" <note>A traditional biblical metaphor for the power or action of the Holy Spirit</note>. Indeed, David says in Psalm 32 <note>Now traditionally numbered as Psalm 33</note>: "By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and all their power by the breath of his mouth." There he also brings forward God, the Word, and the Spirit. For nothing can be brought into being without those three <term>middot<gloss>A Hebrew term meaning "measures" or "attributes," used here to describe the distinct properties of the Trinity</gloss></term>, that is, properties. And likewise: "He will send his word and melt them; his spirit will blow and the waters shall flow." God sends into all natural things—so that forms may be given to them—the Word and the Holy Spirit, without which nothing happens. Yet there is but one thing, one action, and one God, performing all things in all.

But why that eternal mind calls the Son the "Word," I have taught frequently above, especially in the refutation of Muhammad <note>Postel refers to his own writings against Islamic theology, where he argued for the divinity of Christ using reason and linguistics</note>. God has no name that can be bestowed, or that can entirely draw His nature toward the object of the mind; for then our mind would be equal or superior to the First Cause if it could comprehend an absolute notion of it. In this, indeed, we recognize our mind to be greater than the sensible world: that we embrace the immense mass of the heavens within it. Therefore, God, pitying our weakness in contemplating Him who is our goal, revealed to holy men names familiar to them, through whose meaning and similarity we might arrive at a conjecture of such great majesty. Indeed, for explaining the Second Person among the divine persons, nothing more familiar could be given to our senses than "the Word." For just as we have nothing more immediate than to open the concept of the mind through a word after we have thought it, so divine providence—thinking from eternity about creating this mass, and seeing all things in it before matter was created—immediately distinguished that same mass through the Word and Wisdom, and brought it into being when it seemed right. Therefore, He called the Son the "Word," a term which the Greek philosophers borrowed and called <note>original: λογον ἔρ (Logos)</note> the *Logos*. Our evangelist John, weaving the life of Jesus Christ on earth from the eternal generation of the Word, said: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. All things were made through him," etc. Concerning this Word, we shall speak in many places as the occasion arises. Concerning the Wisdom of God, who is Jesus Christ, Solomon says: "The Lord by wisdom founded the earth; he established the heavens by understanding." And David: "In wisdom you have made all things."

From these, the image of the blessed Trinity and the mystery of creation are sufficiently clear. Now, after those things which God willed to say about that blessed Wisdom, we must come to the prophetic revelations, so that we may more diligently discern from them what sort of Messiah he was to be. God promised Abraham, the leader of restored piety, that a son would be born to him in whose seed all nations were to be blessed; and this not in only one place, but in many. God added, truly, that He would give that land to his seed forever. Moreover, God confirmed those promises by giving offspring to the aged Abraham and Sarah, when by the natural course of things it was impossible either for him to beget or for her to conceive; this happened because they believed all things are possible for God. These things are to be weighed diligently, because they are the basis of the sacred matter. 

The Messiah is promised in the seed of Abraham, therefore he was to be a man; and in him all nations were to be blessed—that is, saved and led to the truth. But that is impossible to be achieved through a mere man. Likewise, it is impossible for a man to rule the whole world, since God (while man's free will remains) is unequal to retaining earthly power <note>Postel argues that God does not force political rule, but rules through spirit</note>. Yet it was to happen, because God, who is truthful, said it. Therefore, the promised Messiah was to be both Man and God: Man, because he was truly of the seed of Abraham; God, because he had to save all nations, for a man cannot do that. God, however, even in fleeting things, cannot rule the whole world [directly], as I taught above. Yet He shall rule and does rule: from which it follows that the empire of the Messiah and his law are spiritual, since otherwise it would not endure forever, as this world is not eternal but temporary. But the seed of David and Abraham must reign in the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there shall be no end. Therefore, the Messiah was promised to be God and man, and his empire only spiritual, and the "land" of his faithful ones the fellowship of the Holy Church. And you [Jews] hold in many places in your <term>Gemara<gloss>The component of the Talmud containing rabbinical commentary and analysis</gloss></term> such a happy and great law of the Messiah, and the Messiah himself...

[Messiah]

<summary>Postel argues for the Trinity using Genesis and the Psalms, identifying the Second Person as both "Word" (Logos) and "Wisdom." He concludes that the promised Messiah must be both God and Man to fulfill the promise to Abraham, ruling an eternal spiritual kingdom rather than a temporary earthly one.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Postel’s argument regarding the nature of the Messiah. Having established the Trinitarian foundation in the previous page, he now addresses why the Law of Moses was temporary and how God used earthly rewards to train the Jewish people for a higher, spiritual reality brought by Jesus.</meta>

# ON THE CONCORD OF THE WORLD

...that the future Messiah would be such that the law of Moses, and Moses himself, are almost nothing in comparison to him. But nothing greater than a God-man can be given to humanity; that person is **Jesus**, and his law is a spiritual law. In the use of natural things—from which religion seems to differ only slightly to those who consider it lightly—God teaches that the same thing happens every day, by shaping individual men toward their children in the same way. 

For the sake of virtue, and because of the things that must be sought out where they are born, but especially in persuading works of virtue and piety, parents incite their children (who are unskilled in all things due to their age) toward excellence. They give them those things by which they see them most held captive, and they soothe them with promises of similar things to come daily if they persist in what they have begun, as if it would always be that way for them. In the meantime, they cover with silence the fact that a time will come when, as another age succeeds, they will no longer seek **little treats** <note>original: "crustula"—literally small cookies or sweetcakes used to reward children</note> or small gifts as a reward for virtue, but rather a good reputation. And finally, if they continue to be good, seeing that even reputation is fleeting and an unworthy reward for so many labors, they will refer everything to the praise of the Creator alone, such that they seek no reward for themselves, committing all things to the judgment of Him who placed them here. 

For since they think it most just and believe it with certainty, they cannot fail to attain the most just things from Him (I am speaking here of a person instructed under true religion). Those fathers who, with a single word, used to call all the rewards and gifts of virtue "little treats"—along with glory, reputation, and the hope of eternal life—were they lying? Were they asserting falsehoods on purpose? Not at all. For in order to accommodate themselves to children, who neither understand nor desire other things, they offer and promise those things by which they know the children can then be moved. 

In a similar way, God promised the successors of **Abraham**, as their entire reward, a fertile land and whatever accompanies it for happiness, if they would keep his commandments. The sons of Abraham were enticed and occupied by those "little treats" for about 500 years, being intent on pastoral matters, lacking a formal government, and with little ambition. **Moses** took them up as they were leaving their adolescence <note>original: "ex ephebis"—referring to the transition from youth to manhood</note>. Under him, they spent the consistent age that followed, along with the ages attached to it, in the greatest splendor of affairs: in a republic, in a kingdom, and in an aristocracy, right up until the time came for recognizing those rewards as empty and referring all things back to God. Two parts of their history indeed went well and with the highest favor of God; but when they allowed an error at the "turning point" <note>original: "catastrophen"—the downward turn or resolution of a drama</note>, and judged the rewards of childhood and youth to be suitable even for old age, they went astray into a depraved sense of things. 

Just as in the ages of a man nothing is more certain than change, yet nothing is more uncertain than the exact point of alteration regarding the predefined time (for it is certain that from an infant one becomes a child, from a child a youth, from a youth a man, and from a man an elder; yet when it happens, scarcely anyone knows until after it has already occurred), so it was in the Law. When they ought to have passed over to a greater fortune, they nevertheless forced their protector Moses into exile for forty years; and barely, through daily miracles for those whole forty years, did they submit to him in the name of God. 

They truly flourished under **David** and **Solomon**. But when he arrived who was supposed to draw them from the fleeting and empty toward the perfect reward of virtue, after he had lived among them for nearly forty years (the number below ten pertains to this), they killed him most cruelly. Forty years later, they went to their destruction, until, having been gathered there again, they fell again shortly after forty years. And yet—if it pleases the gods!—these people still expect to have their youth and earthly rewards, and they do not realize they are nursing a plague in their own bosom, even though they have now been without God longer than their youth and strong age lasted. 

But these are side-notes for the sake of interpreting the passage. In that seed of Abraham (as I had said) all nations were to be blessed; he was necessarily going to be God and man as one: most humble, with a spiritual law, possessing hearts and souls rather than things, the king of the whole world. When **Jacob**, inspired by God, blessed his sons, he said: 

> The scepter shall not be taken away from **Judah**, nor a teacher from his thigh, until **Shiloh** <term>Shiloh<gloss>A traditional Messianic title from Genesis 49:10, often interpreted as "He who is sent" or "the one to whom it belongs"</gloss></term> comes, who shall be the expectation of nations, binding his young colt to the vineyard, and his donkey's colt to the vine, O my son. He shall wash his robe in wine, and his cloak in the blood of the grape. 

These things must also be weighed carefully. There is no doubt these things are said of the Messiah. For when he says absolutely, "he shall be the expectation of nations," no one else but the Messiah can be that, who is both man and God. For all peoples ought to hope in no one else but God, because no one is powerful enough to make all people safe except God. But the Messiah was to be a man; therefore, he is also God. A man, so that...
