The prophets have revealed it, O Jews, lest perhaps you think that these things are to be understood of any other Messiah than Jesus. You have seen exactly, without any distortion, that the context of the Scriptures speaks of those things which were done by Jesus and in Jesus; it would be impossible for everything to align so perfectly unless he were the same one who is the Messiah. But so that I do not leave you occupied with a weak belief, I add certain oracles of the prophets to confirm what has been said. Isaiah foretold that the synagogue would never hear of the humble Christ: *For Zion's sake,* he says, *I will not keep silent, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until her righteousness goes forth like brightness, and her salvation is kindled like a lamp.* <note>original: "Propter Zion non tacebo..." quoting Isaiah 62:1</note> The most wicked synagogue <note>Postel uses the term "synagogue" here to refer to the religious leadership of the time who opposed Jesus</note> ordered the prophets to be silent when they openly extolled the humility of Christ. The entire chapter declares that this is to be understood regarding the righteousness of the Messiah. Indeed, by this word he indicates that the Messiah is God, since he asserts his church should be called: *My delight is in them* <note>original: "Voluntas mea in eis"; a translation of the Hebrew name Hephzibah from Isaiah 62:4</note>; and below: *The holy people, the redeemed of the Lord*; and again: *A city sought out, and not forsaken.* <margin>chapter 53.</margin> Likewise: *Who has believed our report, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? For he grew up like a tender plant before him, and like a root out of dry ground; he has no form nor majesty,* etc. <note>original: "Quis credidit auditui nostro..." quoting the famous "Suffering Servant" passage of Isaiah 53:1-2</note> These things are said concerning the humility, gentleness, and other virtues of the Messiah, as will be evident in his passion. And the wicked interpreters <note>Referring to contemporary Jewish commentators who interpreted Isaiah 53 as referring to the suffering of the people of Israel rather than a specific Messiah</note> are not ashamed to interpret these things as referring to a lost people, who were led into captivity because of crimes horrendous to heaven and earth. Truly, I shall deal with them in their proper place.

But under that humble appearance—shabby, ragged, and abject—he dared to undertake a remarkable and more than royal deed: because the glory of God was at stake, he showed himself a man there. The greedy crowd of initiates <term>mystarum: refers here to the temple officials or priests</term> had made the house of God a den of thieves, so that no opportunity for making an offering would be missed. Lest anyone should pretend they could not offer because they had not found items for sale, or did not have gold to exchange, they had brought the marketplace right into the temple—an argument for the insatiable greed from which they suffered. With a whip, with which he had driven the young donkey, he drove the men and animals away from the borders of the sacred place. He overturned the tables of the money-changers, scattering their coins, while speaking the words of Jeremiah before the priests and Pharisees: *Has this house, in which my name is called upon, become a den of thieves?* He even threatens destruction and the overturning of the temple because of that neglect and the vices of the priests, just as happened in Shiloh because of the vices of Hophni and Phinehas. <note>Hophni and Phinehas were the corrupt sons of the High Priest Eli; their sins led to the capture of the Ark and the destruction of the sanctuary at Shiloh (1 Samuel 4)</note>

However, so that Jesus might be related in some way to the primary author of your wealth <note>meaning Joseph, who saved the family of Jacob from famine</note>, the iniquity of your masters began its crime against him with a sale. Although you draw your lineage from Abraham, O Hebrews, you first gathered both power and wealth through the benefit of Joseph, who had been sold by his brothers. For before him you were only <margin>60</margin> souls, and you went out from Egypt numbering 600,000 men capable of bearing arms; to each of these at least two domestics were added, making the number three times greater. Christ matches Joseph in being sold by his own people, in innocence, in returning good for evil, and in virginity and chastity. They match only from the beginning, because Joseph preserved a temporary salvation, while Christ preserved an eternal one. By a domestic enemy (than which no plague is more deadly), Judas the traitor—while the scribes and Pharisees were agitating a council to seize him without a popular riot—sold him for thirty pieces of silver, with a guarantee given to deliver the man by night. That sum, estimated in our currency, would perhaps amount to twenty-one pounds of Tours <term>libras Turonenses: The "Livre Tournois," a standard French currency in Postel's 16th-century context</term>. For a silver piece was worth 14 Parisian shillings; even the most worthless and weak slave would have sold for four times as much. But it was so ordained by God the Father. Zechariah makes mention of that sale in chapter 11, where he spoke of the gates of the temple, which opened of their own accord <margin>40</margin> years before your ruin, as I noted before; and he touched upon the nefarious crimes of the priests, and dealt with the rejection of the covenant of Moses and the lamentation of the unhappy race of the initiates, saying: *And I said to them* (God to the priests) *if it is good in your eyes, bring my price. But if not;*

...rest. *And they weighed out my wages, thirty pieces of silver. And the Lord said to me: Throw it to the potter—that handsome price at which I was valued by them. And I took the thirty pieces of silver, and I threw them into the house of the Lord for the potter.* <note>Postel is quoting Zechariah 11:12-13, which he interprets as a direct prophecy of the betrayal of Jesus by Judas Iscariot for thirty silver coins.</note> These things completely match the context of what happened. For by eternal deliberation, divine providence had determined to give His only-begotten Son for the redemption of the world, and that whatever was done concerning him should take place, since He knew the perversity of the people. However, lest anyone be able to say that God forces this or that person to do evil, He said: *If it seems good to you. But if not, stay quiet.* <note>original: "Si ita uidetur. Sin autem, quiescite."</note> For no force is applied to free will <term>free will: the human capacity to choose between different possible courses of action unimpeded</term> through predestination. The priests gave thirty pieces of silver to Judas, who handed him over to them. Finally, when he saw him being afflicted with unheard-of torments, led by a wild repentance, Judas brought the coins back to the priests. When they refused to receive them, saying to him, "That is your responsibility," he threw them down before them and, departing in misery, broke his own neck with a noose. Those who were still in the temple gathered that money and said that because it was the price of blood, it should not be placed with the sacred offerings—which is called *Corban* <note>original: "Curban"; a Hebrew term for a gift dedicated to God</note>—but should be converted to the use of foreigners. Thus, busy trying to wash away their impiety with a new form of piety, they purchased a small field from a potter not far from the city for the burial of foreigners, and they called it *Akeldama*, that is, the Field of Blood <note>original: "hacaldema, id est agrũ sanguinis"</note>, which remains to this day a witness to your treachery.

This is the history. But lest you think this is the only argument for your ruin and for God withdrawing from you in this chapter, there is another very serious one shortly before: *And I cut off three shepherds in one month.* <note>quoting Zechariah 11:8</note> Shortly before this, the triple "shepherd" and power by which any republic must be ruled was taken from you by Herod. For in a few days, he destroyed the royal, Levitical <note>referring to the priesthood</note>, and judicial powers into one, and he appointed new men in the temple, the court, and the palace; and yet, if it please the gods, the "scepter did not depart from Judah" at that time. Your own unhappiness so possesses and affects you that you do not even wish to recognize it. What shall I say of the doors of the temple? Finally, what was also proven over forty years follows the sale of the Just One. For the priesthood was established by Roman power, and given to the more influential or sold to the wealthier; in addition, it was made an annual office. Those performing this magistracy, because each wanted to scrape everything together during his own year, murdered not only the weak (as is the custom everywhere) but even the wealthy through extortions, which is more suited to a royal and new power. For nothing of private means was safe from the reign of Herod until the time of Titus <note>the Roman Emperor who destroyed the Second Temple in 70 AD</note>. 

The following chapter proceeds to follow your unhappiness, and says that some of you, repenting by the gift of the Holy Spirit, will acknowledge the Christ who was pierced and killed by them. The 13th chapter opens the fountain of God’s grace given through Jesus Christ. And from that time, all your "rabbis" have been false prophets who, by guessing at the arrival of the Messiah through various periods of time, have held you in destruction for a full 1500 years. Finally, your unhappiness followed, heaped up with captivities, so that it seems to hold the history of the future word-for-word. I do not wish to be longer in relating the rest. I wish to be like the Pharisees in writing, just as they were in carrying out the condemnation of Jesus Christ's death. Since in free cities, where law holds place, even when the life of a slave or the most abject man is at stake, the cause is usually weighed among good men for many days; yet Jesus Christ had only six hours of daylight from the time he was captured to the cross. Let all mortals see how much "maturity" there could have been in that judgment, even if it had been a case against a wicked man. On that very day, the princes assembled together against the Lord and against his Christ. For Herod, the second of that name, was reconciled to Pilate, the governor of Judea in the name of the Roman Senate.

<header>GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK IV</header>

Because he <note>Referring to Pontius Pilate</note> had allowed the legal investigation of the case of Jesus—which he knew had been stirred up by the envy of the Pharisees and the scribes—the entire cohort of priests, Pharisees, and scribes convened against the head of the innocent, *against the Lord and against his Christ* <note>original: "aduersus Dominū & aduersus Christum eius"</note> his son. But because that psalm <note>Psalm 2</note> presses upon them, the stubborn opponents will say it is understood to be about David. But I ask them to listen to how individual details can actually apply to David. For about whomever this is said, it is necessary that he have a common cause with God. For the phrase *let us break their bonds,* etc., <note>Psalm 2:3</note> shows that a common law and yoke must be imposed upon all men. But David did not have this; for he was not the author of the law. Indeed, no other bonds could restrain all the kings of the earth other than some universal law; and there was none. The Law of Moses was intended to possess only one people. The Law of the Messiah belongs to everyone. It follows, therefore, that what is written—*He who dwells in the heavens*—is about the Messiah and his law. God would not have mocked all the princes of the earth simply on account of the petty kingdom of a minor ruler like David, because the law under which David lived did not apply to those other princes. Nor should God have been moved to fury against those who did not sin by refusing to accept the "bonds" of Moses. It was the Messiah whom God established as his king upon Mount Zion, so that he might announce the decree and the *new law*. It was true once to say of David, *today I have begotten you* <note>original: "hodie genui te"; Psalm 2:7</note>; but it is always true of Christ and his generation. For just as the action of fire always proceeds from its power as long as it is fire, so His wisdom proceeds from the power of God from eternity. Furthermore, if this is said of David, when did he ever possess the ends of the earth? That belongs to God alone. He rules them with the strict laws of the soul, laws harder than iron and adamant, and he shatters them when he wills. For he is God. It is necessary for the kings of the world to depend upon his example and law. It is necessary for everyone to *kiss the Son, lest the Lord be angry,* etc. Thus, since these things clearly do not fit David at all, or only very little, it follows that it must be understood as referring to the Messiah, the Son of God. 

In this way they distort and subvert the meanings of all the psalms, but they especially subvert Psalm 109 <note>Psalm 110 in modern Protestant and Hebrew Bibles. This psalm contains the line "The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand," which was a central text in early Christian arguments for Christ's divinity.</note> because they are most vehemently pressed by it to recognize the divinity of Christ. But I move on to other things. I judge it superfluous to write about how many things have been written concerning the torments of Jesus Christ, since solid chapters on this matter are found in the prophets. I will be content to refute the impiety of the wicked rabbis where they distort the 53rd chapter of Isaiah with their dreams. It goes like this: *Who has believed our report, and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed?* <note>Isaiah 53:1</note> These things cannot be understood as a physical or common deed like a war. For they ought to have been sufficiently persuaded of what God could do in that regard, whether by afflicting or by saving. Therefore, the prophet declares what this report is that is so wonderful as to be scarcely believable: *And he grew up like a sapling before him* <note>original: "Et ascendit sicut uirgultum coram eo"</note>, that is, before God the Father. The rich, the great, those supported by worldly things, and the wicked are exalted like the cedar of Lebanon; but this one, who is the arm and power of God, rises up like a sapling, so that nothing is more humble and abject or less believable than that the highest being, like God, should be so humble as to seem lower than the lowest. *And like a shrub from parched ground*: because it tends toward the things above. For the affairs of the Hebrew people were never so cut down that they did not retain some splendor. I will not mention how impudently they try to turn a single man into a whole people. *He has no beauty, nor majesty,* he says: *and he had no form for which we should desire him; he was despised, the rejection of men, a man most afflicted, and one who showed weakness. And like one who turns the gazes of men away from himself, he was despised, and we did not esteem him.* If this is said about the Jewish people, who is it that says this about them? Not the enemies who afflict them, nor God who sends the punishment—therefore, no one. For no one speaks of themselves in the third person. All these things are about the affliction of Jesus Christ and his abjection. For he was so defiled by spit, mud, and his own blood, that he seemed more abject than a leper. # ON THE CONCORD OF THE WORLD
### BOOK IV

...the wicked nation thought. <note>Postel is likely referring to the Jewish leaders or those who rejected Jesus.</note>

> Truly he himself has borne our infirmities, and carried our sorrows, and we esteemed him as a leper struck by God and humbled. <note>original: "Vere languores nostros ipse tulit... et nos reputauimus eū lepra percussū à Deo et humiliatū." This is a citation of Isaiah 53:4 from the Latin Vulgate.</note>

These things explain themselves well enough; they do not apply to the people [of Israel], neither today, nor during the Babylonian captivity. For although some may waste away with thinness, it is nothing like leprosy. And even if it were similar, no people can, while being punished themselves, bear the sorrows of another. Furthermore, what a great and unheard-of miracle it would be—so great that no one would believe it—to see (what you almost never see) men worn down and afflicted by wars? Certainly Christ suffered for us, the just for the unjust. For no man, merely as a man, can bear the infirmities and sorrows of another. It follows:

> But he was wounded for our iniquities, he was bruised for our crimes, and the correction was upon him so that we might have peace, and by his bruises we are healed. <note>Isaiah 53:5</note>

<margin>the whole world</margin> 
What is more wonderful than this? That from the bruises and pain of one innocent, righteous, poor, and rejected man, the whole world is healed? That God and man together should bear these signs of weakness?

> All we like sheep have gone astray, and the Lord laid on him the iniquities of us all. <note>Isaiah 53:6</note>

What does this have to do with the [Jewish] people? If this is said of the people, then either the Babylonian captivity did not happen, or this present one is not happening. But since both did occur, it follows that no expiation was ever made for all of you through them. Stop your raving, you impious men, and stop seducing the wretched people. All men were sinners except for Christ and Mary. <note>Postel here includes the Virgin Mary in the state of sinlessness, a common Catholic doctrine known as the Immaculate Conception.</note> Christ died for the sins of all; he alone, on account of his divinity, was able and willing to transmit the fruit of his death—which he paid for our sins—to all men who believe in him. For a pure man <note>i.e., a mere human</note> could not do that. The "bruise" <note>original: "liuor"</note> truly shows the shedding of blood, in which he established a covenant for those who believe. Then:

> While he is oppressed and afflicted, he did not open his mouth. Like a sheep led to the slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer, he did not open his mouth. <note>Isaiah 53:7</note>

Who would believe these things? That the most innocent man would not even emit a sound, being led like a lamb to the execution? O Jesus Christ, how great is your goodness. Weigh these things, you blasphemers; he will have mercy on you, he waits for you to come to mercy.

> He was taken away from distress and from judgment. <note>Isaiah 53:8</note>

But that people [of Israel], if it pleases the Gods, <note>A sarcastic use of a classical Latin idiom ("si Diis placet").</note> did not die, nor was it led to slaughter, but was preserved for servitude.

> Who shall declare his generation? <note>Isaiah 53:8</note>

It follows from this place that he has nothing in common with other men regarding his birth. But everyone knows where and how the Jewish people (the people of the devil) were born and how they were generated. The generation of Christ is eternal and unique; the other is temporary.

> And yet he was cut off from the land of the living. For the crime of my people, I struck him. <note>Isaiah 53:8</note>

This is what Daniel writes: *And Christ shall be killed, but not for himself*—that is, not for his own sake, but for the sake of the salvation of all who believe in him. <note>Postel links Isaiah 53 to Daniel 9:26, a standard move in Christian apologetics to prove the Messiah's death.</note>

> His burial was made with wicked men—that is, his death. The rich were in his death. Because he did no iniquity, nor was there deceit in his mouth. And the Lord willed to crush him in infirmity. When he has placed his soul for sin, he shall see a long-lived seed. <note>Isaiah 53:9–10</note>

Let the Jews see their own ravings in this passage. If the prophet is dealing with a man or men, how can he see "long-lived seed" when he is dead? Does a dead man see long-lived seed? Nonsense. <note>original: "nugæ"</note> Behold, he is God from God, the Son from the Father, eternal from the eternal.

> The will of the Lord shall be directed by his hand. Because his soul has labored in death, he shall see and be satisfied. In his knowledge, my righteous servant shall himself justify many, and he himself shall bear their iniquities. <note>Isaiah 53:10–11</note>

No one besides God can justify. Therefore, he speaks of God, yet calls him a servant. Therefore, he is also man, otherwise he could not have died. Therefore the Messiah, the blessed God, suffered for us—the just for the unjust—so that by his justice we might return to grace with God.

> Therefore, I will give him a great multitude for spoils, and the strong shall be his prey. <note>Isaiah 53:12</note>

All types of men have already partly yielded to him, and partly will yield,

> because he delivered his soul—that is, his life—unto death: and he was counted among the wicked.

# WILLIAM POSTEL, BOOK IV

He was crucified with thieves, so that he might seem to receive from their company the very disgrace that he himself lacked. And he himself "bore the sins of many"—not of all, unless they believe in him—and "prayed for the transgressors." <note>These are further references to the "Suffering Servant" in Isaiah 53:12.</note> When he was fixed to the cross, close to death, he prayed for the wicked Jews, saying:

> Father, spare them, for they know not what they do. <note>original: "Pater parce illis, quia nesciūt quid faciunt." See Luke 23:34.</note>

Oh, divine mercy! By your own people you were beaten with whips, defiled with spit, worn down by blows, and crowned with thorns. Others had their crosses carried for them; you carried your own, and yet you deign to pray for that people who committed those things against you. In the following chapter, [Isaiah] calls the same one the God of the whole earth, the Lord of hosts, and the redeemer of Israel. These things are described no more clearly in the Gospels than they were written by Isaiah.

However, Zechariah revealed the nature of his death in chapter 13. After speaking of false prophets, he says this about the true one and the Messiah: And it shall be said to him (the Messiah, of whom he had spoken shortly before):

> What do these wounds in the middle of your hands mean? <note>original: "Quid sibi uolunt plagæ istæ in medio manuū tuarū?" See Zechariah 13:6.</note>

And he will say:

> With these wounds I was struck in the house of those who loved me; by the judges of Jerusalem, to which I had come to save, I was thus treated.

That this is said of the Messiah is shown when God says:

> O sword, awake against my shepherd: strike the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered. And I will turn my hand to the little ones, and they shall be in all the earth, says the Lord; two parts in it shall be cut off and fail, and the third part shall be left in it. And I will lead the third part through fire, and I will refine them as silver is refined, and test them as gold is tested. He shall call upon my name, and I will hear him. I will say, "You are my people," and he will say, "The Lord is my God." <note>Zechariah 13:7-9. Postel interprets the "two parts" as the unbelieving Jewish population and the "third part" as the burgeoning Christian church.</note>

What follows from that place to the end must be understood as referring to the Messiah. For no mortal is read of before who died from wounds after his hands were pierced during his execution. Those who ought to have loved him did this to him, yet he always held them as friends nonetheless. When the sword was raised against Christ and persecution came, all his disciples—except for a few following from a distance—were scattered for fear of death. For they were not firm in him until the Holy Spirit descended upon them and encouraged them toward death. Meanwhile, however, while Jesus was suffering, the Lord kept the disciples in his love until he should rise again. Finally, two parts from Judea were afflicted unto death and dispersion, but a third part of the Apostles and Christians remained, though they were to be refined and purged by fire. Indeed, that people, famous everywhere for their martyrdom and miracles for 300 years and more, was truly called the people of God.

David mentions the piercing of the hands in Psalm 21:

> They pierced my hands and my feet; they counted all my bones. <note>original: "Foderūt manus meas & pedes meos, dinumerauerūt omnia ossa mea." Psalm 22:16-17 in modern numbering.</note>

This reveals that he was stretched out on the cross, and because of the weight of the body, the joints of the bones were separated. That entire Psalm was written concerning the afflictions of Christ's body and his human nature, by which he was indeed vehemently tortured. It also describes how those passing by mocked him, saying that because he had saved many, he could not save himself. And so these scoundrels moved their heads in mockery and turned up their noses, laughing at the afflicted one. A little later, he mentions those who wanted to divide his garments, which they finally shared by lot. Everything matches the event. 

Nothing more shameful than the cross could be devised by the Jews against Christ. It was necessary for him—just as he possessed all the highest things in himself—to also undergo the highest infamy for our salvation. For since the fruit, the price, and the redemption of the whole world lay in his death, it was fitting for him to undergo a death piled high with every title of infamy (as far as the opinion of the wicked was concerned). 

As for how cruel it was, I leave that to be judged by common estimation. Since no one, even the strongest man, could balance his body for even a few moments if lifted up by a nail through both hands, what could Christ our God suffer, hanging alive on the cross for three whole hours? He did not cling by clutching the nail, but by having his hands and feet pierced through, with the entire mass of his body hanging from the fixing of the nails. O soul, purged by his blood, consider that he suffered these things for you!

Indeed, by a divine account (as I believe), the Egyptians used the cross hieroglyphically <note>original: ἱερογλυφικῶς</note> as a sign many years before the passion of Jesus Christ...

# ON THE CONCORD OF THE WORLD

...they were preserving him as a symbol of eternal life. Yet to him, though he was the highest of the human race, when he thirsted, they offered neither water nor anything drinkable. Instead, mixing wine with gall on a sponge, they offered it to him on a reed. This was exactly what the prophet David predicted in Psalm 68 <note>Original: "psalmo 68." In modern Bibles, this is Psalm 69:21.</note>: *They gave me gall for my food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.*

Indeed, it was no less wonderful than it was memorable that for as long as he was in the pangs of death—from the sixth hour (midday) until the ninth hour (three in the afternoon)—darkness occurred, with the sun suffering an eclipse over the whole world. This event was even noted in the annals of the pagans. <note>Postel likely refers to the reports of Phlegon of Tralles or Thallus, historians often cited by Christian apologists to prove the darkness at the Crucifixion was a global, historical event.</note> The Jewish temple opened of its own accord, and many dead were seen to have risen. Truly, the earthquake was so great that no larger one has ever been seen in the world within the memory of literature or of men. In that hour, twelve cities in Bithynia <note>A Roman province in what is now Turkey.</note> were destroyed by it.

But I am "washing a brick" <note>original: "lauo laterem." A Latin idiom meaning to labor in vain or to perform a useless task.</note> if I hope to prove these things to you by external testimonies when you do not believe your own. The prophet Amos predicted that eclipse word-for-word in his 8th chapter: *And it shall come to pass on that day (namely, when Christ suffers), the sun shall set at midday, and I will darken the earth in the day of light.* For the "day of light" for the world was the day of Christ's death; because until that day, even the most holy fathers had been in the "lake without water," <note>A reference to the Limbo of the Patriarchs.</note> from which he extracted them. The sun failed on that day at the time Christ was fixed to the cross, even though it was the fourteenth moon (a full moon), a time when it is naturally impossible for the sun to suffer an eclipse. The first advent has this in common with the last: that the sun must be deprived of light. However, at the last advent, it will happen for a total transformation, for then the moon and stars will also fail along with the sun.

He rose from the dead on the third day, which David noted by saying: *I slept and was heavy with sleep, and I rose up, because the Lord took me up.* And likewise: *Because you will not leave my soul in hell, nor will you allow your holy one to see corruption.* <note>Psalm 3:5 and Psalm 16:10 respectively.</note> Ascending on high, *he led captivity captive and gave gifts to men*—that is, he led the fathers and patriarchs of the Old Testament, redeemed from Limbo <note>original: "lymbis."</note>, with him into heaven. And he "gave gifts to men" by granting his grace and the remission of sins, and finally by sending the Holy Spirit into the faithful ten days after his ascension. The prophets mention the sending of the Holy Spirit in many places, which is why I will refrain from listing them here. For his apostles clearly enough revealed the grace of Jesus Christ; beyond receiving it in the visible form of fiery tongues, they gave it to all believers by the laying on of hands, so that everyone spoke in various tongues they had not learned and possessed a remarkable knowledge of the Holy Scriptures.

There is much in the prophets concerning the second coming of Christ, which concerns everyone equally. Consider this for yourselves. You Jews have the context of the Gospel drawn from the prophets and from books approved by you, through which it is clear enough that whatever could be said of the Messiah is said of Jesus. Therefore, the Messiah (or Christ) promised to you in the Law and the Prophets, and the Jesus received by us as the Christ, must be one and the same. If you wish to return to him, God is pious and merciful. Now, I shall satisfy the objections usually raised by you against his coming, lest I seem to have failed you in any matter.

### ON JEWISH OBJECTIONS
#### *and their solution.*

In this section, I will follow the order of Petrus Galatinus, the greatest ornament of the Franciscans. <note>Pietro Colonna Galatino (1460–1540), an Italian theologian who used the Talmud and Kabbalah to argue for the truths of Christianity in his work *De Arcanis Catholicae Veritatis*.</note> No one has ever "shaken out" the vanities of the Talmud more learnedly, nor collected from them more effectively those things which serve to refute the lack of faith <note>original: "perfidiam." In a 16th-century theological context, this specifically meant "unbelief" or "rejection of the faith."</note> of the Jews. If he had been as strong in his reasoning as he was in his use of authorities, all the labor of those who followed him would have been superfluous. But...

# GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK IV

Because I proceed by reason wherever I can, and I write this work so that it may be translated into the Hebrew language, I collect in a few short chapters what others have written with great piles of authorities. If any light is added to these matters by my industry, I leave that to be judged by posterity. The Jews rely on twelve principal arguments to prove that the Messiah has not yet come, and therefore that Jesus is not the Messiah. First, because he was to come at the "end of days." But since it is not yet the end, he has not yet come. I hissed away <note>original: "exibilaui." A theatrical term meaning to hiss an actor off the stage; here used to mean rejecting an idea with scorn.</note> this silliness rather than a reason in the previous sections, when I examined the second chapter of Isaiah with this reasoning: No one fails to concede that perfection is better than imperfection. The Jews do not deny that the Messiah must be the most excellent of all men; similarly, his law must be so perfect that no greater or holier law can be given. Since this is so, and since Divine Providence does things in the best way possible, and since every law is established to keep men in their duty, it was necessary for the Messiah to have come long ago. For otherwise, God would have acted in the manner of a fool, making that which is worse more durable than that which is good.

For by the tradition of Elijah, and by the number of the six *alephs* <note>The Hebrew letter 'Aleph' (א) represents the number 1,000. Postel refers to a Kabbalistic interpretation of the six 'alephs' in the first verse of Genesis as signifying 6,000 years of world history.</note> at the beginning of Genesis and the order of natural things, it must be accepted that the world will last 6,000 years—a point they themselves are most convinced of. There were two thousand years of the "law of nature" and *tohu* <note>original: "thohu." Hebrew for "formlessness" or "chaos," referring to the era before the giving of the Mosaic Law.</note> until Abraham; the Law of Moses ought to have lasted at least as long, and the Law of the Messiah for the same amount of time. But if the Messiah has not yet come, then the Law of Moses has lasted three thousand five hundred years—nearly double what is proper. Consider, with the modern Jews, that 260 years have vanished from the annals—for they subtract that many years so that they may more freely sell a "priced hope" to their kinsmen and contradict Christ. Even by that reasoning, we would be 700 years away from the end of the world (granting their tradition, for one must not seriously divine regarding periods of time). Therefore, since God rules this world with the most excellent laws (to the extent that men are capable of them), he must be accused of either ignorance or envy if he does not offer that which is highest for governing men, and meanwhile permits us to be fed on inferior things—as if he were to fill us up with husks and bran, and only set out the most excellent feasts as desserts that vanish immediately. To think this of God is impious.

Thus, according to the tradition of Elijah and following the Hebrew truth, there are two thousand years from Adam to Abraham, and just as many from him to Christ, with a few years anticipated; and already from him [Christ] there are 1,542 years. These numbers correspond to the truth of things—which consist of six different natures—and to the sacred utterances which place rest on the seventh day, and to the tradition of Elijah, and to the opinions of the Kabbalists. Wherefore it follows that the Jews have been in error and a reprobate sense for fifteen hundred years. For if what they assert were true, why would they have been deluded to this day by the innumerable false timelines of the rabbis, since the end of the world has not yet come? I have taught above how the "last days" are to be understood in most passages of the prophets. For when they are spoken of regarding the first coming, they are understood as the last days of the Mosaic Law, whose worship was to be amended under the Messiah. When spoken of regarding the second coming, they are truly understood as the end of the world. But then Jesus Christ will not come to give a law, but to take eternal vengeance on those who neglected the law—he whom the Jews, obstinate until then, will feel as a judge and avenger, not a mediator. A few years before the second coming, they will be mocked by the Antichrist, the son of perdition, who—with reins loosened for every kind of pleasure, and famous for deceptions and war—will rush headlong with his followers into destruction upon Christ's arrival. For he will be desired by those who strive to join all types of pleasure to religion. This you may easily prove by the fact that they have never followed any holy, humble, and pious man, but have approved many wicked men similar to the final Antichrist.

Bar- <note>Catchword for the next page, likely referring to Bar Kokhba, a failed messianic claimant.</note>

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD
### PAGE 418

**Bar Kokhba** <note>original: "Barchozibas." Simon bar Kokhba led the Jewish revolt against Rome in 132–136 AD; many of his followers believed him to be the Messiah.</note>, two others, **Simon Magus** <note>original: "Symonem Samaritanum," the Samaritan sorcerer mentioned in the Book of Acts.</note>, a certain **Egyptian** (whom Josephus mentions, along with many others), **Julian the Apostate**, and a **false Moses** <note>A 5th-century figure in Crete who convinced many Jews he was Moses and could lead them across the sea on dry land, resulting in many drownings.</note> who mocked and drowned countless people in the waters of Crete. Finally, there is **Muhammad**, who in his character is closest to the **Antichrist**. Indeed, if he had joined magical deceptions to his crimes and cruelty, he would have been the very last and greatest one. Aside from those under Julian, an innumerable multitude of Jews perished by the works of these "Messiahs."

I have also satisfied a second objection raised in that same place, in which they say that **Mount Zion** will be higher than all the other mountains of the world upon the arrival of the Messiah. They claim that with **Mount Sinai** and **Mount Carmel** placed on top of it, it will reach a height of three leagues or miles, to the summit of which the Messiah will ascend flying like a cloud, as **Isaiah** said. How ridiculous these things are, and how unworthy of being said or thought, I will not say. They expose themselves. Such fictions are exploded by others. But because those who use authority without reason will subscribe to anything according to how they are moved, I will leave aside the bickering and come to reasons. If that earthly mountain is to be so high that it is lower than none, it must happen for the sake of some great and unheard-of utility or pleasure—either for access to heaven, or for better air, or for a greater and more elegant view. If it were for closer access to heaven, what are 3 miles compared to the 255 miles at which distance **Pliny** (along with **Posidonius**) <note>Ancient Greek and Roman natural philosophers. Their estimates of the distance to the moon were far smaller than reality.</note> thinks the heaven of the moon is from the earth? And how far is the heaven of the moon from the highest heaven? Truly, this would be done in vain for such a cause. It cannot be for the sake of purer air; for at 24 stadia <note>An ancient unit of distance; 24 stadia is roughly 2.8 miles.</note>, whatever is composed of the dregs of clouds is collected. This is indeed the beginning of the "middle region" <note>The *media regio* in ancient meteorology was the cold, middle layer of the atmosphere where clouds and storms were thought to form.</note>. Since, therefore, not utility but loss would be had from this thing, it would be a bad thing to do. Nor is it done for the sake of a view. For the higher you are, although the view opens up further, you nevertheless distinguish things less, whereas the duty of sight is to represent certain and clear notions. Even if you suppose the plain to be open on all sides, with the widest levels of the ground surrounding it, the human eye commonly does not penetrate beyond a hundred thousand paces. I even grant that he might be higher than the sun, so that your Messiah could see the world at a single glance: he would only see half of the terrestrial and aquatic globe. Therefore, in every way, that labor of raising the mountain would be vain. Thus, it is (as is frequent in the sacred writings) that **Christ** is called a **mountain** because of properties akin to the thing, as is the **Church** <margin>The Church</margin> and its holy members, and many other things; let learned theologians distinguish which terms apply in which places and for what reasons.

Because all nations have not flocked to **Jesus**, they argue that Jesus is not the Messiah. I have sufficiently shown above that no man—not even **God** himself—can (except at a specific point in time) rule the whole world by force while free will remains in man, who is subject to corruptible matter. The Jews themselves provide proof of this, for they could neither bear God because of terror, nor obey him because of his power. Yet the most excellent way of maintaining rule over the wicked is terror. Therefore, the Messiah, who must be a man, will never be able to rule the whole world according to their bodies. He will, however, rule according to their souls. He will also gather all nations to his empire—all those from every nation who believe in him. For if there were not going to be evil people under him, even among those who received his law, he would give a law in vain. For a law serves no purpose if there is no sin. God does not do violence to free will, much less does Christ. But if God was never able to rule one nation freely without there always being more evil people in it than good, will the Messiah not be greater than God in the whole world? This brings nothing against Christ. From the whole circle of the earth, Jesus Christ has had and has followers. **Moses** had one nation chosen by God, and that one was most stubborn; Christ calls all without distinction to salvation, and it is set before all that they may follow. If they are unwilling, the fault for that is not in the law, or in the lawgiver...

...is not from the Creator. Very few follow what is good; many follow what is vain and useless. The whole world, whether it wishes to or not, will be forced to gather under the empire of Christ at his second and terrible coming, and be bent toward judgment. Then, the stubbornness of matter <note>original: "materiæ peruicacia," a philosophical concept suggesting that physical substance resists divine perfection or form</note> will no longer harm the blessed; they shall live in total freedom, yet will be unable to sin. Truly, the wicked, the harmful, and the cruel—deprived of repentance—shall suffer eternal punishments. Thus, from the first coming of Christ, all nations (that is, those from all nations who wish to believe in him) approach him; but at the resurrection and the judgment, even those who resist shall obey him.

Next, they <note>Postel refers here to Jewish scholars or critics of Christianity</note> say: "The nations do not yet say this: 'Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord,' etc. Therefore, the Messiah has not yet come." This is utterly false. For in the whole world, from the birth of Christ, there have always been certain people—though very few—who are true Christians. These people never have anything else on their lips but the praises and proclamations of the **Holy Mountain** (which I explained above), so that they may invite all nations to it. As was seen above, "all nations" refers to the elect of all nations gathered during the first coming. However, "all" refers to every single person at the second coming. Indeed, the prophet clearly reveals which mountain should be understood here when he says these things. For if it were understood as a specific local and earthly mountain, it would not hold even a hundred-thousandth part of the people born in the whole world, even if it exceeded the size of the earth's hemisphere. Therefore, it must be understood as Christ and his Church, since he is the highest of mountains, and the whole world has nothing greater—just as they hope for nothing greater than the future Messiah. Thus, since everything attributed to the Messiah matches Jesus, the Son of God and the Virgin Mary, he must necessarily be recognized by the Jews as the Messiah.

They object a fifth time, saying that the Messiah has not yet come because weapons of war have not been converted into agricultural tools, which is supposed to happen upon his arrival. I have already responded to this argument as well. Because humans are still able to sin—whose hearts will be prone to evil from youth until the day of judgment—the King Messiah gave a most excellent law. If humans did not sin, such a holy law would not be necessary; indeed, it would have no power. For things that have no purpose or use are in vain. Since there is a future law, there will also be sin, virtue, and vice. Therefore, evil men and those who wrong others must be punished; there will be rebellious cities, and there will be provinces and wicked kingdoms that must be subdued by mortals. Does this mean the prophet spoke falsely? Not at all. All those who profess Christ from the heart would rather suffer the ultimate extremes than wish to harm another human being even with a finger (unless they rise up against the wicked for the sake of an injury to God or a brother). Let them be plundered, hurt, or despised: they count the greatest injuries as blessings, so that they may one day enjoy Christ face to face. Innumerable examples of this way of life were seen in the times of the early Church. With this patience, the Church of Christ made its beginning against the consensus of the whole world. Therefore, those people truly change their swords and spears into sickles and hoes who do not even take revenge with fists or words. Such people exist, have existed, and will exist from all nations until the second coming, in which there will be no law, because sin will no longer be committed. The same solution applies to "eternal peace." For a Christian carries eternal peace within their heart, as I have already said, and it does not depend on any external thing. God stands in the place of everything for them. Nor can it ever happen that one who has abolished all desires (except those joined to necessity) does <margin>// not</margin> live in peace. Under the law of the Messiah there will be evil men, otherwise that law would serve no purpose. But the prophet wrote, "There is no peace for the wicked, says the Lord" <note>Isaiah 48:22</note>. Therefore, there is peace without end for all those chosen by Christ, but not for the wicked. And after the second coming, peace will belong to the whole world, once sin is exiled. Regarding the dwelling of wild beasts together without mutual harm, the same principle I stated above applies. For there will be beasts...

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD

<margin>e.</margin>
...formerly men who were tyrants, robbers, and criminals—embittered by every kind of wickedness and, as it were, turned into wild beasts—become companions, brothers, and friends with pious and good men once they have submitted their necks to the **light yoke of Christ.** <note>original: "iugo Christi leuissimo," a reference to Matthew 11:30, "For my yoke is easy and my burden is light."</note> There will still be differences in duties and offices, yet people will recognize one another as equals; those to whom they were once accustomed to doing harm, they shall treat as brothers, laying aside their former character. Otherwise, why would such a holy law bind creatures entirely devoid of reason who are incapable of sinning? Why would wild beasts cease to do what they do by the guidance of nature, without any intent to harm, and in which they do not commit a sin? See, O blind people, where you have fallen: you make brute animals equal to humans just so you can follow your own dreams. For if animals were able to sin, they would necessarily possess reason. 

Why then, the **circumcised man** <note>original: "recutitus," a Latin term for one who is circumcised, used here in a polemical sense to refer to a Jewish person.</note> will ask, did the prophet use such names if he understood something else? I will tell you. The cause was the arrogant and glory-hungry magistrates. If the prophet had spoken openly to them, saying that the noble and the ignoble, the king and the subjects, the priest and the people were to be made equal, they would have done away with him as a subverter of public order. Although he did not say this openly, he nevertheless paid the penalty to a wicked prince for speaking the truth too freely. For while **Isaiah** <note>The prophet Isaiah, to whom the prophecy of the wolf and the lamb in Isaiah 11 is attributed.</note> (among whose writings these things are found) miraculously withdrew himself from the sight of Jehu, and there was nothing in the vicinity where he could hide—for he had vanished, as it is handed down, and had entered the trunk of a cedar tree, his holy body giving way as the wood miraculously yielded to him—the prince ordered the trunk to be split with a saw. And so the prophet was cut through the middle of his head. Thus it is read in the histories of the Hebrews. <note>This refers to the "Martyrdom of Isaiah," an ancient non-biblical tradition that Isaiah was martyled by being sawn in half inside a tree.</note> The prophets intentionally wove many miracles and illustrious matters before their stubborn listeners to make room for divine revelations. 

Therefore, in this passage, Isaiah changed the names. Savage men, from the time of the first coming, if they receive the truth from the heart, shall become most gentle and perfected in every part, becoming equal even to the lowliest. But at the **second coming**, there will no longer be any place for laws or social orders. Christ will enter into an accounting of their past lives with all people.

What shall I say of the unhappy hope of the **adulterous Israelites**? <note>Postel uses "adulterous" in the biblical sense of being unfaithful to a covenant.</note> They say: "The Messiah has not yet come because we have not yet entered the Holy Land. For he would have led us back if he had come." This entire nation, blinder than a mole, refers all these things to the pleasures of the body and to earthly delights. Tell me, O Hebrew: have you not learned from at least forty passages in the prophets that Israel was to be rejected? If you deny it, reread the things I collected above regarding the rejection of your race. You will believe it whether you want to or not. If you admit it, then you were destined to be estranged from both Laws. Otherwise, you are still under the Law of Moses. "We are," you will say. Do you believe there is a God? "I do." I suppose you are also willing to confess Him to be merciful, pious, just, holy, and the best. "I am." If He is such a God, and yet for fifteen hundred years He has seen a people living under His law, pouring out prayers to Him from the heart almost every moment, macerating themselves with fasts, and nourishing their brothers with alms so that no one is needy among the Jews—then it would follow that He has become some sort of wicked and impious God who has not looked upon these things for so long, whereas in the time when He was favorable to you, He was ready to help you at a moment's notice. Or, as is most true, you have fallen away from the Law of Him who no longer hears you. For if He approved of His Law within you, He would have heard you at least after several generations of men. But I have shown above what your sin was, by which you fell into the eternal indignation of God. It is necessary, therefore, that you are no longer the people of God. You are not to be gathered together any longer, except for those who will be converted to Christ, or those who will follow the Antichrist. For either you must have no God (which would be unjust, as He would not be hearing His own), or the Jews are not the people of Him who has rejected them for so long. But come, let us look at the condition of your land. You have already confessed that under the Messiah, all nations will gather at the mountain of God. But your land...

# THE FOURTH BOOK OF GUILLAUME POSTEL
### PAGE 421

...you call Syria, which your ancestors inhabited: in the middle of which is Jerusalem. How can it be possible that this Messiah would gather the bodies of all men dispersed throughout the whole world to perform sacred rites in a tiny place that barely covers a four-hundredth part of the entire globe? It is surely impossible. Nevertheless, they shall come together, as it is written. Therefore, it is not by a physical location, but in the harmony of minds and mutual benevolence. You wait in vain, therefore, for what will never happen to you. For 1,542 years now <note>Postel uses this number to date his writing relative to the era of Christ; the work was published in 1544.</note> your land has been possessed by the Gentiles. For such is the faith in the true Messiah, for whose killing by your fathers God seeks punishment from you. For while Pilate did not wish to send him to the cross because he was innocent (so much greater was the justice in the pagans than in you), they said: **"His blood be upon us and upon our children."** <note>original: "Sanguis eius super nos & super filios nostros," a quote from Matthew 27:25.</note> You are paying for the crimes committed by them; this has separated you from God. Do not hope, therefore, that this land subject to generation and corruption <note>A philosophical term referring to the physical, decaying world.</note> was promised to you—a land where even the most fortunate man is unhappy—as if it were a worthy reward for the highest virtue. Just as nothing in the works of man is greater than virtue, so for a reward it can have nothing else but God. Wherever He is, there is the Holy Land, wherever there is faith in Jesus Christ. 

What shall I say to your follies? When you are pressed, you say that the Messiah was indeed born—for he was born when the Temple was destroyed, as is clear from the last chapter of Isaiah: *Before she travailed, she brought forth,* etc. <note>original: "Antequã parturiret," referring to Isaiah 66:7. Postel is mocking a Rabbinic tradition that the Messiah was born on the day the Second Temple was destroyed but remains hidden.</note>—but that he has not yet come. Consider how Satan holds and mocks you, and through the instrument of the Rabbis turns you away from the truth. Was the coming of the Messiah necessary or not? In my judgment, you will say it was necessary, since God and nature do nothing in vain. But if nothing is done in vain, where has that Messiah been hiding for so long, while his people are afflicted and slaughtered everywhere among the nations? Who was ever born and spent 1,500 years in a useless life, especially when his work is so necessary? I set aside the unheard-of lifespan, almost double the life of Adam. Where in the world was he born in the deserts such that at least his father and mother did not know of him? And if they did not speak, who knows he was born? These are dreams and ravings, the mockeries of impostors, worthier of loud laughter than a reply. 

The following argument concerns a certain third temple devised by the modern Rabbis. For because Zechariah speaks of the glory of the church and the harmony of souls in the sixth chapter, where he says: *And he shall build the temple of the Lord* <note>original: "Et ædificabit templũ Dei," from Zechariah 6:12.</note>—they think the Messiah will make a temple out of physical matter and rebuild Jerusalem. But this has not yet happened; therefore, the Messiah has not yet come. You expect a Messiah more perfect and greater than other mortals. Therefore, he will make a temple for God out of the most noble matter in the whole world. But in all of nature, nothing is more noble after God than the human soul and the angelic nature. Therefore, he will take the "matter" of souls for its construction, and from them he will make a temple for himself greater than the corruptible world itself. For he demands souls, so that they may move bodies into the work of God. That third house will be constructed of **living stones**, such as it has already been since the death of Jesus Christ. I would reveal to you the dignity of the stones—that is, the miracles of the apostles and martyrs, with which the entire map of the world could be filled, a taste of which I provided at the beginning of this book. 

But as for the objection concerning the salvation of Israel—that the Jews are not yet saved and therefore the Messiah has not come—I have already satisfied that above. For when the Messiah was sent, he came no less for the salvation of the Gentiles than for the Jews, and from that time there has been no difference in being saved, whether Jew or Gentile. For whoever approaches baptism achieves salvation, not by his own merits, but by the pure grace of Jesus Christ. For unless our salvation depended on his benefit, he would have come in vain. Previous works or laws do nothing (perhaps something toward preparation), but the work is accomplished through faith in him and the merit of his passion.

# ON THE HARMONY OF THE WORLD
### PAGE 422

...at last, with works confirming faith and showing other men that we too are children of God, so that by this reasoning we may prove ourselves to the Father, who will render to each according to his works. You think, O Jews, that you are what you claim to be by confessing and praising God, yet you have fallen from the grace of God; therefore God does not hear you, nor do you now have any greater access to God than any pagan. Yet Jesus awaits you, along with the rest, for repentance—even though he is crucified daily by your Rabbis, just as he was once by your ancestors. He prayed for his persecutors, and this shall benefit you no less than the Gentiles. 

Indeed, I marvel at how you dare to promise yourselves such a restoration, a temple, and a claim to the holy land, since it is written in the book *Sanhedrin*, in the chapter *Helek* <note>Sanhedrin is a tractate of the Talmud; "Helek" (meaning "portion") is its tenth chapter, which discusses who has a "portion" in the world to come.</note>, that the ten tribes are never to enter the holy land and have no part in the future age. Truly, none of you could say from which tribe you descend, except by mere opinion. Only the future coming of Gog and Magog and his slaughter pertains to this; and he will be your messiah, O Jews, when those of you who remain join him against the Christians and the people of God. For although all plagues rising up against the Gospel and inflicting violence through their great numbers are called "Gog and Magog," nevertheless there shall be one man, a "son of perdition," a king of shameless face, who will wear down the world with luxury and portents, and consume the good with unheard-of punishments. Jesus Christ, upon his arrival, will destroy him with the breath of his mouth and destine him to eternal punishments, and immediately bring an end to the world. That this is not a proper name but an allegory is clear from the fact that in the chapter *Helek* in the book *Sanhedrin*, Sennacherib is called Gog and Magog because he rose against the people of God under Hezekiah. However, the following passage from near the end of the chapter proves it refers to the Day of Judgment:

> And it shall be on that day, on the day of the arrival of Gog upon the land of Israel, says the Lord God, that my indignation shall rise up in my fury. And in my zeal, in the fire of my wrath, I have spoken: because on that day there shall be a great commotion upon the land of Israel, and the fish of the sea, and the birds of the sky, and the beasts of the field, and every reptile that moves upon the ground, and all men who are upon the face of the earth shall be moved before my face; and the mountains shall be overturned, and buildings shall fall, and every wall shall collapse to the earth, etc.

From these words, it is most clearly evident that the final judgment is meant. Furthermore, the "land of Israel" signifies the whole world, in which piety shall be trodden down by impiety until the Lord arrives—terrible to all the impious, and ready to put an end to the miseries of mortal life.

There remains a single argument: that Jesus did not leave "seed" <note>original: *semen*, meaning biological offspring or descendants.</note> after him, and therefore was not the Messiah. For in Isaiah 53, it is said of the Messiah:

> He shall see a long-lived seed <note>original: "Videbit semen longæuum"</note> (supply: the Messiah), and the will of God shall prosper in his hand.

I have already satisfied this objection while explaining that chapter; all parts must be connected. And the Lord willed to crush him in infirmity,

> if he shall lay down his life for sin, he shall see a long-lived seed, etc.

See the impiety of these wicked men and those of corrupt mind! When the whole chapter is referred to Christ, to whom it applies just like a history of facts, they then claim it was written about the affliction of the [Jewish] people. But now, where they think they can twist a single word against him, they ascribe it to the Messiah and attribute "seed" to him. The Messiah is killed so that he may see long-lived seed; but after he is dead, he cannot procreate or live on earth among his own. Therefore, these things must be understood as referring to **spiritual seed**. For it is a contradiction to be struck by God and to lay down one's life for the crime of the people, and yet to live as a survivor among men—for those who see a long-lived physical seed must themselves possess a long life. But so it is written. It is also written in Numbers 3: "These are the generations of Moses and Aaron," even though the literal text speaks only of the sons of Aaron. And Rabbi Akiva <note>original: "Rabi Atziba." Postel refers to the famous 2nd-century sage Akiva ben Joseph.</note> explains this passage of Ecclesiastes: "In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening... [do not let your hand rest]" <note>Postel is citing Ecclesiastes 11:6 to argue for a spiritual or continuous "sowing" of followers rather than biological offspring.</note>

# GUILLAUME POSTEL, BOOK IV

...in the evening let not your hand rest <note>A reference to Ecclesiastes 11:6: "In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening let not your hand rest."</note>: this refers to doctrine and learning, poured from the teacher into the disciple, from which one must not desist; hence it is clear that "seed" is used to mean doctrine in two places. But I prefer to argue by reason. The King Messiah ought to be blessed in every part, and most like unto God, as you believe. But no greater likeness to God can exist in man than when he is free from sin. If the Messiah were to have had offspring, he would also have had sin, for no one can procreate without sin, however small—since David says, *and in sin did my mother conceive me* <note>Psalm 51:5.</note>. But it is impious to ascribe the act of biological generation to the Messiah, since his generation is spiritual, as we have already taught. For *he committed no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth* <note>1 Peter 2:22 / Isaiah 53:9.</note>. Furthermore, he who is justice, and salvation, and liberation, must of necessity be God. But Jesus was such a one as the Messiah was described to be. Therefore, he is God and our justice, upon whom no suspicion of sin can fall.

->EPILOGUE OF THE JEWISH ARGUMENT<-

Since we have previously written many and varied things so concisely that they could not be delivered in fewer words, and they can hardly be drawn into an Epilogue since they are like a concluding speech and a compendium, nevertheless, so that they may be more easily held and preserved in your memory, I shall touch upon the main headings. By your captivity of fifteen hundred years, you are now shown to be rejected; if you do not have faith in the countless scriptures, you will be forced to confess it, being taught by your very senses. Indeed, it is clear that you are outside the law of God and his grace, because you have not been able to move God—who is just, good, merciful, and pious—with such long-lasting prayers, fasts, and rituals. Meanwhile, all the periods for the Messiah's coming have long since passed, both those certainly predicted by the sacred writings and those falsely dreamed up by the impostor Rabbis. Truly, the cause of your present calamity and rejection was the killing of the Messiah Jesus, the Son of God and of Mary, as is clear by these arguments:

By the revelation of Elijah, Christ ought to have come in the four-thousandth year: he came, and you killed him. In the six-hundredth year from Isaiah's prophecy, where there is the secret in the *closed Mem* <note>original: "Mem setuma." This refers to a Hebrew scribal anomaly in Isaiah 9:7 where the letter 'Mem' is written in its final (closed) form in the middle of a word. Christian kabbalists like Postel interpreted this "closed" letter as a symbol of the Virgin Birth.</note>: he came, and you killed him. In approximately the 490th year from the construction of the second house <note>The Second Temple.</note> he came, and was killed, as Daniel had predicted. Fifty years before that, by the disciples of Hillel, who hoped they would see him, it was said he would be near, as you have it in the Talmud: he came when that time had elapsed, and was killed. He came at the time when the Egyptian said the Messiah was born in Bethlehem of Judea. He was to come when the scepter should depart from Judah and from your lawgiver <note>A reference to the "Scepter of Judah" prophecy in Genesis 49:10.</note>: he came in the times of Herod, who destroyed the three orders of the Republic by consuming the royal, sacred, and judicial power, and by instituting other magistrates. He was to come when prophecy and the miracles of the temple should fail: he came, and was embraced by Simeon the Just <note>A High Priest mentioned in the Talmud and associated with the transition of authority.</note>, who was the last of your holy men, under whom the sacred flame ceased to be carried to the right. Miracles failed from the temple forty years before the temple’s destruction; and it was forty years before that Jesus was crucified by you. Forty years before, the ten miracles vanished; it was then the Messiah was killed by you. Forty years before, the temple opened of its own accord, which was opened at Christ’s death when its veil was torn. The Messiah was to come before Titus was born: forty years before his arrival, Christ was killed on the cross. Just as Moses waited forty years so that the heart of the stiff-necked people might be softened; for just as many years God was favorable to you in the desert, waiting for your repentance—just as for the Ninevites an equal number of days spent in fasting, weeping, and wailing appeased the wrath of God. As Moses implored pardon for you by fasting for forty days, so God, after his son Jesus Christ was killed, wished to spare you for forty years, if by chance you might repent. You sold the Just One for money, and you were worse than the gentiles, who had already received him in the neighboring cities. In short, no sign...

# ON THE CONCORD OF THE WORLD

...[no sign] of the future Messiah, whether in time, person, or place, was absent from Jesus. Since that time, you have been in exile, you lack a prophet, you lack miracles, and you lack the mercy of God. To all nations, by a natural impulse, you are held in more hatred than a dog, as if you were enemies to the parent of nature itself. Simon bar Kokhba led the Jewish revolt against Rome (132–136 CE). Postel contrasts him with Jesus as a "false" messiah.</note>. Therefore, he is both man and God, the Son of God, the wisdom of the Father, living with Him and the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen.

## THE IMPIOUS OBJECTIONS OF THE JEWS AGAINST CHRIST AND HIS
## GOSPEL, AND THEIR REFUTATION.

Since having put the enemy to flight and routed them is not truly winning a victory if you leave them the weapons with which they are accustomed to attack you, it merely provokes and irritates them; so that they never perform what is commanded as long as there is any hope of evasion: therefore, I wish to strike from their hands those very weapons with which the Jews attack us and strive to pervert the Gospel. I intend to follow through with an absolute treatment of those things which serve to refute them. I have undertaken this work not for a display of intellect or for the sake of attaining a little glory, but so that a version in the Hebrew language might eventually reach the leaders of the Jews wherever they may live. This will, most importantly, make our own people ready, as they are sometimes unable to satisfy the objections of the Jews on the spot. Therefore, if after my Arabic version of the first, second, and the beginning of this [third] part, I am permitted to translate this as well, I shall be earnestly gathered [to the task]. 

But if death or some misfortune prevents me from carrying this out, I pray and beseech by the most holy name of Jesus Christ all professors and those skilled in the Hebrew language that, if they approve of this work, they translate it into that language, whether they include or remove my name. Since Paris <note>original: "Lutetia," the Latin name for Paris.</note> has a man who is easily the prince in the knowledge of this language, Francois Vatable <note>original: "F. Vatablum." A renowned French humanist and Hebraist.</note>—far superior even to the most excellent of the Jews (whose grandsons are also trained in the same singular erudition)—along with Paul Canossa, Alan Caliginus <note>Likely a reference to the Hebraist Jean Cinquarbres.</note>, and one who is excellent in familiar conversation beyond his years, all of them Royal Professors; and truly countless others who have come out of their schools. In Germany, there are indeed many, but the most celebrated and easily the first are Widmanstadt, Masius, Welteficius, and Fagius <note>These were leading 16th-century Christian Hebraists and scholars of Oriental languages.</note>. I would wish all of them to be asked that, if they judge this worthy of their translation, they do not deny their labor to the perishing Jews, as they will receive ample rewards for this labor from Christ. 

As for the objections of the Jews which [Sebastian] Münster <note>A famous German cartographer and Hebraist.</note> attached to his edition of the Gospel of Matthew, I have seen fit to follow them in all respects; although I do not think that specific copy of the Gospel is ancient, as I saw it in many places in Constantinople and brought back a transcript with those same objections, and left it in Venice in the hands of my dearest friend, Marco Antonio Giustiniani, a man of patrician rank and most adorned in both learning and virtue, from whom whatever can be bestowed from friend to friend...

# BOOK IV OF GUILLAUME POSTEL
### PAGE 425

...can be, while we were once received among the Turks. But I begin to run through everything in such a way that I proceed according to those things I have already written. For I shall touch only upon those things which have not previously presented themselves in passing, while repeating the rest. I do not wish to refute the insults they bring against Christ, Mary, and Joseph out of their own impiety, since the whole world cries out against them; indeed, to be reviled by the wicked is no less laudable than to be praised by the most excellent. In the first chapter, they say the genealogy of Christ was described in vain through the line of Joseph, since he himself is not the father of Christ, and that it ought to have been traced back to Mary. Therefore, they argue, Christ is not the son of David because he is not the son of Joseph. This was done by the evangelists for two reasons: first, through **scriptural usage**, and second, on account of the **law** established for the Hebrews, which I shall speak of immediately after repeating the excellence of the Messiah.

Among them, it is agreed that the Messiah, whom the Jews still expect, ought to be the most outstanding of all men and as similar to God as is possible. Therefore, he ought to have been conceived, born, lived, reigned, and died more excellently than other men, and by differing from them as much as possible. For otherwise, if he were like other men in every way, he would have many companions in his virtue and excellence; and since the pinnacle of virtue cannot be held among mortals by one to whom many are equal, a superior could be given. Let him be such a one, then, that compared to him Moses, his law, and his prosperity are nothing in comparison—most worthy, indeed, he who was promised to Abraham to reign forever, whom Jacob, Moses, David, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and the rest of the prophets deservedly predicted, as one greater than whom none would come for the salvation of all nations.

He ought, therefore, to have been conceived and born in a manner unlike others. Not, therefore, from the common seed of others, nor from a corrupted woman; thus he was to be sown by divine inspiration and born of a virgin, than which nothing greater can be given. The prophets predicted this in the places noted by me: *God will give a sign, namely that a virgin shall conceive* <note>original: "Dabit Deus signũ quò scilicet uirgo cõcipiet." A reference to Isaiah 7:14.</note>; *the Lord will do a new thing upon the earth: a woman shall encompass a man* <note>original: "faciet Dominus nouũ super terrã, foemina uirum circundabit." A reference to Jeremiah 31:22, which Christian commentators traditionally interpreted as the Virgin Birth.</note>. To the point, then: the Messiah had to be born of a virgin, but it is not the custom in the sacred records for a woman’s genealogy to be woven except through the father. This is the usage of Sacred Scripture; the Holy Spirit wished to accommodate Himself through the Evangelist to the usage of the Old Scripture, so as not to weave the genealogy in an unusual manner.

To these points, since divinely inspired letters ought to have nothing superfluous, it was sufficient to provide the genealogy of the husband. What woman was more famous than Sarah, from whom you draw your race? Yet not even her father’s name is recorded. From where did Ruth come, from whom the royal line descends? Huldah, Deborah, and countless other most famous women were never celebrated by genealogies. Granting that some were mentioned for an extraordinary deed, the Scripture sufficiently indicates the tribe of the woman from the tribe of the husband. As for what the Jews say in responding to us—that they were not and are not bound to take wives from their own tribes—if they mean as they do today, when they have turned away from God and can no longer show from which tribe they come due to captivities and afflictions, I would certainly easily concede that. But I shall deny it if they mean as it was formerly under the Law. For they either kept the law of God, or they did not. If they did not keep it, they were wicked; if they did keep it, they lie when they say they were not bound by it.

For it is written in the last part of Numbers: *Let them marry whom they will, provided it is to men of their own tribe, so that the possession of the children of Israel may not be mixed from tribe to tribe. For all men shall take wives from their own tribe and kinship, and all women shall receive husbands from the same tribe, so that the inheritance may remain in the families.* <note>Postel is paraphrasing Numbers 36:6-9, a law intended to prevent the transfer of ancestral land between the twelve tribes of Israel.</note> Were these things written to be kept, or not? Although wicked interpreters have perverted these things, and princes and nobles have done the opposite—and though your present calamity may not prove it—nevertheless, the divine law was to be kept. For a law ought not to be abolished because of an inconvenience. Thus, since Mary and Joseph were most just, they wished even to subscribe to the law, although the marriage was a "shadowy" one <term>umbratile matrimonium: a legal marriage that was never physically consummated, serving as a legal cover for the divine conception</term>. Lest the divine conception be turned into a disgrace for the virgin, Mary married a man who would assist her in her needs. As for their minimizing the sin of Adam...
